🌐 Web query:

`Playwright Locator.waitFor state: 'visible' vs 'enabled' difference`

💡 Result:

In Playwright, locator.waitFor({ state: 'visible' }) waits until the element matching the locator has a non-empty bounding box and does not have visibility: hidden computed style (i.e., it is visually present on the page). locator.waitFor({ state: 'enabled' }) is not a valid state option. Valid state options for locator.waitFor are: - 'attached': Element is attached to the DOM. - 'detached': Element is not attached to the DOM. - 'visible': Element is visible (as defined above). - 'hidden': Element is either detached or has empty bounding box / visibility: hidden. To wait for an element to become enabled (not disabled via disabled attribute, etc.), use the retrying assertion await expect(locator).toBeEnabled; instead. Playwright actions like click automatically wait for the element to be enabled as part of actionability checks. Example: const button = page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Submit' }); // Wait for visible await button.waitFor({ state: 'visible' }); // Wait for enabled (using assertion) await expect(button).toBeEnabled; await button.click; // Also auto-waits for enabled Note: Some third-party guides incorrectly list 'enabled' as a state, but official docs and source enum confirm only the four states above. A 2025 GitHub issue requesting 'enabled' state was closed, recommending assertions.

Citations:

- 1: https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-locator
- 2: https://playwright.dev/docs/next/api/class-locator

---

🌐 Web query:

`Playwright expect toBeEnabled API documentation`

💡 Result:

The Playwright expect(locator).toBeEnabled assertion ensures the locator points to an enabled element. It is part of the LocatorAssertions API, added in v1.20. Usage: const locator = page.locator('button.submit'); await expect(locator).toBeEnabled; Arguments: - enabled (boolean, optional, added in v1.26): Expected enabled state (default: true). - timeout (number, optional, added in v1.18): Time to retry in milliseconds (defaults to TestConfig.expect.timeout). ## Problem

PHPUnit and Playwright E2E CI checks fail on all 4 open PRs (#1003, #1009, #1012, #1014) with the same root cause: test files reference PHP classes and methods that don't exist on any current branch because their introducing PRs were closed without merging.

**Missing classes in tests:**
- `GratisAiAgent\Abilities\GitSnapshotAbility`
- `GratisAiAgent\Abilities\GitDiffAbility`
- `GratisAiAgent\Abilities\GitRestoreAbility`
- `GratisAiAgent\Abilities\GitListAbility`
- `GratisAiAgent\Abilities\GitPackageSummaryAbility`
- `GratisAiAgent\Abilities\GitRevertPackageAbility`
- `GratisAiAgent\Abilities\GeneratePluginAbility`
- `GratisAiAgent\Abilities\SandboxTestPluginAbility`
- `GratisAiAgent\Abilities\SandboxActivatePluginAbility`
- `GratisAiAgent\Abilities\UpdatePluginSandboxedAbility`
- `GratisAiAgent\Abilities\ScanPluginHooksAbility`
- `GratisAiAgent\Abilities\ScanThemeHooksAbility`

**Missing method:**
- `GratisAiAgent\Core\AgentLoop::partition_tool_calls()`

**Source of missing classes:** These were introduced in PRs #929 (HookScanner), #925 (PluginUpdater), #923 (PluginBuilderAbilities) — all closed 2026-04-15 without merging. The test suite still references them.

Main branch CI passes because it predates these references. The 4 open PRs fail because their branches include code that depends on the unmerged feature PRs.

## Affected PRs

| PR | Issue | Status |
|----|-------|--------|
| #1003 | (none) | feat: tool call details |
| #1009 | #993 (t191) | Typed DTOs |
| #1012 | #999 (t197) | Interfaces |
| #1014 | #994 (t192) | Settings DI |

## Decision Required

Choose one path:

**Option A: Resurrect the closed PRs first.** Reopen PRs #929, #925, #923, fix any conflicts with main, merge them, then the 4 open PRs will have their dependencies satisfied.

**Option B: Remove the missing-class test references.** Update the test files in each open PR branch to remove or mock the missing classes. The classes themselves can be added in a later PR.

**Option C: Restore the classes without the full PRs.** Cherry-pick only the class files from branches `feature/auto-20260415-*` into the 4 open PR branches, without reopening the full PRs.

## Files to Modify

- EDIT: `tests/` — find test files referencing the missing classes (`rg "GitSnapshotAbility|GeneratePluginAbility|ScanPlugin" tests/`)
- EDIT: affected PR branches (not main)

## What

PR #1019 (`fix/stdclass-error-handling`) introduces `EmptyJsonObject` (a custom class replacing bare `stdClass` for JSON empty-object serialization). title: fix: systemic Playwright E2E failures after DI refactor (t190-t196)
body:
## Problem

All 6 Playwright E2E shards are failing on **main** (and every PR branch) since the DI refactoring series (t190–t196) landed on 2026-04-17. This blocks all PR CI and new development.

Evidence: run [`24590256205`](https://github.com/Ultimate-Multisite/gratis-ai-agent/actions/runs/24590256205) on main at 2026-04-17T22:56Z — identical failure set to every PR since.

## Failing tests (specific)

| Test file | Line | Description | Timeout |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tests/e2e/admin-page.spec.js` | 145 | Session list shows sessions after a message is sent | 26s |
| `tests/e2e/admin-page.spec.js` | 290+ | Abilities Search and Filter — entire block | **6–9s** |
| `tests/e2e/automations.spec.js` | 559 | Creating a scheduled automation submits POST | 12–15s |
| `tests/e2e/automations.spec.js` | 938 | Event-driven automation POST | 1.5m |

## Strongest diagnostic signal

The Abilities Search/Filter tests (line 290+) fail in **6–9s** — the Playwright default for element-not-found. The test waits for `.gratis-ai-agent-abilities-manager` to be visible. If it times out in 6s, the element is simply not in the DOM at all. This is a registration/render failure, not a timing issue.

## Most likely root cause (hypothesis)

t194 (`#1007`) removed `CoreServicesHandler` and converted its 10 static registrations to `#[Handler]` DI classes. If any of those handlers is missing from `Plugin::$handlers[]`, the corresponding REST endpoint or admin page section won't be registered.

Contrast: the `admin-page.spec.js:145` (session list after message) and automations tests have longer timeouts — they're sending REST requests that timeout, suggesting the REST endpoints exist but fail.

## Files to investigate

- `includes/Plugin.php` — verify all handlers from t194 are present in `$handlers[]`
- `includes/Bootstrap/AbilitiesHandler.php` — check `register_abilities()` is still called and abilities manager is enqueued correctly
- `includes/Infrastructure/WordPress/Abilities/AbilityCategoryRegistrar.php` — check registration hook
- The specific test fixtures: `tests/e2e/admin-page.spec.js:290` expects `.gratis-ai-agent-abilities-manager` CSS class in DOM

## Verification

```bash
# Run abilities tests locally to confirm
npx playwright test tests/e2e/admin-page.spec.js --grep "Abilities" --headed
# Expected: all pass after fix
# CI: all 6 shards green on main
```

## Context

- Last passing E2E run on main: before t194 merge (2026-04-17)
- 7 DI refactor PRs landed on 2026-04-17: #1005, #1007, #1008, #1009, #1010, #1011, #1017
- PR #1022 (CSS import fix) already merged — not the cause

title: Anthropic 400: tool_use/tool_result mismatch when continuing sessions with prior tool calls
body:
## Problem

When sending a new message in a session that previously had tool calls, the Anthropic API returns:

```
Error: Bad Request (400) - messages.2: `tool_use` ids were found without `tool_result`
blocks immediately after: toolu_01LKd2D7NR6tMXX2z4qnSraL. Each `tool_use` block must
have a corresponding `tool_result` block in the next message.
```

This happens even when clicking **New Chat** — the UI creates a new sidebar entry but the session state (or conversation history sent to the API) still contains orphaned `tool_use` blocks from the previous session.

## Reproduction

1. Open the AI Agent chat (Anthropic Max / Claude Opus 4.7)
2. Send a message that triggers tool calls (e.g. "List all installed plugins")
3. Wait for the response to complete
4. Click **New Chat**
5. Send a multi-step message (e.g. "Get site info, list plugins, create a page, run phpinfo")
6. **Result:** 400 error with `tool_use` IDs from the _previous_ session

The error references `toolu_01LKd2D7NR6tMXX2z4qnSraL` — a tool call ID from a prior session that leaked into the new session's conversation history.

## Root Cause Hypothesis

The conversation history sent to `POST /gratis-ai-agent/v1/run` includes message parts with `functionCall` entries (tool_use) that don't have matching `functionResponse` entries (tool_result) in the subsequent message. This violates the Anthropic API contract.

Likely locations to investigate:

- **`AgentLoop.php`** — how it constructs the messages array from session history. If the session DB has a `tool_use` part on the last model message but the loop was interrupted before the `tool_result` was recorded, the history is malformed.
- **`SessionController.php`** — the `/run` endpoint builds the prompt from `session.messages`. If a prior job errored mid-tool-call, the session may have a dangling `tool_use` without its `tool_result`.
- **New Chat button** — `clearCurrentSession()` in `sessionsSlice.js` resets the Redux state but the _server-side_ session ID may carry over if the frontend doesn't fully clear `currentSessionId` before the next `streamMessage()` call.

## Files to Investigate

- `EDIT: includes/Core/AgentLoop.php` — message history construction, look for where `functionCall` parts are added without ensuring a matching `functionResponse` exists
- `EDIT: includes/REST/SessionController.php` — the `/run` endpoint, check how `$session['messages']` is passed to the AI client and whether dangling tool calls are stripped
- `EDIT: src/store/slices/sessionsSlice.js` — `clearCurrentSession()` and `streamMessage()`, verify the session ID is fully cleared before creating a new session

## Expected Behavior

- **New Chat** should always start with a clean conversation history — no tool calls from prior sessions
- If a session has a dangling `tool_use` (from a crashed/interrupted job), the history sanitizer should either strip the orphaned tool call or synthesize a stub `tool_result` with an error message before sending to the API

## Environment

- WordPress 7.0-RC2
- Gratis AI Agent 1.5.0 (branch `fix/ability-error-context`)
- Provider: Anthropic Max (Claude Opus 4.7)
- PHP 8.4.20

title: t199: Resumable background jobs & multi-session chat
body:
**Task ID:** `t199` | **Status:** open | **Estimate:** `~10d`
**Logged:** 2026-04-17
**Tags:** `parent` `feature` `resumable-background-jobs`

## Description

Resumable background jobs & multi-session chat

## Plan: Purpose

Users should be able to send a prompt, navigate away (close tab, switch admin pages, open a different chat), and come back to see all progress made while they were gone. Permission prompts that fire while the user is away should persist and notify them via browser notifications. Multiple conversations should be manageable concurrently with tab-based UI.
The server-side architecture already supports this — `fastcgi_finish_request()` decouples processing from the browser, and messages are persisted to the DB on completion. The gaps are all on the frontend reconnection and notification layers.

<details><summary>Plan: Context & Architecture</summary>


**Context**

**Key decisions:**
- Transient becomes cache layer, DB becomes source of truth (fixes silent result loss on network blip or transient eviction)
- `JOB_TTL = 600` stays as transient cache duration but is no longer the authoritative timeout
- All notification/reconnection logic goes into shared components — automatic 3-surface coverage
- Tab bar UI (Phase 5) preferred over split-pane — simpler, more intuitive
- Dead SSE streaming code to be removed (the production path is exclusively job+poll)
**Open questions:**
- Should we add a WordPress admin notification (wp-admin notice bar) for pending confirmations in addition to browser notifications?
- Should the active-jobs table clean up completed rows on a schedule or keep them for audit?
- Should tab state persist across browser sessions (localStorage) or just within a session (sessionStorage)?
**Implementation order:**
Phase 1 (foundation) → Phase 2 (polling refactor) → Phase 4 (sessionStorage, trivial add-on) → Phase 3 (notifications, independent) → Phase 5 (tab UI, polish layer)

**Context from Discussion**

**Key decisions:**
- Transient becomes cache layer, DB becomes source of truth (fixes silent result loss on network blip or transient eviction)
- `JOB_TTL = 600` stays as transient cache duration but is no longer the authoritative timeout
- All notification/reconnection logic goes into shared components — automatic 3-surface coverage
- Tab bar UI (Phase 5) preferred over split-pane — simpler, more intuitive
- Dead SSE streaming code to be removed (the production path is exclusively job+poll)
**Open questions:**
- Should we add a WordPress admin notification (wp-admin notice bar) for pending confirmations in addition to browser notifications?
- Should the active-jobs table clean up completed rows on a schedule or keep them for audit?
- Should tab state persist across browser sessions (localStorage) or just within a session (sessionStorage)?
**Implementation order:**
Phase 1 (foundation) → Phase 2 (polling refactor) → Phase 4 (sessionStorage, trivial add-on) → Phase 3 (notifications, independent) → Phase 5 (tab UI, polish layer)

**Architecture**

**What already works:**
- Server processes independently of browser (`fastcgi_finish_request`, `ignore_user_abort`)
- Job progress stored in transients (polling via `/job/{id}`)
- Messages persisted to DB on completion (`append_to_session`)
- Tool confirmation pause/resume (`awaiting_confirmation` state)
- Per-session job tracking in Redux (`sessionJobs` map — but in-memory only)
- All three chat surfaces (admin page, floating widget, screen-meta) share the **same** `ChatPanel` component and the **same** `@wordpress/data` Redux store singleton
**Code sharing between surfaces:**
- `src/components/` (7,541 lines) — 100% shared across all surfaces
- `src/store/` (3,403 lines) — singleton, shared across all surfaces on same page
- Unique to admin page: ~600 lines (sidebar, onboarding, shortcuts)
- Unique to floating widget: ~400 lines (tabs, drag/resize, FAB)
- Unique to screen-meta: ~80 lines (context builder)

title: t209: Improve block editor content quality
body:
**Task ID:** `t209` | **Status:** open | **Estimate:** `~20h`
**Logged:** 2026-04-17
**Tags:** `parent` `feature` `improve-block-editor-content-quality`

## Description

Improve block editor content quality

## Plan: Purpose

Pages created by the AI agent look awful — raw markdown mixed with block markup, no layout sophistication, no columns/groups/covers/buttons. The root cause is threefold: (1) skills are opt-in and the LLM never loads them, (2) the gutenberg-blocks skill is too thin to be useful even if loaded (73 lines, zero block markup examples), and (3) the system prompt actively steers the LLM toward markdown-only output. This plan fixes the skill delivery mechanism, enriches the skill content, and fixes the mixed-content rendering bug.

<details><summary>Plan: Context & Architecture</summary>


**Context**

**Investigation findings (raising-cows-for-beef page):**
- Page content is a mix of proper `<!-- wp:image -->` blocks and raw markdown (`## headings`, `**bold**`, `- lists`)
- `PostAbilities::maybe_convert_markdown()` short-circuits when it finds `<!-- wp:` anywhere in content — even if 90% of the content is still raw markdown
- The LLM produced hybrid content (image blocks from stock image ability + markdown for text) and the converter never touched the markdown portions
**Skills system architecture gaps identified:**
1. **Skills are passive/opt-in** — `Skill::get_index_for_prompt()` injects a one-line index telling the LLM to "use skill-load tool when a request matches." The LLM ignores this because the system prompt already says "just write markdown."
2. **Block tools are hidden** — `markdown-to-blocks` and `create-block-content` have `'ai_hidden' => true`, so `resolve_abilities()` filters them out. The LLM literally cannot call them.
3. **System prompt contradiction** — Default system instruction (line 173) says "Write content directly using markdown" which conflicts with any skill that says "use block tools for layouts."
4. **Skill content is too thin** — `gutenberg-blocks.md` is 73 lines with zero actual serialized block markup examples. Without examples, even a loaded skill doesn't teach the LLM how to produce correct output.
5. **No skill auto-injection** — Knowledge base has RAG-based auto-injection (`Knowledge::get_context_for_query()`). Skills have nothing equivalent — they're purely manual.
**Key files:**
- `includes/Core/SystemInstructionBuilder.php` — builds system prompt, injects skill index
- `includes/Models/Skill.php` — skill model, `get_index_for_prompt()` produces the passive index
- `includes/Abilities/BlockAbilities.php` — block tools (markdown-to-blocks, create-block-content, etc.)
- `includes/Abilities/PostAbilities.php` — `maybe_convert_markdown()` bug location (line 775-813)
- `includes/Models/MarkdownToBlocks.php` — markdown-to-blocks converter (text-only, no layout blocks)
- `includes/Models/skills/gutenberg-blocks.md` — current skill content (73 lines, too thin)
**Design decisions:**
- Auto-inject skills into system prompt (like knowledge RAG) rather than relying on LLM to call skill-load
- Keyword matching for skill injection is sufficient — no need for semantic search
- Keep `create-block-content` as the primary tool for complex layouts, teach raw block markup for simple content
- `maybe_convert_markdown()` should handle the "freeform blocks between real blocks" case gracefully

title: t215: Adaptive skill system
body:
**Task ID:** `t215` | **Status:** open | **Estimate:** `~30h`
**Logged:** 2026-04-18
**Tags:** `parent` `feature` `adaptive-skill-system`

## Description

Adaptive skill system

## Plan: Purpose

The skill system is static and blind. Built-in skills ship as frozen `.md` files,
the auto-injector uses hardcoded regex patterns (`SkillAutoInjector::TRIGGER_MAP`),
there's no telemetry on which skills help vs. waste tokens, no mechanism for skill
updates between plugin releases, and the auto-injection fires identically for
Claude Opus and a quantized 7B model — burning 1500-3000 tokens per turn on strong
models that would have loaded the skill on demand.
This plan introduces three capabilities: (1) usage tracking so the system learns
which skills help, (2) model-aware tiered injection so weak models get auto-injection
while strong models get the lean index-only path, and (3) an upstream update channel
so skill content can improve between plugin releases.

<details><summary>Plan: Context & Architecture</summary>


**Context**

**Investigation findings (2026-04-18):**
Current skill architecture components:
- `Skill.php` — model with CRUD, seeding from `.md` files, `get_index_for_prompt()`
- `SkillAutoInjector.php` — hardcoded regex `TRIGGER_MAP` (9 patterns), injects up to
  2 full skill guides into every system prompt when patterns match
- `SkillAbilities.php` — `skill-load` and `skill-list` WordPress abilities (tools)
- `SkillService.php` — business logic for REST layer (create, delete, format)
- `SkillController.php` — REST API (CRUD, reset built-in)
- `SystemInstructionBuilder.php` — assembles system prompt, calls both `get_index_for_prompt()`
  AND `inject_for_message()` unconditionally
- `SkillRow.php` — immutable DTO for DB rows
- 11 built-in skills as `.md` files in `includes/Models/skills/`
- DB schema: id, slug, name, description, content, is_builtin, enabled, created_at, updated_at
Claude Code comparison (aidevops framework):
- Uses `SKILL.md` files + MCP tool for on-demand loading — model decides when to load
- `skill-update-helper.sh` tracks upstream via GitHub commit SHA or URL content hash
- Conditional HTTP requests (ETag/If-Modified-Since) avoid re-downloading unchanged content
- `skill-sources.json` stores upstream_url, upstream_commit, upstream_hash, upstream_etag,
  upstream_last_modified, imported_at, last_checked, merge_strategy
- Auto-update creates PRs via worktree workflow with conventional commits and changelogs
- `skills.sh` public registry for community skill discovery and installation
**Token cost analysis:**
- Skill index (`get_index_for_prompt()`): ~15 tokens/skill, ~150 total — cheap, always present
- Auto-injected skill content: ~1000-2000 tokens/skill, up to 2 = 3000 tokens/turn
- Auto-injection fires on broad regex (e.g. any message mentioning "page" triggers gutenberg-blocks)
- Strong models (GPT-4.1, Claude Sonnet/Opus) reliably call `skill-load` from the index alone
- Weak models (Mistral-7B, Phi-3, quantized Llama) ignore the index, need auto-injection
- `ModelHealthTracker` already classifies models as weak/strong via name heuristics + telemetry
**Key design decisions:**
- Auto-injection becomes model-aware: weak models get it, strong models don't
- Cap auto-injection at 1 skill (was 2) — weak models can't use two guides effectively
- Track skill-load tool usage as a signal in ModelHealthTracker
- Remote manifest uses the same hash-comparison pattern as Knowledge system
- User-modified built-in skills protected from auto-updates (`user_modified` flag)
- Server component starts minimal (static JSON manifest) — no dynamic backend initially
- Marketplace/community features deferred until tracking data proves skills matter

**Context from Discussion**

Current skill architecture components:
- `Skill.php` — model with CRUD, seeding from `.md` files, `get_index_for_prompt()`

**Architecture**

```

```

title: t221: Onboarding v2: Gate + AI-driven discovery
body:
**Task ID:** `t221` | **Status:** open | **Estimate:** `~8h`
**Logged:** 2026-04-18
**Tags:** `parent` `feature` `onboarding-v2-gate--ai-driven-discovery`

## Description

Onboarding v2: Gate + AI-driven discovery

## Plan: Purpose

Replace the multi-step onboarding wizard with a two-state flow: a hard connector gate (no AI without a provider) followed by an AI-driven first conversation where the agent explores the site itself before asking any questions. Inspired by OpenClaw's "infrastructure gates are hard, personalisation is conversational" pattern — the agent does the discovery work, infers what it can from existing content, and only asks what it can't figure out.
Current onboarding has 5 wizard steps (Welcome, Provider, Abilities, WooCommerce, Done) plus a separate static interview form. Users can skip past the provider step with no connector configured (broken experience), and the interview asks questions the AI could answer itself by reading the site's content.

<details><summary>Plan: Context & Architecture</summary>


**Context**

**OpenClaw inspiration:** OpenClaw's onboarding has two distinct phases — a hard infrastructure gate (gateway connection, auth) followed by a conversational AI bootstrapping session where the agent reads BOOTSTRAP.md and walks the user through identity/personality setup conversationally. Key quotes from their BOOTSTRAP.md: "Don't interrogate. Don't be robotic. Just... talk." and their kickoff message auto-sends to start the AI conversation immediately.
**Key design decisions:**
- No multi-step wizard at all — two states only (gate or chat)
- The AI explores the site with tools before asking the user anything
- Content analysis determines style/tone/audience when possible — the AI doesn't ask what it can infer
- WooCommerce auto-detected and auto-enabled silently
- RAG indexing queued during onboarding so knowledge base is populated for future sessions
- Empty sites get a different AI flow (ask about goals) vs content-rich sites (present findings)
- The static interview form is eliminated entirely — the AI conversation replaces it
- Memories are stored through normal abilities, not a separate interview-to-memory pipeline

title: Trouble using tools to create content
body:
# Bug Report: `arguments` Parameter Silently Dropped in Tool Calls

**Date:** April 21, 2026
**Reporter:** AI Agent (Claude) via WordPress AI Agent Demo Site
**Site:** https://demo.ultimateagentwp.ai/wp
**Severity:** Critical — blocks all content creation workflows

---

## Summary

When calling `wpab__gratis-ai-agent__ability-call` or the native tools (`wpab__ai-agent__create-post`, `wpab__ai-agent__update-post`), the `arguments` / parameter values are silently dropped in a significant percentage of calls. The tool receives an empty or null arguments object and returns a validation error ("title is required", "post_id is required"), even though the arguments were explicitly provided in the tool invocation.

---

## Environment

- **WordPress version:** 7.0-RC2
- **Site URL:** https://demo.ultimateagentwp.ai/wp
- **Active theme:** Ollie 1.6.0
- **Active plugin:** Ultimate AI Connector for Compatible Endpoints
- **AI Model:** Claude (Anthropic)
- **Interface:** WordPress AI Agent chat panel

---

## Steps to Reproduce

### Reproduction Case A — `ability-call` with `ai-agent/create-post`

1. Open the AI Agent chat panel in WordPress admin
2. Instruct the agent to create a post with a title, content, status, categories, featured image, and excerpt
3. The agent calls `wpab__gratis-ai-agent__ability-call` with:
   - `ability`: `"ai-agent/create-post"`
   - `arguments`: `{"title": "My Post Title", "status": "publish", "content": "...", ...}`
4. Observe the response

**Expected:** Post is created, post_id and permalink returned
**Actual:** Error — `"title is a required property of input"` — meaning the arguments object arrived empty

### Reproduction Case B — `ability-call` with `ai-agent/update-post`

1. Instruct the agent to update an existing post (ID known) with new content
2. The agent calls `wpab__gratis-ai-agent__ability-call` with:
   - `ability`: `"ai-agent/update-post"`
   - `arguments`: `{"post_id": 22, "content": "..."}`
3. Observe the response

**Expected:** Post updated successfully
**Actual:** Error — `"post_id is a required property of input"` — meaning the arguments object arrived empty

### Reproduction Case C — Native tool `wpab__ai-agent__create-post`

1. Instruct the agent to create a post using the native tool (not via ability-call)
2. The agent calls `wpab__ai-agent__create-post` with `title`, `content`, `status`, `categories`, `tags`, `featured_image_id`, `excerpt`
3. The tool call returns a success response with a `post_id` and `permalink`
4. Inspect the created post in WordPress admin

**Expected:** Post created with all fields populated — title, content, featured image, categories, tags
**Actual:** Post created with **title only** — all other parameters (`content`, `status`, `categories`, `tags`, `featured_image_id`, `excerpt`) are silently ignored. Post is saved as a draft with no content.

---

## Observed Behaviour in Detail

### Pattern 1 — Intermittent success
`ai-agent/create-post` via `ability-call` **worked correctly twice** during the session (post IDs 13 and 14 were created with full content, categories, tags, featured image, and correct publish status). In subsequent identical calls in the same session, the arguments were dropped entirely.

### Pattern 2 — Consistent failure after first success
After the first 2 successful `ability-call` invocations, **every subsequent call** to both `ai-agent/create-post` and `ai-agent/update-post` arrived with no arguments, regardless of what was passed. This suggests a **session-level state issue** or a **token/context overflow** causing the arguments to be stripped.

### Pattern 3 — Native tool partially works
`wpab__ai-agent__create-post` (the native tool, not via ability-call) consistently creates a post and returns a valid `post_id`, but **only the `title` parameter is saved**. Content, status, categories, tags, and featured_image_id are all dropped silently. No error is returned.

### Pattern 4 — Other ability-calls work fine
`ai-agent/update-post` with only `{"post_id": X, "status": "trash"}` worked correctly — suggesting **simple/short argument objects succeed** while **large argument objects (with long content strings) are dropped**.

---

## Hypothesis

The most likely cause is a **payload size or serialization issue**:

1. **Argument truncation at a size threshold** — The `content` field in create-post calls can be 5,000–15,000 characters of serialized Gutenberg block HTML. It is possible the arguments object exceeds a size limit somewhere in the tool call pipeline, causing it to be silently dropped or nulled rather than raising a size error.

2. **JSON serialization failure** — If the arguments object fails JSON serialization (e.g. due to unescaped characters in the block HTML content), the entire arguments object may be dropped silently.

3. **Session/context state corruption** — The intermittent nature (works twice, then never again in the same session) suggests a possible memory or context window issue on the bridge between Claude and the Abilities API.

4. **Native tool parameter binding** — For `wpab__ai-agent__create-post`, only `title` appears to be bound correctly. The remaining parameters may not be wired up to the underlying `wp_insert_post()` call, or they may be mapped to wrong field names.

---

## What Does Work

| Operation | Method | Works? |
|-----------|--------|--------|
| `update-option` (short value) | ability-call | ✅ Yes |
| `update-post` with `{"post_id": X, "status": "trash"}` | ability-call | ✅ Yes |
| `import-stock-image` | ability-call | ✅ Yes |
| `markdown-to-blocks` | ability-call | ✅ Yes |
| `create-post` (title only, no content) | native tool | ✅ Yes |
| `create-post` with full content | ability-call | ⚠️ Works first 2 calls, then fails |
| `update-post` with content | ability-call | ❌ Never works |
| `create-post` with content | native tool | ❌ Content silently dropped |
| `update-post` with content | native tool | ❌ Content silently dropped |

---

## Impact

This bug makes it **impossible to reliably build a WordPress site** using the AI Agent. The primary use case — creating pages and posts with rich block content — is completely broken after the first 2 successful calls. The demo site build was halted after creating only 2 of 6 planned posts with content.

---

## Suggested Fixes

1. **Add payload size logging** on the Abilities API bridge — log the raw arguments object received for every ability call so it's clear whether arguments arrive empty or are dropped internally.
2. **Return an error (don't silently succeed)** when `wpab__ai-agent__create-post` receives parameters that it ignores — the silent success with missing content is particularly confusing.
3. **Test argument objects > 5KB** — specifically test `ai-agent/create-post` with a `content` field containing 5,000+ characters of block HTML.
4. **Check JSON escaping** of block HTML in the argument serialization pipeline — Gutenberg block comments (`<!-- wp:paragraph -->`) may be interfering with JSON parsing.
5. **Investigate session state reset** — determine why the first 2 calls succeed and subsequent identical calls fail in the same session.

---

## Posts Created Successfully (for reference)

- **ID 12** — Home page (full content, published) ✅
- **ID 13** — "Build a Restaurant Website in 60 Seconds" (full content) ✅
- **ID 14** — "Write a Complete Blog Post on Any Topic" (full content) ✅
- **ID 22** — "Create a Services Page for a Law Firm" (no content, stub only) ⚠️

title: t226: WP 6.9 compatibility: polyfill WP 7.0 AI APIs + Connectors page
body:
**Task ID:** `t226` | **Status:** open | **Estimate:** `~40h`
**Logged:** 2026-04-21
**Tags:** `parent` `feature` `plan` `wp-69-compat`

## Description

WP 6.9 compatibility: polyfill WP 7.0 AI APIs + Connectors page

## Plan: Purpose

WP 7.0 has been delayed again. The plugin currently hard-requires WP 7.0 for four API layers (php-ai-client SDK, Abilities API, AI Client bridge, Connectors API). We need the plugin to work on WP 6.9 while remaining forward-compatible — when users upgrade to WP 7.0, everything should keep working seamlessly with zero migration.

<details><summary>Plan: Context & Architecture</summary>


**Context**

**Key research findings:**
1. **WooCommerce precedent:** WooCommerce already vendors `wordpress/abilities-api` via Composer in production. This validates the approach of bundling WP 7.0 packages in plugins for pre-7.0 compatibility.
2. **Provider plugins target 6.9:** Both `ai-provider-for-anthropic` and `ai-provider-for-openai` declare `Requires at least: 6.9`. They register via `AiClient::defaultRegistry()->registerProvider()` — they just need the SDK available, which our Composer bundle provides. No bundling needed.
3. **Jetpack Autoloader handles conflicts:** Already in our `composer.json`. It resolves version conflicts by loading the newest copy — when WP 7.0 core provides classes, Jetpack defers to them. When on 6.9, our vendored copy loads.
4. **Same credential option names:** WP 7.0's Connectors API stores API keys in `connectors_ai_{provider}_api_key` options (auto-generated from provider ID). Our polyfill uses the same naming convention, so credentials entered on 6.9 work on 7.0 with zero migration.
5. **WP 7.0 Connectors page is too tightly coupled to copy:** It uses `@wordpress/boot` + script modules + the new WP routing system (none available on 6.9). We build a simpler React page using `@wordpress/components` + `@wordpress/data` (same tech stack we already use) that calls the same REST endpoints.
6. **Bridge classes are small:** `WP_AI_Client_Prompt_Builder` (472 lines) and `WP_AI_Client_Ability_Function_Resolver` (232 lines) are the only non-packaged WP core classes we need. Plus 4 small adapter classes and 2 global function files. Total ~1,100 LOC to copy.
7. **Existing code needs zero changes:** All 30+ ability classes, AgentLoop, ToolDiscovery, CredentialResolver, ProviderCredentialLoader, REST controllers, and the React chat UI work unchanged. The polyfill sits underneath them.
**Risks:**
- `wordpress/php-ai-client` may not be on Packagist yet — fallback: vendor as local path package or copy under `lib/`
- `WP_AI_Client_Prompt_Builder` constructor takes a registry arg in WP 7.0-RC2 but our stub doesn't — need to match the real signature
- Pin to RC2 SDK version and track upstream for breaking changes before 7.0 final
**Forward-compatibility guarantees:**
- Every polyfill guarded by `function_exists()` / `class_exists()` — WP 7.0 definitions win
- Same option names for credentials — zero migration
- Connectors page detects WP 7.0 and shows link to core page instead
- Jetpack Autoloader handles SDK/Abilities class version resolution

**Context from Discussion**

**Key research findings:**
1. **WooCommerce precedent:** WooCommerce already vendors `wordpress/abilities-api` via Composer in production. This validates the approach of bundling WP 7.0 packages in plugins for pre-7.0 compatibility.
2. **Provider plugins target 6.9:** Both `ai-provider-for-anthropic` and `ai-provider-for-openai` declare `Requires at least: 6.9`. They register via `AiClient::defaultRegistry()->registerProvider()` — they just need the SDK available, which our Composer bundle provides. No bundling needed.
3. **Jetpack Autoloader handles conflicts:** Already in our `composer.json`. It resolves version conflicts by loading the newest copy — when WP 7.0 core provides classes, Jetpack defers to them. When on 6.9, our vendored copy loads.
4. **Same credential option names:** WP 7.0's Connectors API stores API keys in `connectors_ai_{provider}_api_key` options (auto-generated from provider ID). Our polyfill uses the same naming convention, so credentials entered on 6.9 work on 7.0 with zero migration.
5. **WP 7.0 Connectors page is too tightly coupled to copy:** It uses `@wordpress/boot` + script modules + the new WP routing system (none available on 6.9). We build a simpler React page using `@wordpress/components` + `@wordpress/data` (same tech stack we already use) that calls the same REST endpoints.
6. **Bridge classes are small:** `WP_AI_Client_Prompt_Builder` (472 lines) and `WP_AI_Client_Ability_Function_Resolver` (232 lines) are the only non-packaged WP core classes we need. Plus 4 small adapter classes and 2 global function files. Total ~1,100 LOC to copy.
7. **Existing code needs zero changes:** All 30+ ability classes, AgentLoop, ToolDiscovery, CredentialResolver, ProviderCredentialLoader, REST controllers, and the React chat UI work unchanged. The polyfill sits underneath them.
**Risks:**
- `wordpress/php-ai-client` may not be on Packagist yet — fallback: vendor as local path package or copy under `lib/`
- `WP_AI_Client_Prompt_Builder` constructor takes a registry arg in WP 7.0-RC2 but our stub doesn't — need to match the real signature
- Pin to RC2 SDK version and track upstream for breaking changes before 7.0 final
**Forward-compatibility guarantees:**
- Every polyfill guarded by `function_exists()` / `class_exists()` — WP 7.0 definitions win
- Same option names for credentials — zero migration
- Connectors page detects WP 7.0 and shows link to core page instead
- Jetpack Autoloader handles SDK/Abilities class version resolution

**Architecture**

**Strategy: conditional polyfill.** Every API layer is wrapped in `function_exists()` / `class_exists()` guards. On WP 6.9, our bundled copies load. On WP 7.0, core's definitions take precedence automatically.
**Four layers to polyfill:**
| Layer | Source | LOC | Approach |
|-------|--------|-----|----------|
| php-ai-client SDK (`WordPress\AiClient\*`) | `wp-includes/php-ai-client/` | ~12,800 | Composer package via Jetpack Autoloader |
| Abilities API (`WP_Ability`, registries, global functions) | `wp-includes/abilities-api/` | ~2,100 | Composer package (same as WooCommerce) |
| WP AI Client bridge (`WP_AI_Client_Prompt_Builder`, resolver, `wp_ai_client_prompt()`) | `wp-includes/ai-client/` | ~1,100 | Copy + conditional guards in `includes/Compat/` |
| Connectors API (`WP_Connector_Registry`, settings, credentials) | `wp-includes/connectors.php` + registry | ~1,800 | Copy + conditional guards + custom admin page |
**Provider plugins (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google) are NOT bundled** — they already target `Requires at least: 6.9` and install as standalone plugins. Our Connectors page provides Install/Activate buttons that call the WP Plugins REST API, identical to WP 7.0's core Connectors page.

</details>

<details><summary>Plan: Progress</summary>

- [ ] (2026-04-21) Phase 1: Add Composer packages (php-ai-client + abilities-api) ~4h — t227
- [ ] (2026-04-21) Phase 2: Create WP AI Client bridge polyfill ~8h — t228
- [ ] (2026-04-21) Phase 3: Create Connectors API polyfill ~8h — t229
- [ ] (2026-04-21) Phase 4: Build Connectors admin page (React) ~16h — t230
- [ ] (2026-04-21) Phase 5: Lower version requirement + test both versions ~4h — t231

</details>

<details><summary>Plan: Decision Log</summary>

- 2026-04-21: Decided NOT to bundle provider plugins — they already target 6.9, install as standalone. Build install/activate UI in our Connectors page instead.
- 2026-04-21: Decided NOT to copy WP 7.0's Connectors SPA — too coupled to @wordpress/boot. Build simpler page with same tech stack we already use.
- 2026-04-21: Decided to use Jetpack Autoloader (already in composer.json) for SDK/Abilities version conflict resolution — proven pattern (WooCommerce uses it).

</details>

<details><summary>Plan: Discoveries</summary>

- WP 7.0's `WP_AI_Client_Prompt_Builder` constructor takes `(ProviderRegistry $registry, $prompt)` — our stub file had `(string $prompt)`. The polyfill must match the real constructor.
- The AI Experiments plugin (`ai`) also requires WP 7.0 (`WPAI_MIN_WP_VERSION = '7.0'`) — it cannot serve as a polyfill source.
- `_wp_connectors_get_provider_settings()` and `_wp_connectors_get_real_api_key()` are used by our existing `ProviderCredentialLoader` — both need to be in the polyfill.

</details>

title: Supervisor health dashboard stale: 2d0h (#1125)
body:
## Premise

The dashboard at #1125 last refreshed `2026-04-21T18:07:43Z` — **2d0h ago** (threshold: 2d0h). The `stats-wrapper.sh` scheduler is likely failing silently.

## Why this matters

The supervisor health dashboard is the framework's primary single-glance health surface. When it stops refreshing, operators keep trusting green numbers that no longer reflect reality — every decision derived from "dashboard says green" becomes invalid.

## Triage

1. Inspect the stats scheduler status (macOS):

   ```bash
   launchctl list | grep -i aidevops-stats-wrapper
   tail -40 ~/.aidevops/logs/stats.log
   ls -la ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.aidevops.aidevops-stats-wrapper.plist
   ```

2. Run the refresh manually and capture the error:

   ```bash
   bash ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/stats-wrapper.sh 2>&1 | tail -40
   ```

3. Check the dashboard issue directly:

   ```bash
   gh api repos/Ultimate-Multisite/gratis-ai-agent/issues/1125 --jq '{updated_at, body_length: (.body|length)}'
   ```

## Remediation

- **Missing plist:** re-run `setup.sh --non-interactive` (or `aidevops update`) with PULSE_ENABLED=true so `setup_stats_wrapper` reinstalls `com.aidevops.aidevops-stats-wrapper.plist`.
- **`set -euo pipefail` fail:** the post-t2418 wrapper emits `HEALTH-DASHBOARD-FAIL exit=<N>` on error. Grep `stats.log` on that prefix.
- **Body size / API error:** inspect `stats.log` — look at `gh` HTTP errors and `_update_health_issue_for_repo` failures.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Root cause identified and documented on this issue.
- [ ] `gh issue view 1125 --repo Ultimate-Multisite/gratis-ai-agent` shows an update within 24h of closing this alert.
- [ ] `last_refresh:` marker is present in the dashboard body.

title: fix(ci): lazy-load html2canvas to fix Bundle Size Budget on PR #1154
body:
## Task

Fix the Bundle Size Budget CI failure on PR #1154 (`feature/screenshot-abilities`) in `Ultimate-Multisite/gratis-ai-agent`.

## Why

PR #1154 adds the html2canvas library (~35KB gzipped) eagerly imported in `src/abilities/screenshot.js` and registered via `src/abilities/index.js`. This import is bundled into every entry point (admin-page, floating-widget, screen-meta), causing all three to exceed the 400KB size-limit budget:

- admin-page: 400kB limit → 435.68kB (35.68kB over)
- floating-widget: 400kB limit → 434.41kB (34.41kB over)
- screen-meta: 400kB limit → 430.9kB (30.9kB over)

**Note:** The PHPCS, PHPStan, and PHPUnit (WP trunk) failures on this PR are pre-existing on `main` (confirmed via CI run on main dated 2026-04-23). Do NOT attempt to fix those — only fix the Bundle Size Budget.

## How

**EDIT: `src/abilities/screenshot.js`**

Replace the top-level static `import html2canvas from 'html2canvas'` with dynamic imports inside each async function that uses it:

```js
// Remove top-level: import html2canvas from 'html2canvas';

// Inside executeCaptureScreenshot (async function), before first html2canvas call:
const { default: html2canvas } = await import('html2canvas');

// Inside executeScreenshotUrl (async function), before first html2canvas call:
const { default: html2canvas } = await import('html2canvas');
```

Both functions are already `async` — dynamic import drops in without structural changes.

**Branch to push to:** `feature/screenshot-abilities` (do NOT create a new PR — push fix commits directly to this branch so PR #1154 picks up the fix automatically)

**Verification:**
```bash
npm run build && npm run size
# All three failing bundles must be ≤ 400kB
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `npm run size` passes all size-limit budgets
- [ ] Fix committed and pushed to branch `feature/screenshot-abilities`
- [ ] PR #1154 Bundle Size Budget CI check passes

title: bug: "Edit & resend" enters edit mode on ALL user messages, not just the clicked one
body:
## Bug Description

Clicking the **Edit & resend** button on any single user message causes **every** user message in the conversation to simultaneously enter edit mode. Only the message whose button was clicked should become editable.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open any conversation that has multiple user messages (≥ 2).
2. Hover over any user message to reveal the action buttons.
3. Click **Edit & resend** on one specific message.

## Expected Behaviour

Only the targeted message enters edit mode (shows inline textarea + Cancel / Send buttons). All other messages remain in their normal read-only display state.

## Actual Behaviour

Every user message in the conversation enters edit mode simultaneously. Three (or more) editable textareas appear at once, each with its own Cancel / Send pair.

## Evidence

```js
// After clicking a single Edit & resend button:
document.querySelectorAll('.gaa-cr-bubble-user--editing').length
// Returns: 3  (one per user message in the conversation)
```

The class `.gaa-cr-bubble-user--editing` is applied to all user message containers, not just the one whose button was clicked.

## Files Likely Involved

- The React component rendering user message bubbles with edit state (look for `.gaa-cr-bubble-user--editing` class assignment)
- The `editAndResend` dispatch action — likely keying on a non-unique field (role = 'user') instead of the specific message index or ID

## Verification

After fix: clicking Edit & resend on message N must produce exactly **1** element matching `.gaa-cr-bubble-user--editing`.

## Environment

- Plugin: AI Agent for WP v1.8.2  
- WordPress: 7.0-RC2  
- Browser: Chrome 147 (Playwright headless, automated QA)

title: bug: Trash tab context menu missing "Delete Permanently" option

## Bug Description

Conversations moved to the Trash can only be **Restored** — there is no option to permanently delete them. Users have no way to remove a conversation forever without direct database access.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open the AI Agent admin page (Chat tab).
2. Hover over any active conversation → open Session options → click **Move to Trash**.
3. Switch to the **Trash** tab.
4. Hover over the trashed conversation and open its Session options menu.

## Expected Behaviour

The Trash context menu should offer two actions:
- **Restore** — move back to Active
- **Delete Permanently** — irreversibly remove the conversation and all its messages

## Actual Behaviour

The Trash context menu only shows **Restore**. There is no Delete Permanently option.

## Impact

Users who want to permanently remove sensitive conversation history cannot do so through the UI. The data remains in the `wp_gratis_ai_agent_sessions` table indefinitely.

## Files Likely Involved

- The session context-menu component that builds the menu items based on current session status
- The `deleteSession` dispatch action likely exists in the store but is not wired to the Trash context menu

## Verification

After fix: Trash tab → session options must show both **Restore** and **Delete Permanently**.

- Plugin: AI Agent for WP v1.8.2
- WordPress: 7.0-RC2

title: bug: "Report an issue with this response" button does nothing

## Bug Description

The **Report an issue with this response** button (shown below each AI message) produces no visible effect when clicked: no modal, no toast, no network request, and no store state change.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open the Chat admin page.
2. Load any conversation that has at least one AI (model) response.

```js
// No network request fired:

// No store state change:

window.wp.data.select('gratis-ai-agent').getInabilityReported()  // null
```

No console errors are thrown.

## Possible Cause

The `feedback_enabled` setting in the plugin defaults to `false`. The button may be conditionally no-op'd when the feedback endpoint is disabled, but no visual indication of this is given.

- `includes/Core/Settings.php` — `feedback_enabled` / `feedback_endpoint_url` settings

title: bug: Settings page "Save Settings" shows no success or error notification
body:
## Bug Description

After clicking **Save Settings** on the Settings page, no toast, snackbar, or notice appears to confirm whether the save succeeded or failed. The user has no feedback that their changes were persisted.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Go to **AI Agent → Settings → General**.
2. Change any setting (e.g. the Greeting Message field).
3. Click **Save Settings**.

## Expected Behaviour

A visible notification should appear — e.g.:
- A WordPress-style admin notice: *"Settings saved."*
- Or a snackbar/toast at the bottom of the screen

## Actual Behaviour

The button click fires a POST to `/wp-json/gratis-ai-agent/v1/settings` (200 OK), but no UI feedback appears. The only persistent notice on the page is the pre-existing "Provider API keys are configured on the Connectors page" informational notice — which is unrelated to the save action.

## Evidence

```js
// After clicking Save Settings, intercepting fetch calls:
window.__netRequests.filter(r => r.method !== 'GET')
// [] — the built-in saveSettings dispatch returns 400 when called
//       directly, but the Save button itself fires a 200 via REST

// No success notice in the DOM:
document.querySelectorAll('[role="status"], .components-snackbar, .notice-success')
// 0 results
```

Note: The `saveSettings()` store action returns a 400 when dispatched directly; the Save Settings button appears to bypass the store action and call the REST endpoint directly. Both paths need to surface success/error state to the user.

## Files Likely Involved

- `src/settings-page/` — the Save Settings button onClick handler
- Should dispatch a success/failure snackbar via `@wordpress/notices` or a custom notice component

## Verification

After fix: clicking Save Settings shows a visible confirmation (success or error) within 2 seconds.

1. Go to **AI Agent → Abilities**.

The categories are present in the `/wp-json/wp-abilities/v1/categories` endpoint response, confirming they exist in the system. title: Supervisor health dashboard stale: 2d0h (#1115)
body:
## Premise

The dashboard at #1115 last refreshed `2026-04-24T10:17:26Z` — **2d0h ago** (threshold: 2d0h). The `stats-wrapper.sh` scheduler is likely failing silently.

## Why this matters

The supervisor health dashboard is the framework's primary single-glance health surface. When it stops refreshing, operators keep trusting green numbers that no longer reflect reality — every decision derived from "dashboard says green" becomes invalid.

## Triage

1. Inspect the stats scheduler status (macOS):

   ```bash
   launchctl list | grep -i aidevops-stats-wrapper
   tail -40 ~/.aidevops/logs/stats.log
   ls -la ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.aidevops.aidevops-stats-wrapper.plist
   ```

2. Run the refresh manually and capture the error:

   ```bash
   bash ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/stats-wrapper.sh 2>&1 | tail -40
   ```

3. Check the dashboard issue directly:

   ```bash
   gh api repos/Ultimate-Multisite/gratis-ai-agent/issues/1115 --jq '{updated_at, body_length: (.body|length)}'
   ```

## Remediation

- **Missing plist:** re-run `setup.sh --non-interactive` (or `aidevops update`) with PULSE_ENABLED=true so `setup_stats_wrapper` reinstalls `com.aidevops.aidevops-stats-wrapper.plist`.
- **`set -euo pipefail` fail:** the post-t2418 wrapper emits `HEALTH-DASHBOARD-FAIL exit=<N>` on error. Grep `stats.log` on that prefix.
- **Body size / API error:** inspect `stats.log` — look at `gh` HTTP errors and `_update_health_issue_for_repo` failures.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Root cause identified and documented on this issue.
- [ ] `gh issue view 1115 --repo Ultimate-Multisite/gratis-ai-agent` shows an update within 24h of closing this alert.
- [ ] `last_refresh:` marker is present in the dashboard body.

title: stats-wrapper hangs indefinitely when gh API call for one repo stalls
body:
## What

`stats-health-dashboard.sh` iterates repos sequentially in `update_health_issues()`. When a `gh` API call for one repo hangs indefinitely (observed: `superdav42/tgc.church`), all subsequent repos in the loop are blocked — their dashboards never get updated that cycle.

## Why

Observed in the investigation of #1190: the stats-wrapper process (PID 821239, 869115) stalled for 7+ minutes on `superdav42/tgc.church`. Process tree showed `gh` with 6 threads, no output, indefinite wait:

```
bash(821239)---bash(859866)---bash(864069)---bash(864852)---gh(864853)-+-{gh}(864854)
```

Without per-call timeouts, a single slow/unresponsive `gh` call prevents `Ultimate-Multisite/gratis-ai-agent`, `Ultimate-Multisite/ultimate-multisite`, and all other repos from getting their dashboard updates.

## How

Wrap individual `gh` API calls in the health dashboard loop with `timeout 30` (or similar).

Target function: `_update_health_issue_for_repo` in `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/stats-health-dashboard.sh`.

Specifically, the `gh issue edit` and `gh issue list` calls within `_check_health_issue_activity_guard`, `_find_health_issue`, and `_resolve_health_issue_number` should be wrapped.

Pattern (existing example in codebase):
```bash
timeout 30 gh api ... 2>/dev/null || { echo "[stats] Timeout on gh call for $slug"; return 0; }
```

## Acceptance

- [ ] Individual `gh` API calls in `_update_health_issue_for_repo` have a timeout (30s recommended).
- [ ] A stalled `gh` call on one repo does not block all subsequent repos in the loop.
- [ ] `shellcheck` passes on the modified file.

## Files to modify

title: t233: Site builder ability improvements
body:
**Task ID:** `t233` | **Status:** open | **Estimate:** `~9h`
**Logged:** 2026-04-26
**Tags:** `parent` `plan` `site-builder-ability-improvements`

## Description

Site builder ability improvements

## Plan: Purpose

Five genuine capability gaps found in the site builder audit. Most critical is the stock image fallback chain — Openverse/Pixabay download failures return hard errors with no retry. The rest are ergonomic improvements that reduce tool-call count and remove ambiguity for the agent.

<details><summary>Plan: Context & Architecture</summary>


**Context**

**Stock image fallback (t236):** `StockImageAbility` calls `ImageSourceFactory::get_available()`, picks the first free source, and returns a hard error if `download()` fails. The factory handles empty search results (falls back to AI generate) but not download failures. Fix: in `ImageSourceFactory::import_image()` on download failure, iterate to next free source then fall back to `generate`. Files: `ImageAbilities/StockImageAbility.php`, `ImageSources/ImageSourceFactory.php`.
**Page template (t237):** `wp_insert_post()` / `wp_update_post()` accept `page_template` as a post data key (maps to `_wp_page_template` meta). Neither `create-post` nor `update-post` expose it. Add to schema + handler in `PostAbilities.php`. Two lines per handler.
**set-featured-image (t238):** Already works via `update-post` (pass `post_id` + `featured_image_id`). A standalone ability removes ambiguity — agents frequently miss that `update-post` can set only the thumbnail without touching other fields. Add as a new `wp_register_ability` call in `PostAbilities.php`.
**batch-create-posts (t239):** A full site build takes ~7 sequential `create-post` calls. A batch ability accepting an array of post definitions reduces that to 1 call. Schema: `{ posts: [{ title, content, post_type, status, featured_image_id, page_template, ... }] }`. Returns `[{ post_id, permalink, title, status }]`. Add handler in `PostAbilities.php`.
**create-contact-form (t240):** WPForms is too plugin-specific. Better: register `ai-agent/create-contact-form` that inserts a simple HTML contact form as a Gutenberg HTML block (no plugin dependency). If Contact Form 7 is active, use its `WPCF7_ContactForm::create()` API instead and return the shortcode. Fallback chain: CF7 → raw HTML block. New ability in `ContentAbilities.php` or a new `FormsAbilities.php`.

- `update-post` — `PostAbilities.php:171`
- `manage-global-styles` (`get-global-styles`, `update-global-styles`, `get-theme-json`, `reset-global-styles`) — `GlobalStylesAbilities.php`

### MEDIUM: coderabbit (coderabbitai[bot])
**File**: `includes/REST/SettingsController.php:992`
**Verification**: kept as unverifiable (no stable snippet extracted)
_⚠️ Potential issue_ | _🟠 Major_

**Per-user cache key + single flush point causes stale providers across admins and after external connector changes.**

Two related invalidation gaps:

1. The transient is keyed on `get_current_user_id()`, but direct provider keys (`Settings::DIRECT_PROVIDERS`) are stored site-wide via `Settings::set_provider_key()`. When admin A saves a key, `flush_providers_cache()` only deletes admin A's transient — admin B continues to see the stale list for up to 5 minutes.
2. Cache is only flushed in `handle_set_provider_key()`. WP SDK providers (AI Experiments / OpenAI-compatible connector) configured via the core Connectors page never invalidate this transient, so a user who adds a connector externally and returns to the chat tab can sit on `ConnectorGate` for up to 5 minutes — the 5 s poll in `AdminPageApp` (`src/admin-page/index.js` line 105–107) and the `visibilitychange` refresh both hit the cached empty result.

Suggested directions (pick what fits the model better):
- If the providers list is truly site-wide, drop the per-user suffix and use a single shared transient (or use `wp_cache_*` with a versioned site option) so any admin's update is visible to all admins.
- If per-user scoping is intentional (e.g., for `ProviderCredentialLoader`-loaded per-user creds), keep a version counter in a site option, bump it from `set_provider_key()` and from a hook fired by the WP SDK / connector save paths, and include the version in the cache key — flushes then become global by construction.
- Additionally, hook `flush_providers_cache()` into the WP-SDK / connectors credential-update path (or a relevant `update_option` hook) so externally configured providers invalidate the cache too.



<details>
<summary>🛠️ Sketch: site-wide key with version, plus a hook for external updates</summary>

```diff
-	private static function providers_cache_key(): string {
-		return 'gratis_ai_providers_' . get_current_user_id();
-	}
-
-	public static function flush_providers_cache(): void {
-		delete_transient( self::providers_cache_key() );
-	}
+	private static function providers_cache_key(): string {
+		$version = (int) get_option( 'gratis_ai_providers_cache_version', 0 );
+		// Per-user suffix kept only because ProviderCredentialLoader may
+		// resolve per-user auth; bump the version to invalidate everyone.
+		return 'gratis_ai_providers_' . $version . '_' . get_current_user_id();
+	}
+
+	public static function flush_providers_cache(): void {
+		update_option(
+			'gratis_ai_providers_cache_version',
+			(int) get_option( 'gratis_ai_providers_cache_version', 0 ) + 1,
+			false
+		);
+	}
```

And wire an action so external connector saves also invalidate (exact hook name depends on the SDK/connector you integrate with):

```php
add_action( 'update_option_<connector_option>', [ SettingsController::class, 'flush_providers_cache' ] );
```
</details>

The inline comment says "Empty after_value means the option was deleted; update_option() recreates it," but the conditional checks `$change->before_value`. The actual semantics are the inverse:

```diff
+				// Otherwise restore the prior value (update_option() recreates the row
+				// if it was deleted). maybe_unserialize() decodes arrays/objects that
+				// the logger stored via maybe_serialize().
```

**Possible regression: always overriding `settings.max_iterations` with hard-coded 25.**

When no `--agent` is provided and no `--max-iterations` flag is set, `$options['max_iterations']` ends up as `25` and is unconditionally written into the options bag at line 171. Previously (when this key was simply omitted), `AgentLoop::__construct()` would fall back to the user's saved `settings['max_iterations']` (see `includes/Core/AgentLoop.php:189-233`). With this change, a site configured with e.g. `settings.max_iterations = 10` will silently get `25` from the CLI.

<details>
<summary>🛠️ Suggested fix — only set the key when an agent or CLI flag actually provided a value</summary>

```diff
-		// Default max_iterations from agent (or 25 global default) unless CLI overrides.
-		$agent_max      = $options['max_iterations'] ?? 25;
-		$cli_max        = isset( $assoc_args['max-iterations'] )
-			? (int) $assoc_args['max-iterations']
-			: null;

-		$options['max_iterations'] = $max_iterations;
```

title: Supervisor health dashboard stale: 2d13h (#1115)
body:
## Premise

The dashboard at #1115 last refreshed `2026-04-26T12:18:40Z` — **2d13h ago** (threshold: 2d0h). The `stats-wrapper.sh` scheduler is likely failing silently.

## Why this matters

The supervisor health dashboard is the framework's primary single-glance health surface. When it stops refreshing, operators keep trusting green numbers that no longer reflect reality — every decision derived from "dashboard says green" becomes invalid.

## Triage

1. Inspect the stats scheduler status (macOS):

   ```bash
   launchctl list | grep -i aidevops-stats-wrapper
   tail -40 ~/.aidevops/logs/stats.log
   ls -la ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.aidevops.aidevops-stats-wrapper.plist
   ```

2. Run the refresh manually and capture the error:

   ```bash
   bash ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/stats-wrapper.sh 2>&1 | tail -40
   ```

3. Check the dashboard issue directly:

   ```bash
   gh api repos/Ultimate-Multisite/gratis-ai-agent/issues/1115 --jq '{updated_at, body_length: (.body|length)}'
   ```

## Remediation

- **Missing plist:** re-run `setup.sh --non-interactive` (or `aidevops update`) with PULSE_ENABLED=true so `setup_stats_wrapper` reinstalls `com.aidevops.aidevops-stats-wrapper.plist`.
- **`set -euo pipefail` fail:** the post-t2418 wrapper emits `HEALTH-DASHBOARD-FAIL exit=<N>` on error. Grep `stats.log` on that prefix.
- **Body size / API error:** inspect `stats.log` — look at `gh` HTTP errors and `_update_health_issue_for_repo` failures.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Root cause identified and documented on this issue.
- [ ] `gh issue view 1115 --repo Ultimate-Multisite/gratis-ai-agent` shows an update within 24h of closing this alert.
- [ ] `last_refresh:` marker is present in the dashboard body.

title: Repair missing event-automation tables when the schema option is already current
body:
<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->
# Repair missing event-automation tables when the schema option is already current

## Pre-flight (auto-populated by briefing workflow)
- [x] Memory recall: `tgc.church production audit missing tables queue failures Caddy OOM` → 0 hits — no relevant lessons
- [x] Discovery pass: PR #1261 and later schema changes including #2264 reviewed / 0 open duplicate issues
- [x] File refs verified: 4 refs checked, all present at HEAD `3ba55e91`
- [x] Tier: `tier:standard` — exact regression is known, but the repair sentinel must avoid per-request schema overhead
- [x] Seeded draft PR decision recorded: skipped — production drift needs a focused regression test first

## Origin
- **Created:** 2026-08-02
- **Session:** OpenCode:production-deploy-audit
- **Created by:** AI DevOps (ai-interactive)
- **Conversation context:** The exact missing-table defect from this issue recurred after PR #1261: production logged 14 failed queries across two network databases for `sd_ai_agent_event_automations` tables.

## What
Extend the prior guard and installer so a present/current `sd_ai_agent_db_version` cannot permanently mask a missing event-automations table. Repair the physical schema idempotently and suppress request-path SQL errors while repair is pending.

## Why
PR #1261 made `EventAutomations::list()` trust only the version option. Current code returns early from `Database::install()` when that option equals `19.9.1`, so a cloned, partially migrated, or otherwise drifted database can keep the marker while lacking the table.

## Tier
**Selected tier:** `tier:standard`

**Tier rationale:** The prior fix and schema are established; implementation must balance a cheap sentinel with reliable physical repair across multisite contexts.

## Seeded Draft PR
- **Decision:** Skipped
- **Rationale:** Add a regression for current marker plus missing table before selecting the sentinel.
- **Status:** `not-created`
- **Freshness evidence:** Issue #1255, PR #1261, current installer, and current tests inspected.
- **Verification run:** 12 errors in one network DB and 2 in another observed after the latest deploy.
- **Stale-assumption warning:** Verify the active network/database prefix in tests; do not assume host multisite switching reaches isolated databases.

## How (Approach)

### Files to Modify
- `EDIT: includes/Core/Database.php:299-339,519-536,895-925` — add bounded physical-schema repair semantics and marker ordering.
- `EDIT: includes/Automations/EventAutomations.php:32-59` — fail closed when the physical table is absent, not only when the version option is absent.
- `EDIT: tests/SdAiAgent/Core/DatabaseSchemaTest.php:76-105` — cover current marker plus missing table and repair.
- `EDIT: tests/SdAiAgent/Automations/EventAutomationsTest.php:256-277` — cover missing table with a present version option and no SQL error.

### Complete Write Surface
- **Callers/readers:** Event hook attachment calls `EventAutomations::list(true)`; admin/runtime handlers call `Database::install()` in bounded contexts.
- **Writers/mutation paths:** `Database::install()` builds all tables with `dbDelta()` then updates the per-site version option.
- **Tests/fixtures:** `tests/SdAiAgent/Core/DatabaseSchemaTest.php` and `tests/SdAiAgent/Automations/EventAutomationsTest.php` already manipulate the version option and table state.
- **Schemas/config:** `Database::DB_VERSION`, `DB_VERSION_OPTION`, and the event-automations CREATE TABLE statement are authoritative.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** Not applicable because existing classes in `includes/Core/Database.php` and `includes/Automations/EventAutomations.php` require no generated asset or autoload change.
- **Migrations/backfills:** `includes/Core/Database.php` must create a missing empty table without altering healthy tables or automation rows.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** Revert sentinel and repair logic in `includes/Core/Database.php` and `includes/Automations/EventAutomations.php`; leave repaired data intact.

### Implementation Steps
1. Reproduce with `DB_VERSION_OPTION` set to current and only the event-automations table dropped.
2. Make the read path fail closed without querying an absent table.
3. Make a bounded install/admin/runtime path repair missing required schema despite a current version marker.
4. Ensure the version marker is written only after repair and add multisite-prefix coverage.

### Hazards and Compatibility
- **Concurrency/atomicity:** Concurrent repair attempts must be idempotent; avoid request-wide locks that can strand schema.
- **Migration/rollback:** Preserve all healthy table rows and indexes; never drop/recreate the whole schema.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** Keep table names and DB option keys canonical; no legacy-name migration.
- **Idempotency/retry:** A failed repair remains retryable; successful repair stops repeated discovery.
- **Partial failure/recovery:** Event hooks return an empty set without SQL errors until repair completes.

### Verification Before Dispatch
```bash
npm run test:php -- --filter='DatabaseSchemaTest|EventAutomationsTest'
npm run lint:php
composer phpstan
```
- **Surface mapping:** Focused tests cover drift and query suppression; lint/static analysis cover all changed PHP.
- **Broad verification trigger:** Repository policy requires full verification before PR.
- **Broad verification command:** `npm run verify`

### Recoverability Checkpoint
- [ ] Focused tests pass.
- [ ] WIP commit created before `npm run verify`: `wip: repair drifted event automation schema`
- [ ] Full repository verification then runs per repository policy.

### Files Scope
- `includes/Core/Database.php`
- `includes/Automations/EventAutomations.php`
- `tests/SdAiAgent/Core/DatabaseSchemaTest.php`
- `tests/SdAiAgent/Automations/EventAutomationsTest.php`

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A current DB version option plus a missing event-automations table is repaired in a bounded install path.
- [ ] Frontend/event-hook reads issue no SELECT against an absent table while repair is pending.
- [ ] Healthy schemas avoid per-request full schema discovery and preserve existing automation rows.
- [ ] Failed repair does not leave a false success marker and remains retryable.

## Context & Decisions
- Reopening #1255 is preferred to filing a duplicate because the production signature is identical and PR #1261's option-only guard is the incomplete boundary.
- Current table suffix is `sd_ai_agent_event_automations`; preserve canonical naming.

## Relevant Files
- `includes/Core/Database.php:299-339,519-536,895-925`
- `includes/Automations/EventAutomations.php:32-59`
- `tests/SdAiAgent/Core/DatabaseSchemaTest.php:76-105`

**Tier rationale:** This is a recovery/salvage task requiring inspection of a closed PR diff, review comments, and CI history to determine what changes are still valid. The worker must make judgment calls about which changes to preserve, making this beyond `tier:simple`.

## How (Approach)

Exact files and line ranges will be determined by inspecting PR #1249 diff.

2. **Check if branch still exists:**

title: investigation: rogue agent renames (PRs #1283, #1289, #1290, #1291) — root cause and guardrails
body:
## Summary

Multiple headless aidevops workers have proposed (and partially merged) PRs that violate the canonical naming convention now documented in [AGENTS.md → CANONICAL NAMING](https://github.com/Ultimate-Multisite/superdav-ai-agent/blob/main/AGENTS.md#canonical-naming---do-not-change). All four cases share the same root cause: an ambiguous parent issue (#1288) and worker briefs that conflate the WP.org plugin slug with internal code prefixes.

This issue tracks the investigation and proposes guardrails so this pattern stops recurring.

## The four offending PRs

| PR | Worker model | Action | Outcome |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| #1289 | `nemotron-3-super-free` | Renamed DI `'id' => 'sd-ai-agent'` → `'superdav-ai-agent'` and `CompiledContainerSdAiAgent` → `CompiledContainerSuperdavAiAgent` | Merged → reverted in #1292 |
| #1290 | `nemotron-3-super-free` | Renamed `gratis-ai-agent` → `superdav-ai-agent` in `AbstractAbility.php`, on a branch `t235-fix-ability-discoverability` whose linked issue (#235) is unrelated and CLOSED | Closed unmerged |
| #1291 | (auto-branch `feature/auto-...-gh1288`) | Renamed `sd-ai-agent/...` ability namespace → `superdav-ai-agent/...` in docblocks | Merged → reverted in #1292 |
| #1283 | (squash `501a25e`) | Added `canonicalise()` auto-migration of legacy `ai-agent/` keys to `sd-ai-agent/` | Merged → reverted in #1292 |

## Root cause: parent issue #1288

Issue #1288 is itself aidevops-generated (`origin:worker`, `auto-dispatch`, `tier:thinking`, signature `minimax-m2.5-free`). Its `## How` section contains the trigger phrasing:

> Rename text domain occurrences (`ai-agent` → `superdav-ai-agent`)
> Align hook prefixes (`ai_agent_` → `sd_ai_agent_` **or similar**)

Problems with that brief:

1. **Conflates two distinct renames.** The WP.org slug rename (`ai-agent` → `superdav-ai-agent`, applies to text-domain headers, folder name) is correct. The internal prefix rename (`ai_agent_` → `sd_ai_agent_`, applies to constants, DB tables, namespaces, REST routes, abilities) is also correct. But an LLM worker can easily merge them into a single "rename everything to `superdav-ai-agent`" interpretation — exactly what PRs #1289 and #1291 did.
2. **"Or similar" gives unbounded latitude.** Workers re-derive the target prefix on every dispatch. Without a fixed target, two different workers will produce two different "canonical" answers.
3. **No prohibition list.** The brief lists what to do, never what NOT to do. Workers had no signal that `'id' => 'sd-ai-agent'` was off-limits.
4. **`tier:thinking` doesn't help here.** A more capable model still reads the same ambiguous brief and confidently picks the wrong interpretation.

## Why PR #1290 (closed unmerged) is the most concerning

PR #1290 was on branch `t235-fix-ability-discoverability`, but issue #235 ("Add Abilities Explorer admin page") is CLOSED and unrelated to the rename. The worker:

- Picked an unrelated stale issue
- Invented a goal ("ability discoverability")
- Picked the wrong rename direction (`gratis-ai-agent` → `superdav-ai-agent` instead of `gratis-ai-agent` → `sd-ai-agent`)
- Spent 4m and 507k tokens before being closed

This is symptomatic of a worker dispatch that proceeded without a valid worker-ready brief, in violation of the aidevops worker discipline rules.

## Guardrails added

- [x] Canonical naming table + "rules for agents" added to [`AGENTS.md`](https://github.com/Ultimate-Multisite/superdav-ai-agent/blob/main/AGENTS.md#canonical-naming---do-not-change) (commit `47cc5e3`).
- [x] All three merged offenders reverted in PR #1292.
- [x] AGENTS.md explicitly lists PR #1283, #1289, #1290, #1291 as examples of mistakes not to repeat.

## Proposed follow-ups

1. **Close issue #1288 and any siblings** that still contain the ambiguous brief. Replace with a fresh issue that:
   - Quotes the AGENTS.md naming table verbatim
   - Lists each rename target as a concrete `from → to` pair
   - Includes an explicit "DO NOT" list (e.g. "do not modify `'id' => 'sd-ai-agent'`")
2. **Audit `auto-dispatch` issue templates** for the same conflation pattern elsewhere (e.g. anything that says "or similar", "align with", "for consistency").
3. **Block worker dispatch on stale/closed linked issues.** PR #1290's branch claimed to address closed issue #235 — pre-dispatch validators should refuse to start.
4. **Stop using `nemotron-3-super-free` and `minimax-m2.5-free` for refactor/rename tasks.** Their token-spend pattern (4m, 500k tokens for a wrong-direction find/replace) suggests they are not exercising judgement; a smaller deterministic codemod would be safer.
5. **Add a CI check** that fails if `superdav-ai-agent.php` doesn't contain `'id' => 'sd-ai-agent'` and `CompiledContainerSdAiAgent`. Cheap regression guard.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Issue #1288 closed or rewritten with the canonical naming table
- [ ] CI regression guard for plugin `'id'` and compile class added
- [ ] Audit of `auto-dispatch` issues for similar conflation completed (with findings)
- [ ] Decision documented re: worker-model allowlist for naming/refactor tasks
