title: General agent's tier_1_tools missing update-post and update-global-styles — system prompt directs model to call them, resolver rejects with ability_not_allowed, agent burns max_iterations and produces empty page
body:
## Bug: General agent's `tier_1_tools` lack `update-post` and `update-global-styles`, but its system prompt instructs the model to use them — agent loops then hits max-iterations with empty page

### Summary

The built-in **General** agent (`includes/Models/Agent.php::get_general_definition`) has its `tier_1_tools` limited to:

```
sd-ai-agent/ability-search
sd-ai-agent/ability-call
sd-ai-agent/memory-save
sd-ai-agent/memory-list
sd-ai-agent/skill-load
sd-ai-agent/knowledge-search
wp-cli/execute
sd-ai-agent/create-post
```

(see `Agent::get_general_tier_1_tools()` at `includes/Models/Agent.php:462-473`)

But the General agent's own system prompt (`Agent::get_general_definition()` at `includes/Models/Agent.php:600-625`) explicitly instructs the model to **build landing pages with serialized Gutenberg block markup** and to **chain operations** (create then refine), and the broader `SystemInstructionBuilder` (`includes/Core/SystemInstructionBuilder.php:376,383`) tells the model to call `sd-ai-agent/update-post` (Step 5) and `sd-ai-agent/update-global-styles` (Step 7) during site-builder workflows.

When the model follows those instructions, the resolver at `includes/Compat/ai-client/class-wp-ai-client-ability-function-resolver.php:125-132` rejects the calls with `code: ability_not_allowed`. The model then loops trying to discover/recover, burns through `max_iterations` (50), and produces an empty page plus an apologetic summary admitting it could not complete the work.

### Reproduction

1. Use a fresh demo signup that lands on a site with the **General** agent + Anthropic Max + Claude Sonnet 4.5 (this is the default for new "AI Agent Free" signups via the demo flow).
2. Send a long landing-page build prompt that asks for: theme color updates, a published page with multiple Gutenberg sections (hero, features grid, pricing, slider, carousel, FAQ, sticky CTA).
3. Wait for the agent to compose its reply (~6m).

**Expected:** the agent updates global styles, creates the page, then iteratively updates `post_content` with the full block markup until the request is satisfied.

**Observed (verified end-to-end on a production demo subsite):**

- 24 tool calls made over 384.8s.
- `sd-ai-agent/create-post` succeeded (page ID 42 published, but `post_content` empty).
- `sd-ai-agent/update-global-styles` rejected: `ability_not_allowed`.
- `sd-ai-agent/update-post` rejected: `ability_not_allowed`.
- `sd-ai-agent/theme-json-presets` reached but called incorrectly (`missing_styles` — agent did not include the `styles` argument because it had only seen the schema indirectly via `ability-call`).
- Agent hit max_iterations and self-summarized: *"I encountered a technical issue with the tool system that prevented me from adding the actual Gutenberg block content to the page."*

### Evidence

Captured directly from `wp_71_sd_ai_agent_sessions` row id=4 (user 1028, model `claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929`, tool_calls JSON):

```json
{"role":"user","parts":[{"channel":"content","type":"function_response","functionResponse":{
  "id":"toolu_01NmmMoSP5MS33FUdyAmyobq",
  "name":"wpab__sd-ai-agent__update-global-styles",
  "response":{
    "error":"Ability \"sd-ai-agent/update-global-styles\" was not specified in the allowed abilities list.",
    "code":"ability_not_allowed"
  }
}}]}
```

```json
{"role":"user","parts":[{"channel":"content","type":"function_response","functionResponse":{
  "id":"toolu_01RXNLK1fRY6p9TAMiWBhseC",
  "name":"wpab__sd-ai-agent__update-post",
  "response":{
    "error":"Ability \"sd-ai-agent/update-post\" was not specified in the allowed abilities list.",
    "code":"ability_not_allowed"
  }
}}]}
```

Aggregate counts of error responses in this session:

| Ability called | Error code | Count |
|---|---|---|
| `sd-ai-agent/update-post` | `ability_not_allowed` | 2 |
| `sd-ai-agent/update-global-styles` | `ability_not_allowed` | 2 |
| `sd-ai-agent/ability-call` | `ability_invalid_input` | 4 |
| `sd-ai-agent/ability-call` → `theme-json-presets` | `missing_styles` | 1 |

### Why this matters

**The General agent is the default agent for new demo signups.** The demo flow is the user's first impression of the product. With this configuration, a user asking the default agent to "build me a landing page" — exactly the kind of prompt the marketing copy and the system prompt itself implies should work — gets:

- A blank page in their site (visible failure).
- A 6-minute wait (no streaming sense of progress).
- An apologetic summary that ends with "Would you like me to complete the content population using WP-CLI?" — which a typical demo user cannot answer.

### Comparison to other built-in agents

(from `wp_71_sd_ai_agent_agents`, `tier_1_tools` column)

| Agent | Has `update-post`? | Has `update-global-styles`? | Has `list-posts`? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `onboarding` | no | no | yes |
| **`general`** | **no** | **no** | **no** |
| `content-creator` | yes | no | yes |
| `seo` | yes | no | yes |
| `ecommerce` | no | no | no |

So `update-global-styles` is **not in any built-in profile's tier_1_tools**, despite `SystemInstructionBuilder.php:383` and `SkillAutoInjector.php:198` both referencing it as the canonical way to apply theme colors. It is registered as a callable ability in `includes/Abilities/GlobalStylesAbilities.php:74` and used in benchmarks (`includes/Benchmark/BenchmarkSuite.php:1328-1356`), so it exists — it's just never reachable from a real chat session through any built-in agent.

### Suggested fixes

Two layers of fix:

**A. Tier 1 tool surface (minimum)**

Add `sd-ai-agent/update-post` to `Agent::get_general_tier_1_tools()` (`includes/Models/Agent.php:462-473`). Without it, the General agent literally cannot iterate on its own page after `create-post`, which the prompt at `includes/Models/Agent.php:600-602` explicitly tells the model to do.

Add `sd-ai-agent/update-global-styles` to at least one built-in profile (General, or a new "Web Builder" profile). Right now it is unreachable.

Add `sd-ai-agent/list-posts` to General — without it the agent cannot inspect its own creations, which several prompt steps in the codebase assume it can.

**B. Fail loudly instead of looping**

When `class-wp-ai-client-ability-function-resolver.php` returns `ability_not_allowed`, the agent currently keeps trying. Two improvements would help:

1. Include the agent's actual `tier_1_tools` list in the error response, so the model immediately knows what *is* available rather than calling `ability-search` and burning iterations.
2. After 2 `ability_not_allowed` errors in a single run, short-circuit with a user-visible message ("This agent can't update pages — try the **Content Creator** agent for this task") rather than letting `max_iterations` deplete silently.

**C. Keep the system prompt and the tool surface in sync**

There's a maintainability bug here: `Agent::get_general_definition()` system prompt and `SystemInstructionBuilder` reference abilities that aren't in the tier list. A unit test that asserts every ability mentioned in a built-in agent's `system_prompt` is present in its `tier_1_tools` would catch this regression. (See `tests/SdAiAgent/Core/RolePermissionsTest.php` for an existing pattern.)

### Environment

- Plugin: `superdav-ai-agent` `1.10.0` (production deploy `20260508033200`)
- Site: a fresh demo signup site cloned from template, running on a multisite network (`wp_71_*` tables)
- WordPress: 6.5.x via Bedrock
- PHP: 8.2
- Theme: Ollie 1.6.0
- Provider: `ai-provider-for-anthropic-max` (OAuth, working — confirmed `success: 9` in `sd_ai_agent_model_health`)
- Model: `claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929`
- Agent: `general` (default for new sessions)

### Files referenced

- `includes/Models/Agent.php:462-473` — `get_general_tier_1_tools()` (the missing abilities)
- `includes/Models/Agent.php:600-625` — General agent system prompt (mentions iteration that requires `update-post`)
- `includes/Core/SystemInstructionBuilder.php:376,383` — references `update-post` and `update-global-styles`
- `includes/Core/SkillAutoInjector.php:198` — maps `update-global-styles` → `full-site-editing` skill
- `includes/Compat/ai-client/class-wp-ai-client-ability-function-resolver.php:125-132` — emits `ability_not_allowed`
- `includes/Abilities/GlobalStylesAbilities.php:74` — registers `update-global-styles`
- `includes/Benchmark/BenchmarkSuite.php:1328-1356` — assumes `update-global-styles` is reachable in benchmark scenarios
- `tests/SdAiAgent/Core/RolePermissionsTest.php` — existing pattern for ability-list tests

title: feat: payment-method gating notice when usage cap is reached on metered subsites
body:
## Context

The companion plugin [`ultimate-multisite-metered-plans`](https://github.com/Ultimate-Multisite/ultimate-multisite-metered-plans) is shipping a free→paid transition (PR coming next) where:

- A subsite starts on a free metered plan ($0/mo recurring base, e.g. \$10 of AI usage included).
- When usage hits the cap AND no payment method is on file, generation is blocked.
- A new REST endpoint `GET /sd-metered/v1/payment-method-status` returns the current state.
- The user must visit the WP Ultimo checkout page to attach a card (Stripe SetupIntent) — the same plan, just collecting a payment method.
- After a card is attached, `hard_cutoff` flips off and the user is billed monthly for usage above the included amount.

The metered-plans REST endpoint will return:

```json
{
  \"has_payment_method\": false,
  \"is_metered\": true,
  \"current_usage_usd\": 10.00,
  \"limit_usd\": 10.00,
  \"checkout_url\": \"https://madclaw.mygratis.site/wp/wp-admin/admin.php?page=wu-checkout&membership=HHHHKND2K5\",
  \"membership_hash\": \"HHHHKND2K5\"
}
```

## Required UI changes in this plugin

Two notice surfaces, both linking to `checkout_url` from the endpoint:

### 1. Persistent banner

Add a banner at the top of the AI Agent admin UI when the endpoint reports `has_payment_method: false` AND `current_usage_usd >= limit_usd * 0.8` (warn at 80%, hard-block at 100%).

- Below 80%: no banner.
- 80–99%: yellow warning banner — \"You've used X of \$Y in AI credits this month. [Add a payment method] to continue past the included usage.\"
- 100%+: red blocking banner — \"You've reached the AI usage cap for this month. [Add a payment method] to continue using AI features.\"

### 2. Inline error in chat

When a generation request is blocked by the metered-plans runtime gate (the SDK throws `TokenLimitReachedException` with a message containing \"not available on your plan\" or \"AI usage cap\"), display an inline error in the chat panel:

> You've reached your AI usage cap for this month. [Add a payment method →](checkout_url) to continue.

The link must open in a new tab.

## Endpoint contract

- Path: `GET /sd-metered/v1/payment-method-status`
- Auth: requires logged-in user with cap to read membership (subsite admins).
- Response: JSON shape above.
- 200 even when not on a metered plan (returns `is_metered: false`); the UI should hide the banner in that case.
- The endpoint is exposed by the `ultimate-multisite-metered-plans` addon. If the addon isn't active, the endpoint won't exist — handle 404/network errors by hiding the banner (fail open, don't block the UI).

## Out of scope

- Embedding the checkout form inside the AI Agent UI (just link to it).
- PayPal payment-method flow (Stripe only for now).
- Network admin views (subsite-only feature).

## Verification

- [ ] On a subsite with no PM and usage < 80%: no banner, chat works.
- [ ] On a subsite with no PM and usage at 80%: yellow banner, chat works.
- [ ] On a subsite with no PM and usage at 100%: red banner, generation blocked, inline error appears with checkout link.
- [ ] On a subsite with PM attached: no banner regardless of usage.
- [ ] On a subsite where addon is inactive (endpoint 404): no banner, chat works (fail open).

## References

- Companion PR: TBA on `Ultimate-Multisite/ultimate-multisite-metered-plans`
- Existing AI usage cap implementation: `ultimate-multisite-metered-plans/inc/managers/class-ai-usage-listener.php`
- Existing model-availability filter: `ultimate-multisite-metered-plans/inc/managers/class-model-availability-filter.php`

title: fix(tests): RestControllerTest tool_result_409 tests fail with "Undefined array key type" under WP trunk
body:
## Summary

Three PHPUnit tests in `tests/SdAiAgent/REST/RestControllerTest.php` have been failing with `Undefined array key "type"` in WordPress core REST schema validation since the merge of #1296. The failures are not introduced by changes to the controllers under test — they appear to stem from a missing `'type' => '…'` key in an `args` schema definition that became newly enforced under WP trunk.

## Failing tests

- `test_tool_result_409_clears_stale_awaiting_client_tools_transient` — `RestControllerTest.php:1479`
- `test_tool_result_409_preserves_complete_transient` — `RestControllerTest.php:1542`
- `test_tool_result_409_no_job_id_is_safe` — `RestControllerTest.php:1583`

## Error

```
Undefined array key "type"
/tmp/wordpress/wp-includes/rest-api.php:2207
/tmp/wordpress/wp-includes/rest-api.php:2402
/tmp/wordpress/wp-includes/rest-api.php:2239
/tmp/wordpress/wp-includes/rest-api.php:2495
/tmp/wordpress/wp-includes/rest-api.php:2242
/tmp/wordpress/wp-includes/rest-api.php:1442
/tmp/wordpress/wp-includes/rest-api.php:1479
/tmp/wordpress/wp-includes/rest-api/class-wp-rest-request.php:850
/tmp/wordpress/wp-includes/rest-api/class-wp-rest-server.php:1113
```

## Investigation pointers

- `wp-includes/rest-api.php:2207` is inside `rest_validate_value_from_schema()` — the test args schema or controller route registration is missing a top-level `'type'` for one of the parameters.
- The route under test is `POST /sd-ai-agent/v1/chat/tool-result` registered in the chat REST controller (search for `register_rest_route( … 'chat/tool-result'` in `includes/REST/`).
- Compare with sibling routes (e.g. `chat/sessions`, `chat/jobs`) that pass schema validation under WP trunk.
- Likely fix: ensure every `args` entry in the route registration has `'type' => 'string|integer|object|array'` and not just a `validate_callback`.

## Verification

- Run `npm run test:php` locally (requires `wp-env`).
- After fix, the 3 errors above should disappear from the **PHPUnit** check on PR builds.
- Ensure other `chat/tool-result` tests still pass.

## Context

- Discovered while merging #1300. PR #1300 left these pre-existing failures untouched because they are unrelated to its banner/error-filter changes.
- Affected check: **PHPUnit** (failing) — does not block merges (no branch protection on `main`) but pollutes CI signal.

Refs #1296

title: Supervisor health dashboard stale: 2d0h (#1115)
body:
## Premise

The dashboard at #1115 last refreshed `2026-05-07T19:24:22Z` — **2d0h ago** (threshold: 2d0h). The `stats-wrapper.sh` scheduler is likely failing silently.

## Why this matters

The supervisor health dashboard is the framework's primary single-glance health surface. When it stops refreshing, operators keep trusting green numbers that no longer reflect reality — every decision derived from "dashboard says green" becomes invalid.

## Triage

1. Inspect the stats scheduler status (macOS):

   ```bash
   launchctl list | grep -i aidevops-stats-wrapper
   tail -40 ~/.aidevops/logs/stats.log
   ls -la ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.aidevops.aidevops-stats-wrapper.plist
   ```

2. Run the refresh manually and capture the error:

   ```bash
   bash ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/stats-wrapper.sh 2>&1 | tail -40
   ```

3. Check the dashboard issue directly:

   ```bash
   gh api repos/Ultimate-Multisite/superdav-ai-agent/issues/1115 --jq '{updated_at, body_length: (.body|length)}'
   ```

## Remediation

- **Missing plist:** re-run `setup.sh --non-interactive` (or `aidevops update`) with PULSE_ENABLED=true so `setup_stats_wrapper` reinstalls `com.aidevops.aidevops-stats-wrapper.plist`.
- **`set -euo pipefail` fail:** the post-t2418 wrapper emits `HEALTH-DASHBOARD-FAIL exit=<N>` on error. Grep `stats.log` on that prefix.
- **Body size / API error:** inspect `stats.log` — look at `gh` HTTP errors and `_update_health_issue_for_repo` failures.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Root cause identified and documented on this issue.
- [ ] `gh issue view 1115 --repo Ultimate-Multisite/superdav-ai-agent` shows an update within 24h of closing this alert.
- [ ] `last_refresh:` marker is present in the dashboard body.

title: bug: WP-CLI execute ability fails with proc_open_failed on restricted hosting
body:
## Description

When a user starts their first session, the agent attempts to use the WP-CLI execute ability to list posts. The ability returns `proc_open_failed`, which indicates PHP's `proc_open()` function is disabled or the subprocess cannot be spawned. The agent retries via ability search but the user-facing session begins with a silent tool failure.

## Expected Behavior

The WP-CLI ability should detect that `proc_open` is unavailable and either:
- Fall back to the equivalent REST API ability, or
- Return a clear error message so the agent can explain the limitation and use an alternative path.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Install the plugin on a shared hosting environment where PHP `proc_open()` is disabled
2. Start a new chat session
3. Ask: "Hi! I just set up this plugin and I'm ready to get started."
4. Observe: agent calls `wpab__wp-cli__execute` with `post list ...` — gets `{"error":"Failed to execute WP-CLI command.","code":"proc_open_failed"}`

## Environment

- Plugin version: unknown (no environment data in report)
- WordPress: unknown
- PHP: unknown (shared hosting environment inferred from `proc_open_failed`)
- Multisite: unknown
- Provider: unknown
- Error code: `proc_open_failed`

## Notes

The agent recovered by searching abilities for alternatives, but this wastes a round-trip. The WP-CLI ability should proactively guard against `proc_open` being disabled at ability registration or first-call time.

**Files to investigate:**
- `includes/Abilities/` — WP-CLI execute ability class
- Check `proc_open()` availability guard in `WP_CLI_Execute` or equivalent class

**Verification:** reproduce on a PHP environment with `disable_functions = proc_open`; confirm graceful fallback.

## Feedback Report

title: security: scrub credentials from session_messages before feedback report submission
body:
## Description

The feedback submission system stores raw `session_messages` from the plugin's chat UI. During triage of incoming reports it was observed that a user accidentally pasted a credential string into their prompt message. That credential was stored verbatim in the feedback server's database and transmitted in the full report payload.

## Risk

Any user who pastes an API key, password, or token into the chat input will have that secret stored in:
- The WordPress database on their own install (expected, accepted risk)
- The remote feedback server database (unexpected, higher risk — outside the user's control)

## Expected Behaviour

Before the plugin submits a feedback report, `session_messages` should be scanned for common credential patterns and those values should be redacted (replaced with `[REDACTED]`) prior to transmission.

## Suggested Fix

Add a server-side scrubbing pass in the feedback submission handler before the payload is sent to the remote endpoint. Patterns to match at minimum:
- OpenAI API key patterns (`sk-...`, `sk-proj-...`)
- Generic long high-entropy strings (≥40 chars, base62/base64 charset) in positions that look like values (after `=`, `:`, or as standalone tokens)
- `Bearer <token>` strings

This should happen in the plugin's feedback submission code path, not on the server side, so the credential never leaves the user's install.

**Files to investigate:**
- `includes/` — feedback submission or session-export code
- `includes/REST/` — any webhook/outbound POST handler used for feedback

**Verification:** unit test that a message containing a mock API key string is redacted before the payload is constructed.

## Feedback Report Reference

body:

**Logged:** 2026-04-26
**Tags:** `parent` `plan` `site-builder-ability-improvements`

## Description

Site builder ability improvements

## Plan: Purpose

Five genuine capability gaps found in the site builder audit. Most critical is the stock image fallback chain — Openverse/Pixabay download failures return hard errors with no retry. The rest are ergonomic improvements that reduce tool-call count and remove ambiguity for the agent.

<details><summary>Plan: Context & Architecture</summary>


**Context**

**Stock image fallback (t236):** `StockImageAbility` calls `ImageSourceFactory::get_available()`, picks the first free source, and returns a hard error if `download()` fails. The factory handles empty search results (falls back to AI generate) but not download failures. Fix: in `ImageSourceFactory::import_image()` on download failure, iterate to next free source then fall back to `generate`. Files: `ImageAbilities/StockImageAbility.php`, `ImageSources/ImageSourceFactory.php`.
**Page template (t237):** `wp_insert_post()` / `wp_update_post()` accept `page_template` as a post data key (maps to `_wp_page_template` meta). Neither `create-post` nor `update-post` expose it. Add to schema + handler in `PostAbilities.php`. Two lines per handler.
**set-featured-image (t238):** Already works via `update-post` (pass `post_id` + `featured_image_id`). A standalone ability removes ambiguity — agents frequently miss that `update-post` can set only the thumbnail without touching other fields. Add as a new `wp_register_ability` call in `PostAbilities.php`.
**batch-create-posts (t239):** A full site build takes ~7 sequential `create-post` calls. A batch ability accepting an array of post definitions reduces that to 1 call. Schema: `{ posts: [{ title, content, post_type, status, featured_image_id, page_template, ... }] }`. Returns `[{ post_id, permalink, title, status }]`. Add handler in `PostAbilities.php`.
**create-contact-form (t240):** WPForms is too plugin-specific. Better: register `ai-agent/create-contact-form` that inserts a simple HTML contact form as a Gutenberg HTML block (no plugin dependency). If Contact Form 7 is active, use its `WPCF7_ContactForm::create()` API instead and return the shortcode. Fallback chain: CF7 → raw HTML block. New ability in `ContentAbilities.php` or a new `FormsAbilities.php`.

- `update-post` — `PostAbilities.php:171`

## Description

Block theme generation in onboarding (Automattic wp-site-creator inspired)

## Plan: Purpose

Add a "Design a custom theme" branch to onboarding. After provider setup, fresh-install users can opt into a 4-phase agent conversation that interviews them about their site, presents 3 distinct topic-grounded design directions as HTML previews, and on selection generates a complete block theme (theme.json, style.css, functions.php, templates/, parts/) deployed to `wp-content/themes/<slug>/` and activated — all inside the existing chat UI.
Architecture adapted from [Automattic/wordpress-agent-skills/claude-code/wp-site-creator](https://github.com/Automattic/wordpress-agent-skills/tree/trunk/claude-code/wp-site-creator). We take the 4-phase flow, the site-specification skill, and the topic-grounded design thinking. We do NOT take their Claude-Code-plugin packaging, WordPress Studio CLI dependency, parallel Task() subagent pattern, or block-fixer Node script (we have `validate-block-content` already).
Closes the PLANS.md "AI site generation from prompt" P0 gap on the visual-container side (t060-t062 handle pages; this handles themes).

<details><summary>Plan: Context & Architecture</summary>


**Context**

**Source comparison.** Studied [Automattic's `/quick-build` command](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Automattic/wordpress-agent-skills/trunk/claude-code/wp-site-creator/commands/quick-build.md), [`/preview-designs`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Automattic/wordpress-agent-skills/trunk/claude-code/wp-site-creator/commands/preview-designs.md), and [site-specification SKILL](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Automattic/wordpress-agent-skills/trunk/claude-code/wp-site-creator/skills/site-specification/SKILL.md) against our `OnboardingManager` + `BootstrapPrompt` + `OnboardingWizard` + `OnboardingBootstrap`. Our existing flow is discovery-only: explores the site, presents 4 starter prompts. Their flow generates a complete theme. Fresh-install conversion is the opportunity.
**Capability gap.** We have most of what we need: `create-block-content`, `validate-block-content`, `list-block-templates`, `list-block-patterns`, `update-global-styles`, `get-theme-json`, and `FileAbilities` (writes anywhere under wp-content when `FILE_WRITE` cap is on). Missing: directory + theme.json scaffold ability and a switch_theme wrapper. That's two new abilities, both small.
**Why phases not one PR.** Phase 1 (site-spec skill) alone improves every content-creation interaction (post drafts, page builds, product descriptions). Phase 2 (block-themes skill expansion) compounds for all theme-aware work, not just onboarding. Phases 3-4 are where the theme-builder onboarding actually lights up. Each phase ships value independently — if we stop after Phase 2 we've still made the agent meaningfully better.
**What we explicitly are NOT doing:**
- Generating Gutenberg patterns library (separate work — t060-t062)
- WooCommerce-aware theme variants (Phase 3 ships a generic theme; Woo-specific templates are follow-up)
- Multi-language theme generation
- Child-theme generation
- AI-redesigning existing themes
- Adopting WordPress Studio CLI (irrelevant inside a running WP install)
- Telemetry scripts from the Automattic plugin
**Topic-grounded design thinking.** Their key insight: don't generate "modern dark theme / minimalist light theme / colorful theme" — instead, ask what aesthetic worlds the *topic* could authentically inhabit. A craft brewery is not "generic dark/light/colorful"; it's taproom-warmth vs label-art-maximalism vs industrial-grain-and-steel. This is what Phase 4's skill captures.
**No stock image URLs ever.** Their prompts repeat this rule; we adopt it. Generated themes rely on CSS gradients, color blocks, and typography when the user hasn't supplied imagery.

## Task Brief

# t170 — Block theme generation in onboarding (inspired by Automattic wp-site-creator)

## Pre-flight

- [x] Memory recall: `wp-site-creator wordpress agent skills` → 0 hits — no prior lessons; new territory in this repo, recall confirmed fresh
- [x] Discovery pass: 0 open PRs and 0 in-flight commits touch `OnboardingManager.php`, `BootstrapPrompt.php`, `onboarding-wizard.js`, `onboarding-bootstrap.js`, or `block-themes.md` in last 48h (verified on branch `fix/orphan-tool-result-trim`)
- [x] File refs verified: 8 refs checked, all present at HEAD (`OnboardingManager.php:341-456`, `BootstrapPrompt.php`, `onboarding-bootstrap.js`, `onboarding-wizard.js:326-463`, `GeneratePluginAbility.php`, `BlockAbilities.php:217-246`, `GlobalStylesAbilities.php`, `block-themes.md`, `kadence-theme.md`)
- [x] Tier: `tier:thinking` — parent task with UX + system-prompt design decisions; phase children re-evaluate their own tier when filed
- [x] Seeded draft PR decision recorded: skipped — parent task, no implementation. Phase 1 child should be the first PR.

## Session origin

Filed 2026-05-13 after studying [Automattic/wordpress-agent-skills/claude-code/wp-site-creator](https://github.com/Automattic/wordpress-agent-skills/tree/trunk/claude-code/wp-site-creator)
and comparing it with our existing onboarding flow (`OnboardingManager`,
`BootstrapPrompt`, `OnboardingWizard`, `OnboardingBootstrap`). Their plugin
generates a complete WordPress block theme from a one-line description via a
4-phase agent flow. Our onboarding is purely discovery — we explore an
existing site and present starter prompts, but we never *create* a theme.
For a fresh-install user, having the agent design and activate a custom
block theme during onboarding would be a real differentiator (currently
only 10Web/ZipWP do this, and neither runs as a plugin you own).

## What

Add a "Design a custom theme" branch to onboarding that, after the user has
a working AI provider, can interview the user, present 3 distinct visual
design directions, and on selection generate a complete activated block
theme — all inside the existing chat UI, without leaving WordPress.

The deliverable is a working onboarding branch where:

1. After provider setup, the user is offered three onboarding modes:
   - **Explore my existing site** (current behaviour, default for non-empty installs)
   - **Design a custom theme** (new, default for fresh installs)
   - **Skip — just chat** (current behaviour)
2. The theme-builder branch runs a 4-phase conversation:
   - **Phase 1** Interview: extract a site spec (name, type, audience, tone, brand keywords, key sections, typography). Uses the new `site-specification` skill. #1369
   - **Phase 2** Present 3 topic-grounded design directions as HTML previews stored in `wp-content/uploads/sd-ai-agent/design-previews/<session>/design-{1,2,3}.html` and shown inline in chat. #1378
   - **Phase 3** User picks a direction (1, 2, 3, or "2 but darker"). Modifications fold back into the spec. #1384
   - **Phase 4** Generate the full block theme into `wp-content/themes/<slug>/` (theme.json, style.css, functions.php, parts/header.html, parts/footer.html, templates/index.html, templates/page.html) and activate it.
3. All theme files are validated via existing `sd-ai-agent/validate-block-content` before write.

We do **not** ship the Automattic plugin verbatim — it's a Claude Code
plugin, not a WordPress plugin, and depends on WordPress Studio CLI which
isn't relevant inside a running WP install. We adapt the *architecture*
(phases, skills, references) to our agent loop.

## Why

1. **Fresh-install conversion.** Right now a fresh-install user activates
   the plugin, sees an empty discovery summary, and gets generic starter
   prompts. They are not impressed and they bounce. A "design a theme for
   my SaaS in 5 minutes" flow is what 10Web and ZipWP use to convert.
2. **Showcases agent capability.** Generating a coherent block theme
   requires our agent to chain `create-block-content`, `validate-block-content`,
   `update-global-styles`, `list-block-patterns`, file writes, and theme
   activation — exactly the kind of multi-step tool-calling we built the
   loop for. It's a credible demo.
3. **PLANS.md gap closure.** PLANS.md identifies "AI site generation from
   prompt" as P0 (t060-t062 line) but those tasks are about generating
   *pages*, not themes. This complements them — themes are the visual
   container, pages are the content. Both are needed.
4. **Reusable skill scaffolding.** The `site-specification` skill alone
   improves every content-creation interaction (page builds, post drafts,
   product descriptions), not just onboarding.

## Tier

`tier:thinking` — parent/planning task. UX decisions, system-prompt design,
and integration sequencing are judgment work. The 4 phase children below
are individually `tier:standard` (skills + abilities + UI wiring with
clear file targets), but Phase 3 specifically may be `tier:thinking`.

## Phases

This is a parent task. Each phase is a separate PR.

- **Phase 1 — Site-specification skill** ~3h — add `includes/Models/skills/site-specification.md` mirroring Automattic's per-site-type inference tables. New memory category `site_brief` for storing extracted specs across sessions. No UI changes. #1369
- **Phase 2 — Block-themes skill expansion** ~4h — expand `includes/Models/skills/block-themes.md` with theme.json patterns, template-part composition, animation/motion classes, and editor-visibility CSS lifted from Automattic's `wordpress-block-theming.md` reference (29KB → distil to ~400 lines, keep our existing 150-line structure as the spine). #1378
- **Phase 3 — Theme-builder onboarding branch** ~12h — new `ThemeBuilderPrompt` (mirrors `BootstrapPrompt`), new REST endpoint `POST /onboarding/theme-builder-start`, choose-mode UI in `OnboardingWizard`, and two new abilities: `sd-ai-agent/scaffold-block-theme` (creates the directory + theme.json + style.css + functions.php) and `sd-ai-agent/activate-theme` (wraps `switch_theme()`). Existing `FileAbilities` handles HTML file writes. #1384
- **Phase 4 — Design-system reference skills** ~5h — add `includes/Models/skills/design-system-aesthetics.md` covering the "topic-grounded visual worlds" framework (brewery → taproom vs label-art vs industrial), referenced by Phase 3's system prompt during the design-direction step.

Each phase PR uses `For #NNN` referencing the parent issue until Phase 4
ships, which uses `Closes #NNN`.

## How (Approach)

### Progressive Context Plan

- **Read first:** `includes/Core/BootstrapPrompt.php` and `includes/Core/OnboardingManager.php` — the discovery-bootstrap flow this work mirrors and extends.
- **Read first:** `src/components/onboarding-bootstrap.js` and `src/components/onboarding-wizard.js` — the React entry points the new branch plugs into.
- **Load only if:** [Automattic wp-site-creator commands/quick-build.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Automattic/wordpress-agent-skills/trunk/claude-code/wp-site-creator/commands/quick-build.md) — only when designing Phase 3's system prompt; we don't copy it, we use it as a reference for phase ordering.
- **Load only if:** [Automattic site-specification SKILL.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Automattic/wordpress-agent-skills/trunk/claude-code/wp-site-creator/skills/site-specification/SKILL.md) — direct source for Phase 1 inference tables.
- **Stop when:** the parent issue body lists 4 phase children with clear file targets and acceptance criteria each.

### Files to Modify (across all phases)

- `NEW: includes/Models/skills/site-specification.md` — Phase 1
- `EDIT: includes/Models/skills/block-themes.md` — Phase 2 (expand from 150 → ~400 lines)
- `NEW: includes/Core/ThemeBuilderPrompt.php` — Phase 3 (model on `BootstrapPrompt.php`)
- `EDIT: includes/Core/OnboardingManager.php` — Phase 3 (add `rest_theme_builder_start` REST callback paralleling `rest_bootstrap_start`)
- `NEW: includes/Abilities/ScaffoldBlockThemeAbility.php` — Phase 3 (model on `GeneratePluginAbility.php`)
- `NEW: includes/Abilities/ActivateThemeAbility.php` — Phase 3 (wraps `switch_theme()` with cap check `switch_themes`)
- `EDIT: src/components/onboarding-wizard.js` — Phase 3 (add mode-picker step between provider setup and finish)
- `NEW: src/components/onboarding-theme-builder.js` — Phase 3 (new entry component, parallel to `onboarding-bootstrap.js`)
- `NEW: includes/Models/skills/design-system-aesthetics.md` — Phase 4

### Implementation Steps (high-level — each phase brief will detail its own)

1. **Phase 1:** Read Automattic's `site-specification/SKILL.md` (already in this session's context), adapt to our skill markdown format (matches `block-themes.md` and `kadence-theme.md` style), wire the new memory category `site_brief` via `Memory::create()`. Test: agent extracts spec from "build me a theme for my coffee shop Bean & Brew" and stores it in memory.

2. **Phase 2:** Diff Automattic's `wordpress-block-theming.md` (29KB) against our `block-themes.md` (150 lines). Lift the theme.json color/typography presets, animation classes, prefers-reduced-motion patterns, and editor-styles-wrapper CSS guidance. Keep our existing tool references intact. Test: word count and section ratchet, plus a manual read-pass for accuracy.

3. **Phase 3:** Largest phase. Subphases:
   - **3a** New abilities: `ScaffoldBlockThemeAbility` + `ActivateThemeAbility`. Cap gates: `install_themes` and `switch_themes` respectively.
   - **3b** New `ThemeBuilderPrompt` class generating a 4-phase system instruction (interview → designs → choose → build). Use `sd-ai-agent/memory-save` after each phase to checkpoint state.
   - **3c** REST endpoint `POST /onboarding/theme-builder-start` paralleling `rest_bootstrap_start`. Returns `{ session_id, kickoff_message, theme_builder_system_prompt }`.
   - **3d** UI: add a "Choose your start" step to `OnboardingWizard` with 3 buttons. New `OnboardingThemeBuilder` React component parallel to `OnboardingBootstrap`. Wire selection through the existing `bootstrap_system_prompt` channel.
   - **3e** E2E test: from a fresh install, complete the flow end-to-end, verify a theme exists at `wp-content/themes/<slug>/` and is the active stylesheet.

4. **Phase 4:** Topic-grounded aesthetics skill. Document the "explore visual worlds" thinking (brewery → 3 distinct authentic worlds, not generic style swaps). Reference from Phase 3's system prompt when generating design directions.

### Verification (parent task — phase children specify their own)

```bash
# Phase 1 lands
test -f includes/Models/skills/site-specification.md

# Phase 2 lands (skill expanded)
wc -l includes/Models/skills/block-themes.md  # should be 350-450 lines

# Phase 3 lands (E2E)
npm run test:e2e:playwright -- tests/e2e/onboarding-theme-builder.spec.js

# Phase 4 lands
test -f includes/Models/skills/design-system-aesthetics.md
```

### Files Scope

Parent task — phase children declare their own scopes. As an aggregate
guard, the following globs cover all phases:

- `includes/Models/skills/site-specification.md`
- `includes/Models/skills/block-themes.md`
- `includes/Models/skills/design-system-aesthetics.md`
- `includes/Core/ThemeBuilderPrompt.php`
- `includes/Core/OnboardingManager.php`
- `includes/Abilities/ScaffoldBlockThemeAbility.php`
- `includes/Abilities/ActivateThemeAbility.php`
- `src/components/onboarding-wizard.js`
- `src/components/onboarding-theme-builder.js`
- `src/components/__tests__/OnboardingThemeBuilder.test.js`
- `tests/e2e/onboarding-theme-builder.spec.js`
- `todo/PLANS.md`
- `todo/tasks/t170-brief.md`
- `todo/tasks/t170[a-z]-*.md`
- `TODO.md`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Phase 1 PR merged: `site-specification` skill markdown exists with all 7 site-type inference tables (SaaS, e-commerce, professional-services, restaurant, portfolio, blog, non-profit) and at least 3 worked examples (coffee shop, law firm, esports team).

  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: bash
    run: "test -f includes/Models/skills/site-specification.md && grep -c '^### ' includes/Models/skills/site-specification.md | xargs test 7 -le"
  ```

- [ ] Phase 2 PR merged: `block-themes.md` expanded with theme.json presets, animation classes, and editor-visibility CSS sections.

  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: codebase
    pattern: "Editor Visibility|editor-styles-wrapper|prefers-reduced-motion"
    path: "includes/Models/skills/block-themes.md"
  ```

- [ ] Phase 3 PR merged: theme-builder branch reachable from onboarding; activates a generated block theme on a fresh install.

  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: bash
    run: "test -f includes/Core/ThemeBuilderPrompt.php && test -f includes/Abilities/ScaffoldBlockThemeAbility.php && test -f includes/Abilities/ActivateThemeAbility.php"
  ```

- [ ] Phase 4 PR merged: `design-system-aesthetics.md` skill exists and is referenced from `ThemeBuilderPrompt`.

  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: codebase
    pattern: "design-system-aesthetics"
    path: "includes/Core/ThemeBuilderPrompt.php"
  ```

- [ ] No regression to existing discovery onboarding: the "Explore my existing site" branch continues to call `/onboarding/bootstrap-start` and behaves identically to today.

  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: codebase
    pattern: "bootstrap-start"
    path: "src/components/onboarding-bootstrap.js"
  ```

- [ ] Lint + tests clean on each phase PR: `npm run lint:js && npm run lint:php && npm run test:php`.

- [ ] No raw `wp-content/themes/` writes happen without `current_user_can('install_themes')` gating in the new abilities.

  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: codebase
    pattern: "current_user_can.*install_themes"
    path: "includes/Abilities/ScaffoldBlockThemeAbility.php"
  ```

## Context & Decisions

- **Adopt the architecture, not the code.** Automattic's plugin is a Claude Code plugin coupled to WordPress Studio CLI. We're a WP plugin running inside the install. We take the 4-phase flow, the skill structure, and the topic-grounded design thinking — we do *not* take the `.claude-plugin/` packaging, the `studio` CLI calls, the `block-fixer/cli.js` Node script (we have `validate-block-content`), or the parallel `Task()` subagent pattern (we run one model per `AgentLoop` iteration).
- **No stock image URLs ever.** Automattic's prompts repeat this rule; we should too. Generated themes use CSS gradients, color blocks, and typography for visual richness when the user hasn't provided their own images.
- **Phase boundary discipline.** Phases are independently shippable. If we ship only Phases 1–2 and stop, the site-specification skill still improves every other interaction. Phases 3–4 are where the theme-builder onboarding lights up.
- **Why not a full PRD?** The deliverable is well-scoped and adapts a known reference architecture. Phase briefs carry the detail; a separate PRD would duplicate this brief.

title: test: SkillTest::test_apply_update_skips_user_modified_builtin_skill fails — Skill::create ignores user_modified
body:
## Summary

`SdAiAgent\Tests\Models\SkillTest::test_apply_update_skips_user_modified_builtin_skill` (`tests/SdAiAgent/Models/SkillTest.php:330-351`) fails on `origin/main` (verified at commit 2fd9b34, branch `feat/t226a-site-spec-skill` pre-changes).

## Reproduction

```bash
vendor/bin/phpunit \
  --filter test_apply_update_skips_user_modified_builtin_skill \
  tests/SdAiAgent/Models/SkillTest.php
```

Result: `Failed asserting that true is false.` at line 346.

## Root cause

`Skill::create()` at `includes/Models/Skill.php:260` hard-codes `'user_modified' => 0` in the `$wpdb->insert()` payload, ignoring any `user_modified` value passed in `$data`:

```php
'user_modified' => 0,
```

The test's `create_skill( [ 'user_modified' => true ] )` therefore persists `user_modified=0`. `Skill::apply_update()` then sees `$skill->user_modified === false`, skips the guard at line 534, and proceeds with the update — returning `true` instead of the expected `false`.

## Fix options

1. Honour `user_modified` in `Skill::create()` (mirroring how `is_builtin` is handled at line 252) — preferred; the test contract already expects this and `update()` accepts the field.
2. Change the test to call `Skill::update($id, [ 'user_modified' => true ])` after creation. Less faithful to the original test intent.

## Verification

- `composer phpcs` clean on `includes/Models/Skill.php`.
- `composer phpstan` clean (199 files).
- After fix, the full `SkillTest` suite should be 55/55 passing (currently 54/55).

## Scope note

This failure is **not** caused by t226a (site-specification skill) work — t226a only adds a new entry to `Skill::BUILTIN_META` and does not touch `create()`, `apply_update()`, or this test. Filed as a separate defect.

## Description

Block theme generation in onboarding (Automattic wp-site-creator inspired)

## Plan: Purpose

Add a "Design a custom theme" branch to onboarding. After provider setup, fresh-install users can opt into a 4-phase agent conversation that interviews them about their site, presents 3 distinct topic-grounded design directions as HTML previews, and on selection generates a complete block theme (theme.json, style.css, functions.php, templates/, parts/) deployed to `wp-content/themes/<slug>/` and activated — all inside the existing chat UI.
Architecture adapted from [Automattic/wordpress-agent-skills/claude-code/wp-site-creator](https://github.com/Automattic/wordpress-agent-skills/tree/trunk/claude-code/wp-site-creator). We do NOT take their Claude-Code-plugin packaging, WordPress Studio CLI dependency, parallel Task() subagent pattern, or block-fixer Node script (we have `validate-block-content` already).
Closes the PLANS.md "AI site generation from prompt" P0 gap on the visual-container side (t060-t062 handle pages; this handles themes).

<details><summary>Plan: Context & Architecture</summary>


**Context**

**Source comparison.** Studied [Automattic's `/quick-build` command](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Automattic/wordpress-agent-skills/trunk/claude-code/wp-site-creator/commands/quick-build.md), [`/preview-designs`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Automattic/wordpress-agent-skills/trunk/claude-code/wp-site-creator/commands/preview-designs.md), and [site-specification SKILL](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Automattic/wordpress-agent-skills/trunk/claude-code/wp-site-creator/skills/site-specification/SKILL.md) against our `OnboardingManager` + `BootstrapPrompt` + `OnboardingWizard` + `OnboardingBootstrap`. Our existing flow is discovery-only: explores the site, presents 4 starter prompts. Their flow generates a complete theme. Fresh-install conversion is the opportunity.
**Capability gap.** We have most of what we need: `create-block-content`, `validate-block-content`, `list-block-templates`, `list-block-patterns`, `update-global-styles`, `get-theme-json`, and `FileAbilities` (writes anywhere under wp-content when `FILE_WRITE` cap is on). Missing: directory + theme.json scaffold ability and a switch_theme wrapper. That's two new abilities, both small.
**Why phases not one PR.** Phase 1 (site-spec skill) alone improves every content-creation interaction (post drafts, page builds, product descriptions). Phase 2 (block-themes skill expansion) compounds for all theme-aware work, not just onboarding. Phases 3-4 are where the theme-builder onboarding actually lights up. Each phase ships value independently — if we stop after Phase 2 we've still made the agent meaningfully better.
**What we explicitly are NOT doing:**
- Generating Gutenberg patterns library (separate work — t060-t062)
- WooCommerce-aware theme variants (Phase 3 ships a generic theme; Woo-specific templates are follow-up)
- Multi-language theme generation
- Child-theme generation
- AI-redesigning existing themes
- Adopting WordPress Studio CLI (irrelevant inside a running WP install)
- Telemetry scripts from the Automattic plugin
**Topic-grounded design thinking.** Their key insight: don't generate "modern dark theme / minimalist light theme / colorful theme" — instead, ask what aesthetic worlds the *topic* could authentically inhabit. A craft brewery is not "generic dark/light/colorful"; it's taproom-warmth vs label-art-maximalism vs industrial-grain-and-steel. This is what Phase 4's skill captures.
**No stock image URLs ever.** Their prompts repeat this rule; we adopt it. Generated themes rely on CSS gradients, color blocks, and typography when the user hasn't supplied imagery.

## Task Brief

# t226 — Block theme generation in onboarding (inspired by Automattic wp-site-creator)

> **ID note:** filed 2026-05-13 as t170, renumbered to t226 in this PR to avoid collision with a completed t170 ("Benchmark validation: ac-016 restaurant website end-to-end test", merged 2026-04-09 as PR #848). Phase children use the t226a–t226d suffix scheme to keep the parent-child relationship visible in TODO.md without colliding with adjacent numeric IDs (t227+ were already taken).

## Pre-flight

- [x] Memory recall: `wp-site-creator wordpress agent skills` → 0 hits — no prior lessons; new territory in this repo, recall confirmed fresh
- [x] Discovery pass: 0 open PRs and 0 in-flight commits touch `OnboardingManager.php`, `BootstrapPrompt.php`, `onboarding-wizard.js`, `onboarding-bootstrap.js`, or `block-themes.md` in last 48h (verified on branch `fix/orphan-tool-result-trim`)
- [x] File refs verified: 8 refs checked, all present at HEAD (`OnboardingManager.php:341-456`, `BootstrapPrompt.php`, `onboarding-bootstrap.js`, `onboarding-wizard.js:326-463`, `GeneratePluginAbility.php`, `BlockAbilities.php:217-246`, `GlobalStylesAbilities.php`, `block-themes.md`, `kadence-theme.md`)
- [x] Tier: `tier:thinking` — parent task with UX + system-prompt design decisions; phase children re-evaluate their own tier when filed
- [x] Seeded draft PR decision recorded: skipped — parent task, no implementation. Phase 1 child should be the first PR.

## Session origin

Filed 2026-05-13 after studying [Automattic/wordpress-agent-skills/claude-code/wp-site-creator](https://github.com/Automattic/wordpress-agent-skills/tree/trunk/claude-code/wp-site-creator)
and comparing it with our existing onboarding flow (`OnboardingManager`,
`BootstrapPrompt`, `OnboardingWizard`, `OnboardingBootstrap`). Their plugin
generates a complete WordPress block theme from a one-line description via a
4-phase agent flow. Our onboarding is purely discovery — we explore an
existing site and present starter prompts, but we never *create* a theme.
For a fresh-install user, having the agent design and activate a custom
block theme during onboarding would be a real differentiator (currently
only 10Web/ZipWP do this, and neither runs as a plugin you own).

## What

Add a "Design a custom theme" branch to onboarding that, after the user has
a working AI provider, can interview the user, present 3 distinct visual
design directions, and on selection generate a complete activated block
theme — all inside the existing chat UI, without leaving WordPress.

The deliverable is a working onboarding branch where:

1. After provider setup, the user is offered three onboarding modes:
   - **Explore my existing site** (current behaviour, default for non-empty installs)
   - **Design a custom theme** (new, default for fresh installs)
   - **Skip — just chat** (current behaviour)
2. The theme-builder branch runs a 4-phase conversation:
   - **Phase 1** Interview: extract a site spec (name, type, audience, tone, brand keywords, key sections, typography). Uses the new `site-specification` skill. #1376
   - **Phase 2** Present 3 topic-grounded design directions as HTML previews stored in `wp-content/uploads/sd-ai-agent/design-previews/<session>/design-{1,2,3}.html` and shown inline in chat. #1381
   - **Phase 3** User picks a direction (1, 2, 3, or "2 but darker"). Modifications fold back into the spec. #1385
   - **Phase 4** Generate the full block theme into `wp-content/themes/<slug>/` (theme.json, style.css, functions.php, parts/header.html, parts/footer.html, templates/index.html, templates/page.html) and activate it.
3. All theme files are validated via existing `sd-ai-agent/validate-block-content` before write.

We do **not** ship the Automattic plugin verbatim — it's a Claude Code
plugin, not a WordPress plugin, and depends on WordPress Studio CLI which
isn't relevant inside a running WP install. We adapt the *architecture*
(phases, skills, references) to our agent loop.

## Why

1. **Fresh-install conversion.** Right now a fresh-install user activates
   the plugin, sees an empty discovery summary, and gets generic starter
   prompts. They are not impressed and they bounce. A "design a theme for
   my SaaS in 5 minutes" flow is what 10Web and ZipWP use to convert.
2. **Showcases agent capability.** Generating a coherent block theme
   requires our agent to chain `create-block-content`, `validate-block-content`,
   `update-global-styles`, `list-block-patterns`, file writes, and theme
   activation — exactly the kind of multi-step tool-calling we built the
   loop for. It's a credible demo.
3. **PLANS.md gap closure.** PLANS.md identifies "AI site generation from
   prompt" as P0 (t060-t062 line) but those tasks are about generating
   *pages*, not themes. This complements them — themes are the visual
   container, pages are the content. Both are needed.
4. **Reusable skill scaffolding.** The `site-specification` skill alone
   improves every content-creation interaction (page builds, post drafts,
   product descriptions), not just onboarding.

## Tier

`tier:thinking` — parent/planning task. UX decisions, system-prompt design,
and integration sequencing are judgment work. The 4 phase children below
are individually `tier:standard` (skills + abilities + UI wiring with
clear file targets), but Phase 3 specifically may be `tier:thinking`.

## Phases

This is a parent task. Each phase is a separate PR.

- **Phase 1 — Site-specification skill** ~3h — add `includes/Models/skills/site-specification.md` mirroring Automattic's per-site-type inference tables. New memory category `site_brief` for storing extracted specs across sessions. No UI changes. [auto-fire:on-prior-merge] #1376
- **Phase 2 — Block-themes skill expansion** ~4h — expand `includes/Models/skills/block-themes.md` with theme.json patterns, template-part composition, animation/motion classes, and editor-visibility CSS lifted from Automattic's `wordpress-block-theming.md` reference (29KB → distil to ~400 lines, keep our existing 150-line structure as the spine). [auto-fire:on-prior-merge] #1381
- **Phase 3 — Theme-builder onboarding branch** ~12h — new `ThemeBuilderPrompt` (mirrors `BootstrapPrompt`), new REST endpoint `POST /onboarding/theme-builder-start`, choose-mode UI in `OnboardingWizard`, and two new abilities: `sd-ai-agent/scaffold-block-theme` (creates the directory + theme.json + style.css + functions.php) and `sd-ai-agent/activate-theme` (wraps `switch_theme()`). Existing `FileAbilities` handles HTML file writes. [auto-fire:on-prior-merge] #1385
- **Phase 4 — Design-system reference skills** ~5h — add `includes/Models/skills/design-system-aesthetics.md` covering the "topic-grounded visual worlds" framework (brewery → taproom vs label-art vs industrial), referenced by Phase 3's system prompt during the design-direction step.

Each phase PR uses `For #NNN` referencing the parent issue until Phase 4
ships, which uses `Closes #NNN`.

## How (Approach)

### Progressive Context Plan

- **Read first:** `src/components/onboarding-bootstrap.js` and `src/components/onboarding-wizard.js` — the React entry points the new branch plugs into.

### Implementation Steps (high-level — each phase brief will detail its own)

1. **Phase 1:** Read Automattic's `site-specification/SKILL.md` (already in this session's context), adapt to our skill markdown format (matches `block-themes.md` and `kadence-theme.md` style), wire the new memory category `site_brief` via `Memory::create()`. 2. **Phase 2:** Diff Automattic's `wordpress-block-theming.md` (29KB) against our `block-themes.md` (150 lines). Lift the theme.json color/typography presets, animation classes, prefers-reduced-motion patterns, and editor-styles-wrapper CSS guidance. Keep our existing tool references intact. Test: word count and section ratchet, plus a manual read-pass for accuracy.

3. **Phase 3:** Largest phase. Subphases:
   - **3a** New abilities: `ScaffoldBlockThemeAbility` + `ActivateThemeAbility`. Cap gates: `install_themes` and `switch_themes` respectively.
   - **3b** New `ThemeBuilderPrompt` class generating a 4-phase system instruction (interview → designs → choose → build). Use `sd-ai-agent/memory-save` after each phase to checkpoint state.
   - **3c** REST endpoint `POST /onboarding/theme-builder-start` paralleling `rest_bootstrap_start`. Returns `{ session_id, kickoff_message, theme_builder_system_prompt }`.
   - **3d** UI: add a "Choose your start" step to `OnboardingWizard` with 3 buttons. New `OnboardingThemeBuilder` React component parallel to `OnboardingBootstrap`. Wire selection through the existing `bootstrap_system_prompt` channel.
   - **3e** E2E test: from a fresh install, complete the flow end-to-end, verify a theme exists at `wp-content/themes/<slug>/` and is the active stylesheet.

4. **Phase 4:** Topic-grounded aesthetics skill. Document the "explore visual worlds" thinking (brewery → 3 distinct authentic worlds, not generic style swaps). Reference from Phase 3's system prompt when generating design directions.

- [ ] Phase 3 PR merged: theme-builder branch reachable from onboarding; activates a generated block theme on a fresh install.

  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: bash
    run: "test -f includes/Core/ThemeBuilderPrompt.php && test -f includes/Abilities/ScaffoldBlockThemeAbility.php && test -f includes/Abilities/ActivateThemeAbility.php"
  ```

  ```yaml

    method: codebase
    pattern: "current_user_can.*install_themes"
    path: "includes/Abilities/ScaffoldBlockThemeAbility.php"
  ```

- **Adopt the architecture, not the code.** Automattic's plugin is a Claude Code plugin coupled to WordPress Studio CLI. We're a WP plugin running inside the install. We take the 4-phase flow, the skill structure, and the topic-grounded design thinking — we do *not* take the `.claude-plugin/` packaging, the `studio` CLI calls, the `block-fixer/cli.js` Node script (we have `validate-block-content`), or the parallel `Task()` subagent pattern (we run one model per `AgentLoop` iteration).
- **No stock image URLs ever.** Automattic's prompts repeat this rule; we should too. Generated themes use CSS gradients, color blocks, and typography for visual richness when the user hasn't provided their own images.
- **Phase boundary discipline.** Phases are independently shippable. If we ship only Phases 1–2 and stop, the site-specification skill still improves every other interaction. Phases 3–4 are where the theme-builder onboarding lights up.
- **Why not a full PRD?** The deliverable is well-scoped and adapts a known reference architecture. Phase briefs carry the detail; a separate PRD would duplicate this brief.
- **Non-goals:**
  - Generating Gutenberg patterns library (covered separately by t060-t062 page-generation work).
  - WooCommerce-aware theme variants (Phase 3 generates a generic theme; WooCommerce-specific templates can be a follow-up).
  - Multi-language theme generation.
  - Child-theme generation.
  - Importing existing themes and "AI-redesigning" them.

title: Retry provider 5xx errors with exponential backoff up to 10 attempts and surface progress to user
body:
## Problem

When a provider (Anthropic, OpenAI, etc.) returns a 5xx error mid-loop, the agent loop terminates immediately, surfaces the raw `Error: Internal Server Error (500) - Internal server error` to the user, and discards the in-progress session state. The user has no way to recover except to start over.

This is especially painful for long multi-turn tool sessions because all the work done across previous successful turns is effectively wasted when a single transient upstream failure interrupts the loop.

## Evidence

Session 17 (`fix/orphan-tool-result-trim @ 2795aab`, 2026-05-13, Opus 4.7 landing-page prompt):

- 8 successful Anthropic API calls (`wp_sd_ai_agent_provider_trace` ids 136-144, all 200 OK)
- 9th call (trace id 145): `status_code=500`, `duration_ms=123537`, response body `{"type":"error","error":{"type":"api_error","message":"Internal server error"},"request_id":"req_011Cb1Fs3oC5QxrdwJNi7EBj"}`
- User saw `Error: Internal Server Error (500) - Internal server error` in chat
- Session row `wp_sd_ai_agent_sessions.id=17` stayed `active` with empty `messages = '[]'` — the partial work (9 tool cycles) was discarded
- Total cumulative time 297.6s — the 500 alone burned 123.5s before bubbling up

## Proposed Behaviour

When `send_prompt()` (and similar provider-call sites in `AgentLoop`) returns a 5xx HTTP status:

1. **Retry with exponential backoff up to 10 attempts**
   - Suggested schedule: 1s, 2s, 4s, 8s, 16s, 32s, 60s, 60s, 60s, 60s (cap at 60s to avoid runaway)
   - Reset retry counter after any successful response within the same loop iteration
   - Total worst-case wait: ~5 minutes — caller can configure shorter if needed
2. **Stream progress to the user**
   - Emit a progress event/message: `"Provider returned 500. Retrying in 4s (attempt 3/10)…"`
   - Surface via the existing `progress_callback` mechanism in `AgentLoop` (used by the job system) and through the chat UI's `tool_calls` stream
3. **Only after all retries fail**, surface the final error with a clear "Retry failed after 10 attempts over Xs — try resending your last message" message and **preserve `paused_state` so the user can resume** rather than starting over
4. **Distinguish retryable from non-retryable**
   - Retry: 500, 502, 503, 504, 408, 429 (with `Retry-After` honoured), network errors (timeout, connection reset)
   - Do not retry: 400, 401, 403, 404, 422 (real client/auth errors — bubble immediately)

## Files To Modify (likely)

- `includes/Core/AgentLoop.php`
  - `send_prompt()` is the central provider call site. Wrap the `$builder->generate_text_result()` call in a retry loop.
  - May need a new `RetryPolicy` service class to keep the loop body clean
- `includes/Core/ProviderTraceLogger.php`
  - Already captures 5xx into `wp_sd_ai_agent_provider_trace` — extend to tag retried attempts (`attempt_number` column?) so users/diagnostics can see how many retries happened
- `includes/REST/SessionController.php`
  - Job loop should treat "retrying upstream" as a non-terminal state so the polling endpoint surfaces the progress message instead of immediately failing the job
- Frontend (`src/components/chat/...`) — render retry progress events as a status banner inside the message stream rather than a full error

## Verification

- Add unit test in `tests/SdAiAgent/Core/` that mocks `generate_text_result()` to return 500 three times then 200; assert the loop ultimately succeeds and that 3 retry-attempt records exist
- Add unit test that returns 400; assert the loop terminates immediately without retry
- Add a manual test plan: trigger a real long landing-page run, kill Anthropic's connection mid-flight via `network route`, confirm retry banner appears and run completes

## Reference Pattern

`includes/Core/ProviderTraceLogger.php` already uses `pre_http_request`/`http_response` hooks to log every provider call. The retry policy can hook the same level (intercept before the error bubbles up to `generate_text_result()`'s caller), or sit one layer up inside `AgentLoop::send_prompt()`. The latter is preferred because it keeps the trace log as the raw transcript (one row per attempt) while the loop logic handles the recovery.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] 5xx errors from any provider retry up to 10 times with exponential backoff
- [ ] Each retry attempt is visible to the user in the chat UI (progress message)
- [ ] After exhausting retries, the user is shown a clear "retry failed" message and can resume the session without losing prior turns
- [ ] 4xx errors (except 408/429) are NOT retried and bubble immediately
- [ ] Provider trace table records each retry attempt as a separate row
- [ ] Unit tests cover retry-then-success, retry-exhausted, and no-retry-on-4xx paths

## Origin

Discovered while verifying the weak-model-overrides disable in PR series ending at `2795aab`. The Anthropic 500 happened during the verification test (session 17, 2026-05-13) and demonstrated the full impact: a 3-minute productive session lost to a single transient upstream blip with no recovery path.

title: AgentLoop: detect stop_reason=max_tokens on tool_use and surface explicit truncation error
body:
## Context

Follow-up to sd-ai-7rl (per-model `max_tokens` resolver, commit 025fbe9). The resolver fix raises the cap so the truncation that broke chat session 16 no longer happens at 4096 tokens. This issue addresses the *secondary* failure mode: when truncation **does** still occur (an unusually large tool-call input, a future smaller model, a custom-low user override, or a reasoning model consuming output budget on internal thinking), the agent loop currently reports it via a misleading error.

## Current behaviour

When Anthropic returns `stop_reason: max_tokens` with a `tool_use` block whose `input` JSON was cut off mid-object:

1. SDK parses the truncated `input` and surfaces it as `[]` or `{ability: "..."}` (the leading fragment that happened to be valid JSON before truncation).
2. AgentLoop dispatches the tool call.
3. Ability schema validator rejects with `arguments is a required property of input` (or similar — depends on which fragment survived).
4. Model sees an error pointing at *missing arguments*, not at *truncation*, and retries with the same payload-shape pattern.
5. Loop spins through every available alternative ability that needs a large input, all of which truncate the same way, until the per-session tool-call cap fires.

Evidence: `wp_sd_ai_agent_provider_trace` rows 124–130 in the session-16 trace, all `output_tokens` 4094-4096, all `stop_reason=max_tokens`, all rejected by the schema validator with misleading errors.

## Proposed behaviour

In `AgentLoop::execute_tool_calls()` (or wherever the SDK result is unwrapped into per-tool dispatch), check whether the just-returned `GenerativeAiResult` carries `stop_reason=max_tokens` (Anthropic) / `finish_reason=length` (OpenAI) / `finishReason=MAX_TOKENS` (Gemini). When it does *and* the message contains one or more `tool_use` blocks:

1. **Do not dispatch the truncated tool calls.** Their input JSON is unsafe.
2. **Inject a synthetic next-turn message**:
   > Your previous response was truncated because it hit the `max_tokens` cap (current cap: N). The tool call you started (`<name>`) was discarded because its input JSON was incomplete. Either split this work into smaller tool calls, reduce the payload size, or use a tool that accepts file/post references instead of inline content.
3. **Log the event** to the change-log/tool-call-log with reason `truncated_tool_call`.
4. **Optional**: increment a counter and after N consecutive truncations on the same ability, surface a user-facing message recommending they raise `max_output_tokens` in Settings → Model Parameters.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A test (unit or integration) feeds a synthetic provider response with `stop_reason=max_tokens` + a partial `tool_use` block and asserts:
  - the truncated tool is NOT dispatched
  - the next-turn prompt contains the synthetic guidance message
  - the loop continues (no premature termination)
- [ ] The provider-trace UI shows truncation events distinctly from validator-rejection events (separate badge / column / colour).
- [ ] If the model honours the guidance and emits smaller tool calls, the loop completes successfully without iteration-cap exhaustion.

## Out of scope

- Auto-retrying with a higher `max_tokens` (we already clamp at the per-model resolver value; raising further is a user decision).
- Splitting large arguments automatically — that would require ability-specific knowledge.

## References

- Root-cause analysis: chat session 16, model `claude-opus-4-7`, traces 124-130 (output_tokens=4094-4096, stop_reason=max_tokens).
- Primary fix shipped in commit 025fbe9 (per-model `MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS` resolver, default raised from 4096 to per-model 8K-32K).
- Files likely to touch: `includes/Core/AgentLoop.php` (loop dispatch), `includes/Core/ProviderTraceLogger.php` (trace categorisation), `tests/SdAiAgent/Core/AgentLoopTest.php` (new test).

title: feat: add Google Gemini explicit prompt-caching (cachedContents resource lifecycle)
body:
## Goal

Add explicit prompt-caching support for Google Gemini, complementing the multi-provider prompt-cache framework introduced in #1387.

## Background

PR #1387 introduced provider-aware prompt caching via `CacheStrategyResolver` keyed by URL host. It covers:

- Anthropic (explicit `cache_control` markers) — done.
- OpenAI / DeepSeek / xAI / Groq / Cerebras / Together / Fireworks (automatic server-side caching) — done.
- Telemetry extraction for Gemini's `usageMetadata.cachedContentTokenCount` — done (already in `CacheUsageExtractor::extract()` under `case 'google'`).

**What's still missing**: Gemini does not opt in via inline body markers. Its caching is a **separate resource lifecycle**:

1. `POST https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/cachedContents` with the content to cache, returning a `name` like `cachedContents/abc123`.
2. Subsequent `POST /v1beta/models/{model}:generateContent` calls reference the cache by `cachedContent: "cachedContents/abc123"` in the request body.
3. Cache resources have a TTL (default 1h) and must be refreshed or recreated when the underlying content changes.

This is fundamentally different from Anthropic's "stamp markers on the body" pattern, so it needs its own subsystem rather than another `CacheStrategyInterface` implementation.

## Design sketch

### New components

- `includes/Core/PromptCache/GeminiCacheManager.php`
  - `find_or_create(string $api_key, string $model, array $contents, array $tools, string $system): string|null`
  - Hashes the cacheable prefix (system + tools + stable context), looks up in a transient (`sd_ai_agent_gemini_cache_{hash}`), creates a new `cachedContents` resource if miss.
  - Stores `{name, expire_time, model, hash}` in transient with TTL ~= cache TTL minus 5 min safety margin.
  - On cache resource expiry (404 from generateContent), invalidates transient and retries once.
- `includes/Core/PromptCache/GeminiCacheStrategy.php` implements `CacheStrategyInterface`
  - `matches()` → host is `generativelanguage.googleapis.com` AND path contains `:generateContent` AND body has cacheable size.
  - `apply()` → calls `GeminiCacheManager::find_or_create()`, splices `cachedContent` into the request body, optionally strips the now-redundant `systemInstruction` / `tools` from the inline request.

### Constraints

- **Minimum cacheable size**: Gemini requires ≥32,768 tokens (~128KB) for caching to be cost-effective. Use a similar `MIN_CHARS_FOR_CACHE` constant tuned for Gemini.
- **API key handling**: the `cachedContents` POST needs the same API key as the `generateContent` call. Extract from `Authorization` header / query string of the inbound request.
- **Idempotency**: two concurrent requests with the same prefix must not race-create two cache resources. Use a short-lived lock (e.g. `wp_cache_add()` with `sd_ai_agent_gemini_cache_lock_{hash}`).
- **DI placement**: `GeminiCacheStrategy` registers into `CacheStrategyResolver` via the constructor's default strategy list (same wiring as `AnthropicCacheStrategy`).

### Telemetry

Telemetry is already wired — `CacheUsageExtractor` reads `usageMetadata.cachedContentTokenCount` for `provider_id = 'google'`. The new strategy will populate cache_read_tokens automatically once Gemini reports cache hits in the response.

Cache_creation_tokens will remain 0 for Gemini because Gemini bills the cache-creation `POST` separately from the inference call — we'd need to also surface that out-of-band cost. **Out of scope for v1**; file as a sub-followup if needed.

## Acceptance criteria

- New Gemini conversation with ≥32k cacheable tokens shows `cache_read_tokens > 0` on turn 2+ in `wp_sd_ai_agent_provider_trace`.
- `cachedContents` resources are reused across turns within the same conversation (verify via Gemini's cached content list endpoint).
- Cache lifecycle test: TTL expiry triggers transparent re-creation without surfacing the 404 to the caller.
- Setting `prompt_caching_enabled = false` skips Gemini caching entirely (consistent with Anthropic behaviour).
- Unit tests for `GeminiCacheManager` (hit, miss, expired, race-condition).
- Unit tests for `GeminiCacheStrategy` (body mutation, system/tools stripping, min-size gate).

## Files to read first

- `includes/Core/PromptCache/CacheStrategyResolver.php` — strategy registration
- `includes/Core/PromptCache/AnthropicCacheStrategy.php` — reference implementation for body mutation
- `includes/Core/PromptCache/CacheUsageExtractor.php` (lines 84–88) — Gemini telemetry already wired
- `includes/Bootstrap/HttpTraceHandler.php` — filter wiring point

## References

- Gemini API caching docs: https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/caching
- PR #1387 for the strategy pattern this extends.

## Priority

P2 — significant cost win for Gemini users with large context, but Gemini is not the primary provider today. Not blocking #1387 release.

title: feat: extend prompt-cache host coverage (Azure OpenAI, OpenRouter, Vertex Anthropic)
body:
## Goal

Extend `CacheStrategyResolver` to recognise additional LLM endpoint hosts so prompt-cache strategies and telemetry apply correctly for Azure OpenAI, OpenRouter, and Vertex AI (Anthropic on GCP).

## Background

PR #1387 introduced the prompt-caching framework with a fixed list of auto-cache hosts:

```
api.openai.com, api.deepseek.com, api.x.ai, api.groq.com,
api.cerebras.ai, api.together.xyz, api.fireworks.ai
```

And one explicit-marker strategy for `api.anthropic.com`.

The default fallback in `CacheUsageExtractor` already reads OpenAI-shape `prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens` for unknown providers, so **telemetry already works** for OpenAI-compatible endpoints. What's missing is:

1. The resolver doesn't recognise these hosts → no explicit `NoopCacheStrategy` registered → trace logger doesn't classify them as cacheable LLM endpoints (cosmetic at the moment, but affects future logic that gates on `resolve()` returning non-null).
2. Vertex Anthropic uses the Anthropic wire format but on a Google-hosted URL → `AnthropicCacheStrategy` doesn't match → no `cache_control` markers injected → no cache benefit.

## Hosts to add

### Auto-cache hosts (extend `AUTO_CACHE_HOSTS`)

| Host pattern | Provider | Cache shape |
|---|---|---|
| `*.openai.azure.com` | Azure OpenAI Service | OpenAI shape (auto, ≥1024 tok) |
| `openrouter.ai` | OpenRouter (pass-through aggregator) | Depends on routed model; OpenAI shape from OpenRouter's response |

The current `is_auto_cache_host()` already supports subdomain matching via `str_ends_with($host, '.' . $known)`, so adding `openai.azure.com` is sufficient for the Azure case.

### Anthropic-on-Vertex (extend `AnthropicCacheStrategy::matches()`)

| URL pattern | Notes |
|---|---|
| `https://{region}-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/{project}/locations/{region}/publishers/anthropic/models/{model}:rawPredict` | Vertex AI's Anthropic endpoint accepts the standard Anthropic request body and respects `cache_control` markers. |
| `https://{region}-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/{project}/locations/{region}/publishers/anthropic/models/{model}:streamRawPredict` | Streaming variant. |

`AnthropicCacheStrategy::matches()` should accept either:

- host `api.anthropic.com`, OR
- host ending in `-aiplatform.googleapis.com` AND path containing `/publishers/anthropic/models/`.

The body mutation logic is unchanged because Vertex relays the Anthropic body verbatim.

### Bedrock (out of scope — see "Non-goals")

AWS Bedrock requires SigV4-signed requests and a different `cachePoint` block structure for Claude. File a separate issue if/when we have Bedrock users.

## Acceptance criteria

- `CacheStrategyResolverTest` extended with cases for:
  - `https://my-resource.openai.azure.com/openai/deployments/gpt-4o/chat/completions?api-version=...` → resolves to `NoopCacheStrategy`.
  - `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/chat/completions` → resolves to `NoopCacheStrategy`.
  - `https://us-central1-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/p/locations/us-central1/publishers/anthropic/models/claude-3-5-sonnet:rawPredict` → resolves to `AnthropicCacheStrategy`.
  - `https://my-resource.openai.azure.com/.../embeddings` → still resolves to `NoopCacheStrategy` (not LLM-only, but harmless because noop is a pass-through).
- `AnthropicCacheStrategyTest` extended with one Vertex-URL case to confirm body mutation works at the Vertex endpoint.
- No change to existing tests (additive).

## Files to modify

- `includes/Core/PromptCache/CacheStrategyResolver.php` — extend `AUTO_CACHE_HOSTS`.
- `includes/Core/PromptCache/AnthropicCacheStrategy.php` — extend `matches()` URL predicate.
- `tests/SdAiAgent/Core/PromptCache/CacheStrategyResolverTest.php` — new cases.
- `tests/SdAiAgent/Core/PromptCache/AnthropicCacheStrategyTest.php` — Vertex URL case.

## Non-goals

- AWS Bedrock support (different signing + different cache shape — separate issue).
- Custom OpenAI-compatible gateways behind unknown hostnames (already handled via the `sd_ai_agent_resolve_cache_strategy` filter hook for operators who need it).

## Priority

P3 — telemetry already works via the default OpenAI-shape fallback, and Vertex Anthropic users are rare. Worth shipping as a small follow-up but not blocking.

title: fix: admin asset URLs malformed when plugin loaded via symlink (plugin_dir_url returns realpath)
body:
## Summary

Admin asset URLs are malformed when the plugin is loaded via a symlink in `wp-content/plugins/`. WordPress core's `plugin_dir_url(__FILE__)` resolves the symlink and returns an absolute filesystem path appended to `/wp-content/plugins/`, which produces 404s for every admin asset and prevents the React chat UI from mounting.

## Repro

1. Check out the repo at `~/Git/superdav-ai-agent`.
2. Symlink it: `ln -s ~/Git/superdav-ai-agent ~/Git/wordpress/wp-content/plugins/superdav-ai-agent`.
3. Activate the plugin.
4. Visit `/wp-admin/admin.php?page=sd-ai-agent`.

Browser DevTools → Network shows requests to:
```
/wp-content/plugins/home/dave/Git/superdav-ai-agent/build/admin-page.js
/wp-content/plugins/home/dave/Git/superdav-ai-agent/build/unified-admin.js
```

These 404. `#sdaa-root` stays empty; chat panel never mounts.

## Root cause

`superdav-ai-agent.php:25`:

```php
define( 'SD_AI_AGENT_URL', plugin_dir_url( __FILE__ ) );
```

When the plugin's main file is a symlink, `__FILE__` is the realpath. WP core's `plugins_url()` checks whether the path lives under `WP_PLUGIN_DIR` — for a symlinked plugin it does not, so it falls through to a relative-path computation that produces the malformed URL.

WordPress provides `wp_register_plugin_realpath()` precisely for this case. Plugins that call it at the top of their main file work correctly under symlinks.

## Suggested fix

In `superdav-ai-agent.php`, add a single line before the URL constant is defined:

```php
// Allow the plugin to load from a symlinked path (dev installs and some
// shared-host configs). Without this, plugin_dir_url() returns the
// realpath-joined directory and admin asset URLs 404.
wp_register_plugin_realpath( __FILE__ );

define( 'SD_AI_AGENT_URL', plugin_dir_url( __FILE__ ) );
```

This is the standard WordPress idiom. Zero risk: the function is a no-op for plugins not loaded via symlink.

## Why now

Surfaced while doing a real-browser test of the merged t226c-3a theme-builder abilities (PR #1392 + PR #1395). The abilities themselves work; the chat UI used to drive them in a browser fails to mount on the standard dev workflow described in `AGENTS.md` ("This plugin: symlinked into `../wordpress/wp-content/plugins/$(basename $PWD)`").

## Scope

- Files: `superdav-ai-agent.php` (1 line added).
- No canonical-naming changes.
- No behavioural change for non-symlinked installs.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `wp_register_plugin_realpath( __FILE__ )` added before `SD_AI_AGENT_URL` definition.
- [ ] Browser-loaded admin script src for `admin-page.js` resolves to `/wp-content/plugins/superdav-ai-agent/build/admin-page.js` (matching the symlink basename, not the realpath).
- [ ] `#sdaa-root` mounts the React chat panel on `/wp-admin/admin.php?page=sd-ai-agent`.
