title: feat(t226c-3b): seed theme-builder built-in agent (Phase 3 of #1373)
body:
**Task ID:** `t226c-3b` | **Parent:** #1373 | **Phase:** 3, subphase 3b of 5 | **Tier:** `tier:standard` | **Estimate:** ~3h

## Pre-flight

- [x] Memory recall: queried `theme builder onboarding prompt agent slug` — 0 hits, fresh territory.
- [x] Discovery pass: parent #1373 plan said this subphase needs a new `ThemeBuilderPrompt.php` class; PR #1392 body documented that the parent plan was wrong about that. Confirmed in `includes/Core/OnboardingManager.php:285-336` (`rest_bootstrap_start`) — the bootstrap flow does **not** use a standalone prompt class. It resolves `Agent::get_by_slug( Agent::ONBOARDING_AGENT_SLUG )` and uses the agent's stored `system_prompt`. **Mirror that pattern**.
- [x] File refs verified at HEAD `b0adf0b`:
  - `includes/Models/Agent.php:33` `DEFAULT_AGENT_SLUG = 'general'`
  - `includes/Models/Agent.php:38` `ONBOARDING_AGENT_SLUG = 'onboarding'`
  - `includes/Models/Agent.php:491` `get_builtin_definitions()`
  - `includes/Models/Agent.php:409` `seed_defaults()` — idempotent skip if slug exists
  - `includes/Models/Agent.php:429` `reset_defaults()` — overwrites name/description/system_prompt/greeting/tier_1_tools/suggestions/avatar_icon
  - `includes/Abilities/ScaffoldBlockThemeAbility.php` and `includes/Abilities/ActivateThemeAbility.php` — abilities shipped by PR #1392 + #1395 that this agent must call.
- [x] Tier: `tier:standard` — concrete pattern to follow, no UX decision; system-prompt drafting is the only judgement work and the parent #1373 specifies the 4-phase flow.

## What

Add a new built-in **Theme Builder** agent (slug `theme-builder`) seeded by `Agent::seed_defaults()` exactly like the `onboarding` agent. Its stored `system_prompt` encodes the 4-phase theme-builder flow described in #1373:

1. **Interview** — extract a site spec using the `site-specification` skill (already shipped: `includes/Models/skills/site-specification.md`).
2. **Designs** — propose 3 topic-grounded design directions as HTML previews under `wp-content/uploads/sd-ai-agent/design-previews/<session>/design-{1,2,3}.html` (writes via existing `sd-ai-agent/file-write`).
3. **Choose** — user picks a direction (or modifies one); modifications fold into the spec.
4. **Build** — chain `sd-ai-agent/scaffold-block-theme` → write `parts/header.html`, `parts/footer.html`, `templates/index.html`, `templates/page.html` via `sd-ai-agent/file-write` → `sd-ai-agent/activate-theme`.

The agent's `tier_1_tools` must list at minimum: `sd-ai-agent/scaffold-block-theme`, `sd-ai-agent/activate-theme`, `sd-ai-agent/file-write`, `sd-ai-agent/memory-save`, `sd-ai-agent/skill-load`, `sd-ai-agent/validate-block-content`, `sd-ai-agent/get-theme-json`, `sd-ai-agent/update-global-styles`. Tools `ability-search`/`ability-call` are appended automatically by `ToolDiscovery`.

No new PHP class is added. No new REST routes. No UI changes.

## Why

Subphase 3a shipped the abilities the rest of Phase 3 depends on (PR #1392, #1395, #1397). 3b is the smallest next step — once a `theme-builder` agent exists, an interactive user can already chat with it via the existing chat UI by selecting it from the agent dropdown, and the next subphases (3c REST endpoint + 3d UI mode-picker) become straightforward wiring.

## Files to Modify

- **EDIT:** `includes/Models/Agent.php`
  - Add `public const THEME_BUILDER_AGENT_SLUG = 'theme-builder';` next to existing slug constants (lines 33, 38).
  - Append a new entry to `get_builtin_definitions()` (line 491) following the structure of the existing `onboarding` definition (line ~517) and the `general` definition (line ~604). Include `slug`, `name`, `description`, `system_prompt` (the 4-phase prompt — see Implementation Steps below), `greeting`, `tier_1_tools`, `suggestions`, `avatar_icon`.
- **NEW:** `tests/SdAiAgent/Models/AgentThemeBuilderTest.php`
  - Tests: `seed_defaults` creates the theme-builder agent on a fresh install; `seed_defaults` is idempotent (no duplicate); `reset_defaults` restores the canonical `system_prompt`, `greeting`, `tier_1_tools` after they were edited; agent row contains the four theme-builder abilities in `tier_1_tools`.

## Implementation Steps

1. **Add constant + builtin definition.** Mirror the `onboarding` slug constant and its definition in `get_builtin_definitions()`. Use the same structure (associative array keyed by slug). The `system_prompt` should:
   - Reference the existing skills by name: `site-specification`, `block-themes`, `design-system-aesthetics` (the last is Phase 4 — gracefully degrade when the skill is absent; do **not** require it).
   - Tell the agent to call `sd-ai-agent/skill-load` for `site-specification` at the start.
   - Specify the 4-phase contract verbatim from #1373.
   - Explicitly forbid stock-image URLs (per the parent plan rule).
   - Direct the agent to memo-save the chosen design direction with `sd-ai-agent/memory-save` (category `site_brief`).
2. **Set tier_1_tools** as listed under "What" above. Use the same string-array shape as other builtin definitions.
3. **suggestions** — three short starter prompts: "Design a theme for a craft brewery", "Design a theme for a SaaS startup", "Design a theme for a personal portfolio".
4. **avatar_icon** — pick a Dashicons or emoji consistent with the existing builtin agents (e.g. the SEO agent uses a magnifier; the e-commerce agent uses a cart; the theme builder can use `dashicons-art` or similar).
5. **Tests** — file `tests/SdAiAgent/Models/AgentThemeBuilderTest.php`. Pattern after any existing test in `tests/SdAiAgent/` that exercises `Agent::seed_defaults` / `Agent::get_by_slug`. The tests are unit-level — no WP database fixtures beyond what `WP_UnitTestCase` already provides.

## Verification

```bash
composer phpcs -- includes/Models/Agent.php tests/SdAiAgent/Models/AgentThemeBuilderTest.php
composer phpstan
npm run test:php -- --filter AgentThemeBuilderTest
```

Manual smoke (worker dev environment is not required to perform this — CI is sufficient):

```bash
wp eval '
\SdAiAgent\Models\Database::install();
$a = \SdAiAgent\Models\Agent::get_by_slug( \SdAiAgent\Models\Agent::THEME_BUILDER_AGENT_SLUG );
echo $a ? "OK slug={$a->slug} tools=".count( json_decode( $a->tier_1_tools, true ) )."\n" : "MISSING\n";
'
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `Agent::THEME_BUILDER_AGENT_SLUG` constant defined with value `'theme-builder'`.
- [ ] `get_builtin_definitions()` includes an entry for the new slug with all 8 required fields populated.
- [ ] `Agent::seed_defaults()` creates the theme-builder agent on a fresh install and is idempotent on re-run.
- [ ] `Agent::reset_defaults()` restores the canonical fields when the agent has been edited.
- [ ] `tier_1_tools` includes the four core theme abilities (`scaffold-block-theme`, `activate-theme`, `file-write`, `validate-block-content`) plus `skill-load`, `memory-save`, `get-theme-json`, `update-global-styles`.
- [ ] System prompt explicitly references skills `site-specification` and `block-themes`, the 4-phase contract, and the no-stock-images rule.
- [ ] No new PHP classes, no new REST routes, no JS changes.
- [ ] `composer phpcs` / `composer phpstan` / `npm run test:php` all pass on the changed surface.

## Scope guard — DO NOT do any of the following in this PR

- Do **not** create a `ThemeBuilderPrompt.php` class. The parent plan was wrong about that; we mirror the `onboarding` agent pattern.
- Do **not** add a REST endpoint (that is subphase 3c, separate PR).
- Do **not** modify any React component (that is subphase 3d, separate PR).
- Do **not** rename any canonical identifier (`sd-ai-agent/`, `SdAiAgent\\`, `SD_AI_AGENT_`, `superdav-ai-agent` text domain).

title: feat(t226c-3c): /onboarding/theme-builder-start REST endpoint (Phase 3 of #1373)
body:
**Task ID:** `t226c-3c` | **Parent:** #1373 | **Phase:** 3, subphase 3c of 5 | **Tier:** `tier:standard` | **Estimate:** ~2h | **Depends on:** #1385 / `t226c-3b` (theme-builder agent must exist).

## Pre-flight

- [x] Discovery pass: 0 open PRs / 0 in-flight commits touch `includes/Core/OnboardingManager.php` on `main` (checked at HEAD `b0adf0b` 2026-05-13).
- [x] File refs verified at HEAD `b0adf0b`:
  - `includes/Core/OnboardingManager.php:189-280` — `register_rest_routes()` registers `/onboarding/status` and `/onboarding/bootstrap-start`.
  - `includes/Core/OnboardingManager.php:285-360` — `rest_bootstrap_start()` callback to mirror.
  - `includes/Core/OnboardingManager.php:48` — `BOOTSTRAP_SESSION_OPTION` constant; this PR adds a parallel `THEME_BUILDER_SESSION_OPTION`.
  - `includes/Models/Agent.php:38` `ONBOARDING_AGENT_SLUG`; will be joined by `THEME_BUILDER_AGENT_SLUG` from #t226c-3b.
- [x] Tier: `tier:standard` — clear pattern to mirror; no design decisions.
- [x] Blocker: this PR depends on subphase 3b shipping the `theme-builder` builtin agent. CI on this PR fails until 3b is on `main`. Rebase after 3b merges.

## What

Add a new REST endpoint `POST /sd-ai-agent/v1/onboarding/theme-builder-start` that mirrors the existing `rest_bootstrap_start`. The endpoint:

1. Creates a new session.
2. Resolves the theme-builder agent via `Agent::get_by_slug( Agent::THEME_BUILDER_AGENT_SLUG )`.
3. Persists the session id under a new `sd_ai_agent_theme_builder_session_id` option so repeat calls return the same session.
4. Returns `{ success, session_id, agent_id, kickoff_message }` in the same JSON shape as `bootstrap-start`.
5. Does **not** mark onboarding complete (this branch is opt-in — the user may still want the bootstrap discovery flow after the theme is built).

No UI changes, no new abilities, no system-prompt changes.

## Why

3b ships the agent. 3d (UI) wires a mode-picker that has to hit either `/onboarding/bootstrap-start` (discovery branch) or `/onboarding/theme-builder-start` (theme-build branch). The frontend cannot dispatch the theme-builder branch without this endpoint.

## Files to Modify

- **EDIT:** `includes/Core/OnboardingManager.php`
  - Add `const THEME_BUILDER_SESSION_OPTION = 'sd_ai_agent_theme_builder_session_id';` next to `BOOTSTRAP_SESSION_OPTION` (line 48 area).
  - Register the new route in `register_rest_routes()` (line 189): same `permission_callback`, same `args` shape, callback `[ __CLASS__, 'rest_theme_builder_start' ]`.
  - Add a new static method `rest_theme_builder_start(): \WP_REST_Response|\WP_Error` modelled on `rest_bootstrap_start` (line 285). Differences from the bootstrap callback:
    - Resolve `Agent::get_by_slug( Agent::THEME_BUILDER_AGENT_SLUG )` instead of `ONBOARDING_AGENT_SLUG`.
    - Use a different kickoff message: `__( "I'd like to design a custom block theme for my site. Please start the interview.", 'superdav-ai-agent' )`.
    - **Do NOT** mark onboarding complete (omit `self::mark_complete()` and `$settings->update( [ 'onboarding_complete' => true ] )` — the user may still want bootstrap discovery after).
    - **Do NOT** auto-detect WooCommerce (the bootstrap flow does this; the theme-builder flow doesn't need it).
    - Use `THEME_BUILDER_SESSION_OPTION` for persistence (not `BOOTSTRAP_SESSION_OPTION`).
    - Return shape identical to `bootstrap-start` so the React entry component (subphase 3d) can use a single helper.
- **NEW:** `tests/SdAiAgent/Core/OnboardingManagerThemeBuilderTest.php`
  - Tests:
    - Endpoint registered (`rest_get_server()->get_routes()` contains `/sd-ai-agent/v1/onboarding/theme-builder-start`).
    - First POST creates a session and returns its id + agent_id + kickoff_message.
    - Repeat POST returns the same session id (option persistence is idempotent).
    - `permission_callback` rejects unauthenticated requests (HTTP 401).
    - Endpoint does **not** flip `onboarding_complete` in Settings or set `COMPLETE_OPTION`.

## Implementation Steps

1. Copy-edit `rest_bootstrap_start` as a starting point; delete the WooCommerce auto-detect block, the `mark_complete()` call, and the Settings `onboarding_complete` write.
2. Swap the agent slug and the session-option name throughout.
3. Use the same `register_rest_route` `args` and `permission_callback` patterns as the existing `/onboarding/bootstrap-start` line 210-220.
4. Keep the kickoff message i18n-wrapped with the `superdav-ai-agent` text domain.
5. Add tests that exercise both success paths (first call + repeat call) and the permission path. Use `WP_UnitTestCase`'s `wp_set_current_user` and `rest_get_server()->dispatch( new \WP_REST_Request(...) )` pattern — see other REST controller tests in `tests/SdAiAgent/REST/` for examples.

## Verification

```bash
composer phpcs -- includes/Core/OnboardingManager.php tests/SdAiAgent/Core/OnboardingManagerThemeBuilderTest.php
composer phpstan
npm run test:php -- --filter OnboardingManagerThemeBuilderTest
```

Manual smoke (after 3b is merged):

```bash
wp eval '
\SdAiAgent\Models\Database::install();
$req = new \WP_REST_Request( "POST", "/sd-ai-agent/v1/onboarding/theme-builder-start" );
wp_set_current_user( 1 );
$response = rest_get_server()->dispatch( $req );
echo "STATUS: ".$response->get_status()."\n";
echo "BODY: ".wp_json_encode( $response->get_data() )."\n";
'
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Route `/sd-ai-agent/v1/onboarding/theme-builder-start` is registered with method `POST`.
- [ ] Callback returns `{ success: true, session_id: int, agent_id: int, kickoff_message: string }` on first invocation.
- [ ] Repeat invocations return the same `session_id` without creating a new row.
- [ ] `onboarding_complete` is **not** flipped by this endpoint.
- [ ] WooCommerce detection is **not** triggered by this endpoint.
- [ ] Unauthenticated request returns HTTP 401.
- [ ] Tests pass under `npm run test:php`.
- [ ] No JS changes, no other PHP classes touched beyond `OnboardingManager.php`.

## Scope guard

- Do **not** rename any canonical identifier.
- Do **not** edit `bootstrap-start` behaviour (out of scope; if you find a bug there, file a separate issue).
- Do **not** add UI / React work — that is subphase 3d.

title: feat(t226c-3d): onboarding mode-picker + OnboardingThemeBuilder component (Phase 3 of #1373)
body:
**Task ID:** `t226c-3d` | **Parent:** #1373 | **Phase:** 3, subphase 3d of 5 | **Tier:** `tier:thinking` | **Estimate:** ~4h | **Depends on:** #1385 / `t226c-3b` and `t226c-3c`.

## Pre-flight

- [x] Discovery pass: 0 open PRs / 0 in-flight commits touch `src/components/onboarding-wizard.js` or `src/components/onboarding-bootstrap.js` on `main` (checked at HEAD `b0adf0b` 2026-05-13).
- [x] File refs verified at HEAD `b0adf0b`:
  - `src/components/onboarding-wizard.js:111` `const [ step, setStep ] = useState( 0 );`
  - `src/components/onboarding-wizard.js:326` `const steps = [ ... ]` — the array to extend with a new mode-picker step.
  - `src/components/onboarding-wizard.js:488-510` — Back / Next button handlers.
  - `src/components/onboarding-bootstrap.js` (77 lines) — exemplar component to mirror for `onboarding-theme-builder.js`. Note: its `useEffect` posts to `/sd-ai-agent/v1/onboarding/bootstrap-start`, sets `agent_id`, opens the returned session, and auto-sends the kickoff message.
- [x] Tier: `tier:thinking` — there is one judgement call on **where** to surface the mode picker in the existing wizard flow (after provider setup, before abilities? as the last step? a parallel branch?). See Implementation Steps for the recommended placement and the reasoning.

## What

Wire a "choose your start" mode-picker into the existing `OnboardingWizard`, and ship a new React entry component `OnboardingThemeBuilder` paralleling `OnboardingBootstrap` that bootstraps the theme-builder session by hitting `/sd-ai-agent/v1/onboarding/theme-builder-start` (delivered by `t226c-3c`).

Three onboarding modes per #1373:

1. **Explore my existing site** — existing bootstrap flow (default for non-empty installs).
2. **Design a custom theme** — new theme-builder flow (default for fresh installs).
3. **Skip — just chat** — existing skip flow.

## Why

3b shipped the agent and 3c shipped the REST endpoint. Without the UI mode-picker, a non-power-user can't reach the theme-builder branch. This PR is the moment Phase 3 becomes visible to end users.

## Files to Modify

- **NEW:** `src/components/onboarding-theme-builder.js`
  - Parallel to `onboarding-bootstrap.js` but posts to `/sd-ai-agent/v1/onboarding/theme-builder-start`. Same `useRef` double-invocation guard, same `openSession`/`sendMessage`/`setSelectedAgentId` store dispatchers, same `ChatRedesign` render.
- **EDIT:** `src/components/onboarding-wizard.js`
  - Add a new "Choose your start" step to the `steps` array. Recommended placement: **after the Provider setup step but before the Abilities overview step** (so the user only sees the picker once a provider is configured). The picker shows three primary buttons; on click it stores the chosen mode in a new local state slot (e.g. `useState< 'explore' | 'theme-builder' | 'skip' >`) and proceeds.
  - Default selection logic:
    - If `wp_count_posts()` data (already fetched by other onboarding code, or fetch fresh via `/sd-ai-agent/v1/onboarding/status`) shows the site has any published posts/pages, default to `'explore'`.
    - Otherwise default to `'theme-builder'`.
  - Persist the selection so the subsequent mount of `OnboardingBootstrap` or `OnboardingThemeBuilder` knows which path to take. Recommended: pass the selection up via the same mechanism the rest of the wizard uses to finish onboarding (store action or top-level state in the wrapper component that decides which of the two onboarding components to mount).
- **EDIT:** `src/index.js` or wherever the bootstrap mount currently lives — mount `OnboardingThemeBuilder` when the persisted mode is `'theme-builder'`, mount `OnboardingBootstrap` for `'explore'`, mount the plain `ChatRedesign` for `'skip'`. (Confirm the exact wrapper file by searching for `OnboardingBootstrap` usage; the worker should not guess.)
- **EDIT:** `package.json` — no entry-point changes needed if `onboarding-theme-builder.js` is imported by the existing wrapper rather than registered as a separate webpack entry. **Worker decision point:** if the existing wrapper imports `OnboardingBootstrap` directly, you import `OnboardingThemeBuilder` alongside it — no webpack config change. If `onboarding-bootstrap` is a separate entry in `webpack.config.js`, add `onboarding-theme-builder` as a parallel entry. Document the choice in the PR body.
- **NEW:** `src/components/__tests__/OnboardingThemeBuilder.test.js`
  - Jest tests for the new component: renders, calls `apiFetch` with the correct path, dispatches `setSelectedAgentId` / `openSession` / `sendMessage` after a successful response, no-op on missing `session_id`, double-mount guard works.
- **EDIT:** `src/components/onboarding-wizard.js` — add a Jest test in the existing wizard test file (if one exists) for the new mode-picker step: shows three buttons, default selection follows the count-posts rule, clicking a button advances to the next step.

## Implementation Steps

1. **Component first.** Write `onboarding-theme-builder.js`. Run the Jest tests in isolation.
2. **Wrapper switch.** Locate the wrapper that mounts `OnboardingBootstrap` today (`rg -n "OnboardingBootstrap" src/`). Add a branch for the persisted mode and mount the right component.
3. **Wizard step.** Add the new step to `steps[]` at index ~2 (after Provider setup, before Abilities overview). Render three `Button` components (use `@wordpress/components`). On click, store the choice in the wrapper state (or via `useDispatch(STORE_NAME)`).
4. **Defaults.** Probe site posts via the existing `/onboarding/status` response if it carries that signal; otherwise call `/wp/v2/posts?per_page=1&status=publish` via `apiFetch` once on step mount and pick the default.
5. **i18n.** Every visible string wrapped in `__( ..., 'superdav-ai-agent' )` — text domain `superdav-ai-agent` (not `sd-ai-agent`).
6. **CSS.** New class names must be prefixed `sd-ai-agent-` (e.g. `sd-ai-agent-onboarding-mode-picker`, `sd-ai-agent-onboarding-mode-picker__button`). Add styles in the same directory as the component or as part of `style.css` per the existing pattern.

## Verification

```bash
npm run lint:js
npm run lint:css
npm run test:js -- --testPathPattern OnboardingThemeBuilder
npm run build
```

Manual E2E sanity (worker dev env not required; CI Playwright covers this if 3e is in flight, otherwise local smoke is informational):

```bash
# After build, in browser at /wp-admin/admin.php?page=sd-ai-agent
# with provider configured and onboarding_complete=false:
#   - mode-picker visible after provider step
#   - "Design a custom theme" selected by default on a fresh install
#   - clicking it advances to a screen that mounts OnboardingThemeBuilder
#   - network shows POST /sd-ai-agent/v1/onboarding/theme-builder-start
#   - chat panel auto-loads the theme-builder agent with its greeting
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `OnboardingThemeBuilder` component exists at `src/components/onboarding-theme-builder.js`, mirrors `OnboardingBootstrap` structure, posts to `/sd-ai-agent/v1/onboarding/theme-builder-start`.
- [ ] `OnboardingWizard` has a new "Choose your start" step inserted after Provider setup with three buttons (Explore / Design / Skip).
- [ ] Default selection rule:
  - non-empty install → "Explore" pre-selected
  - empty install → "Design a custom theme" pre-selected
- [ ] Wrapper component mounts the correct onboarding entry component based on the chosen mode (`OnboardingBootstrap` / `OnboardingThemeBuilder` / `ChatRedesign`).
- [ ] All new CSS class names prefixed `sd-ai-agent-`.
- [ ] All visible strings i18n-wrapped with text domain `superdav-ai-agent`.
- [ ] `npm run lint:js`, `npm run lint:css`, `npm run test:js` all pass.
- [ ] `npm run build` succeeds without bundle-size regression.
- [ ] No PHP changes, no REST changes (rely on 3b/3c).

## Scope guard

- Do **not** modify or rename `sd-ai-agent/`, `SdAiAgent\\`, `SD_AI_AGENT_`, or the `superdav-ai-agent` text domain.
- Do **not** add Playwright tests in this PR — that is subphase 3e.
- Do **not** ship Phase 4's `design-system-aesthetics.md` skill in this PR.

title: test(t226c-3e): E2E Playwright spec for theme-builder onboarding flow (Phase 3 of #1373)
body:
**Task ID:** `t226c-3e` | **Parent:** #1373 | **Phase:** 3, subphase 3e of 5 (final) | **Tier:** `tier:standard` | **Estimate:** ~3h | **Depends on:** #1385 / `t226c-3b`, `t226c-3c`, `t226c-3d`.

## Pre-flight

- [x] Discovery pass: existing E2E specs live in `tests/e2e/` (verified: `admin-page.spec.js`, `chat-interactions.spec.js`, `floating-widget.spec.js`, `agent-builder.spec.js`, etc.). Playwright config is `playwright.config.js` at repo root. The CI workflow has Playwright as a required gate (PR #1392 ran "Playwright E2E (WP trunk shard 1/2/3)").
- [x] File refs verified at HEAD `b0adf0b`:
  - `tests/e2e/admin-page.spec.js` — header style; uses `./utils/wp-admin` for `loginToWordPress`, `goToAgentPage`, `getMessageInput`, `getSendButton`, etc.
  - `tests/e2e/chat-interactions.spec.js` — example of a chat-driven test that submits prompts and asserts on response.
  - `playwright.config.js` — base configuration. Worker should read this before adding a new spec.
- [x] Tier: `tier:standard` — straightforward Playwright spec mirroring existing patterns.

## What

Add a Playwright E2E spec that drives the theme-builder onboarding flow end-to-end:

1. Reset the site to a fresh state where `onboarding_complete=false` and no theme called `e2e-test-theme` exists.
2. Log in as admin.
3. Open the unified admin page.
4. Walk through the onboarding wizard, selecting "Design a custom theme" at the mode picker.
5. Assert that the theme-builder chat session opens with the theme-builder agent selected and the agent's greeting visible.
6. Send a deterministic instruction to the agent:
   > "Use sd-ai-agent/scaffold-block-theme with slug=e2e-test-theme and name=\"E2E Test Theme\", then call sd-ai-agent/activate-theme with stylesheet=e2e-test-theme. Reply only with: DONE."
7. Wait for the agent reply containing "DONE" (with a generous timeout — agent loops can run for tens of seconds).
8. Assert via REST (`/wp/v2/themes?status=active`) or a server-side check that:
   - Theme `e2e-test-theme` exists at `wp-content/themes/e2e-test-theme/`.
   - It is the active stylesheet.
9. Clean up: switch back to `twentytwentyfive` (or whichever theme was active before), and remove the test theme directory.

## Why

This is the verification gate of the whole Phase 3. Without an E2E test that exercises the user-facing flow end-to-end, the next regression in any of OnboardingWizard, the REST endpoint, the theme-builder agent system prompt, or the two abilities goes unnoticed.

Subphase 3e being the final subphase, **this PR uses `Closes #1385`** in the PR body — it ships the last child of Phase 3.

## Files to Modify

- **NEW:** `tests/e2e/onboarding-theme-builder.spec.js`
- **EDIT:** `tests/e2e/utils/wp-admin.js` — only if a generic helper is missing (e.g. a `selectOnboardingMode( page, mode )` helper). Add only what's reused, keep the spec self-contained otherwise.
- **EDIT (optional):** `playwright.config.js` — only if the new spec needs a longer per-test timeout than the default. Document the change in the PR body if you make one.
- **EDIT (optional):** `package.json` if a new script is needed to run this single spec, but don't add one unless it materially helps; the existing `npm run test:e2e:playwright -- tests/e2e/onboarding-theme-builder.spec.js` is fine.

## Implementation Steps

1. **Read first:** `tests/e2e/admin-page.spec.js` and `tests/e2e/chat-interactions.spec.js` for patterns. Read `tests/e2e/utils/wp-admin.js` to learn the helpers already available.
2. **Pretest reset.** Use a `test.beforeAll` that resets `onboarding_complete` and deletes any stale `e2e-test-theme`. Two ways depending on what utilities exist:
   - Preferred: call WP-CLI from the test (`require('child_process').execSync(...)`) since the dev environment ships WP-CLI.
   - Fallback: hit a small REST endpoint already used by other E2E specs to reset state.
3. **Stable mocks for the agent reply.** The agent's *Send DONE only* prompt narrows nondeterminism but does not eliminate it. To make this E2E reliable in CI, the spec should set the active provider to a deterministic test backend if one exists in this repo. If no test backend exists, the spec must accept the natural agent latency — use `expect(...).toHaveText(/DONE/, { timeout: 120000 })`. Do **not** add a fake provider in this PR; if reliability is a concern, file a follow-up rather than expanding scope.
4. **Assertions.**
   - The mode picker shows three buttons.
   - "Design a custom theme" is pre-selected on a fresh install.
   - After clicking through, the page mounts `ChatRedesign` (assert the chat panel `[data-testid=...]` or known class).
   - After the test prompt, the theme directory `wp-content/themes/e2e-test-theme/` exists with `theme.json`, `style.css`, `functions.php`, `templates/index.html`.
   - `get_stylesheet()` (via WP-CLI or REST) returns `e2e-test-theme`.
5. **Cleanup.** `test.afterAll` restores the previous active theme and removes the test directory.
6. **Tag the test.** Use `test.describe.serial(...)` since the steps share state. Tag with a `theme-builder` describe-level name for future grep.

## Verification

```bash
npm run test:e2e:playwright -- tests/e2e/onboarding-theme-builder.spec.js
```

Should pass locally and in CI on `Playwright E2E (WP trunk shard X)`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `tests/e2e/onboarding-theme-builder.spec.js` exists.
- [ ] Spec resets state in `beforeAll` and cleans up in `afterAll`.
- [ ] Spec asserts the mode-picker, the auto-select default, the chat-panel mount, and the post-prompt theme state.
- [ ] Test passes in CI on the existing Playwright matrix.
- [ ] No flake under 3 consecutive CI runs (or if flake observed, file a follow-up and tag this PR's reviewer; do not skip the test).
- [ ] PR body uses `Closes #1385` (this is the final subphase of Phase 3).
- [ ] PR body uses `Ref #1373` (parent stays open until Phase 4 also ships).

## Scope guard

- Do **not** modify production code in this PR. If you find a bug while writing the test, file a separate issue + PR.
- Do **not** rename canonical identifiers.

title: feat(t226d): design-system-aesthetics skill (topic-grounded visual worlds) — Phase 4 of #1373
body:
**Task ID:** `t226d` | **Parent:** #1373 | **Phase:** 4 of 4 | **Tier:** `tier:standard` | **Estimate:** ~5h | **Depends on:** subphase 3b (#`t226c-3b`) for the agent that will reference the new skill.

## Pre-flight

- [x] Discovery pass: 0 commits touch `includes/Models/skills/` introducing a `design-system-aesthetics` file on `main` (HEAD `b0adf0b`).
- [x] File refs verified at HEAD `b0adf0b`:
  - `includes/Models/skills/site-specification.md` — Phase 1 deliverable; structure to mirror.
  - `includes/Models/skills/block-themes.md` — Phase 2 deliverable; structure to mirror for the "skill" section conventions.
  - `includes/Models/skills/kadence-theme.md` — older skill, parallel structure.
- [x] Tier: `tier:standard` — markdown drafting with a clear inspiration source (#1373 documents the "topic-grounded visual worlds" framework).

## What

Add a new skill `design-system-aesthetics.md` (~400–600 lines, matching the size of `block-themes.md`) under `includes/Models/skills/` capturing the **topic-grounded visual worlds** framework described in #1373:

> Their key insight: don't generate "modern dark theme / minimalist light theme / colorful theme" — instead, ask what aesthetic worlds the *topic* could authentically inhabit. A craft brewery is not "generic dark/light/colorful"; it's taproom-warmth vs label-art-maximalism vs industrial-grain-and-steel.

The skill is referenced from the theme-builder agent's system prompt (subphase 3b) at Phase 2 ("propose 3 topic-grounded design directions"). It is not auto-loaded — the agent calls `sd-ai-agent/skill-load` for `design-system-aesthetics` at the start of Phase 2.

## Why

Without this skill, the theme-builder agent will produce generic "light / dark / colorful" design directions and the differentiator the parent plan calls out is lost. Phase 4 is what makes the theme-builder visually credible.

## Files to Modify

- **NEW:** `includes/Models/skills/design-system-aesthetics.md` — the skill itself.
- **EDIT (optional, only if 3b is already merged):** the theme-builder agent's `system_prompt` in `Agent::get_builtin_definitions()` — add an explicit `skill-load design-system-aesthetics` instruction at the start of Phase 2.
  - If 3b has not yet merged when this PR opens, this edit moves to subphase 3b (or a follow-up); document the choice in the PR body.

## Implementation Steps

1. **Read first:**
   - `includes/Models/skills/site-specification.md` (Phase 1 — the data this skill consumes).
   - `includes/Models/skills/block-themes.md` (Phase 2 — the technical theme.json patterns this skill complements).
   - The source inspiration in #1373's "Context & Decisions" section, especially the brewery → taproom / label-art / industrial example.
2. **Draft structure** (suggested):
   - **Section: When to use this skill** — load this when the agent reaches Phase 2 of the theme-builder flow.
   - **Section: The topic-grounded framework** — the core principle (replace generic style adjectives with topic-authentic worlds).
   - **Section: A worked taxonomy by site type.** Cover the 7 site types already in `site-specification.md` (SaaS, e-commerce, professional-services, restaurant, portfolio, blog, non-profit). For each, give 3 authentic visual worlds with: name, mood/atmosphere descriptor, signature color directions (no specific hex codes — color is the agent's job), typography category, layout density preference, one or two short example use-cases.
   - **Section: Worked examples** — 3 fully-rendered examples (e.g. craft brewery, SaaS startup, family law firm), each presenting 3 distinct directions with the same fields above.
   - **Section: Anti-patterns** — what to avoid: stock-image dependence, "modern minimal" cliché, palette swaps masquerading as direction changes, derivative copies of well-known site themes.
   - **Section: Output contract for the agent** — when the agent emits design preview HTML files, each direction must include a title, a 1-sentence atmosphere descriptor, a representative palette swatch row, a sample headline+subhead in the chosen typography, and a short body sample. No stock-image URLs.
3. **i18n note:** skills are read by the agent as raw markdown; they are **not** translated. Keep the markdown English-only and do not wrap strings with `__()`.
4. **Word/section budget:** aim for 350–550 lines; the file should be substantial enough to materially shift agent output but not so long that loading it bloats the context window. Use the existing `block-themes.md` length as the upper bound.
5. **No stock-image URLs anywhere in the document.** This rule applies to the skill content itself, not just to the output contract it teaches.

## Verification

```bash
test -f includes/Models/skills/design-system-aesthetics.md
wc -l includes/Models/skills/design-system-aesthetics.md   # expect 350–600
grep -c '^### ' includes/Models/skills/design-system-aesthetics.md  # expect ≥ 10
! grep -q 'unsplash\|pexels\|pixabay' includes/Models/skills/design-system-aesthetics.md
```

If the optional system-prompt edit lands in this PR, also:

```bash
grep -q 'design-system-aesthetics' includes/Models/Agent.php
composer phpcs -- includes/Models/Agent.php
composer phpstan
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `includes/Models/skills/design-system-aesthetics.md` exists.
- [ ] File length is in the 350–600 line range.
- [ ] At least 7 site-type taxonomies plus at least 3 worked examples.
- [ ] An explicit "no stock-image URLs" rule in the output-contract section.
- [ ] No stock-image hostnames (`unsplash`, `pexels`, `pixabay`) anywhere in the file.
- [ ] (Optional, if shipped together) Theme-builder agent's system prompt references the skill by name.
- [ ] Skill is loadable by the agent: `sd-ai-agent/skill-load` with slug `design-system-aesthetics` returns the file content (smoke via `wp eval`).

## Scope guard

- Do **not** add CSS / theme.json templates here — that's `block-themes.md`'s job.
- Do **not** wire UI changes.
- Do **not** add stock-image hosting or remote-URL dependencies.

title: Epic (sd-ai-aey): Standards-aligned third-party ability visibility (meta.mcp.public + tiered trust)
body:
# Epic: Standards-aligned third-party ability visibility (meta.mcp.public + tiered trust)

> Tracking issue for beads epic `sd-ai-aey`. Foundation already landed in #1403 (`sd-ai-xok`). This issue stays open until every child below is merged.

## Why

Today every registered WordPress ability is exposed to the in-chat AI agent and the public MCP endpoint by default. Visibility is opt-OUT via the proprietary `meta.ai_hidden` flag. There is no opt-IN signal, no gate on the MCP endpoint, and no policy for third-party abilities that pour in from plugins like WooCommerce, Multisite Ultimate, or any future MCP-aware plugin.

The senior dev review surfaced this directly: "not all Abilities should be exposed as AI tools" — and the WordPress ecosystem already has a published convention. The MCP Adapter v0.5.0 ([WordPress/mcp-adapter](https://github.com/WordPress/mcp-adapter), Apr 2026) defines `meta.mcp.public = true` as the canonical signal. WooCommerce 10.3+ already follows it. Plugin authors are increasingly expected to declare it.

## Children (dispatch order)

| Beads | Status | Title | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sd-ai-xok` | merged | AbilityVisibility resolver + PartnerAllowlist | #1403 — foundation |
| `sd-ai-3ns` | #1405 | Thread AbilityVisibility through all four exposure surfaces | parallel-safe, auto-dispatch |
| `sd-ai-w7a` | #1406 | Add `meta.mcp.public = true` to all `sd-ai-agent/*` registrations | parallel-safe, auto-dispatch |
| `sd-ai-dam` | #1407 | Preserve tri-state annotations (stop coercing `null → false`) | parallel-safe, auto-dispatch |
| `sd-ai-0zq` | blocked on #1405 | Admin notice: batched unclassified-ability summary | not yet mirrored |
| `sd-ai-f8y` | blocked on #1405 | Wire `meta.ai.usage_instructions` into Tier-1 + Tier-2 context | not yet mirrored |
| `sd-ai-u21` | blocked on 0zq + #1405 | Default `sd_ai_agent_third_party_mode` flip: legacy → auto (with migration) | not yet mirrored |
| `sd-ai-aqv` | blocked on u21 | Documentation: ability visibility decision tree + four exposure surfaces | not yet mirrored |
| `sd-ai-8t5` | blocked on u21 | Upstream PRs: add `meta.mcp.public` to top 3 most-used plugins | not yet mirrored |

## Tiered trust model (zero per-ability user config)

- **Tier A — explicit public:** `meta.mcp.public === true`. Always exposed.
- **Tier B — explicit private:** `meta.mcp.public === false` OR `meta.ai_hidden === true`. Never exposed.
- **Tier C — implicit:** deterministic heuristic in `AbilityVisibility::classify()`:
  1. First-party namespace allowlist (`sd-ai-agent/*`, `wp-cli/*`).
  2. Verified-partner namespace allowlist (`woocommerce-rest/*`, `multisite-ultimate/*`, `mcp-adapter/*`).
  3. Partner category allowlist (`site`, `user`, `ai-experiments`, …).
  4. Schema-quality: non-empty `description` AND `category` → `public-heuristic`.
  5. Otherwise → `private-unknown` (surfaced in batched admin notice).

## Surfaces affected

1. In-chat Tier-1 (FunctionDeclarations) — `AgentLoop::resolve_abilities()` line 1422
2. In-chat Tier-2 manifest — `ToolDiscovery::build_manifest_section()` line 343
3. MCP endpoint — `McpController::get_mcp_tools()` line 228 (**currently UNGATED — security gap**)
4. Admin ability picker — `AgentController::handle_list_abilities()` line 583
5. Abilities Explorer — `AbilityExplorerService::get_explorer_list()` (visibility column)

## ⚠ Canonical naming guard — DO NOT RENAME

Per `AGENTS.md`:

- `sd-ai-agent/` is the canonical ability namespace, REST namespace, CSS prefix, DB prefix, and DI container ID. **Never** rewrite to `superdav-ai-agent/` anywhere except the plugin folder name and the i18n text domain.
- `superdav-ai-agent` is the canonical text domain and WP.org slug. **Never** rewrite to `sd-ai-agent` in `__( 'text', '...' )` calls.
- No legacy-name migrations: `ai-agent/`, `gratis-ai-agent`, and any other historical prefix are unsupported and must not be reintroduced.

PRs that flip these identifiers will be closed unmerged (examples: #1289, #1290, #1291).

## References

- `WordPress/mcp-adapter` v0.5.0 README — canonical `meta.mcp.public` pattern
- `AGENTS.md` "Canonical Naming" — preserves `sd-ai-agent/` namespace
- `WooCommerceIntegrationHandler.php` — partner integration pattern
- Beads epic: `sd-ai-aey`

title: feat(sd-ai-3ns): Thread AbilityVisibility through all four exposure surfaces (replace ai_hidden checks)
body:
# Thread AbilityVisibility through all four exposure surfaces (replace ai_hidden checks)

> Beads task `sd-ai-3ns`. Depends on `sd-ai-xok` (merged #1403). Parent epic #1404.

## Why

Now that `SdAiAgent\Core\AbilityVisibility` exists (#1403), every inline `! empty( $meta['ai_hidden'] )` check is a candidate for replacement. The four surfaces must agree on visibility or we get drift bugs.

**Critical:** `includes/REST/McpController.php` currently exposes ALL abilities (no `ai_hidden` filter at all). This is the highest-value fix in the whole epic — external MCP clients should not see third-party abilities the site owner hasn't sanctioned.

## What

Replace inline checks with the appropriate `AbilityVisibility::for_*()` call at each site. Use the resolver's `for_ai_chat()`, `for_mcp()`, or `for_admin_picker()` predicate as listed.

|---|---|---|---|
| `includes/Core/AgentLoop.php` | 1422 | `! empty( $meta['ai_hidden'] )` | `! AbilityVisibility::for_ai_chat( $ability )` |
| `includes/Tools/ToolDiscovery.php` | 343 (manifest) | inline `ai_hidden` | `for_ai_chat()` |
| `includes/Tools/ToolDiscovery.php` | 993 (search candidates) | inline `ai_hidden` | `for_ai_chat()` |
| `includes/REST/AgentController.php` | 583 (admin picker) | inline `ai_hidden` | `for_admin_picker()` |
| `includes/REST/McpController.php` | 228 (`get_mcp_tools()`) | **no gate at all** | **add `for_mcp()` filter (NEW)** |
| `includes/Services/AbilityExplorerService.php` | column build | n/a | surface `AbilityVisibility::classify( $ability )` as a new `visibility` column (admin sees everything, but knows what AI sees) |

## Settings flag

Introduce `sd_ai_agent_third_party_mode` in `includes/Core/Settings.php` with three values:

- `legacy` (default in this PR): current behaviour — everything except `ai_hidden` is public. Each call site uses `for_ai_chat()`/`for_mcp()` but the resolver is forced to allow when mode is `legacy`. **Adjust `AbilityVisibility` to read this setting** so semantics can flip in a later PR (`sd-ai-u21`).
- `auto`: full tiered-trust model (current resolver behaviour without legacy shim).
- `strict`: only explicit `meta.mcp.public === true` passes.

Default stays `legacy` for now so this PR has zero behavioural change. The flip to `auto` ships in `sd-ai-u21`.

title: fix(sd-ai-dam): Preserve tri-state annotations (stop coercing null to false in AbilityExplorerService)
body:
# Preserve tri-state annotations (readonly/destructive/idempotent) — stop coercing null to false

> Beads bug `sd-ai-dam`. Independent of other epic children. Parent epic #1404.

## Why

`SdAiAgent\Abilities\AbstractAbility::meta()` returns this default:

```php
'annotations' => [
    'readonly'    => null,
    'destructive' => null,
    'idempotent'  => null,
],
```

`null` is the documented "unknown" tri-state from MCP spec annotation semantics.

But `includes/Services/AbilityExplorerService.php:152-159` coerces every value to `(bool)`, turning `null → false`. That silently mis-classifies "we don't know" as "we know it's not destructive" — a security and UX antipattern. A destructive ability with `destructive => null` reads as **safe** in the explorer UI.

## What

1. In `AbilityExplorerService::format_ability_for_explorer()`, preserve the null tri-state:

   ```php
   'annotations' => [
       'readonly'    => is_bool( $annotations['readonly']    ?? null ) ? $annotations['readonly']    : null,
       'destructive' => is_bool( $annotations['destructive'] ?? null ) ? $annotations['destructive'] : null,
       'idempotent'  => is_bool( $annotations['idempotent']  ?? null ) ? $annotations['idempotent']  : null,
   ],
   ```

2. Update the React abilities-explorer component (`src/abilities-explorer/abilities-explorer-app.js`, or wherever annotations render) to show three states:
   - `true`  → ✓
   - `false` → ✗
   - `null`  → ? (tooltip: "Not declared by ability author — assume destructive for safety")

3. Add a `@since` note to the JSDoc/PHPDoc that the contract is now tri-state. Older consumers should treat unknown as "assume destructive" for safety.

## Files

- Modify: `includes/Services/AbilityExplorerService.php` (lines 152–159)
- Modify: `src/abilities-explorer/abilities-explorer-app.js` (or wherever the React component renders annotations)
- Modify or create: `tests/SdAiAgent/Services/AbilityExplorerServiceTest.php`

## Acceptance criteria

- Abilities with all-null annotations show `?` in UI, not `false`.
- Existing abilities with explicit booleans (e.g. `PostAbilities`) render unchanged.
- New PHPUnit case in `AbilityExplorerServiceTest`:
  - Ability with `annotations.destructive => null` → output preserves `null`.
  - Ability with `annotations.destructive => true` → output is `true`.
- React tests (if any cover annotation rendering) updated.
- `composer phpcs`, `composer phpstan`, `npm run test:js`, `npm run test:php` all clean.

## Verification

```bash
composer phpcs -- includes/Services/AbilityExplorerService.php
composer phpstan
npm run test:php
npm run test:js
```

## ⚠ Canonical naming guard — DO NOT RENAME

Per `AGENTS.md`: do not rename `sd-ai-agent` to `superdav-ai-agent` (or vice-versa) anywhere outside their canonical contexts (plugin folder + i18n text domain only).

title: fix(post-abilities): replace oneOf with type-array union in create-post / update-post / bulk schemas (Claude 2020-12 rejection)
body:
## Bug

The `categories` and `tags` parameter schemas in `sd-ai-agent/create-post`, `sd-ai-agent/update-post`, and the `posts[]` items of `sd-ai-agent/bulk-update-posts` (or equivalent — line 400 of `includes/Abilities/PostAbilities.php`) use the JSON Schema construct:

```php
'items' => [
    'oneOf' => [
        [ 'type' => 'string' ],
        [ 'type' => 'integer' ],
    ],
],
```

Anthropic's Claude tool-use API rejects this with:

```
Bad Request (400) - tools.1.custom.input_schema: JSON schema is invalid.
It must match JSON Schema draft 2020-12 (https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12).
Learn more about tool use at https://docs.claude.com/en/docs/tool-use.
```

Result: ANY agent run that loads the default Tier-1 tools through the Anthropic provider fails at the first `/v1/run` call, before the LLM is ever invoked. Because `update-post` and `create-post` are both in `ToolDiscovery::DEFAULT_TIER_1` (`includes/Tools/ToolDiscovery.php:56-78`), this affects the cold-start agent loop for every Anthropic-backed install.

## Reproduction

1. WordPress 7.0-RC2, plugin at `main` (`d051a32`), `ai-provider-for-anthropic-max` active and configured.
2. POST `/wp-json/sd-ai-agent/v1/run` with `provider_id: ultimate-ai-connector-anthropic-max`, any Claude model, default Tier-1 abilities.
3. Job transitions straight to `status: error` with the message above.

Reproduced today against `mygratis.site` (local dev, Bedrock multisite). Verified that other Tier-1 tools (`ability-search`, `ability-call`, `memory-save`, `memory-list`, `skill-load`, `knowledge-search`, `update-global-styles`, `wp-cli/execute`) have schema sizes 33–585 bytes with no `oneOf`/`anyOf`/`allOf`/`format`/`const`/`$ref`. Only `update-post` (1164 bytes) and `create-post` (1420 bytes) contain `oneOf`.

## Files

- `includes/Abilities/PostAbilities.php`
  - line 122 — `create-post` `categories.items`
  - line 210 — `update-post` `categories.items`
  - line 400 — `bulk` posts items `categories.items`

## Fix

Replace each occurrence with the draft-2020-12-compatible form Claude accepts:

```php
'items' => [
    'type' => [ 'string', 'integer' ],
],
```

This is semantically identical for this use case (string OR integer scalar), shorter, and natively supported by both Anthropic and OpenAI tool APIs. Keep the existing `description` on `categories` ("Array of category IDs (integers) or names (strings) to assign.") unchanged.

## Verification

After the patch, end-to-end test against a Claude model:

```bash
curl -sk -u USER:APP_PASSWORD https://SITE/wp-json/sd-ai-agent/v1/run \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "message": "Create a draft post titled Hello with category News.",
    "provider_id": "ultimate-ai-connector-anthropic-max",
    "model_id": "claude-haiku-4-5-20251001",
    "max_iterations": 3
  }'
# poll /wp-json/sd-ai-agent/v1/job/<job_id> until status: complete
# expect: tool_calls includes sd-ai-agent/create-post, no schema error
```

Also add a unit test that asserts none of the abilities returned by `ToolDiscovery::tier_1_for_run()` contains a top-level `oneOf`/`anyOf`/`allOf` inside `items`. PostAbilitiesTest is a natural home; a registry-level guard in a new `Tier1SchemaComplianceTest` would catch any future regression of this class.

## Reference

Issue surfaced while verifying epic #1404 end-to-end. The visibility work in #1403 / #1415 / #1419 / #1408 is unaffected and correct — this is a pre-existing schema defect in `PostAbilities.php` that blocks any practical browser test of update-post through the Anthropic provider. Independent of `meta.mcp.public` and `AbilityVisibility`.

## Summary
When the agent calls `sd-ai-agent/create-post` and then narrates the result back to the user, it **fabricates the published URL in its prose reply** — wrong year, wrong slug — even though the post is created correctly in the database with the correct permalink.

## Reproduction
On a local dev install (real date `2026-05-13`, dev URL `http://wordpress.local:8080`):

```bash
wp sd-ai-agent prompt prompt 'write a 200-word blog post intro about headless WordPress' --skip-tools
```

(Note: `--skip-tools` is also broken; see separate report.)

The model called `sd-ai-agent/create-post` and replied:

```
Here's your blog post intro, published and live!
"What Is Headless WordPress — And Why Should You Care?"
[View post →](http://wordpress.local:8080/2025/07/22/what-is-headless-wordpress-and-why-should-you-care/)
```

Inspecting the actual post:

```
$ wp post get 29 --field=post_date
2026-05-13 17:36:34
$ wp eval 'echo get_permalink(29);'
http://wordpress.local:8080/2026/05/13/home/
```

So:
- **Real permalink**: `http://wordpress.local:8080/2026/05/13/home/`
- **What the agent printed**: `http://wordpress.local:8080/2025/07/22/what-is-headless-wordpress-and-why-should-you-care/`

Both date segment and slug are fabricated.

## Diagnosis
- `PostAbilities::handle_create_post()` (`includes/Abilities/PostAbilities.php:833`) correctly returns `['post_id', 'permalink', 'status', 'post_type']` using `get_permalink( $post_id )`.
- The output schema (`includes/Abilities/PostAbilities.php:149-157`) also declares those four keys.
- The string `"Post created successfully"` and the `success / url / message` shape that the agent claimed to have received as the tool result do **not** exist anywhere in the codebase (`rg "Post created successfully" includes/` returns nothing).
- Conclusion: the model hallucinated both the surrounding `tool_result` JSON it claimed to have received **and** the URL it printed in prose. The actual tool ran with the correct return shape and stored the post with the correct date.

## Why this matters
- Users will copy-paste a non-existent URL.
- A hallucinated date / slug in the published-content confirmation undermines trust in every other "I did it" reply the agent gives.
- Slug `home` (instead of the title-derived slug) is itself worth investigating — likely a collision with an existing page using the post's slug.

## Suggested fixes
1. **Anchor the model**: post-process the assistant's final reply when the conversation contains a successful `sd-ai-agent/create-post` response. Rewrite or append a verified line containing the real `permalink` from the tool response, so the user always sees the truth even if the model invents URL text.
2. **System-prompt rule**: explicitly instruct the agent that it must quote the `permalink` field of the create-post response verbatim and must never invent a date- or slug-based URL.
3. **CLI verbose mode**: print real tool responses (already in `tool_call_log`) above the assistant reply when `--verbose` is set, so users can see the discrepancy.

## Repro environment
- Plugin version: 1.11.1
- Provider: Anthropic (claude-sonnet-4-6)
- WordPress: 7.0-RC2 local
- Dev URL: `http://wordpress.local:8080` (port `8080`)

## Related
- Side observation: `--skip-tools` flag was ignored in the same run (the agent still called `skill-load` and `create-post` despite passing the flag). Will file separately if not already tracked.

title: feat(trace): structured trace channel via wp_ai_client_before/after_generate_result SDK events
body:
## Background

PR #1457 fixed the immediate problem that provider tracing only captured
four hardcoded hosts and silently dropped every other connector (Kimi via
HuggingFace, OpenRouter, custom OpenAI-compatible endpoints, etc.). That
PR widens the **HTTP-level** capture so any LLM call goes through.

The HTTP-level capture has known limits the wider matcher cannot solve:

1. **No row on SDK exceptions or timeouts.** When the WP AI Client SDK
   throws (HTTP 5xx after retries, network error, JSON parse error), no
   trace row is written if the request was preempted or if our hook
   missed it. This is exactly the class of failure that motivated PR
   #1457 (Kimi K2.6 stalled mid-execution with no trace row).
2. **Raw wire data only.** `request_body` and `response_body` are stored
   as JSON strings. Searching by capability, finish-reason, or token
   usage requires re-parsing every row.
3. **Token-cache usage extraction** is heuristic and provider-specific
   (see `CacheUsageExtractor`).

## Proposal

Add a parallel, structured trace channel that listens on the WP AI Client
SDK's PSR-14 event hooks dispatched by
`WP_AI_Client_Event_Dispatcher`:

- `wp_ai_client_before_generate_result` — receives `BeforeGenerateResultEvent`
  carrying `Message[]`, `ModelInterface`, `CapabilityEnum|null`.
- `wp_ai_client_after_generate_result` — receives `AfterGenerateResultEvent`
  carrying the same plus a `GenerativeAiResult` with id, candidates,
  `TokenUsage`, `ProviderMetadata`, `ModelMetadata`, finish reason, and
  additional data.

Sources:

- `lib/php-ai-client/src/Events/BeforeGenerateResultEvent.php`
- `lib/php-ai-client/src/Events/AfterGenerateResultEvent.php`
- `includes/Compat/ai-client/adapters/class-wp-ai-client-event-dispatcher.php`
- Dispatch sites in `lib/php-ai-client/src/Builders/PromptBuilder.php`
  around `generateResult()`.

### Design sketch

1. New handler `includes/Bootstrap/AiClientEventTraceHandler.php` registered
   on both action hooks via `#[Action]` decorators. Stash the Before
   timestamp in a static keyed by `spl_object_id($event)`-equivalent stable
   correlation; on After, compute `duration_ms` and write a structured row.

2. Structured columns to surface (either as new DB columns or via a JSON
   `metadata` blob — to be decided in the PR):

   - `capability` — `BeforeGenerateResultEvent::getCapability()->value`
   - `provider_id` — `getModel()->providerMetadata()->getId()`
   - `model_id` — `getModel()->metadata()->getId()`
   - `finish_reason` — normalised from result candidates
   - `token_usage` — `TokenUsage` DTO (input, output, cache_creation,
     cache_read) — replaces the heuristic `CacheUsageExtractor` for SDK
     paths
   - `result_id` — `GenerativeAiResult::getId()` for cross-referencing
     against retries / streamed parts
   - `messages_in` — JSON of `Message[]` sent
   - `result_out` — JSON of `GenerativeAiResult`

3. **Before-without-After watchdog.** When a Before fires but the matching
   After never arrives within the SDK request timeout, write a synthetic
   row with `error='no_result_event'` and the model/provider/messages
   that were attempted. This is the missing piece that would have caught
   the stalled Kimi case.

4. **Deduplication.** When the SDK events fire and the HTTP-level capture
   also writes a row for the same call, mark the HTTP row as the wire
   trace (`source='http'`) and the SDK row as semantic (`source='sdk'`).
   Add a `source` column to `wp_sd_ai_agent_provider_trace` or store on
   the existing `additional_data` blob.

5. **Trace viewer UX.** Group by `result_id` so the SDK row and its
   matching HTTP row(s) display together. Show capability/finish-reason
   prominently — they are far more diagnostic than raw status codes.

## Why not just rely on the SDK events

The SDK events alone are insufficient because they do not fire on the
failure modes we most need to debug (SDK exceptions, malformed responses,
provider-side truncations that throw during result construction). The
HTTP-level capture from PR #1457 must remain the safety net.

## Constraints

- Must remain gated on `ProviderTrace::is_enabled()` (debug only).
- Must not double-count successful calls in the trace viewer.
- The Before/After correlation must be safe across nested SDK calls
  (one user turn can trigger multiple prompts) and across re-entrant
  PHP requests (cron + REST overlapping).
- No new vendor dependencies — the SDK is already bundled in
  `lib/php-ai-client/`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] New handler captures Before+After event pairs as structured rows.
- [ ] Before-without-After watchdog captures stalled / exception cases
      and reproduces the Kimi K2.6 stall as a recorded row in a test.
- [ ] Trace viewer surfaces capability, finish-reason, and token-usage
      from the SDK source when present.
- [ ] HTTP-source rows from PR #1457 remain unchanged and continue to
      capture non-SDK paths.
- [ ] Tests: at least Before+After happy path, Before-without-After
      watchdog, and nested-call correlation.

## Related

- PR #1457 — the HTTP-level allowlist fix this issue builds on.
- Stalled session reference: `wp_sd_ai_agent_sessions.id=38` (Kimi K2.6
  via `ai-provider-for-any-openai-compatible-2`, last `changes_log` write
  at 2026-05-15 20:21:41, model emitted only preamble text and no
  follow-up `function_call`).

title: fix: guard WP_Ability stub in tests/bootstrap.php against WP 7.0 trunk redeclaration fatal
body:
## Problem

The entire PHPUnit suite crashes against WP trunk with a fatal error:

```
PHP Fatal error: Cannot declare class WP_Ability, because the name is already in use
in /tmp/wordpress/wp-includes/abilities-api/class-wp-ability.php on line 21
```

**Root cause**: `tests/bootstrap.php` defines a test double for `WP_Ability` (used as a stub when running against WP 6.x, where the class does not exist in core). WP 7.0 trunk now ships a real `WP_Ability` class in `wp-includes/abilities-api/class-wp-ability.php`. When PHPUnit loads against WP trunk, WordPress core defines `WP_Ability` first; the unconditional redeclaration in bootstrap.php causes a fatal error before any test runs.

## Fix

**File**: `tests/bootstrap.php`

Wrap the `WP_Ability` stub class declaration with a `class_exists()` guard:

```php
// Before (line that causes fatal on WP 7.0+):
class WP_Ability { ... }

// After:
if ( ! class_exists( 'WP_Ability' ) ) {
    class WP_Ability {
        // ... existing stub body unchanged ...
    }
}
```

**Note**: Verify that the stub's public API (`get_name()`, `get_label()`, `get_description()`, `get_params()`) is compatible with WP 7.0's actual `WP_Ability` implementation. If WP 7.0's class has different method signatures, additional test adaptations may be needed. Check `wp-includes/abilities-api/class-wp-ability.php` in WP trunk.

The same pattern may be needed for `stubs/wordpress-7-runtime.php` if that stub is loaded during PHPUnit runs.

## Verification

- `vendor/bin/phpunit` must complete (not crash on startup) when run against WP trunk.
- All tests that previously relied on the `WP_Ability` stub must still pass.
- CI workflow **Tests → PHPUnit** must show green against WP trunk.

## Evidence

- Failed CI run: https://github.com/Ultimate-Multisite/superdav-ai-agent/actions/runs/25939084582/job/76251888175
- Surfaced by post-merge CI on PR #1451
- WP 6.9 PHPUnit not affected (WP_Ability not in WP 6.x core)

title: Default-model resolution does not validate against registered providers (root cause of gemma4:e4b demo error)
body:
## Summary

When the saved `sd_ai_agent_settings.default_model` (or its legacy precursor
`ultimate_ai_connector_default_model`) references a model that is not from a
currently registered provider, every new chat fails immediately with a
top-level error banner — no graceful fallback to the built-in
`SD_AI_AGENT_DEFAULT_MODEL` constant or to any installed Anthropic/OpenAI/
Compatible-Endpoint provider.

This is what produced the production-blocking "Error: The AI model
\"gemma4:e4b\" is not available on your plan." failure that every brand-new
demo signup on `ultimateagentwp.ai` hit between the initial provisioning of
the demo template and 2026-05-18T13:36Z (now patched at the data layer on
`demo.ultimateagentwp.ai`). The data fix prevents new demos from inheriting
the broken value; this issue tracks the code hardening that would have
caught the situation regardless.

## Reproduction

1. On any site running this plugin, run from WP-CLI:
   ```bash
   wp option patch insert sd_ai_agent_settings default_provider some-bogus-provider --url=<site>
   wp option patch insert sd_ai_agent_settings default_model bogus:model --url=<site>
   ```
2. Visit `?page=sd-ai-agent`, start a new chat, send any message.
3. Observe: an error banner appears immediately — "The AI model
   \"bogus:model\" is not available on your plan." — and the conversation is
   unusable until the user manually changes provider/model in the dropdown
   for *every* chat.

Production evidence (now cleaned):

| Site | Previous broken value | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `demo.ultimateagentwp.ai` (template) | `gemma4:e4b` via `ultimate_ai_connector_default_model` | fixed |
| `davidclaude.ultimateagentwp.ai` (cloned demo) | inherited `gemma4:e4b` | fixed |
| 3 other stale sites | legacy `ultimate_ai_connector_default_model` | cleaned |

## Impact

- Every demo signup between the initial demo template provisioning and
  2026-05-18 hit a hard error on first chat — the user's first impression of
  the AI agent was a red error banner.
- Operator-controlled defaults are silently invalidated whenever a provider
  plugin is uninstalled or renamed (e.g. switching from
  `ai-provider-for-any-openai-compatible` to a different connector).
- Recovery requires either WP-CLI access or manually changing the model on
  every conversation — neither is a reasonable end-user step.

## Files

- `superdav-ai-agent.php:45` — defines the built-in default
  `SD_AI_AGENT_DEFAULT_MODEL = 'claude-sonnet-4'`.
- `includes/Core/Settings.php` — `get_default_model()` at ~line 542 reads
  `sd_ai_agent_settings.default_model` first, falls back to the constant,
  then exposes the `sd_ai_agent_default_model` filter for runtime override.
  The current path does **not** verify that the resolved
  `(provider, model)` pair maps to a registered provider/model.
- `includes/Core/Settings.php:530-536` — docblock for the
  `sd_ai_agent_default_model` filter (relevant for the fix).

The legacy option that caused the production incident is
`ultimate_ai_connector_default_model`, set by the OpenAI-Compatible Endpoint
provider (`ai-provider-for-any-openai-compatible`). It is no longer set on
any production site, but the underlying weakness — taking the saved value at
face value — is what this issue is about.

## Suggested fix

In `Settings::get_default_model()` (and the matching
`get_default_provider()`):

1. Resolve the saved `(provider, model)` pair.
2. Ask `ProviderCredentialLoader` (or the registry) whether that provider is
   currently registered **and** whether it advertises the requested model.
3. If validation fails, log a one-time admin notice (`admin-notices` channel)
   and fall through to:
   a. The `sd_ai_agent_default_model` filter (operator override).
   b. Any registered provider's "default model" entry that matches the
      `SD_AI_AGENT_DEFAULT_MODEL` constant family
      (e.g. `claude-sonnet-4` → `ultimate-ai-connector-anthropic-max` /
      `claude-sonnet-4-6`).
   c. The first registered provider's first listed model, as a last resort.

Do not add a plugin-level cache around provider/model discovery — per
`AGENTS.md → Provider Credentials and Model Discovery`, the WP AI Client SDK
already caches metadata and an extra layer requires brittle invalidation.
Resolve at request time via `ProviderCredentialLoader::load()`.

## Verification

- Repeat the reproduction steps above. After fix, chat works — the error
  banner is replaced with a one-time admin notice and the agent responds
  using a real registered model.
- New WordPress unit test covering: saved bogus model → resolved to constant
  default → registered provider invoked.
- Manual regression: existing demo sites continue to behave normally
  (saved Sonnet 4.6 default is honoured).

## Related

- The `gemma4:e4b` production data was cleaned across the affected sites on
  2026-05-18; the long-term defence is this code change.
- Plugin uses `bd` (beads) for internal task tracking
  (`AGENTS.md → Beads Issue Tracker`); this GitHub issue exists as a
  cross-system bug report and can be mirrored to `bd` if preferred.

title: Resend uses old model instead of currently selected dropdown value
body:
## Summary

After a chat message fails (e.g. with a model-availability error), if the
user changes the model in the dropdown and clicks "Resend", the second send
appears to use the **original** (failed) model rather than the newly
selected one. The visible dropdown stays on the new value, but the request
payload and the resulting error message reference the old model.

This was observed during the `davidclaude.ultimateagentwp.ai` test run on
2026-05-18: after a first message failed against `gemma4:e4b`, switching to
Claude Sonnet 4.5 and clicking Resend produced the same `gemma4:e4b` error.
Only starting a brand-new chat picked up the new selection.

## Reproduction

1. On a site where the saved default model is invalid (or temporarily mock
   one with the bogus value from the issue on default-model validation):
   ```bash
   wp option patch insert sd_ai_agent_settings default_model bogus:model --url=<site>
   ```
2. Open `?page=sd-ai-agent`, send a message — observe the
   model-unavailable error banner.
3. Without starting a new chat, change the model dropdown to a known-good
   model (e.g. `claude-sonnet-4-6` under `ultimate-ai-connector-anthropic-max`).
4. Click "Resend" on the failed message.
5. Observe: the same error appears, referencing the *old* model name.
6. Start a new chat with the same prompt — works as expected.

Screenshots in the session test artefacts:
`/tmp/opencode/ultimateagentwp-test/13-model-error.png` (initial failure),
`/tmp/opencode/ultimateagentwp-test/14-provider-dropdown.png` (dropdown
switched), `/tmp/opencode/ultimateagentwp-test/15-model-selected.png`,
`/tmp/opencode/ultimateagentwp-test/16-resend.png` (still failing with
original model).

## Impact

- Confusing UX: the dropdown looks updated but the resend ignores it.
- Forces users to start a new chat just to recover from a transient model
  failure, losing whatever conversation context they had.
- Made root-causing the `gemma4:e4b` production issue harder during the
  initial UX walkthrough.

## Files

Investigation needed in: the chat panel's message-resend handler.
Candidates based on file naming:

- `src/components/chat/` (React tree, names like `ChatPanel`, `MessageList`,
  per `AGENTS.md → JavaScript`).
- The Redux store slice under `src/store/` that owns
  `currentModel` / `currentProvider` — the resend action likely closes over
  the model that was set at message creation time, rather than reading the
  current store value.

A quick way to triage: search for the resend action handler / thunk and
verify it reads `getState().settings.currentModel` (or equivalent) at
dispatch time, not from the failed message's metadata.

## Suggested fix

When the user clicks Resend, treat it as a new send with the *current*
dropdown selection, not as a replay of the original message envelope. Two
options:

1. Re-read `currentModel` / `currentProvider` from the store at the moment
   the resend thunk dispatches, and overwrite the message's model fields
   before posting. (Minimal change; preserves the conversation thread.)
2. Surface a small "Resend with current model?" affordance that explicitly
   shows which model will be used, so the user can confirm before the second
   send fires.

Option (1) is the simpler bug-fix; (2) is an enhancement on top.

## Verification

- After fix, reproduction step 5 sends against the new model and succeeds (or
  fails with a *new* error, not the old one).
- New JS test that mocks two providers, fails the first send, switches the
  dropdown, and asserts the second send's payload carries the new
  provider+model.

title: No streaming / tool-call indicator during agent loop; users reload mid-run
body:
## Summary

During an active agent loop (tool calls in progress, e.g. creating pages,
uploading media, writing content), the chat UI shows no visible
streaming / tool-use indicator. From the user's perspective the chat is
"stuck": no spinner, no typing dots, no live tool-call list, no incremental
progress. The user's natural reaction is to reload the page, which
interrupts the agent loop and forces a recovery via the conversation
sidebar.

Observed during the `davidclaude.ultimateagentwp.ai` build of "The Golden
Spoon" on 2026-05-18: after the user prompt, the UI sat silent for a long
period. A reload revealed that pages had been created in the background
(post IDs 38-42 with priced menus, contact, reservations content). Without
the reload, there was no visible signal that the agent was actually working.

## Reproduction

1. Open `?page=sd-ai-agent` with a valid model selected (e.g.
   `claude-sonnet-4-6`).
2. Send a multi-step prompt that will trigger several tool calls, e.g.:
   "Build me a generic restaurant website. Homepage with hero, About page,
   Menu page with sample dishes, Contact page with a form, and a
   Reservations page."
3. Watch the chat panel.

Observed:

- No typing indicator.
- No "running tool X" line.
- No partial assistant text being streamed in.
- The conversation appears frozen for 30+ seconds.
- A page reload shows pages have been created and the agent has been running.

## Impact

- High false-positive "the chat is broken" rate, leading to reloads.
- Reloads interrupt the agent loop mid-tool-call. Recovery requires opening
  the sidebar and resuming the conversation, which is non-obvious.
- The agent's tool-call activity is invisible to the user, breaking the
  mental model of "agentic AI loop with tool-calling via the Abilities API"
  that the plugin advertises in its repo description.

## Files

Investigation needed in: the chat-stream / agent-loop client wiring. Likely
candidates:

- `src/components/chat/` — React message list, last-assistant-message
  rendering, partial/incremental update handling.
- `src/store/` — chat slice; whether streaming chunks are dispatched as the
  AgentLoop emits them.
- `includes/Core/AgentLoop.php` and `includes/REST/RestController.php` — the
  server side; whether SSE / streaming responses are emitted, or whether the
  REST endpoint blocks until the whole tool-call sequence completes.
- `build/admin-page.js` shows references to streaming-related state but the
  user-visible surfacing of that state is what is missing.

## Suggested fix

Three improvements that compound:

1. **Tool-call timeline indicator:** As each tool call dispatches, render a
   compact row in the chat panel ("✓ created page Home", "✓ created page
   About", "⟳ writing menu content…"). The plugin already logs changes via
   `ChangeLogger` and `ChangeLoggingHandler` — surface that stream to the
   UI in near real-time.
2. **Typing dots / streaming text:** If the underlying provider supports SSE
   streaming, render partial assistant tokens as they arrive. If not, at
   minimum show a "Working…" badge with elapsed seconds.
3. **Reload survivability:** If the user reloads mid-run, the resumed
   conversation should clearly show the active tool calls already in
   progress, not just the prior user message.

The plugin uses `bd` (beads) for internal task tracking — this issue exists
for cross-system visibility; happy to mirror to `bd` if that is preferred.

## Verification

- Repeat the reproduction prompt. After fix, the chat panel shows a visible
  stream of tool-call rows or partial text within the first ~2 s of the
  send, and continues to update as the loop progresses.
- Reload mid-run; the resumed view shows the in-progress tool calls.
- E2E test using the existing `tests/e2e/*.spec.js` harness that asserts at
  least one tool-call row is rendered before the final assistant message.

title: Agent over-reports completion: front page, site title, and nav menu claimed but not set
body:
## Summary

When the AI agent reports "I've completed X" at the end of a multi-step
build, several of its claims do not match the actual WordPress state. In the
`davidclaude.ultimateagentwp.ai` test run on 2026-05-18 the agent reported
("I've built your complete restaurant website…") that it had:

1. **Set the homepage as the static front page** — actually
   `show_on_front = 'posts'` was unchanged, so the site root still showed the
   blog index, not the Home page.
2. **Renamed the site to "The Golden Spoon"** — actually `blogname` was
   still `davidclaude` (the auto-generated subdomain slug).
3. **Created a navigation menu** — actually no `nav_menu` term existed for
   the site and no menu locations were assigned.

Pages themselves were created correctly (Home post-38, About, Menu post-40
with priced items, Contact post-41, Reservations post-42). The discrepancy
is between the agent's summary and the site-config-level actions it claims
to have taken.

## Reproduction

1. Provision a fresh demo with the model on Claude Sonnet 4.5 (or any
   capable model).
2. Send a multi-step build prompt, e.g.: "Build me a generic restaurant
   website. Homepage with hero, About page, Menu page with sample dishes,
   Contact page with a form, and a Reservations page. Use a warm,
   inviting design with food-friendly imagery placeholders."
3. After the agent reports completion, run from WP-CLI on the new subsite:
   ```bash
   wp option get show_on_front --url=<subsite>     # expected: page; actual: posts
   wp option get page_on_front --url=<subsite>     # expected: 38 (Home); actual: 0
   wp option get blogname --url=<subsite>          # expected: "The Golden Spoon"; actual: "davidclaude"
   wp menu list --url=<subsite>                    # expected: at least one menu; actual: empty
   wp menu location list --url=<subsite>           # expected: primary assigned; actual: empty
   ```

Screenshots: `20-ai-success.png` (agent's "done" message),
`21-pages-list.png` (pages created), `26-site-root.png` (front page is still
the blog index, not the Home page).

## Impact

- The agent's "I have built your site" message is misleading; trust is
  damaged when the user clicks through and sees the default blog index.
- Sites land with a worse first impression than they would if the agent
  silently did less but reported it accurately.
- Demos suffer most: the public-facing root URL is the first thing the
  prospect sees after signup, and it shows posts rather than the
  Home page the agent claims to have set up.

## Files

Investigation needed in three areas:

1. **Front-page settings ability** — search for any
   `update_option('show_on_front', …)` or `update_option('page_on_front',
   …)` call in `includes/Abilities/`. If absent, the agent has no tool to
   set the static homepage at all, and the system prompt should be updated
   to either (a) include such an ability or (b) instruct the agent not to
   claim it has done so.
2. **Site title (blogname) ability** — search for
   `update_blog_option(*, 'blogname', …)` / `update_option('blogname', …)`
   in `includes/Abilities/OptionsAbilities.php` and related files. The
   existing `ChangeRevertServiceTest` references
   `update_option('sd_test_blogname_revert', 'New Name')`, suggesting the
   plumbing exists; the question is whether the agent is calling it.
3. **Nav menu ability** — `MenuAbilities` (in
   `includes/Abilities/MenuAbilities.php`) already has
   `wp_create_nav_menu()` and add-item helpers (see line 468). So the tool
   exists; the agent appears not to call it, but reports it did.

The common thread: the agent's system prompt / completion checklist should
either drive the actual tool calls, or stop summarising work it did not do.

## Suggested fix

Two-layer fix:

1. **Behaviour:** Update the agent's site-build system prompt (or
   build-mode workflow) to explicitly call:
   - `wp_create_nav_menu` + add menu items + assign to a theme location for
     any "build me a website" intent.
   - `update_option('show_on_front', 'page')` +
     `update_option('page_on_front', $home_id)` after creating a "Home" or
     "Homepage" titled page.
   - `update_option('blogname', $derived_name)` when the user supplies or
     implies a site name (e.g. "The Golden Spoon" in the build prompt).
2. **Honesty:** Constrain the completion-summary step so the agent can only
   claim work that the `ChangeLogger` actually recorded for this
   conversation. Any unrecorded action should be omitted from the "I've
   done X" list. The plugin already has the change-logging plumbing in
   `includes/Core/ChangeLogger.php` and
   `includes/Bootstrap/ChangeLoggingHandler.php` — surface that record to
   the completion-summary tool/prompt.

## Verification

- Re-run the build prompt on a fresh demo. After fix, the WP-CLI checks in
  the reproduction section all return the expected values, and the agent's
  completion summary matches the recorded `ChangeLogger` entries verbatim.
- E2E test that runs the build prompt against a Playwright session and
  asserts on the post-build site state, not just the chat message.

## Related

- Plugin uses `bd` (beads) for task tracking; this issue can be mirrored to
  `bd` if that is preferred over GitHub.
- Issues on default-model validation, resend-uses-old-model, and missing
  streaming/tool-call indicators are filed separately in this batch.
