title: skill-load ability ignores auto-enable rules (block-themes returns skill_disabled on FSE sites)
body:
## Description

`SkillAbilities::handle_skill_load()` rejects `block-themes` (and any other
conditionally-enabled built-in skill) with `skill_disabled` even when the
skill should be auto-enabled for the active environment (FSE theme, active
plugin, multisite, etc.).

This breaks the documented "Adjacent Skills" handoff in `site-specification`:
when the agent loads `site-specification` first and then follows its
instruction to load `block-themes` on an FSE site, the second `skill-load`
fails. The user-visible effect is a confusing "Skill 'X' is disabled" error
mid-flow, with no path for the model to recover.

The root cause is a divergence between two API paths:

- `Skill::get_content_by_slug()` (used for auto-injection) checks
  `$skill->enabled` **and** falls through to
  `Skill::is_skill_auto_enabled($slug)` (`includes/Models/Skill.php:160-178`).
  This honours `PLUGIN_SKILL_MAP` and `theme_skill_map()`.
- `SkillAbilities::handle_skill_load()` (used for the
  `sd-ai-agent/skill-load` ability) checks `$skill->enabled` **only**
  (`includes/Abilities/SkillAbilities.php:123-126`) and returns `skill_disabled`.

`block-themes` and `classic-themes` ship with `enabled => false` by design
(see `Skill::theme_skill_map()` and the seed table around line 727 of
`Skill.php`) — they are intended to be auto-enabled by the active theme,
not by the admin.

## Expected Behavior

When the agent calls the `sd-ai-agent/skill-load` ability with a slug that
is conditionally auto-enabled for the current environment, the ability
should return the skill content (same behaviour as `get_content_by_slug`).

## Steps to Reproduce

1. On an FSE site (e.g. block theme such as `ollie`), ensure `block-themes`
   skill has `enabled = 0` in `wp_sd_ai_agent_skills` (this is the
   default for fresh installs).
2. Verify `Skill::is_skill_auto_enabled('block-themes')` returns `true`
   (it will, because `theme_skill_map()` matches FSE templates).
3. Start a new agent session and send any onboarding-style prompt (e.g.
   "Let's go" from the getting-started flow).
4. The agent loads `site-specification`, reads its "Adjacent Skills"
   section, and calls
   `sd-ai-agent/skill-load { "slug": "block-themes" }`.
5. The ability returns
   `{"error":"Skill 'block-themes' is disabled.","code":"skill_disabled"}`.

Reproduced via feedback report #10 (see Feedback Report below).

## Suggested Fix

Either:

- **Option A (preferred):** have `handle_skill_load()` defer to
  `Skill::get_content_by_slug()` (or a sibling helper that returns the
  full row) so the auto-enable rules apply consistently. Verify with the
  PHPUnit suite under `tests/php/` and add a regression test that loads
  `block-themes` on an FSE theme.
- **Option B:** promote `is_skill_auto_enabled()` to public API and call
  it from `handle_skill_load()` after the explicit-enabled check. Same
  regression test required.

Either way, error messaging should distinguish "skill genuinely off" from
"skill conditionally off and current environment does not enable it" so
the model can react sensibly when a skill really is unavailable.

## Files to Modify

- `includes/Abilities/SkillAbilities.php` (lines 108-153) — fix the
  enabled check.
- `includes/Models/Skill.php` — only if Option B is chosen (visibility
  change on `is_skill_auto_enabled`).
- `tests/php/...` — add regression test covering FSE theme +
  `block-themes`, classic theme + `classic-themes`, and the truly-disabled
  case.

## Verification

- `composer phpstan` clean.
- `npm run test:php` covers the new regression test.
- Manual: on a dev site with `ollie` (or any FSE theme), call the ability
  via REST and confirm it returns content. Repeat with a classic theme
  and `classic-themes`. Then disable the skill *and* set the theme to one
  that does NOT auto-enable it, and confirm `skill_disabled` is still
  returned in that case (negative path).

## Environment

- Plugin version: 1.13.0 (latest at time of report)
- WordPress: 7.0-RC2
- PHP: 8.4.20
- Multisite: yes
- Provider: ultimate-ai-connector-anthropic-max / claude-sonnet-4-6
- Theme: ollie (FSE)
- Active plugins: ai-agent, ai-provider-for-anthropic-max,
  ai-provider-for-any-openai-compatible

## Feedback Report

Report ID: 10 (submitted 2026-05-19 00:48:11)
User description: "skills not found or not allowed. WTF?"

**Task ID:** `t226` | **Status:** open | **Estimate:** `~24h`
**Logged:** 2026-05-13
**Tags:** `enhancement` `parent-task` `plan` `onboarding-theme-builder`

## Description

Block theme generation in onboarding (Automattic wp-site-creator inspired)

## Plan: Purpose

Add a "Design a custom theme" branch to onboarding. After provider setup, fresh-install users can opt into a 4-phase agent conversation that interviews them about their site, presents 3 distinct topic-grounded design directions as HTML previews, and on selection generates a complete block theme (theme.json, style.css, functions.php, templates/, parts/) deployed to `wp-content/themes/<slug>/` and activated — all inside the existing chat UI.
Architecture adapted from [Automattic/wordpress-agent-skills/claude-code/wp-site-creator](https://github.com/Automattic/wordpress-agent-skills/tree/trunk/claude-code/wp-site-creator). We take the 4-phase flow, the site-specification skill, and the topic-grounded design thinking. We do NOT take their Claude-Code-plugin packaging, WordPress Studio CLI dependency, parallel Task() subagent pattern, or block-fixer Node script (we have `validate-block-content` already).
Closes the PLANS.md "AI site generation from prompt" P0 gap on the visual-container side (t060-t062 handle pages; this handles themes).

<details><summary>Plan: Context & Architecture</summary>


**Context**

**Source comparison.** Studied [Automattic's `/quick-build` command](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Automattic/wordpress-agent-skills/trunk/claude-code/wp-site-creator/commands/quick-build.md), [`/preview-designs`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Automattic/wordpress-agent-skills/trunk/claude-code/wp-site-creator/commands/preview-designs.md), and [site-specification SKILL](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Automattic/wordpress-agent-skills/trunk/claude-code/wp-site-creator/skills/site-specification/SKILL.md) against our `OnboardingManager` + `BootstrapPrompt` + `OnboardingWizard` + `OnboardingBootstrap`. Our existing flow is discovery-only: explores the site, presents 4 starter prompts. Their flow generates a complete theme. Fresh-install conversion is the opportunity.
**Capability gap.** We have most of what we need: `create-block-content`, `validate-block-content`, `list-block-templates`, `list-block-patterns`, `update-global-styles`, `get-theme-json`, and `FileAbilities` (writes anywhere under wp-content when `FILE_WRITE` cap is on). Missing: directory + theme.json scaffold ability and a switch_theme wrapper. That's two new abilities, both small.
**Why phases not one PR.** Phase 1 (site-spec skill) alone improves every content-creation interaction (post drafts, page builds, product descriptions). Phase 2 (block-themes skill expansion) compounds for all theme-aware work, not just onboarding. Phases 3-4 are where the theme-builder onboarding actually lights up. Each phase ships value independently — if we stop after Phase 2 we've still made the agent meaningfully better.
**What we explicitly are NOT doing:**
- Generating Gutenberg patterns library (separate work — t060-t062)
- WooCommerce-aware theme variants (Phase 3 ships a generic theme; Woo-specific templates are follow-up)
- Multi-language theme generation
- Child-theme generation
- AI-redesigning existing themes
- Adopting WordPress Studio CLI (irrelevant inside a running WP install)
- Telemetry scripts from the Automattic plugin
**Topic-grounded design thinking.** Their key insight: don't generate "modern dark theme / minimalist light theme / colorful theme" — instead, ask what aesthetic worlds the *topic* could authentically inhabit. A craft brewery is not "generic dark/light/colorful"; it's taproom-warmth vs label-art-maximalism vs industrial-grain-and-steel. This is what Phase 4's skill captures.
**No stock image URLs ever.** Their prompts repeat this rule; we adopt it. Generated themes rely on CSS gradients, color blocks, and typography when the user hasn't supplied imagery.

Phase 2 (block-themes skill expansion) compounds for all theme-aware work, not just onboarding. Phases 3-4 are where the theme-builder onboarding actually lights up. </details>

- [x] (2026-05-13) Phase 1: `site-specification` skill — markdown + new memory category `site_brief` ~3h — t226a (merged in PR #1371)

</details>

## Task Brief

# t226 — Block theme generation in onboarding (inspired by Automattic wp-site-creator)

> **ID note:** filed 2026-05-13 as t170, renumbered to t226 in this PR to avoid collision with a completed t170 ("Benchmark validation: ac-016 restaurant website end-to-end test", merged 2026-04-09 as PR #848). Phase children use the t226a–t226d suffix scheme to keep the parent-child relationship visible in TODO.md without colliding with adjacent numeric IDs (t227+ were already taken).

## Pre-flight

- [x] Memory recall: `wp-site-creator wordpress agent skills` → 0 hits — no prior lessons; new territory in this repo, recall confirmed fresh
- [x] Discovery pass: 0 open PRs and 0 in-flight commits touch `OnboardingManager.php`, `BootstrapPrompt.php`, `onboarding-wizard.js`, `onboarding-bootstrap.js`, or `block-themes.md` in last 48h (verified on branch `fix/orphan-tool-result-trim`)
- [x] File refs verified: 8 refs checked, all present at HEAD (`OnboardingManager.php:341-456`, `BootstrapPrompt.php`, `onboarding-bootstrap.js`, `onboarding-wizard.js:326-463`, `GeneratePluginAbility.php`, `BlockAbilities.php:217-246`, `GlobalStylesAbilities.php`, `block-themes.md`, `kadence-theme.md`)
- [x] Tier: `tier:thinking` — parent task with UX + system-prompt design decisions; phase children re-evaluate their own tier when filed
- [x] Seeded draft PR decision recorded: skipped — parent task, no implementation. Phase 1 child should be the first PR.

## Session origin

Filed 2026-05-13 after studying [Automattic/wordpress-agent-skills/claude-code/wp-site-creator](https://github.com/Automattic/wordpress-agent-skills/tree/trunk/claude-code/wp-site-creator)
and comparing it with our existing onboarding flow (`OnboardingManager`,
`BootstrapPrompt`, `OnboardingWizard`, `OnboardingBootstrap`). Their plugin
generates a complete WordPress block theme from a one-line description via a
4-phase agent flow. Our onboarding is purely discovery — we explore an
existing site and present starter prompts, but we never *create* a theme.
For a fresh-install user, having the agent design and activate a custom
block theme during onboarding would be a real differentiator (currently
only 10Web/ZipWP do this, and neither runs as a plugin you own).

## What

Add a "Design a custom theme" branch to onboarding that, after the user has
a working AI provider, can interview the user, present 3 distinct visual
design directions, and on selection generate a complete activated block
theme — all inside the existing chat UI, without leaving WordPress.

The deliverable is a working onboarding branch where:

1. After provider setup, the user is offered three onboarding modes:
   - **Explore my existing site** (current behaviour, default for non-empty installs)
   - **Design a custom theme** (new, default for fresh installs)
   - **Skip — just chat** (current behaviour)
2. The theme-builder branch runs a 4-phase conversation:
   - **Phase 1** Interview: extract a site spec (name, type, audience, tone, brand keywords, key sections, typography). Uses the new `site-specification` skill.
   - **Phase 2** Present 3 topic-grounded design directions as HTML previews stored in `wp-content/uploads/sd-ai-agent/design-previews/<session>/design-{1,2,3}.html` and shown inline in chat.
   - **Phase 3** User picks a direction (1, 2, 3, or "2 but darker"). Modifications fold back into the spec.
   - **Phase 4** Generate the full block theme into `wp-content/themes/<slug>/` (theme.json, style.css, functions.php, parts/header.html, parts/footer.html, templates/index.html, templates/page.html) and activate it.
3. All theme files are validated via existing `sd-ai-agent/validate-block-content` before write.

We do **not** ship the Automattic plugin verbatim — it's a Claude Code
plugin, not a WordPress plugin, and depends on WordPress Studio CLI which
isn't relevant inside a running WP install. We adapt the *architecture*
(phases, skills, references) to our agent loop.

## Why

1. **Fresh-install conversion.** Right now a fresh-install user activates
   the plugin, sees an empty discovery summary, and gets generic starter
   prompts. They are not impressed and they bounce. A "design a theme for
   my SaaS in 5 minutes" flow is what 10Web and ZipWP use to convert.
2. **Showcases agent capability.** Generating a coherent block theme
   requires our agent to chain `create-block-content`, `validate-block-content`,
   `update-global-styles`, `list-block-patterns`, file writes, and theme
   activation — exactly the kind of multi-step tool-calling we built the
   loop for. It's a credible demo.
3. **PLANS.md gap closure.** PLANS.md identifies "AI site generation from
   prompt" as P0 (t060-t062 line) but those tasks are about generating
   *pages*, not themes. This complements them — themes are the visual
   container, pages are the content. Both are needed.
4. **Reusable skill scaffolding.** The `site-specification` skill alone
   improves every content-creation interaction (page builds, post drafts,
   product descriptions), not just onboarding.

## Tier

`tier:thinking` — parent/planning task. UX decisions, system-prompt design,
and integration sequencing are judgment work. The 4 phase children below
are individually `tier:standard` (skills + abilities + UI wiring with
clear file targets), but Phase 3 specifically may be `tier:thinking`.

## Phases

This is a parent task. Each phase is a separate PR.

- **Phase 1 — Site-specification skill** ~3h — add `includes/Models/skills/site-specification.md` mirroring Automattic's per-site-type inference tables. New memory category `site_brief` for storing extracted specs across sessions. No UI changes. [auto-fire:on-prior-merge]
- **Phase 2 — Block-themes skill expansion** ~4h — expand `includes/Models/skills/block-themes.md` with theme.json patterns, template-part composition, animation/motion classes, and editor-visibility CSS lifted from Automattic's `wordpress-block-theming.md` reference (29KB → distil to ~400 lines, keep our existing 150-line structure as the spine). [auto-fire:on-prior-merge]
- **Phase 3 — Theme-builder onboarding branch** ~12h — new `ThemeBuilderPrompt` (mirrors `BootstrapPrompt`), new REST endpoint `POST /onboarding/theme-builder-start`, choose-mode UI in `OnboardingWizard`, and two new abilities: `sd-ai-agent/scaffold-block-theme` (creates the directory + theme.json + style.css + functions.php) and `sd-ai-agent/activate-theme` (wraps `switch_theme()`). Existing `FileAbilities` handles HTML file writes. [auto-fire:on-prior-merge]
- **Phase 4 — Design-system reference skills** ~5h — add `includes/Models/skills/design-system-aesthetics.md` covering the "topic-grounded visual worlds" framework (brewery → taproom vs label-art vs industrial), referenced by Phase 3's system prompt during the design-direction step.

Each phase PR uses `For #NNN` referencing the parent issue until Phase 4
ships, which uses `Closes #NNN`.

## How (Approach)

### Progressive Context Plan

- **Read first:** `includes/Core/BootstrapPrompt.php` and `includes/Core/OnboardingManager.php` — the discovery-bootstrap flow this work mirrors and extends.
- **Read first:** `src/components/onboarding-bootstrap.js` and `src/components/onboarding-wizard.js` — the React entry points the new branch plugs into.
- **Load only if:** [Automattic wp-site-creator commands/quick-build.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Automattic/wordpress-agent-skills/trunk/claude-code/wp-site-creator/commands/quick-build.md) — only when designing Phase 3's system prompt; we don't copy it, we use it as a reference for phase ordering.
- **Load only if:** [Automattic site-specification SKILL.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Automattic/wordpress-agent-skills/trunk/claude-code/wp-site-creator/skills/site-specification/SKILL.md) — direct source for Phase 1 inference tables.
- **Stop when:** the parent issue body lists 4 phase children with clear file targets and acceptance criteria each.

### Files to Modify (across all phases)

- `NEW: includes/Models/skills/site-specification.md` — Phase 1
- `EDIT: includes/Models/skills/block-themes.md` — Phase 2 (expand from 150 → ~400 lines)
- `NEW: includes/Core/ThemeBuilderPrompt.php` — Phase 3 (model on `BootstrapPrompt.php`)
- `EDIT: includes/Core/OnboardingManager.php` — Phase 3 (add `rest_theme_builder_start` REST callback paralleling `rest_bootstrap_start`)
- `NEW: includes/Abilities/ScaffoldBlockThemeAbility.php` — Phase 3 (model on `GeneratePluginAbility.php`)
- `NEW: includes/Abilities/ActivateThemeAbility.php` — Phase 3 (wraps `switch_theme()` with cap check `switch_themes`)
- `EDIT: src/components/onboarding-wizard.js` — Phase 3 (add mode-picker step between provider setup and finish)
- `NEW: src/components/onboarding-theme-builder.js` — Phase 3 (new entry component, parallel to `onboarding-bootstrap.js`)
- `NEW: includes/Models/skills/design-system-aesthetics.md` — Phase 4

### Implementation Steps (high-level — each phase brief will detail its own)

1. **Phase 1:** Read Automattic's `site-specification/SKILL.md` (already in this session's context), adapt to our skill markdown format (matches `block-themes.md` and `kadence-theme.md` style), wire the new memory category `site_brief` via `Memory::create()`. Test: agent extracts spec from "build me a theme for my coffee shop Bean & Brew" and stores it in memory.

2. **Phase 2:** Diff Automattic's `wordpress-block-theming.md` (29KB) against our `block-themes.md` (150 lines). Lift the theme.json color/typography presets, animation classes, prefers-reduced-motion patterns, and editor-styles-wrapper CSS guidance. Keep our existing tool references intact. Test: word count and section ratchet, plus a manual read-pass for accuracy.

3. **Phase 3:** Largest phase. Subphases:
   - **3a** New abilities: `ScaffoldBlockThemeAbility` + `ActivateThemeAbility`. Cap gates: `install_themes` and `switch_themes` respectively.
   - **3b** New `ThemeBuilderPrompt` class generating a 4-phase system instruction (interview → designs → choose → build). Use `sd-ai-agent/memory-save` after each phase to checkpoint state.
   - **3c** REST endpoint `POST /onboarding/theme-builder-start` paralleling `rest_bootstrap_start`. Returns `{ session_id, kickoff_message, theme_builder_system_prompt }`.
   - **3d** UI: add a "Choose your start" step to `OnboardingWizard` with 3 buttons. New `OnboardingThemeBuilder` React component parallel to `OnboardingBootstrap`. Wire selection through the existing `bootstrap_system_prompt` channel.
   - **3e** E2E test: from a fresh install, complete the flow end-to-end, verify a theme exists at `wp-content/themes/<slug>/` and is the active stylesheet.

4. **Phase 4:** Topic-grounded aesthetics skill. Document the "explore visual worlds" thinking (brewery → 3 distinct authentic worlds, not generic style swaps). Reference from Phase 3's system prompt when generating design directions.

### Verification (parent task — phase children specify their own)

```bash
# Phase 1 lands
test -f includes/Models/skills/site-specification.md

# Phase 2 lands (skill expanded)
wc -l includes/Models/skills/block-themes.md  # should be 350-450 lines

# Phase 3 lands (E2E)
npm run test:e2e:playwright -- tests/e2e/onboarding-theme-builder.spec.js

# Phase 4 lands
test -f includes/Models/skills/design-system-aesthetics.md
```

### Files Scope

Parent task — phase children declare their own scopes. As an aggregate
guard, the following globs cover all phases:

- `includes/Models/skills/site-specification.md`
- `includes/Models/skills/block-themes.md`
- `includes/Models/skills/design-system-aesthetics.md`
- `includes/Core/ThemeBuilderPrompt.php`
- `includes/Core/OnboardingManager.php`
- `includes/Abilities/ScaffoldBlockThemeAbility.php`
- `includes/Abilities/ActivateThemeAbility.php`
- `src/components/onboarding-wizard.js`
- `src/components/onboarding-theme-builder.js`
- `src/components/__tests__/OnboardingThemeBuilder.test.js`
- `tests/e2e/onboarding-theme-builder.spec.js`
- `todo/PLANS.md`
- `todo/tasks/t226-brief.md`
- `todo/tasks/t226[a-z]-*.md`
- `TODO.md`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Phase 1 PR merged: `site-specification` skill markdown exists with all 7 site-type inference tables (SaaS, e-commerce, professional-services, restaurant, portfolio, blog, non-profit) and at least 3 worked examples (coffee shop, law firm, esports team).

  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: bash
    run: "test -f includes/Models/skills/site-specification.md && grep -c '^### ' includes/Models/skills/site-specification.md | xargs test 7 -le"
  ```

- [ ] Phase 2 PR merged: `block-themes.md` expanded with theme.json presets, animation classes, and editor-visibility CSS sections.

  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: codebase
    pattern: "Editor Visibility|editor-styles-wrapper|prefers-reduced-motion"
    path: "includes/Models/skills/block-themes.md"
  ```

- [ ] Phase 3 PR merged: theme-builder branch reachable from onboarding; activates a generated block theme on a fresh install.

  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: bash
    run: "test -f includes/Core/ThemeBuilderPrompt.php && test -f includes/Abilities/ScaffoldBlockThemeAbility.php && test -f includes/Abilities/ActivateThemeAbility.php"
  ```

- [ ] Phase 4 PR merged: `design-system-aesthetics.md` skill exists and is referenced from `ThemeBuilderPrompt`.

  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: codebase
    pattern: "design-system-aesthetics"
    path: "includes/Core/ThemeBuilderPrompt.php"
  ```

- [ ] No regression to existing discovery onboarding: the "Explore my existing site" branch continues to call `/onboarding/bootstrap-start` and behaves identically to today.

  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: codebase
    pattern: "bootstrap-start"
    path: "src/components/onboarding-bootstrap.js"
  ```

- [ ] Lint + tests clean on each phase PR: `npm run lint:js && npm run lint:php && npm run test:php`.

- [ ] No raw `wp-content/themes/` writes happen without `current_user_can('install_themes')` gating in the new abilities.

  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: codebase
    pattern: "current_user_can.*install_themes"
    path: "includes/Abilities/ScaffoldBlockThemeAbility.php"
  ```

## Context & Decisions

- **Adopt the architecture, not the code.** Automattic's plugin is a Claude Code plugin coupled to WordPress Studio CLI. We're a WP plugin running inside the install. We take the 4-phase flow, the skill structure, and the topic-grounded design thinking — we do *not* take the `.claude-plugin/` packaging, the `studio` CLI calls, the `block-fixer/cli.js` Node script (we have `validate-block-content`), or the parallel `Task()` subagent pattern (we run one model per `AgentLoop` iteration).
- **No stock image URLs ever.** Automattic's prompts repeat this rule; we should too. Generated themes use CSS gradients, color blocks, and typography for visual richness when the user hasn't provided their own images.
- **Phase boundary discipline.** Phases are independently shippable. If we ship only Phases 1–2 and stop, the site-specification skill still improves every other interaction. Phases 3–4 are where the theme-builder onboarding lights up.
- **Why not a full PRD?** The deliverable is well-scoped and adapts a known reference architecture. Phase briefs carry the detail; a separate PRD would duplicate this brief.
- **Non-goals:**
  - Generating Gutenberg patterns library (covered separately by t060-t062 page-generation work).
  - WooCommerce-aware theme variants (Phase 3 generates a generic theme; WooCommerce-specific templates can be a follow-up).
  - Multi-language theme generation.
  - Child-theme generation.
  - Importing existing themes and "AI-redesigning" them.

## Relevant Files

- `includes/Core/BootstrapPrompt.php` — model for `ThemeBuilderPrompt`.
- `includes/Core/OnboardingManager.php:341-456` — `rest_bootstrap_start` is the pattern for the new `rest_theme_builder_start`.
- `src/components/onboarding-bootstrap.js` — parallel structure for `onboarding-theme-builder.js`.
- `src/components/onboarding-wizard.js:326-463` — the step array gets a new mode-picker step inserted.
- `includes/Abilities/GeneratePluginAbility.php` — closest existing scaffolding ability to model `ScaffoldBlockThemeAbility` on.
- `includes/Abilities/BlockAbilities.php:217-246` — existing `list-block-templates` and validate/create patterns the new theme-builder leverages.
- `includes/Abilities/GlobalStylesAbilities.php` — theme.json update patterns we reuse.
- `includes/Models/skills/block-themes.md` — Phase 2 target.
- `includes/Models/skills/kadence-theme.md` — alternate skill style reference.
- [Automattic site-specification](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Automattic/wordpress-agent-skills/trunk/claude-code/wp-site-creator/skills/site-specification/SKILL.md) — Phase 1 source.
- [Automattic quick-build](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Automattic/wordpress-agent-skills/trunk/claude-code/wp-site-creator/commands/quick-build.md) — Phase 3 architectural reference.
- [Automattic preview-designs](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Automattic/wordpress-agent-skills/trunk/claude-code/wp-site-creator/commands/preview-designs.md) — Phase 3 design-direction reference.
- [Automattic wordpress-block-theming reference (29KB)](https://github.com/Automattic/wordpress-agent-skills/blob/trunk/claude-code/wp-site-creator/references/wordpress-block-theming.md) — Phase 2 source.

## Dependencies

- **Blocked by:** none (Phase 1 can start immediately).
- **Blocks:** future fresh-install onboarding metrics and resale-API "white-label theme generation" follow-ups.
- **External:** none. All work happens inside the plugin and the WP install. No new API providers, no new credentials.

## Estimate Breakdown

| Phase | Time | Notes |
|-------|------|-------|
| Phase 1 (site-spec skill) | ~3h | Markdown only + 1 memory category constant |
| Phase 2 (block-themes expansion) | ~4h | Distil 29KB reference into ~250 added lines |

| **Total** | **~24h** | Spread over 3-5 calendar weeks of background work |

title: feat(onboarding): add Restart Setup Assistant control to Settings → Advanced
body:
## Goal

Add a "Restart Setup Assistant" affordance to Settings → Advanced that resets onboarding state and re-launches the Onboarding v2 direct-routing gate (Setup Assistant agent for sites with content, Theme Builder agent for empty installs).

## Why

PR #1503 deleted the legacy multi-step wizard and replaced it with a direct-routing gate in `src/admin-page/index.js`. There is currently no user-facing way to re-fire that gate once `onboarding_complete=true`. Users who want to re-run the Setup Assistant (e.g., to re-introduce the agent to the site after major content changes, or because they dismissed the first session by accident) have no remediation.

This is the v2-correct version of the affordance PR #1502 attempted (and PR #1503 reverted). The behaviour is different: **it does not re-launch a wizard** — it clears onboarding state and the existing v2 gate fires on the next chat-page mount, dropping the user into the right agent automatically.

## Scope

### Files to modify

- `includes/Core/OnboardingManager.php`
  - Add a `reset()` instance method that clears: `COMPLETE_OPTION`, `BOOTSTRAP_SESSION_OPTION`, `THEME_BUILDER_SESSION_OPTION`, and any onboarding-related scan options.
  - Register a new REST route `POST /sd-ai-agent/v1/onboarding/reset`.
  - Add a `rest_reset()` handler that calls `reset()`, calls `Settings::update(['onboarding_complete' => false])`, and returns `{success: true, message: '…', chat_url: admin_url('admin.php?page=sd-ai-agent#/chat')}`.
  - Permission callback: `current_user_can('manage_options')`.

- `src/settings-page/settings-app.js`
  - Add a new "Onboarding" section at the bottom of the Advanced tab.
  - Button label: "Restart Setup Assistant" (NOT "Restart Onboarding Wizard" — the wizard is gone).
  - Inline help text explaining what it does ("Clears onboarding state. Next time you open the chat, the Setup Assistant will reintroduce itself.").
  - `window.confirm()` prompt before POSTing.
  - Busy state while the request is in flight.
  - On success: `Notice` with a "Open AI Agent chat →" link to the returned `chat_url`.
  - On error: `Notice` with the error message.
  - Mirror onboarding_complete locally so the section state stays consistent without forcing a settings save round-trip.
  - Use the canonical text domain: `__( '…', 'superdav-ai-agent' )`.

- `tests/SdAiAgent/Core/OnboardingManagerTest.php`
  - Test 1: `/onboarding/reset` route is registered.
  - Test 2: Calling reset clears `COMPLETE_OPTION`, `BOOTSTRAP_SESSION_OPTION`, `THEME_BUILDER_SESSION_OPTION`.
  - Test 3: REST response shape — `success: true`, `chat_url` set, includes `#/chat`.
  - Test 4: Settings `onboarding_complete` is flipped to `false` after reset.

### Reference pattern

PR #1502 (https://github.com/Ultimate-Multisite/superdav-ai-agent/pull/1502) shows the previous shape — REUSE the endpoint structure and the React button structure, but:

1. Change button label and help text per v2 (no "wizard" language).
2. The REST handler can be cleaner since v2 doesn't need to clear a `TRIGGERED_OPTION` (that path is gone).
3. Tests should assert the v2-correct shape (no wizard re-launch expectations).

PR #1503 (the v2 cleanup) is the authority on the current onboarding architecture — read it before implementing to confirm the direct-routing gate behaviour you're triggering.

### Out of scope

- Changing the v2 gate logic in `src/admin-page/index.js`.
- Resetting AI provider configuration (that lives in WordPress Connectors and is orthogonal to onboarding state).
- Resetting agent memories, RAG indexes, conversation history, or any agent-created artefacts.
- Bringing back any wizard, mode picker, or interview UI.

## Verification

```bash
composer phpstan
composer phpcs
npm run lint:js
npm run build
npm run test:js
npm run test:php
```

Manual:

1. With `onboarding_complete=true`, open Settings → Advanced → Onboarding section → click "Restart Setup Assistant" → confirm.
2. Expect Notice with link.
3. Click link → `admin.php?page=sd-ai-agent#/chat` opens.
4. `AdminPageApp` re-runs the `/wp/v2/posts` probe and mounts `OnboardingBootstrap` (site with content) or `OnboardingThemeBuilder` (empty install).
5. The agent auto-sends a kickoff message and is ready for input.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Button labelled "Restart Setup Assistant" (not "Wizard") with confirmation prompt.
- [ ] REST endpoint `POST /sd-ai-agent/v1/onboarding/reset` exists, requires `manage_options`, returns `{success, message, chat_url}`.
- [ ] PHPUnit tests cover route registration, option clearing, settings flip, and response shape.
- [ ] PHPCS, PHPStan, ESLint, build, Jest all clean.
- [ ] No re-introduction of `onboarding-wizard.js`, `onboarding-interview.js`, or `.sdaa-wizard*` CSS.

## Dependencies

Depends on PR #1503 being merged.

## Caveats

- Resetting onboarding does NOT close the user's existing chat session — it just makes the gate re-fire on the next admin-page mount. If the user already has a chat session open in the tab, they should reload to see the bootstrapper.
- If the site has neither content nor a configured provider, the connector gate takes precedence over the bootstrapper. The reset endpoint should still succeed and let the connector gate render — no special-casing needed in `OnboardingManager::reset()`.

title: bug(activate-theme): validate WP version + PHP requirements before switch_theme()
body:
## Summary

`ActivateThemeAbility` calls `switch_theme()` without first validating that the
target theme's `Requires at least:` and `Requires PHP:` headers are satisfied by
the running environment. When the requirements are NOT met:

1. The ability returns `success=true` (because `switch_theme()` does update the
   option), but
2. WordPress's `validate_current_theme()` reverts to the default theme on the
   next page load (silent revert), and
3. The AgentLoop appears to hang — the user sees a "Running
   sd-ai-agent/activate-theme…" spinner indefinitely, no provider trace is
   emitted after the tool call, and the `wp_sd_ai_agent_active_jobs` row stays
   in `processing` forever.

This is the bug that ended my manual Theme Builder onboarding walkthrough on
2026-05-18 against a WP **6.9.4** install with a theme whose generated
`style.css` declared `Requires at least: 7.0`. The plugin's own AGENTS.md states
"Requires WordPress 7.0+", so the scaffolded value was internally consistent
with the plugin — but the environment was one minor version behind. No surface
error reached the user; the build phase silently died.

## Reproduction

Setup:

```bash
# WordPress install at version < the plugin's stated 7.0 minimum
wp core version             # e.g. 6.9.4
wp plugin activate superdav-ai-agent
```

Steps:

1. Open the plugin admin page on an empty site → Theme Builder onboarding
   mounts.
2. Complete the interview, pick a design direction, instruct the agent to
   build it.
3. Agent scaffolds the theme under `wp-content/themes/{slug}/` (succeeds).
4. Agent emits `wpab__sd-ai-agent__activate-theme {stylesheet: "{slug}"}`.
5. Inspect `wp_sd_ai_agent_provider_trace` — the response for the activate-
   theme call is the LAST trace. No further provider calls are made.
6. UI shows "Running sd-ai-agent/activate-theme…" forever; reload does not
   recover progress (see also linked kickoff-loop and stuck-job issues).

Direct repro of the underlying validation gap (no agent needed):

```bash
# Use any installed theme whose style.css "Requires at least:" exceeds wp core version.
wp theme activate {slug}
# => Error: Current WordPress version does not meet minimum requirements for {Theme Name}.
# wp-cli reports it; the plugin's ActivateThemeAbility does not.
```

Evidence from the walkthrough (provider_trace IDs):

- Trace `805/806` (first attempt): assistant text "Now let me activate the
  theme and create all four pages simultaneously:", single tool_use for
  `activate-theme {stylesheet: "bramble-and-bean"}`, stop_reason `tool_use`.
- Trace `837/838` (second attempt): same pattern, `activate-theme` is the
  last call. No further messages traced.
- `wp option get stylesheet` continues to return `twentytwentyfive` after
  both attempts — `switch_theme()` ran but was reverted on the next request.

## Impact

- **Onboarding "Build" phase fails silently on every WP install below 7.0**
  even though the plugin documents 7.0 as the minimum (a wide swath of
  shared hosts still on 6.7 / 6.8).
- The user sees a perfect interview, three beautiful design previews, a
  successful theme scaffold — then hangs on the LAST step with no
  diagnostic. Worst possible UX positioning.
- AgentLoop's `processing` job row never updates → orphan jobs accumulate.
- Could similarly fail on PHP version mismatch (e.g. plugin sets
  `Requires PHP: 8.2` and the host is on 8.0).

## Files

- `includes/Abilities/ActivateThemeAbility.php`
  - `execute_callback()` (lines 77–142): currently checks `$theme->exists()`
    and `$theme->errors()` but does NOT call
    `validate_theme_requirements( $theme )`. `WP_Theme::errors()` is only
    populated by `scandir()` failures — it does NOT carry the requirements
    error.
  - Add a requirements check BEFORE `switch_theme( $stylesheet )` using
    WordPress's `validate_theme_requirements( $stylesheet )` (returns
    `true` or `WP_Error`). On `WP_Error`, return a new
    `WP_Error('sd_ai_agent_theme_requirements_unmet', $err->get_error_message())`
    so the AgentLoop receives a tool result it can act on.

- `tests/SdAiAgent/Abilities/ActivateThemeAbilityTest.php` (create if
  missing — mirror the existing ability-level unit test pattern in
  `tests/SdAiAgent/Abilities/`).
  - Add a test case that stages a theme with `Requires at least: 99.9.9`
    on disk and asserts the ability returns
    `sd_ai_agent_theme_requirements_unmet` without flipping the
    stylesheet option.

### Reference pattern

WordPress core's own theme installer path:

- `wp-admin/themes.php` calls `validate_theme_requirements( $stylesheet )`
  before redirecting to the activation handler. Mirror that gate.
- `wp-cli/wp-cli` (the `wp theme activate` command, in
  `vendor/wp-cli/extension-command/src/Theme_Command.php`) calls the same
  function and produces the exact error wording we want surfaced.

## Out of scope

- Do NOT also patch `switch_theme()` itself or core's revert behaviour —
  the fix is entirely inside `ActivateThemeAbility`.
- Do NOT remove the existing `$theme->errors()` check — it catches a
  different class of failure (scandir, malformed style.css) and is still
  useful.
- Don't change `ScaffoldBlockThemeAbility`'s default `Requires at least:`
  value (that's a separate concern, currently consistent with plugin docs).

## Verification

```bash
composer phpstan
composer phpcs
composer test -- --filter ActivateThemeAbilityTest
npm run lint:php
```

Manual:

1. Apply fix; on WP 6.9.x install a theme whose `style.css` requires 7.0.
2. Drive an agent build that ends in activate-theme.
3. Confirm: the agent receives a structured tool error, posts a user-
   visible message ("This theme requires WordPress 7.0; your site runs
   6.9.4. Lower the requirement or upgrade WordPress before activating."),
   and the AgentLoop continues (it does NOT hang).
4. `wp option get stylesheet` is unchanged.
5. The `wp_sd_ai_agent_active_jobs` row eventually transitions out of
   `processing` (via natural loop completion, not timeout).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `validate_theme_requirements()` (or equivalent compatible call) is
      invoked before `switch_theme()` in `execute_callback()`.
- [ ] On requirement failure, returns
      `WP_Error('sd_ai_agent_theme_requirements_unmet', <core message>)`
      instead of silently switching.
- [ ] Unit test covers the version-too-low case AND the
      PHP-version-too-low case.
- [ ] PHPCS, PHPStan, PHPUnit pass.
- [ ] Manual walkthrough on WP < plugin minimum no longer hangs at
      activate-theme — agent reports the error and the user can take
      action.

## Caveats

- `validate_theme_requirements()` has been in core since WP 5.5 and is
  always available on supported WP versions for this plugin.
- The ability's permission_callback still requires `switch_themes` cap —
  unchanged.
- This bug compounds with the "active-jobs row stuck" and "kickoff loop"
  issues filed alongside; fixing this one alone restores forward progress
  but does NOT fix the orphan-job housekeeping.

## Related

- Active-jobs stuck-in-processing bug (filed in same batch).
- Theme-builder kickoff loop bug (filed in same batch).
- PR #1503 (Onboarding v2 cleanup) — the v2 flow that hits this bug.

title: bug(theme-builder): kickoff message re-sent on every reload during build phase
body:
## Summary

The Theme Builder onboarding agent re-sends its kickoff message ("I'd like to
design a custom block theme for my site. Please start the interview.") **every
time the admin chat page is reloaded**, until `sd_ai_agent_settings.onboarding_complete=true`
is flipped some other way. Observed twice during a single manual walkthrough.

Root cause is a deliberate asymmetry between the two onboarding REST endpoints:

- `/onboarding/bootstrap-start` (Setup Assistant flow) sets `onboarding_complete=true`
  on first call, which prevents the gate in `src/admin-page/index.js` from re-mounting
  `OnboardingBootstrap` on reload.
- `/onboarding/theme-builder-start` does NOT set that flag. The intent was to
  keep the Theme Builder mounted during a multi-turn build, but the side-effect
  is the React component re-mounts on every reload and re-fires its kickoff
  effect.

`OnboardingThemeBuilder`'s `bootstrappedRef.current` guard is component-local
React state — it resets to `false` on every mount, so it does nothing to stop
the loop across reloads.

## Reproduction

1. Empty WP install (no published posts), provider configured, fresh session.
2. Open `wp-admin/admin.php?page=sd-ai-agent` → ThemeBuilder mounts and the
   agent auto-sends "I'd like to design a custom block theme…".
3. Answer Q1 of the interview.
4. Reload the page (Ctrl+R / Cmd+R).
5. **Observed**: ThemeBuilder re-mounts, the kickoff message is sent AGAIN
   (the conversation now has two identical user-side kickoffs and two
   greetings from the Designer).

Inspect server-side:

```bash
wp option get sd_ai_agent_onboarding_complete    # empty / false
wp option get sd_ai_agent_settings --format=json | jq .onboarding_complete   # false
```

Inspect provider trace: there will be two near-identical provider calls
with the same kickoff message, several seconds apart.

## Impact

- Conversation history quickly fills with duplicate kickoffs and greetings
  → confusing for users, wasteful on tokens.
- Mid-build reload (which users do during long activate-theme/build steps,
  especially when other bugs trigger hangs) wipes context: the agent re-
  greets, asks the interview questions again, and may re-scaffold over the
  partially-built theme.
- Compounds with the activate-theme-hang bug — when that fails and users
  reload to "try again", they lose all design selections and re-enter the
  interview.

## Files

### Server side

- `includes/Core/OnboardingManager.php`
  - The handler for `/onboarding/theme-builder-start` is the one that does
    NOT flip `onboarding_complete`. Compare it with the
    `/onboarding/bootstrap-start` handler immediately above it.
  - Add a new dedicated option (not the global onboarding flag) e.g.
    `sd_ai_agent_theme_builder_started` (boolean), set to `true` on first
    successful call.
  - Return `started_at` and `session_id` so the client can hydrate without
    re-issuing the kickoff.

### Client side

- `src/components/onboarding-theme-builder.js`
  - The `bootstrappedRef` guard is component-local. Replace it with a
    server-truth check: on mount, GET `/onboarding/theme-builder-start`
    (or a new `/onboarding/theme-builder-status`) and skip the kickoff
    POST if the server already records a started session for the current
    user.
  - Alternatively, persist the started-state in
    `wp.data.dispatch( CORE_STORE ).receiveCurrentUser` adjacent state,
    or in `localStorage` keyed by user_id + site_id (lower fidelity,
    acceptable as a belt-and-braces second guard).
  - Either way, the React component must NOT be the source of truth for
    "have we kicked off this session yet" — the server must be.

- `src/admin-page/index.js`
  - The gate logic that picks Bootstrap vs ThemeBuilder is correct.
    Do not change it.

### Tests

- `tests/SdAiAgent/Core/OnboardingManagerTest.php`
  - Test: calling `/onboarding/theme-builder-start` twice for the same
    user must NOT create a second kickoff session (session ID is stable
    across calls).
  - Test: the new option `sd_ai_agent_theme_builder_started` (or
    equivalent) is set after the first call.

- `tests/e2e/onboarding-theme-builder.spec.js`
  - Add a reload step after the first answer and assert the page does NOT
    re-send the kickoff.

### Reference pattern

The Setup-Assistant side already handles this correctly:

- `/onboarding/bootstrap-start` → sets `onboarding_complete=true` →
  `src/admin-page/index.js` gate sees the flag and mounts the regular
  chat UI (not the bootstrapper) on next reload.

Replicate the same "server-truth, set-once" pattern for the Theme
Builder, but with a dedicated flag (not the global `onboarding_complete`)
so other code paths that care about "is the user past onboarding" still
work correctly.

## Out of scope

- Conversation persistence / mid-build state recovery — that is a separate
  problem covered by the "build phase messages not persisted" bug filed in
  this batch. The minimum bar here is just "don't re-fire the kickoff".
- Changes to the Setup-Assistant onboarding flow — leave
  `/onboarding/bootstrap-start` untouched.
- Re-introducing any wizard UI.

## Verification

```bash
composer phpstan
composer phpcs
npm run lint:js
npm run lint:php
npm run build
npm run test:php
npm run test:js
npm run test:e2e:playwright -- onboarding-theme-builder
```

Manual:

1. Empty install + fresh session: open the admin page → kickoff sent
   ONCE.
2. Reload the page mid-interview → kickoff is NOT re-sent; the existing
   session is reattached.
3. Logout and re-login → still no duplicate kickoff.
4. Different user logs in on the same site → that user gets their own
   first-time kickoff (per-user flag, not site-global).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Reloading the admin chat page during the Theme Builder flow does
      NOT add a duplicate kickoff message to the conversation.
- [ ] The kickoff is sent at most once per user per site, even across
      multiple reloads, sessions, and tabs.
- [ ] The persistence is server-side (a flag or session record), not
      relying on React component state alone.
- [ ] PHP + JS lint, build, unit, and E2E all green.
- [ ] No regression in the Setup Assistant (Bootstrap) flow — its
      kickoff still fires exactly once.

## Caveats

- A per-user (rather than per-site) flag matters on multisite installs
  where multiple admins may each want to see the kickoff once.
- The Theme Builder flag must not block re-opening the chat after the
  build completes; it just blocks re-firing the kickoff message.
- Consider whether to also add a "restart Theme Builder" affordance
  similar to issue #1505's restart-Setup-Assistant for symmetry, but
  do NOT bundle that work into this fix.

## Related

- #1505 — restart Setup Assistant affordance (sibling design pattern).
- PR #1503 — Onboarding v2 cleanup that introduced the asymmetric
  REST handlers.
- Filed-in-batch: activate-theme requirements, active-jobs stuck,
  theme.json schema version.

title: bug(active-jobs): rows stuck in 'processing' when AgentLoop request terminates abnormally
body:
## Summary

Rows in `wp_sd_ai_agent_active_jobs` become permanently stuck in
`status='processing'` when the PHP request running an AgentLoop terminates
abnormally (PHP fatal, FastCGI / nginx timeout, killed worker process,
client disconnect mid-tool-execution, etc.). The job row's `updated_at` never
advances past its `created_at`, and nothing in the codebase reaps it.

This manifested twice in a 2026-05-18 manual walkthrough — both attempts at
the Theme Builder "build" phase died inside the `activate-theme` tool call.
Active-jobs row #94 (session 56) has remained `status=processing`,
`pending_tools=[]`, `tool_calls=[]`, with `updated_at = created_at = 2026-05-19 04:26:20`
ever since.

## Reproduction

Minimum repro (no agent needed):

```bash
# 1) Provoke a long-running AgentLoop request, then SIGKILL the PHP worker
#    mid-flight, OR simulate by manually inserting a "processing" row and
#    leaving it.
wp db query "INSERT INTO wp_sd_ai_agent_active_jobs
  (session_id, job_id, user_id, status, pending_tools, tool_calls,
   created_at, updated_at)
  VALUES (1, 'test-stuck-1', 1, 'processing', '[]', '[]', NOW(), NOW());"

# 2) Wait any amount of time. Nothing cleans it up.
wp db query "SELECT * FROM wp_sd_ai_agent_active_jobs WHERE job_id='test-stuck-1';"
# status still 'processing', updated_at unchanged.
```

In-the-wild trigger from the walkthrough:

1. Theme Builder agent reaches activate-theme tool call.
2. `switch_theme()` runs, validate_current_theme reverts (separate bug),
   PHP request continues executing the AgentLoop but eventually exits the
   request (timeout, fatal, or normal completion without updating the
   job row).
3. Active-jobs row is left forever in `processing`.

## Impact

- Database accumulates "zombie" job rows that look like in-flight work
  but aren't.
- Front-end UIs that count active jobs (or render a "X jobs running"
  badge) display misleading numbers.
- Any pulse / scheduler / dedup logic that gates on "is a job already
  processing for this session?" will block legitimate retries indefinitely.
- Diagnostic confusion: I personally lost time investigating "is the loop
  running?" because the active-jobs row said it was, but the PHP process
  was long dead.

## Files

### Cleanup paths to wire up

1. **Shutdown handler** — guaranteed best-effort cleanup on normal-or-
   abnormal request exit.

   - `includes/Core/AgentLoop.php` (or whichever class creates the
     active-jobs row).
     - When inserting the `processing` row, also `register_shutdown_function()`
       a closure that, if the row is still `processing` at shutdown,
       updates it to `status='interrupted'`, sets a `notes` /
       `error` column to "shutdown handler — request terminated without
       loop completion", and `updated_at=NOW()`.
     - Use `connection_aborted()` and `connection_status()` to
       differentiate user-disconnect vs PHP timeout in the notes.

2. **Periodic reaper** — for cases where the shutdown handler itself
   couldn't run (SIGKILL, OOM, FPM child exit).

   - Add a `cleanup_stale_active_jobs()` cron job, scheduled hourly.
   - Marks rows as `status='abandoned'` when:
     - `status='processing'`, AND
     - `updated_at < NOW() - INTERVAL 15 MINUTE` (configurable via
       filter `sd_ai_agent_stale_job_threshold_minutes`).
   - Logs each reaped row via the existing logger plumbing.
   - Register the cron event in `includes/Core/Database.php` activation
     hook or wherever other plugin cron events are registered.

3. **AgentLoop heartbeat** — already implied to exist but verify.
   - Every iteration of the loop should `UPDATE wp_sd_ai_agent_active_jobs
     SET updated_at=NOW() WHERE id=...` so the 15-minute reaper threshold
     is honest about "this loop has actually stopped progressing".
   - If no heartbeat exists, add one. Search for where the loop iterates;
     add the update statement at the top of the iteration.

### Schema

- `includes/Core/Database.php` (look for `wp_sd_ai_agent_active_jobs`
  CREATE TABLE).
  - Add an optional `error TEXT NULL` and `interrupted_at DATETIME NULL`
    column via the standard schema migration pattern (`dbDelta`). This
    avoids polluting `pending_tools`/`tool_calls` with cleanup metadata.
  - Add an `idx_status_updated_at` index for the reaper query.

### Tests

- `tests/SdAiAgent/Core/AgentLoopTest.php` (or create a dedicated
  `ActiveJobsCleanupTest.php`).
  - Test: shutdown handler closes a `processing` row.
  - Test: cron reaper marks rows older than threshold as `abandoned`.
  - Test: heartbeat advances `updated_at` on each loop iteration.

### Reference pattern

WordPress core's `wp_doing_cron()` + `wp_schedule_event()` is the
canonical scheduling pattern. Look at how this plugin already schedules
its skill-update WP-Cron job (issue #1492 / t219 added a `WP-Cron skill
update checker`) — mirror that.

For shutdown handlers, see PHP's `register_shutdown_function()`
documentation and any existing usage in the plugin (`rg -n "register_shutdown_function" includes/`).

## Out of scope

- Do NOT try to "resume" interrupted jobs automatically — that needs
  separate design (the conversation messages from the dead loop are
  often lost too, per the related "build phase not persisted" issue).
- Do NOT change the AgentLoop's tool-execution semantics or its provider-
  call retry behaviour.
- Do NOT add a UI surface for inspecting stuck jobs in this PR;
  ship the data plumbing first, then a follow-up enhancement can add
  the admin diagnostic page.

## Verification

```bash
composer phpstan
composer phpcs
composer test -- --filter ActiveJobsCleanupTest
composer test -- --filter AgentLoop
npm run lint:php
```

Manual:

1. Insert a synthetic stuck row via the repro SQL above, set its
   `updated_at` to 30 minutes ago, run `wp cron event run
   sd_ai_agent_cleanup_stale_active_jobs`, confirm the row moves to
   `abandoned`.
2. Kill a real AgentLoop mid-flight (kill -9 the PHP-FPM worker) and
   confirm the row eventually moves to `abandoned` after the next cron
   run.
3. Watch `wp_sd_ai_agent_active_jobs.updated_at` advance during a
   normal agent run (heartbeat working).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] No row stays in `status='processing'` for more than the
      configured threshold (default 15 minutes) without `updated_at`
      advancing.
- [ ] Shutdown handler closes rows on normal request exit.
- [ ] Cron reaper closes rows when shutdown handler didn't fire.
- [ ] Heartbeat updates `updated_at` on each loop iteration.
- [ ] PHPCS, PHPStan, PHPUnit clean.
- [ ] No regression in existing AgentLoop tests.

## Caveats

- Threshold must be longer than the longest expected legitimate loop
  iteration (some tool calls — image generation, large RAG queries — can
  legitimately take several minutes). 15 minutes is a starting point,
  not a hard rule; make it filterable.
- Cron may not run on extremely low-traffic sites; the shutdown handler
  is the primary defence and the cron is the safety net.
- Make sure the new columns and index have `dbDelta`-compatible syntax
  and update `DB_VERSION` so the migration actually runs.

## Related

- Activate-theme requirements bug — its hang triggered the cascade that
  surfaced this housekeeping gap.
- Filed in same batch: kickoff loop, theme.json version, fonts rule.
- Issue #1492 (t219) — already-shipped WP-Cron scheduling pattern.

title: bug(scaffold-block-theme): generated theme.json uses schema version 2 instead of current 3
body:
## Summary

When the Theme Builder agent invokes
`sd-ai-agent/scaffold-block-theme` with an explicit `theme_json` argument,
the model is choosing `"version": 2` instead of the current schema version
`3`. `ScaffoldBlockThemeAbility::default_theme_json()` correctly emits
`"version" => 3` when no override is supplied, so the regression is
entirely on the model-prompt side: the agent is over-providing a stale
template that overrides the better default.

Walkthrough on 2026-05-18 produced this `theme.json` header in
`wp-content/themes/bramble-and-bean/theme.json`:

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://schemas.wp.org/trunk/theme.json",
  "version": 2,
  ...
}
```

The default scaffold (lines 397-398 of `ScaffoldBlockThemeAbility.php`)
emits:

```php
'$schema' => 'https://schemas.wp.org/trunk/theme.json',
'version' => 3,
```

## Reproduction

1. Run the Theme Builder onboarding to the point where the agent calls
   `sd-ai-agent/scaffold-block-theme`.
2. Inspect the generated `theme.json` at
   `wp-content/themes/{slug}/theme.json`.
3. Observe `"version": 2`.

Alternative — inspect the provider trace JSON. The agent's `tool_use`
input for `scaffold-block-theme` will contain a `theme_json` object whose
`version` is 2.

## Impact

- Schema version 2 is the old format. Version 3 (WordPress 6.6+,
  required since 7.0) supports newer features such as section-style
  variations, root-level `background` controls, and other recent
  additions. A v2 file does not error, but it misses features and
  signals "stale" to anyone reading it.
- Because the plugin's minimum WP is 7.0+, v3 is the only correct
  default for new themes.
- The model's choice is being silently accepted; nothing in the
  ability rejects or normalises it.

## Files

### System prompt (where the model gets the wrong template)

- `includes/Models/Agent.php`
  - Locate the Theme Builder agent system prompt block (the one that
    references `sd-ai-agent/scaffold-block-theme`, `activate-theme`,
    `update-global-styles`, etc.). It begins around line 608+ and
    includes design guidance lines mentioning "Never embed stock image
    URLs…" (around line 625, 647).
  - Find any example `theme.json` snippets, schema mentions, or
    instructions to the model about the file's shape. Update any
    `"version": 2` references to `"version": 3` and add explicit
    guidance:

    > When emitting a `theme_json` argument to
    > `sd-ai-agent/scaffold-block-theme`, always use schema version 3 with
    > `"$schema": "https://schemas.wp.org/trunk/theme.json"`. Never use
    > version 2 — this plugin requires WordPress 7.0+, where version 3 is
    > standard and unlocks section-style variations and root background
    > controls.

  - If the system prompt has no current schema example, add a short one
    so the model has a concrete reference.

### Ability — server-side guardrail

- `includes/Abilities/ScaffoldBlockThemeAbility.php`
  - In the path that consumes the caller-supplied `theme_json` array
    (around lines 182-196), if the supplied document has
    `version < 3`, log a warning AND coerce to `version = 3` before
    encoding. Justification: the plugin's documented minimum WP is 7.0+
    and v3 is the right shape; protect against model regressions by
    normalising rather than blindly trusting.
  - Alternative: hard-fail with a `WP_Error` so the agent retries with
    a corrected document — but that's noisier; prefer silent
    coercion + log.

### Tests

- `tests/SdAiAgent/Abilities/ScaffoldBlockThemeAbilityTest.php`
  - Test: caller supplies `theme_json` with `"version" => 2` →
    on-disk file has `"version": 3`.
  - Test: caller supplies `theme_json` with `"version" => 3` → on-disk
    file unchanged at v3.
  - Test: caller omits `theme_json` → default v3 written (already
    covered? — verify).

## Reference pattern

The canonical schema URLs:

- v3 (current, what we want): `https://schemas.wp.org/trunk/theme.json`
- v3 (pinned): `https://schemas.wp.org/wp/6.7/theme.json`,
  `…/wp/7.0/theme.json`

Use `trunk` for forward-compat; do not pin to a specific WP version
unless there's a tested-against reason.

Recent WP themes that ship v3 for reference:

- Core `twentytwentyfive` (read its `theme.json` to confirm the v3
  shape — has `version: 3`, uses `settings.layout.contentSize` and
  `wideSize`, etc.).

## Out of scope

- Do not migrate any existing user-installed themes — only new
  scaffolds.
- Do not change the rest of the Theme Builder system prompt (interview
  questions, design rules) in this PR — keep the diff focused on the
  schema version.
- Do not add a v4 future-proofing path; WordPress has not announced one.

## Verification

```bash
composer phpstan
composer phpcs
composer test -- --filter ScaffoldBlockThemeAbilityTest
npm run lint:php
```

Manual:

1. Drive the Theme Builder onboarding to scaffold a new theme.
2. Inspect `wp-content/themes/{slug}/theme.json` — first line of the
   document body must be `"version": 3`.
3. Also inspect the provider trace for the `scaffold-block-theme`
   tool_use input — confirm the model is now emitting v3 (system prompt
   fix worked) OR the ability coerced it (guardrail worked).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] New scaffolded themes always have `"version": 3` in `theme.json`
      on disk.
- [ ] System prompt explicitly instructs v3.
- [ ] Server-side coercion catches stale model templates.
- [ ] All linters + unit tests pass.
- [ ] Walkthrough produces a v3 file for a fresh theme.

## Caveats

- Coercion changes the model's exact intent on disk. The change-log
  plumbing should record "version coerced from 2 to 3" for
  transparency.
- The system prompt fix alone is best-effort (the model can still
  regress); the server-side coercion is the durable safety net.

## Related

- Filed in same batch: activate-theme requirements, kickoff loop,
  active-jobs reaper, fonts/external URLs prompt gap.
- `ScaffoldBlockThemeAbility::default_theme_json()` already correct
  — just keeping the override path honest.

title: enhancement(theme-builder): extend 'no external URLs' system-prompt rule to web fonts
body:
## Summary

The Theme Builder agent's system prompt explicitly forbids external image URLs
in previews and templates ("Never embed stock image URLs, external image URLs,
or placeholder image services. Use CSS gradients and typographic layouts.") but
is silent about **web fonts**. As a result, both the in-flow HTML design
previews AND the scaffolded theme files routinely load Google Fonts via
`https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?...` and `https://fonts.gstatic.com/...`.

Observed in the 2026-05-18 walkthrough (theme "Bramble & Bean"):

- `wp-content/themes/bramble-and-bean/functions.php` — enqueues a
  `https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=…` stylesheet.
- `wp-content/themes/bramble-and-bean/theme.json` — references
  `https://fonts.googleapis.com/...` URLs in its `typography.fontFamilies`
  block.
- `wp-content/uploads/sd-ai-agent/design-previews/bramble-bean/design-1.html`
  (and -2.html, -3.html) — each preview file has `<link
  href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/...">` in `<head>`.

## Why this is a problem

1. **GDPR / privacy** — Google Fonts loaded from `googleapis.com` exposes
   visitor IPs to Google. EU operators have lost cases over this (German
   district court 2022). Self-hosting is the safe default and is
   increasingly the WordPress.org reviewer expectation.
2. **WordPress.org review surface area** — the wporg variant of this
   plugin (`bin/build.sh --target=both` produces `*-wporg.zip`) is
   subjected to reviewer scrutiny. Themes scaffolded by the plugin that
   pull external resources at runtime is exactly the kind of thing
   reviewers flag, and any plugin-generated theme will be perceived as
   "the plugin's output".
3. **Offline / air-gapped sites** — themes that fail to render
   correctly without internet access are a poor default for production
   sites.
4. **Internal inconsistency** — the system prompt forbids external URLs
   for images on the basis that the agent should produce self-contained
   work product. The same principle applies (more strongly, in fact) to
   fonts because fonts are loaded on every page view, not just inside
   one preview file.

## Files

### System prompt — extend the existing rule

- `includes/Models/Agent.php`
  - In the Theme Builder agent system prompt (around lines 625 and 647 where
    the no-external-URL rule lives for images), extend the rule to cover
    web fonts. Suggested replacement / addition:

    > **No external assets in generated previews, templates, or theme
    > files.** This includes:
    >
    > - Stock image URLs (any host)
    > - Placeholder image services (placehold.co, picsum.photos, etc.)
    > - **Web fonts from external CDNs** including `fonts.googleapis.com`,
    >   `fonts.bunny.net`, `use.typekit.net`, `fonts.adobe.com`.
    >
    > For typography:
    >
    > - In previews: use system font stacks
    >   (`-apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", Roboto, "Helvetica
    >   Neue", Arial, sans-serif`) and pair them with creative CSS
    >   treatments (weight, letter-spacing, transform). Never `<link>` a
    >   Google Fonts stylesheet.
    > - In scaffolded themes: declare font families in `theme.json` using
    >   `fontFace` entries that reference WOFF2 files bundled with the
    >   theme under `assets/fonts/`. Do not enqueue any external font
    >   stylesheet from `functions.php`.

  - Mirror the change in any other agent that produces frontend output
    (Setup Assistant agent, content-generation agent if they exist) to
    keep the rule consistent across personas.

### New ability (companion, optional but recommended)

- `includes/Abilities/AddBundledFontAbility.php` (new) — given a font
  family name and a list of weights, the ability:
  - Resolves a WOFF2 source (from a vetted internal cache, OR by failing
    gracefully and telling the agent "self-host the font manually — I
    cannot fetch from external CDNs").
  - Writes the WOFF2 file under `wp-content/themes/{slug}/assets/fonts/`.
  - Returns paths the agent can stitch into `theme.json` `fontFace`
    entries.
  - This is genuinely scope-y; if it's too large for one PR, ship just
    the prompt-rule change first and file a separate enhancement.

### Tests

- `tests/SdAiAgent/Models/AgentTest.php` (or wherever agent system-prompt
  tests live).
  - Test: the Theme Builder system prompt contains the font-no-external
    rule. (String assertion is fine — it's a regression guard, not a
    semantics test.)

### Optional: server-side scanner

- `includes/Abilities/ScaffoldBlockThemeAbility.php` and
  `includes/Abilities/FileWriteAbility.php` (or whichever writes templates):
  - Scan the file content for `fonts.googleapis.com` /
    `fonts.gstatic.com` substrings. If detected, log a warning and reject
    the write with a `WP_Error('sd_ai_agent_external_font_blocked', …)`.
  - This is the durable safety net — the system prompt instructs the
    model, but a guardrail prevents regressions.

## Reference pattern

The image-no-external-URL rule's wording lives in the same prompt block
(`includes/Models/Agent.php` lines 625, 647). Reuse the exact tone and
imperative shape so the prompt reads consistently.

For the server-side scanner pattern, look at how
`ToolCapabilities::current_user_can()` is used in the existing abilities
— same return-early-with-WP_Error pattern.

## Out of scope

- Bundled font catalog — choosing WHICH fonts to ship with the plugin is
  a separate, larger decision (licensing, file size, naming).
- Rewriting existing user-installed themes — only new scaffolds.
- Cracking down on developer hand-written themes (not generated by this
  plugin).
- Image-side rule changes — the image part of the rule is already in
  place and works.

## Verification

```bash
composer phpstan
composer phpcs
npm run lint:php
composer test
```

Manual:

1. Drive the Theme Builder onboarding to design preview output. Grep the
   generated HTML files in `wp-content/uploads/sd-ai-agent/design-previews/`
   for `fonts.googleapis.com` — expect zero matches.
2. Complete the scaffold. Grep `wp-content/themes/{slug}/` for
   `googleapis.com` and `gstatic.com` — expect zero matches.
3. Inspect `functions.php` — no external font stylesheet enqueue.
4. Inspect `theme.json` — either uses system fonts OR references local
   `file:./assets/fonts/...` paths.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] System prompt explicitly forbids external font CDNs in addition to
      external image URLs.
- [ ] Design previews use system font stacks.
- [ ] Scaffolded themes either use system stacks OR self-host fonts
      bundled within the theme directory.
- [ ] Server-side scanner (if implemented in this PR) rejects writes
      containing external font URLs.
- [ ] All linters + tests pass.
- [ ] Walkthrough produces zero `googleapis.com` / `gstatic.com` matches
      in any plugin-generated file.

## Caveats

- Creative typography is part of what makes the three design previews
  feel distinctive. Losing Google Fonts narrows the design vocabulary
  unless the bundled-font ability lands too. Mitigation: invest in CSS
  treatments (weight contrast, letter-spacing, transform, gradient text
  fills) per the existing prompt guidance about gradients-and-
  typographic layouts for images.
- System font stacks vary by platform — be explicit about the chosen
  stack so previews render predictably across OSes.

## Related

- Filed in same batch: activate-theme requirements, kickoff loop,
  active-jobs reaper, theme.json schema version.
- Image-side rule lives in `includes/Models/Agent.php` around lines
  625, 647 — preserve and extend, don't replace.

title: bug(theme-builder): auto-kickoff never fires on fresh start (regression in #1520)
body:
## Summary

PR #1520 (the fix for #1509 "kickoff message re-sent on every reload") **over-corrected** and introduced a new regression: the kickoff message now **never fires automatically**, not even on the very first call to `/onboarding/theme-builder-start` for a brand-new site.

End result on a clean install:

- Empty WordPress site, fresh session, `sd_ai_agent_settings.onboarding_complete=false`,
  `sd_ai_agent_theme_builder_started` option absent.
- User opens the AI Agent admin page → `OnboardingThemeBuilder` mounts → POSTs
  `/onboarding/theme-builder-start`.
- Server creates session, stamps `THEME_BUILDER_STARTED_OPTION = time()`, **returns
  `started_at: <unix timestamp>`** in the response (even on the first-create path).
- React component checks `if ( ! data.started_at ) sendMessage( ... )` — `started_at` is
  truthy (a timestamp number), so **kickoff is skipped**.
- User sees an empty chat with no greeting, no interview question, no Designer persona —
  just the regular chat UI with the model picker showing "Theme Builder". To proceed they
  must type a kickoff message manually.

This is verified end-to-end against `main @ 96728bf` (v1.14.0 prep) on WP 6.9.4:

```
wp option get sd_ai_agent_theme_builder_session_id   # 1
wp option get sd_ai_agent_theme_builder_started      # 1779203410
wp db query "SELECT LENGTH(messages) FROM wp_sd_ai_agent_sessions WHERE id=1;"
# => 2   (i.e. the JSON array '[]' — no kickoff message persisted)
```

## Root cause

`includes/Core/OnboardingManager.php::rest_theme_builder_start()` returns
`started_at` in **both** branches:

- **Resume branch (existing_session_id is set)** — returns
  `'started_at' => get_option( self::THEME_BUILDER_STARTED_OPTION )` (the saved value).
  Correct — this is the resume case, and kickoff should be skipped.
- **Fresh-create branch (no existing session)** — stamps
  `$started_at = time(); update_option( self::THEME_BUILDER_STARTED_OPTION, $started_at, false );`
  and then returns `'started_at' => $started_at`. **Wrong — this is the fresh-start case,
  and kickoff should fire.**

The JS check `if ( ! data.started_at )` (`src/components/onboarding-theme-builder.js`)
cannot distinguish "this server-side flag was just stamped 50 ms ago in the same request"
from "this server-side flag was stamped on a previous request". Both look the same from
the JSON payload.

## Reproduction

```bash
# 1. Start from a clean install.
wp post delete $(wp post list --post_type=any --format=ids) --force
wp db query "TRUNCATE TABLE wp_sd_ai_agent_sessions; TRUNCATE TABLE wp_sd_ai_agent_active_jobs;"
wp option delete sd_ai_agent_onboarding_complete sd_ai_agent_bootstrap_session_id \
  sd_ai_agent_theme_builder_session_id sd_ai_agent_theme_builder_started
wp eval '$s = get_option("sd_ai_agent_settings", []); $s["onboarding_complete"] = false; update_option("sd_ai_agent_settings", $s);'

# 2. Open the admin chat page.
xdg-open http://wordpress.local:8080/wp-admin/admin.php?page=sd-ai-agent

# 3. Observe: empty chat, no greeting. Reload — still empty (kickoff still won't fire).

# 4. Confirm the React path actually called the REST endpoint:
wp db query "SELECT id, LENGTH(messages) FROM wp_sd_ai_agent_sessions;"   # 1 row, 2 bytes
wp option get sd_ai_agent_theme_builder_session_id                          # 1
wp option get sd_ai_agent_theme_builder_started                             # <recent timestamp>
```

## Suggested fix

Two clean options — pick one. **Option A is recommended** because it keeps the truth on
the server and keeps the client check trivial.

### Option A — return an `is_fresh_start` boolean explicitly

```php
// includes/Core/OnboardingManager.php::rest_theme_builder_start()

// Resume branch:
return new \WP_REST_Response( [
    'success'        => true,
    'session_id'     => $existing_session_id,
    'agent_id'       => $theme_builder_agent_id,
    'kickoff_message'=> $kickoff_message,
    'started_at'     => get_option( self::THEME_BUILDER_STARTED_OPTION ),
    'is_fresh_start' => false,                          // <-- new
], 200 );

// ... full-create branch:
$started_at = time();
update_option( self::THEME_BUILDER_SESSION_OPTION, $session_id, false );
update_option( self::THEME_BUILDER_STARTED_OPTION, $started_at, false );

return new \WP_REST_Response( [
    'success'        => true,
    'session_id'     => $session_id,
    'agent_id'       => $theme_builder_agent_id,
    'kickoff_message'=> $kickoff_message,
    'started_at'     => $started_at,
    'is_fresh_start' => true,                           // <-- new
], 200 );
```

```js
// src/components/onboarding-theme-builder.js
.then( () => {
    if ( data.is_fresh_start ) {
        sendMessage( data.kickoff_message || /* default */ );
    }
} )
```

### Option B — don't stamp `started_at` until AFTER returning, and let the JS check whether
`started_at` is null

This is more fragile (requires `register_shutdown_function` or a follow-up POST to mark
the session "actually started"), and creates a window where two near-simultaneous mounts
could both try to send the kickoff. Not recommended.

### Existing test coverage

Look at the unit tests added in PR #1520 (file
`tests/SdAiAgent/Core/OnboardingManagerTest.php` or similar). They likely assert that
`started_at` is non-null on first call — that assertion is **the wrong shape** and needs
updating. The test that protects against the original bug (no duplicate kickoff on
second call) is still correct; just add an additional assertion that the **first** call
distinguishes itself from the second (via `is_fresh_start`).

## Verification

```bash
composer phpstan
composer phpcs
npm run lint:js
npm run build
npm run test:php
npm run test:js
npm run test:e2e:playwright -- onboarding-theme-builder
```

Manual:

1. Clean state (per the Reproduction section above).
2. Open admin chat page → `OnboardingThemeBuilder` mounts → kickoff message
   "I'd like to design a custom block theme..." appears in the chat,
   followed by the agent's interview question 1.
3. Reload the page → kickoff message is NOT re-sent (the original #1509 protection
   still works).
4. Conversation state persists across reloads.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] On a clean install, opening the admin chat page automatically sends the kickoff
      message and the agent responds with the interview start.
- [ ] Reload during the interview / build phase does NOT add a duplicate kickoff
      (the original #1509 fix continues to hold).
- [ ] `is_fresh_start` (or equivalent unambiguous signal) is returned by
      `/onboarding/theme-builder-start` and used by `OnboardingThemeBuilder`.
- [ ] Existing unit tests updated; new test asserts the first-call vs resume distinction.
- [ ] PHPCS, PHPStan, ESLint, build, Jest, PHPUnit, Playwright all green.

## Caveats

- This is a regression introduced by PR #1520 — it didn't exist before, only after.
- Severity: **P1** — the Theme Builder onboarding **does not start automatically** any
  more. Users have to know to type a kickoff phrase manually. That's worse than the
  original duplicate-kickoff bug because at least with the original bug the user knew
  the agent was alive and trying to talk to them.
- The fix is small and localised.

## Related

- PR #1520 / Issue #1509 — original fix that over-corrected.
- The original #1509 problem (kickoff re-sent on reload) is still correctly prevented
  by this fix; we only need to differentiate fresh-start from resume.
- Verified during the post-fix Theme Builder walkthrough on 2026-05-19.

title: bug(create-menu): preserve requested menu item order
body:
> **MANDATORY before opening a PR:** satisfy the [Worker Self-Verification Protocol](https://github.com/Ultimate-Multisite/superdav-ai-agent/blob/main/AGENTS.md#worker-self-verification-protocol) in `AGENTS.md`. Run the full PHPUnit suite (`npm run test:php`, not filtered), `npm run lint:php|js|css`, `composer phpstan`, `npm run build`, and paste the verification summary block in the PR body. Filtered PHPUnit runs are NOT sufficient — they shipped CI-broken PRs in the first dispatch batch (closed PR #1537, PR #1538).

## Summary

`sd-ai-agent/create-menu` does not preserve the order of menu items as
specified by the agent. Items end up alphabetised in the rendered nav.

Observed during the post-fix walkthrough on 2026-05-19: the Theme Builder
agent requested the nav order `HOME · MENU · OUR STORY · EVENTS · FIND
US · SHOP`. The live nav rendered as `EVENTS · HOME · MENU · OUR STORY ·
SHOP OUR BEANS · VISIT US` — alphabetical by post title.

## Root cause (likely)

`CreateMenuAbility::add_menu_item()` either:

1. Does not set `menu_order` at all, leaving WordPress to default-sort
   by post title.
2. Sets `menu_order = 0` for every item, ditto.

WP_CLI `nav-menu item add` and `wp_update_nav_menu_item()` both accept a
`menu-item-position` argument that controls ordering. The ability should
auto-increment this based on the order of items passed in the request.

## Proposed fix

In `includes/Abilities/CreateMenuAbility.php`:

```php
$position = 1;
foreach ( $items as $item ) {
    wp_update_nav_menu_item(
        $menu_id,
        0,
        [
            'menu-item-title'    => $item['title'],
            'menu-item-object'   => 'page',
            'menu-item-object-id'=> $item['page_id'],
            'menu-item-type'     => 'post_type',
            'menu-item-status'   => 'publish',
            'menu-item-position' => $position,  // <-- new
        ]
    );
    $position++;
}
```

The schema MAY also accept an explicit `position` per item for callers
that want to insert at a specific slot, but the default behaviour MUST
be "preserve the order I gave you".

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Calling `sd-ai-agent/create-menu` with items
  `[Home, Menu, Our Story, Events, Find Us, Shop]` produces a nav in
  exactly that order.
- [ ] Existing tests still pass.
- [ ] New PHPUnit test asserts position is set on each
  `wp_update_nav_menu_item` call.

## Verification

```bash
composer phpstan
composer phpcs
npm run test:php -- --filter CreateMenuAbility
```

Then run the Theme Builder walkthrough and confirm the live nav matches
the requested order.

## Caveats

- WordPress site editor (block themes) reads `wp_navigation` post types
  for site-editor nav, not the classic `nav_menu_item` taxonomy. Confirm
  which path the Theme Builder agent uses — if it builds a block
  navigation, the fix is different (`<!-- wp:navigation-link {...} -->`
  block ordering inside the parent `<!-- wp:navigation -->`).

## Related

- Filed during post-#1522 design review.
- Same walkthrough that produced PRs #1514, #1515, #1516, #1520, #1521,
  #1523.
