title: feat(theme-builder): require a real primary CTA in every front-page hero
body:
> **MANDATORY before opening a PR:** satisfy the [Worker Self-Verification Protocol](https://github.com/Ultimate-Multisite/superdav-ai-agent/blob/main/AGENTS.md#worker-self-verification-protocol) in `AGENTS.md`. Run the full PHPUnit suite (`npm run test:php`, not filtered), `npm run lint:php|js|css`, `composer phpstan`, `npm run build`, and paste the verification summary block in the PR body. Filtered PHPUnit runs are NOT sufficient — they shipped CI-broken PRs in the first dispatch batch (closed PR #1537, PR #1538).

## Summary

The Theme Builder agent produces hero sections with no call-to-action
button. For conversion-driven sites (cafés, restaurants, shops, services,
events) the front-page hero is the highest-value pixel on the site and
MUST include a primary CTA pointing to the most-likely-converting page.

Example from the post-#1522 walkthrough: a single-location café front
page rendered with "Slow down. Sip something good." + opening hours +
address, but no `ORDER ONLINE` / `RESERVE` / `VIEW MENU` / `GET
DIRECTIONS` button. The hours-and-address block is good, but a button
should sit immediately under the hero copy.

## Root cause

The agent's system prompt and the `scaffold-block-theme` ability's
default `front-page.html` template do not require a hero CTA. The agent
treats the CTA as optional and frequently omits it.

## Proposed fix

Three layers:

### 1. System prompt update (theme-builder agent)

Add a hard rule to the Theme Builder agent's system prompt
(`includes/Models/Agent.php` seed data and any prompt builder logic):

> Every front-page hero MUST include exactly one primary CTA button.
> The CTA text and target are derived from the business vertical:
> - Café / restaurant → "View menu" → /menu/
> - Shop / e-commerce → "Shop now" → /shop/
> - Service business → "Get a quote" → /contact/
> - Event / venue → "Reserve" → /book/ or /events/
> - Content site → most-recent-post or featured category
>
> The CTA MUST be a real link to an existing page on the site, not
> "#" or a placeholder. If the target page does not yet exist, create
> it first.

### 2. `scaffold-block-theme` template default

Update `includes/Abilities/ScaffoldBlockThemeAbility.php` so the
default `front-page.html` template includes a `<!-- wp:button -->` block
slot in the hero, with a tool-callback marker the agent fills with the
real link.

### 3. Validation

Add a `validate_front_page_has_cta()` check that runs after scaffold
+ page creation. If the rendered front-page has no `<a class="...
wp-block-button__link">` inside the hero section, return a non-fatal
warning the agent can act on.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every Theme Builder walkthrough produces a front-page with a
      visible CTA button in the hero.
- [ ] CTA text and target are vertical-appropriate, not generic.
- [ ] CTA links to an existing published page (never `#`).
- [ ] System prompt rule is documented in the seed data.
- [ ] PHPUnit test asserts the scaffold default includes a CTA block
      slot.
- [ ] E2E test asserts the rendered front-page contains
      `.wp-block-button__link[href]:not([href="#"])` inside the hero.

## Verification

```bash
composer phpstan
composer phpcs
npm run test:php -- --filter ScaffoldBlockTheme
npm run test:e2e:playwright -- onboarding-theme-builder
```

Manual: run the Theme Builder walkthrough as a coffee shop, restaurant,
shop, and service business. Verify each gets an appropriate CTA.

## Caveats

- The CTA target may not exist at scaffold time if pages haven't been
  created yet. The agent SHOULD plan page creation order so the CTA's
  target page exists before the front-page is finalised.

## Related

- Filed during post-#1522 design review.
- Pairs with `feat(theme-builder): no placeholder content` — both
  enforce the principle that nothing ships incomplete.

title: feat(theme-builder): enforce real content or no content for generated pages
body:
> **MANDATORY before opening a PR:** satisfy the [Worker Self-Verification Protocol](https://github.com/Ultimate-Multisite/superdav-ai-agent/blob/main/AGENTS.md#worker-self-verification-protocol) in `AGENTS.md`. Run the full PHPUnit suite (`npm run test:php`, not filtered), `npm run lint:php|js|css`, `composer phpstan`, `npm run build`, and paste the verification summary block in the PR body. Filtered PHPUnit runs are NOT sufficient — they shipped CI-broken PRs in the first dispatch batch (closed PR #1537, PR #1538).

## Summary

The Theme Builder agent must ship every generated page as fully-developed
published content with no placeholder text, no Lorem-style filler, and no
"Edit this section to add your story" prompts. Any information the agent
needs MUST be gathered from the user during the interview phase before
any page is created.

## Principle

> Real content or no content. Never publish a stub.

The agent owns the interview. If it needs to write a 200-word About
section, it must KNOW (from the user) the founding year, the location,
the people, the values, the voice. If it needs to fill a Menu page, it
must HAVE the actual menu items + prices. If it has a Shop page, it
must HAVE real products.

Missing information is a blocker for that page, not a licence to fill
with placeholder copy.

## Root cause

Current behaviour observed during the post-#1522 walkthrough: the agent
created "Events" and "Shop Our Beans" pages with generic copy because
the interview didn't ask the user for events or for products. The pages
shipped published with content that reads like marketing-template
boilerplate.

## Proposed fix

### 1. Interview expansion

The Theme Builder agent's interview MUST be vertical-aware and cover
the full information surface needed for every page that will be
created. For a café, that means:

- Brand name, tagline, founding year, location(s), opening hours
- Story / about copy (collected verbatim or guided via several
  questions)
- Full menu (categories, items, prices, optional descriptions)
- Upcoming events (or "no events page" decision)
- Products to sell online (or "no shop page" decision)
- Team members + bios (or "no team page" decision)
- Photos available (see image-acquisition issues)

### 2. Page-creation prerequisite check

Before any `create-post` call, the agent must run a self-check: do I
have real, user-supplied content for this page? If not, the page is
not created. The user is told which information is missing and asked
to supply it (or asked whether to skip the page entirely).

### 3. Vertical-aware interview templates

Add interview question packs per vertical (café, restaurant, shop,
service business, portfolio, blog, event venue, etc.) in
`includes/Models/Agent.php` or a new `InterviewTemplate` model. The
Theme Builder agent picks the right pack based on vertical detected
in the first 2-3 questions.

### 4. Site-scrape ability as accelerator

If the user has an existing site, the agent can scrape it for brand
info, hours, address, and about copy to pre-fill the interview. See
the separate `site-scrape` ability issue.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] No generated page contains placeholder text, Lorem ipsum,
      "Replace this", "Edit this", "Add your...", or template-fill
      language.
- [ ] No generated page is `post_status = draft`. Pages are either
      published with real content, or not created at all.
- [ ] Interview covers every page the agent intends to create.
- [ ] Missing information triggers an explicit user prompt, not a
      placeholder.
- [ ] System prompt encodes the "real content or no content" rule.
- [ ] PHPUnit/Jest tests verify the system-prompt rule is loaded.
- [ ] E2E test asserts no page on the built site contains the strings
      `Lorem`, `Edit this`, `Add your`, `Replace this`.

## Verification

```bash
composer phpstan
composer phpcs
npm run test:php
npm run test:e2e:playwright -- onboarding-theme-builder
```

Manual: run walkthroughs for café, restaurant, shop, and service
business. Inspect every page. Reject any page with placeholder copy.

## Caveats

- This is a behaviour change that may make the interview longer.
  That's the right trade — longer interview, real published site,
  versus quick interview, fake-content site.
- The interview should still feel conversational, not like a form.
  The agent breaks information gathering into short natural
  questions, not a wall of fields.

## Related

- Extends the honesty principle from #1497 / #1518 (site
  configuration must reflect reality).
- Filed during post-#1522 design review.
- Pairs with `feat(abilities): site-scrape` and the image-acquisition
  abilities — both accelerate complete content collection.

title: feat(abilities): generate sanitised SVG logo candidates for Theme Builder
body:
**⚠️ PRIOR-FAILURE ANALYSIS (2026-05-20T01:11Z)** — PR #1543 closed: `GenerateLogoSvgAbilityTest::test_sanitize_svg_removes_external_xlink_href` failed in CI:

```
1) SdAiAgent\Tests\Abilities\GenerateLogoSvgAbilityTest::test_sanitize_svg_removes_external_xlink_href
Failed asserting that '<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" viewBox="0 0 100 50" width="100" height="50"><use xlink:href="https://evil.example/sprite.svg#icon"/></svg>' does not contain "https://evil.example".

Tests: 2322, Assertions: 6274, Failures: 1, Skipped: 104.
```

The worker added the test (correct assertion: `sanitize_svg()` should strip external `xlink:href` attributes pointing to non-self URLs) but the implementation does **not** actually remove them. The failing input is a `<use xlink:href="https://evil.example/sprite.svg#icon"/>` — the sanitizer must either delete the `<use>` element, strip the `xlink:href` attribute, or replace it with a safe local fragment.

**Required fix for the next worker:** In `includes/Abilities/GenerateLogoSvgAbility.php::sanitize_svg()` (or wherever the sanitiser lives), strip `xlink:href` AND `href` attributes whose values are external URLs (anything containing `://` or starting with `//`). Apply the same external-URL check you already use for `<image>` href attributes. The test fixture is the canonical regression — run that single test first to confirm fix, then run the full `npm run verify` suite and **paste the PHPUnit summary line with `Failures: 0` in the PR body under `## Worker self-verification`** before pushing.

**Do not skip the full suite this time.** The previous worker ran style/PHPStan cleanup commits which suggested partial verify, but a single failing test slipped through because the suite was never completed before the worker exited at `service_interruption_exhausted`. The protocol explicitly requires `Failures: 0` on the full suite as evidence in the PR body.

title: feat(stock-image): add candidate selection and attribution for Theme Builder imagery
body:
> **MANDATORY before opening a PR:** satisfy the [Worker Self-Verification Protocol](https://github.com/Ultimate-Multisite/superdav-ai-agent/blob/main/AGENTS.md#worker-self-verification-protocol) in `AGENTS.md`. Run the full PHPUnit suite (`npm run test:php`, not filtered), `npm run lint:php|js|css`, `composer phpstan`, `npm run build`, and paste the verification summary block in the PR body. Filtered PHPUnit runs are NOT sufficient — they shipped CI-broken PRs in the first dispatch batch (closed PR #1537, PR #1538).

## Summary

Enhance the existing `sd-ai-agent/stock-image` ability so the Theme Builder can search multiple candidate stock images, present choices to the user, and import the selected result into the WordPress media library with attribution metadata.

The current code already registers `SdAiAgent\Abilities\ImageAbilities\StockImageAbility` and sources through Openverse/Pixabay (`includes/Abilities/ImageAbilities/StockImageAbility.php`, `includes/Abilities/ImageSources/ImageSourceFactory.php`). This issue is NOT to add a duplicate ability; it is to upgrade the existing stock-image path for the Theme Builder visual pipeline.

## Why

Theme Builder walkthroughs currently produce visually empty sites because the agent has no UX-friendly way to gather and choose imagery for specific sections. The no-external-URLs rule for theme files is correct — the solution is to import media first, then use local `/wp-content/uploads/...` URLs.

## Proposed scope

- Extend `sd-ai-agent/stock-image` to support search-result candidates instead of importing only the first viable hit.
- Add optional inputs: `orientation`, `colour`, `min_width`, `min_height`, `limit`, and provider preference.
- Preserve the existing Openverse/Pixabay chain; add Unsplash/Pexels only if credentials and licence handling are implemented cleanly.
- Store attribution in `_wp_attachment_image_alt` and `_sd_ai_agent_attribution` when an image is imported.
- Teach the Theme Builder agent to request stock imagery when the user has no uploaded photos and generic photography is suitable.
- Ensure theme/template files receive only local media-library URLs after import.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Existing `sd-ai-agent/stock-image` remains the canonical ability name. No duplicate `stock-image-search` ability is introduced unless maintainers explicitly choose a search/select split.
- [ ] The ability can return multiple candidates with thumbnail URL, provider, dimensions, licence, attribution, and provider image ID.
- [ ] A selected candidate can be imported into the media library.
- [ ] Imported attachments store attribution metadata.
- [ ] Theme Builder prompt knows when to call stock-image versus generate-image or user upload.
- [ ] No external image URLs are written to theme files; output used by scaffold is local media URL / attachment ID.
- [ ] PHPUnit covers provider mocks, attribution storage, and import path.

## Verification

```bash
composer phpstan
composer phpcs
npm run test:php -- --filter StockImage
```

Manual: run the Theme Builder walkthrough; confirm the agent fetches imagery, lets the user choose, imports selected assets, and uses local URLs in the rendered site.

## Related

- Existing ability: `includes/Abilities/ImageAbilities/StockImageAbility.php`
- Existing provider chain: `includes/Abilities/ImageSources/ImageSourceFactory.php`
- Filed during post-#1522 design review.
- Pairs with Theme Builder photo upload and AI image generation enhancements.

title: feat(generate-image): add Theme Builder options, variations, and provenance metadata
body:
> **MANDATORY before opening a PR:** satisfy the [Worker Self-Verification Protocol](https://github.com/Ultimate-Multisite/superdav-ai-agent/blob/main/AGENTS.md#worker-self-verification-protocol) in `AGENTS.md`. Run the full PHPUnit suite (`npm run test:php`, not filtered), `npm run lint:php|js|css`, `composer phpstan`, `npm run build`, and paste the verification summary block in the PR body.
>
> **Previous attempt closed: PR #1538.** Worker added `tests/SdAiAgent/Abilities/AiImageAbilitiesTest.php` with 2 failing assertions:
> - `Failed asserting that an array has the key 'attachments'` — implementation did not return an `attachments` key on the success path.
> - `Failed asserting that an array does not have the key 'error'` — implementation returned an `error` key on a path the test expects to be clean.
>
> Re-implement so that `GenerateImageAbility::execute()` returns the structured shape the tests assert, then run `npm run test:php` (not `--filter`) and confirm `Errors: 0, Failures: 0` before opening the PR.

## Summary

Enhance the existing `sd-ai-agent/generate-image` ability for Theme Builder usage: richer inputs, multiple variations, media provenance metadata, and clearer prompt guidance for when AI generation beats stock photography.

The current code already registers `SdAiAgent\Abilities\ImageAbilities\GenerateImageAbility` through `sd-ai-agent/generate-image`. This issue is NOT to add a duplicate ability; it is to upgrade the existing implementation so Theme Builder can reliably produce brand-specific raster imagery.

## Why

Stock images cover generic photography. AI-generated images cover brand-specific compositions, concept illustrations, pattern backgrounds, product visualisations, and section accents. User feedback from the post-#1522 review: Theme Builder needs lots of visuals for best-quality websites.

## Proposed scope

- Extend `sd-ai-agent/generate-image` inputs with provider-supported options such as `size`, `style`, `variations`, and optional media-library reference images where supported.
- Save provenance metadata on generated attachments: provider/model, generation prompt, dimensions, and creation timestamp.
- Validate generated files after import: MIME type, dimensions, and moderation/safety flags when provider returns them.
- Teach Theme Builder prompt when to use `stock-image` vs `generate-image` (generic photography → stock; brand-specific/illustration/background motif → generate).
- Ensure all outputs are media-library attachments and scaffolded templates use local URLs/attachment IDs only.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Existing `sd-ai-agent/generate-image` remains the canonical ability name.
- [ ] Ability supports at least size/style/variation inputs where the configured provider supports them, with graceful no-op/fallback where unsupported.
- [ ] Generated images land in media library with provenance meta.
- [ ] Theme Builder prompt teaches stock vs generated-image selection.
- [ ] No external image URLs are written to theme files after generation.
- [ ] PHPUnit covers provider client mock, prompt validation, attachment meta storage, and unsupported-option fallback.

## Verification

```bash
composer phpstan
composer phpcs
npm run test:php -- --filter GenerateImage
```

Manual: run the Theme Builder walkthrough; confirm the agent generates a hero image, section accents, or pattern backgrounds when stock imagery is not specific enough.

## Related

- Existing ability: `includes/Abilities/ImageAbilities/GenerateImageAbility.php`
- Existing prompt references: `includes/Models/Agent.php`, `includes/Core/SystemInstructionBuilder.php`
- Filed during post-#1522 design review.

title: feat(abilities): scrape existing sites to pre-fill Theme Builder interviews
body:
> **MANDATORY before opening a PR:** satisfy the [Worker Self-Verification Protocol](https://github.com/Ultimate-Multisite/superdav-ai-agent/blob/main/AGENTS.md#worker-self-verification-protocol) in `AGENTS.md`. Run the full PHPUnit suite (`npm run test:php`, not filtered), `npm run lint:php|js|css`, `composer phpstan`, `npm run build`, and paste the verification summary block in the PR body.
>
> **Previous attempt closed: PR #1537.** Worker added `tests/SdAiAgent/Abilities/SiteScrapeAbilityTest.php` with 1 error + 3 failures, all caused by `SiteScraper::scrape()` URL validation rejecting test-fixture URLs before reaching cache / robots / parser logic:
> - `test_schema_org_parser_extracts_local_business_data` — `Undefined array key 0` at `SiteScrapeAbilityTest.php:78` (parser path)
> - `test_scrape_uses_transient_cache_to_prevent_redundant_fetches` — got `sd_ai_agent_invalid_scrape_url` WP_Error instead of cached array (`SiteScrapeAbilityTest.php:114`)
> - `test_scrape_respects_robots_txt_disallow` — got `sd_ai_agent_invalid_scrape_url` instead of `sd_ai_agent_site_scrape_robots_disallowed` (`SiteScrapeAbilityTest.php:132`)
> - `test_site_scrape_ability_returns_complete_optional_shape` — got `sd_ai_agent_invalid_scrape_url` instead of array (`SiteScrapeAbilityTest.php:151`)
>
> The URL validator must accept the fixture URLs used in the test (typically `https://example.com/...`). Either widen the validator to accept any valid absolute HTTP/HTTPS URL, or have the tests mock at the HTTP layer (`pre_http_request` filter) so they exercise the cache/robots/parser code paths without hitting the validator. The Playwright failures may cascade from this same defect — verify after the PHPUnit fix.

## Summary

Add a new ability `sd-ai-agent/site-scrape` that fetches and parses an
existing website to bootstrap the Theme Builder interview with real
brand data (name, tagline, address, phone, hours, about copy,
existing logo URL, social links, etc.). Used to dramatically shorten
the interview when the user already has a site they're rebuilding.

## Why

Most Theme Builder users will be migrating from an existing site, not
starting from nothing. Asking them to retype their address, hours,
about copy, and team bios is wasted effort. Scraping the existing
site once and pre-filling the interview turns a 20-minute interview
into a 2-minute "confirm what we found" session.

## Scope

### Inputs

- URL of an existing site (required)
- Optional: max pages to crawl (default 10)
- Optional: pages to target explicitly (e.g. `['/', '/about',
  '/contact', '/menu']`)
- Optional: extract preferences (full text vs structured-only)

### Outputs

Structured data:

```json
{
  "brand": {
    "name": "Bramble & Bean Coffee Co.",
    "tagline": "Slow down. Sip something good.",
    "logo_url": "https://existing-site.example/logo.png"
  },
  "contact": {
    "address": "47 Mill Lane, Hawthornden, Edinburgh EH18",
    "phone": "0131 555 0147",
    "email": "hello@example.com"
  },
  "hours": [
    { "day": "Tue", "open": "07:00", "close": "16:00" },
    ...
  ],
  "social": {
    "instagram": "https://instagram.com/example",
    "facebook": "..."
  },
  "pages": [
    { "url": "...", "title": "...", "text": "...", "headings": [...] }
  ]
}
```

### Implementation notes

- New `includes/Abilities/SiteScrapeAbility.php`
- New `includes/Services/SiteScraper.php` with:
  - `fetch()` via `wp_safe_remote_get()`
  - Schema.org JSON-LD parsing for structured data (lots of sites
    expose `Organization`, `LocalBusiness`, `Restaurant`, etc.)
  - Microformats / OpenGraph metadata parsing
  - Heuristic extraction for common patterns (phone regex, address
    via Google's libpostal-style parser or simple heuristics, hours
    in `<table>` patterns)
  - Fallback: send extracted page text + headings to the AI model
    with a structured-output schema and let the model fill the gaps
- Polite crawling: respect `robots.txt`, 1 req/s default rate
  limit, identify as `SuperdavAI/x.y.z (+plugin-url)`
- Cache results for 24 hours per URL to avoid re-fetching during
  the same interview session

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] New ability `sd-ai-agent/site-scrape` registered
- [ ] Returns the structured data shape above (with all fields
      optional — missing fields are returned as null, not absent)
- [ ] Schema.org / OpenGraph parsers cover common cases (test
      against 5+ real sites in test fixtures)
- [ ] Heuristic extractors handle phone, email, address, hours
- [ ] Falls back to AI-assisted extraction when heuristics fail
- [ ] Respects robots.txt and rate-limits
- [ ] Cache layer prevents redundant fetches
- [ ] Theme Builder agent prompt teaches it to offer this at the
      start of the interview: "Do you have an existing site? If yes,
      paste the URL and I'll pre-fill what I can."
- [ ] PHPUnit covers: schema.org parser, opengraph parser, hour
      heuristic, phone heuristic, address heuristic, cache layer,
      robots respect

## Verification

```bash
composer phpstan
composer phpcs
npm run test:php -- --filter SiteScrape
```

Manual: run the Theme Builder walkthrough; provide a real existing
café site URL; confirm the interview is shorter and starts pre-filled.

## Caveats

- Single-page apps (SPAs) won't yield useful HTML from a plain GET.
  Optional follow-up: integrate Playwright or a headless browser
  fallback for SPA sites. Out of scope for v1.
- Sites with anti-scraping (CloudFlare challenge, Akamai, etc.) will
  fail. Handle gracefully — return what was obtainable and let the
  agent ask for the rest.
- The user should consent to the scrape (one-line confirmation) since
  it makes outbound HTTP from their server. The ability surfaces this
  to the agent's UI layer.

## Related

- Filed during post-#1522 design review.
- Major accelerator for the "no placeholder content" issue — scraping
  produces the real data the agent then validates with the user.

title: feat(theme-builder): generate structured hospitality menu pages with prices
body:
> **MANDATORY before opening a PR:** satisfy the [Worker Self-Verification Protocol](https://github.com/Ultimate-Multisite/superdav-ai-agent/blob/main/AGENTS.md#worker-self-verification-protocol) in `AGENTS.md`. Run the full PHPUnit suite (`npm run test:php`, not filtered), `npm run lint:php|js|css`, `composer phpstan`, `npm run build`, and paste the verification summary block in the PR body. Filtered PHPUnit runs are NOT sufficient — they shipped CI-broken PRs in the first dispatch batch (closed PR #1537, PR #1538).

## Summary

For hospitality verticals (café, restaurant, bar, food truck), the
`/menu/` page is the single highest-traffic page on the site. It must
auto-generate as a structured categorised price list (categories →
items → prices, optionally descriptions), not as a single block of
prose.

## Why

A café's menu is the conversion-relevant content. A user landing on
`/menu/` wants to scan categories, find a drink, see a price, and
decide whether to visit. A prose paragraph saying "We serve a variety
of seasonal drinks" fails this completely.

## Scope

### Interview additions

The Theme Builder agent must ask, during the interview for hospitality
verticals:

1. "What categories does your menu have?" (e.g. Espresso, Pour-Over,
   Filter, Cold, Tea, Food)
2. For each category: "List the items, with prices."
3. Optional per item: short description (2 lines max), allergens,
   dietary tags (V, VG, GF)

### Page generation

Build `/menu/` with a structured layout. Possible block compositions:

- `<!-- wp:columns -->` per category, with `<!-- wp:heading -->` for
  the category name and `<!-- wp:group -->` per item containing the
  item name + price (right-aligned) + optional description.
- Or a custom block pattern `sd-ai-agent/menu-section` providing the
  same structure with theme-aware styling.

### Other verticals follow the same principle

- Restaurant → starters/mains/desserts/wines
- Service business → services with price ranges or "from £X"
- Shop → at minimum, featured products with price + buy buttons
  (WooCommerce required; agent should detect and integrate)
- Portfolio → projects with image + role + year

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] For hospitality verticals, the interview captures structured
      menu data (categories + items + prices + optional descriptions)
- [ ] The `/menu/` page renders as a categorised price list, not
      prose
- [ ] Item prices align consistently (right-aligned or tabular)
- [ ] Each category has a clear visual break
- [ ] Allergen / dietary tags render as small badges next to items
- [ ] No placeholder copy ("Our menu changes seasonally") — the page
      contains the user's real items or is not created
- [ ] PHPUnit covers menu structure rendering
- [ ] E2E test asserts `/menu/` contains at least one category and
      at least one priced item

## Verification

```bash
composer phpstan
composer phpcs
npm run test:php
npm run test:e2e:playwright -- onboarding-theme-builder
```

Manual: run the Theme Builder walkthrough for a café and a restaurant.
Inspect `/menu/`. It must be skim-readable in 5 seconds.

## Caveats

- Some businesses want a downloadable PDF menu instead of an HTML
  menu (à la carte restaurants do this). The interview should
  detect this preference and the agent can embed a PDF viewer
  alongside or instead of inline HTML.
- Price formatting depends on locale. Default to the locale of the
  WP site (`get_locale()`), with currency derived from address /
  country or asked in the interview.

## Related

- Filed during post-#1522 design review.
- Pairs with `feat(theme-builder): no placeholder content` — both
  require structured user input during interview.

title: feat(theme-builder): show mobile previews during design direction selection
body:
> **MANDATORY before opening a PR:** satisfy the [Worker Self-Verification Protocol](https://github.com/Ultimate-Multisite/superdav-ai-agent/blob/main/AGENTS.md#worker-self-verification-protocol) in `AGENTS.md`. Run the full PHPUnit suite (`npm run test:php`, not filtered), `npm run lint:php|js|css`, `composer phpstan`, `npm run build`, and paste the verification summary block in the PR body. Filtered PHPUnit runs are NOT sufficient — they shipped CI-broken PRs in the first dispatch batch (closed PR #1537, PR #1538).

## Summary

During the "pick a design direction" step, the Theme Builder agent
should present each candidate design as both a desktop preview
(~1280px) AND a mobile preview (~375px) side-by-side. The user is
choosing how their site will FEEL across devices, not just on
desktop.

## Why

The post-#1522 walkthrough produced three desktop-only previews. The
chosen direction (split layout: dark brown left + cream right) is
striking on desktop but its reflow behaviour at mobile width is
critical — a poorly-reflowed split layout becomes a tall, awkward
scroll. The user is making a design decision blind to half the
viewport spectrum.

## Scope

### Preview generation

The current preview pipeline writes one full HTML file per direction.
The new pipeline writes the same content but renders TWO viewports:

- Desktop: 1280×800 viewport screenshot
- Mobile: 375×812 viewport screenshot

Both are rendered server-side using Playwright or Chromium-headless
against the preview HTML, then saved to
`wp-content/uploads/sd-ai-agent/design-previews/<theme-slug>/`.

### UI presentation

The admin chat surfaces both screenshots side-by-side per direction.
Click-to-zoom on either. The screenshots are the ground truth — the
HTML preview file itself is also viewable for advanced inspection.

### Implementation notes

- Add a `PreviewRenderer` service in `includes/Services/`
- Reuse the existing Playwright setup from E2E tests for the
  headless rendering, or use a lighter `wp-cli puppeteer` if
  available
- Cache rendered screenshots so they don't regenerate on every
  message
- Add a `viewport` parameter to the file-write preview output so
  the agent can request additional viewports (tablet, ultra-wide)
  if needed

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Each design direction renders both desktop and mobile
      screenshots
- [ ] Both are shown to the user during direction selection
- [ ] Click-to-zoom works on both
- [ ] Screenshot generation is reliable (fails-soft: if mobile
      render fails, desktop still ships with a clear "mobile preview
      unavailable" marker — not a blocker)
- [ ] PHPUnit covers the PreviewRenderer service
- [ ] E2E test asserts both viewports are present in the chat UI

## Verification

```bash
composer phpstan
composer phpcs
npm run test:php -- --filter PreviewRenderer
npm run test:e2e:playwright -- onboarding-theme-builder
```

Manual: run the Theme Builder walkthrough; confirm both viewports
appear; pick a direction that looks bad on mobile; verify it's
visually obvious.

## Caveats

- Headless rendering on shared hosts may be blocked (no Chromium
  binary, restricted exec()). Provide a clean fallback that
  renders previews client-side via responsive iframes if
  server-side rendering is unavailable.
- This adds load time to the direction-selection step. Render in
  parallel and stream the desktop screenshot first so the user
  isn't blocked.

## Related

- Filed during post-#1522 design review.
- Pairs with `feat(theme-builder): preview-to-scaffold fidelity` —
  both improve trust in the preview step.

title: investigation(theme-builder): audit preview-to-scaffold visual fidelity gaps
body:
> **MANDATORY before opening a PR:** satisfy the [Worker Self-Verification Protocol](https://github.com/Ultimate-Multisite/superdav-ai-agent/blob/main/AGENTS.md#worker-self-verification-protocol) in `AGENTS.md`. Run the full PHPUnit suite (`npm run test:php`, not filtered), `npm run lint:php|js|css`, `composer phpstan`, `npm run build`, and paste the verification summary block in the PR body. Filtered PHPUnit runs are NOT sufficient — they shipped CI-broken PRs in the first dispatch batch (closed PR #1537, PR #1538).

## Summary

Investigate and document the gap between Theme Builder DESIGN PREVIEWS
(rich HTML mockups) and SCAFFOLD OUTPUT (the actual WordPress block
theme). Where design moments are lost during scaffold, either close
the gap or set the user's expectation honestly before they choose a
direction.

## Why

In the post-#1522 walkthrough, the chosen direction ("The Handwritten
Journal") featured a distinctive dashed-orange line under the
header. That detail was the soul of the direction. The built theme
did NOT clearly carry that detail through — it was either omitted or
visually attenuated.

This breaks user trust: "you showed me this, you built me that".

## Scope

This is an investigation issue first, then a corrective work issue.

### Phase 1: audit

For each of 5 sample directions across different verticals, produce a
side-by-side comparison:

- Original preview HTML render (desktop + mobile)
- Final scaffold render (desktop + mobile)
- Bullet list of design elements PRESENT in preview but ABSENT in
  scaffold

Output as a single doc at `docs/theme-builder-fidelity-audit.md`.

### Phase 2: classify gaps

For each gap, classify as:

- **Mechanical** — scaffold ability literally doesn't support this
  element (e.g. dashed borders aren't expressible in default block
  styles). Fix by extending `scaffold-block-theme`.
- **Promptable** — the agent could include this if its system
  prompt and tool descriptions explained how. Fix by updating
  prompts and adding examples.
- **Out of scope** — the preview took a liberty (e.g. custom JS
  animations) that no scaffold should ever ship. Fix by tightening
  the preview generation prompt so it doesn't promise what it can't
  deliver.

### Phase 3: close the top 10 gaps

Implement the top 10 fixes by total impact (preview → scaffold
fidelity). Each as a small PR.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Audit doc exists at `docs/theme-builder-fidelity-audit.md`
- [ ] At least 5 sample verticals are audited
- [ ] Each gap is classified and assigned a fix path
- [ ] Top 10 fixes are implemented and merged
- [ ] After fixes, re-running the same walkthrough produces a
      scaffold that visually matches the chosen preview at >= 85%
      identity (subjective design-team review)

## Verification

Visual review by user + at least one design-aware reviewer. Optional:
pixelmatch or odiff-based diff between rendered preview and rendered
scaffold over the same viewport, with a threshold check in E2E.

## Caveats

- This is a multi-PR effort. Phase 1 (audit) is small. Phase 2
  (classification) is medium. Phase 3 (fixes) may produce 10+ PRs.
- The honest path may be to constrain the preview generation prompt
  to ONLY use design elements the scaffold can faithfully reproduce.
  That's a cleaner contract than chasing parity in every direction.

## Related

- Filed during post-#1522 design review.
- Pairs with `feat(theme-builder): mobile preview` — both improve
  the trust contract around preview selection.

title: feat(theme-builder): add photo upload step to the discovery interview
body:
> **MANDATORY before opening a PR:** satisfy the [Worker Self-Verification Protocol](https://github.com/Ultimate-Multisite/superdav-ai-agent/blob/main/AGENTS.md#worker-self-verification-protocol) in `AGENTS.md`. Run the full PHPUnit suite (`npm run test:php`, not filtered), `npm run lint:php|js|css`, `composer phpstan`, `npm run build`, and paste the verification summary block in the PR body. Filtered PHPUnit runs are NOT sufficient — they shipped CI-broken PRs in the first dispatch batch (closed PR #1537, PR #1538).

## Summary

The Theme Builder interview should explicitly ask the user to upload
photos of their space, products, team, and events. Uploads land
directly in the media library and the agent weaves them into the
generated site (hero, gallery, about, menu items, etc.).

This is the third leg of the image acquisition strategy alongside
stock-image-search and generate-image.

## Why

User-supplied photos are always the most valuable imagery — they show
the actual business. The agent should treat photo upload as a
first-class interview step, not an afterthought.

## Scope

### Interview UX

During the discovery interview, after the brand vertical is
established, the agent asks:

> "I can use real photos to make this site shine. Do you have photos
> of (a) your space / shopfront, (b) your products / drinks / food,
> (c) your team, (d) any events or special moments? Upload as many
> as you like — I'll pick the best ones for each section. If you
> don't have any yet, I'll use a mix of stock and AI-generated
> images, and you can swap them later."

A drag-and-drop area appears inline in the chat. Uploaded files:

- Land in the media library
- Are tagged with `_sd_ai_agent_interview_upload` meta and a
  category guess (`space` / `product` / `team` / `event`) from
  filename + visual recognition (optional ML step) + the agent's
  conversation context
- Are surfaced back to the agent immediately with media IDs +
  thumbnails so it can plan their use

### Implementation notes

- New React component `OnboardingPhotoUpload` in
  `src/components/`
- Drag-and-drop wrapper around `wp.media.editor` or a direct
  `media-handle-upload` REST call
- Server-side: extend `MediaAbility` (or add a new
  `BulkUploadAbility`) to accept multiple files in one call
- Categorisation: simple heuristic on first pass (filename
  keywords); optional later upgrade via image classification

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Interview asks for photos at the appropriate moment
- [ ] User can drag-and-drop multiple files in the chat UI
- [ ] Uploaded files reach the media library
- [ ] Files are tagged so the agent can find them later
- [ ] The agent acknowledges uploads in the chat ("Got the 8
      photos — I'll use the shopfront for the hero and the latte
      art set for the menu page")
- [ ] No placeholder copy — if the user has zero photos, the agent
      falls back to stock + AI generation (per the other abilities)
- [ ] PHPUnit covers the bulk-upload path and meta tagging

## Verification

```bash
composer phpstan
composer phpcs
npm run test:php
npm run test:e2e:playwright -- onboarding-theme-builder
```

Manual: walkthrough with 5+ real photos uploaded. Confirm they
appear on the built site.

## Caveats

- Large uploads stress PHP `upload_max_filesize` and
  `post_max_size`. The component should chunk large files or warn
  the user to compress first.
- EXIF orientation handling matters — many phone photos come
  rotated. WordPress core handles this, but verify against the
  generated theme's image blocks.

## Related

- Filed during post-#1522 design review.
- Completes the image-acquisition trio with stock-image-search and
  generate-image.

title: feat(theme-builder): validate palette contrast before scaffold
body:
> **MANDATORY before opening a PR:** satisfy the [Worker Self-Verification Protocol](https://github.com/Ultimate-Multisite/superdav-ai-agent/blob/main/AGENTS.md#worker-self-verification-protocol) in `AGENTS.md`. Run the full PHPUnit suite (`npm run test:php`, not filtered), `npm run lint:php|js|css`, `composer phpstan`, `npm run build`, and paste the verification summary block in the PR body. Filtered PHPUnit runs are NOT sufficient — they shipped CI-broken PRs in the first dispatch batch (closed PR #1537, PR #1538).

## Summary

Before scaffolding a block theme, validate the chosen palette against
WCAG AA contrast minimums (4.5:1 for body text, 3:1 for large text and
UI components). Reject or auto-adjust palettes that fail.

## Why

The post-#1522 walkthrough produced a theme using sage green on
parchment for all-caps small-text kickers. Visually charming but
borderline on contrast. A site that fails WCAG isn't just an
accessibility problem — for businesses operating in the UK / EU /
US public sector it's a legal exposure.

The agent should catch this automatically, not rely on the user to
spot it.

## Scope

### Palette validation

Add a `PaletteValidator` service in `includes/Services/`:

```php
$validator = new PaletteValidator( $palette );
$result    = $validator->check();
// $result->failures: array of failing pairs (fg, bg, ratio, required)
// $result->suggestions: minimal hex adjustments to pass
```

For each pair the theme will combine (heading-on-bg, body-on-bg,
button-text-on-button-bg, link-on-bg, kicker-on-bg, etc.), compute
relative luminance and contrast ratio.

### Auto-correction

If a pair fails, offer the user:

1. A nudge to one or both colours that brings the pair into
   compliance (darken the foreground, lighten the background, or
   pick the nearest passing tone from a Material/Tailwind-style
   ramp).
2. The option to mark the pair as non-text (decorative) — those are
   exempt from contrast minimums.
3. The option to accept the failure with a documented exception
   (the resulting theme.json includes a comment noting the choice).

### Integration

Runs at the END of the direction-selection step, before
`scaffold-block-theme` is called. If a direction fails, the agent
either fixes it autonomously or surfaces the failure to the user
with options.

### Tooling

There are well-tested PHP libraries for this (e.g. `mexitek/phpcolors`
for manipulation, `tinycolor` patterns for contrast). Pick a small
dependency or implement from scratch — the WCAG contrast formula
is ~20 lines.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `PaletteValidator` service implemented and tested
- [ ] Theme Builder flow runs validation pre-scaffold
- [ ] Failing palettes trigger user-visible options
- [ ] Selected palette guaranteed to pass AA for body + large-text
      defined pairs, OR explicitly marked decorative
- [ ] PHPUnit covers ratio computation, failure detection, and
      suggestion logic
- [ ] E2E test runs a deliberately-failing palette and confirms the
      flow does not proceed to scaffold without resolution

## Verification

```bash
composer phpstan
composer phpcs
npm run test:php -- --filter PaletteValidator
npm run test:e2e:playwright -- onboarding-theme-builder
```

Manual: run the walkthrough with a low-contrast direction. Confirm
the agent surfaces the failure and resolves it before scaffolding.

## Caveats

- AAA (7:1) is stricter; we target AA. Document this clearly in the
  theme.json output.
- Some directions intentionally use low-contrast pairing for
  decorative-only elements. The validator must not produce false
  positives on those.

## Related

- Filed during post-#1522 design review.
- Lower priority than the content / imagery issues, but it's the
  kind of automation that quietly raises the floor on every site
  the agent produces.

title: bug(create-menu): support navigation labels distinct from page titles
body:
> **MANDATORY before opening a PR:** satisfy the [Worker Self-Verification Protocol](https://github.com/Ultimate-Multisite/superdav-ai-agent/blob/main/AGENTS.md#worker-self-verification-protocol) in `AGENTS.md`. Run the full PHPUnit suite (`npm run test:php`, not filtered), `npm run lint:php|js|css`, `composer phpstan`, `npm run build`, and paste the verification summary block in the PR body. Filtered PHPUnit runs are NOT sufficient — they shipped CI-broken PRs in the first dispatch batch (closed PR #1537, PR #1538).

## Summary

`sd-ai-agent/create-menu` should accept a `navigation_label` per item
that is distinct from the linked page's `post_title`. Current behaviour
forces the nav label to match the page title.

Example from the post-#1522 walkthrough: page titled "Shop Our Beans"
appeared in the nav verbatim, when the agent's design preview had
already (correctly) shortened it to "Shop" — three letters instead of
fifteen.

## Root cause

`CreateMenuAbility` (or whatever powers create-menu) uses
`wp_update_nav_menu_item()` with `menu-item-title` derived from the
linked post's title rather than from the caller's explicit value.

`wp_update_nav_menu_item()` already accepts a custom title via
`menu-item-title` — the ability just needs to plumb the caller-supplied
label through.

## Proposed fix

In `includes/Abilities/CreateMenuAbility.php`:

```php
'menu-item-title' => $item['navigation_label'] ?? $item['title'] ?? $page->post_title,
```

Schema addition:

```json
{
  "items": [
    {
      "page_id": 123,
      "navigation_label": "Shop"
    }
  ]
}
```

If `navigation_label` is omitted, fall back to the page title (current
behaviour, no regression).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Schema accepts `navigation_label` per item, optional
- [ ] Provided label is used as the rendered nav label
- [ ] Omitted label falls back to the page title (no regression)
- [ ] PHPUnit covers both the override and fallback paths

## Verification

```bash
composer phpstan
composer phpcs
npm run test:php -- --filter CreateMenuAbility
```

Manual: re-run the Theme Builder walkthrough; confirm "Shop Our Beans"
page renders as "Shop" in the nav.

## Caveats

- Same caveat as the menu-ordering issue: if the Theme Builder uses
  the block-navigation system (`wp:navigation-link`) instead of the
  classic nav menu, the fix is in the block markup the agent emits,
  not in `wp_update_nav_menu_item`.

## Related

- Filed during post-#1522 design review.
- Companion to `bug(create-menu): respect requested menu item order`.

title: feat(theme-builder): add sd-ai-agent/site-scrape to Theme Builder tier_1_tools
body:
## Context

PR #1546 adds the `sd-ai-agent/site-scrape` ability but does not add it to the Theme Builder agent's `tier_1_tools` list in `includes/Models/Agent.php`.

Currently the Theme Builder agent description (via `ThemeBuilderAbilities.php`) instructs the agent to use `site-scrape` at the start of every interview, but the ability is not explicitly listed as a Tier 1 tool. The agent can still reach it via `sd-ai-agent/ability-search` + `sd-ai-agent/ability-call` (which are in `$base_tools`), but this costs 2 extra round-trips.

## Fix

Add `'sd-ai-agent/site-scrape'` to the Theme Builder's curated `tier_1_tools` list in `Agent::get_theme_builder_definition()`, alongside `'sd-ai-agent/stock-image'` and `'sd-ai-agent/generate-image'` (the precedent from PR #1544).

**File:** `includes/Models/Agent.php` ~line 747-756

**Change:**
```php
// Before (line ~753-755):
// Image tools required for brand-specific and stock imagery (issue #1529).
'sd-ai-agent/stock-image',
'sd-ai-agent/generate-image',

// After:
// Site pre-fill (issue #1530) and imagery tools (issues #1528, #1529).
'sd-ai-agent/site-scrape',
'sd-ai-agent/stock-image',
'sd-ai-agent/generate-image',
```

**Test:** Add or extend a test in `tests/SdAiAgent/` verifying `site-scrape` appears in the Theme Builder `tier_1_tools`.

## Verification
```bash
npm run test:php
composer phpstan
```

No other files to change. PHPStan/lint should pass with no other changes needed.

title: bug(tests): StockImageAbilityTest asserts 'action: search' but implementation uses 'action=search'
body:
## Summary

`StockImageAbilityTest::test_theme_builder_system_prompt_references_imagery_workflow`
asserts the Theme Builder system prompt contains the literal string `'action: search'`
(colon-separated), but the actual `StockImageAbility::get_description()` body and the
system prompt baked from it use `'action=search'` (equals-separated, the standard
enum-parameter style).

Result: PHPUnit fails with `Failed asserting that '...action=search...' contains "action: search"`.

## Evidence

- `tests/SdAiAgent/Abilities/StockImageAbilityTest.php:461` — asserts `'action: search'`.
- `includes/Abilities/ImageAbilities/StockImageAbility.php:47` — uses `'action=search'`
  in both the registered description and the `get_description()` return.
- `includes/Abilities/ImageAbilities/StockImageAbility.php:228` — code comment uses
  `'action=search'` too.

`grep -n "action: search" includes/` returns no matches.

This failure shipped to `main` in PR #1544 (after the conflict-resolution merge) but
was not surfaced because CI on the merge commit was the WSV unit-test step running
under a slightly different fixture state. The next worker (#1531) hit the failure on
its own rebase against `main` and could not distinguish a pre-existing failure from
its own regression.

## Reproduction

```bash
git checkout main && git pull
npm run test:php -- --filter test_theme_builder_system_prompt_references_imagery_workflow
# expect Failures: 1
```

## Decision needed

Two valid fixes; reviewer to pick:

1. **Update the test** to match the actual prompt syntax — change `'action: search'`
   to `'action=search'` (and the same for `import`). This is the smaller change and
   matches the existing in-code description style.

2. **Update the implementation** so the system prompt uses `'action: search'`
   (colon style). This is more invasive — touches the ability description, the
   system prompt template in `ThemeBuilderAbilities`, and any UI text that mirrors
   it.

Preference: option 1 (update the test). The `action=NAME` style is consistent with
how every other tool in the codebase documents enum parameters in their
descriptions.

## Affects

- `tests/SdAiAgent/Abilities/StockImageAbilityTest.php` (line 461, 466)
- (option 2 only) `includes/Abilities/ImageAbilities/StockImageAbility.php`
- (option 2 only) `includes/Abilities/ThemeBuilderAbilities.php`

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `StockImageAbilityTest::test_theme_builder_system_prompt_references_imagery_workflow`
      passes against current `main`.
- [ ] No regression in the imagery-workflow guidance — the prompt still references
      `stock-image` action selection.

title: bug(tests): PluginUpdaterTest fails with sd_ai_agent_mkdir_failed in tests-wordpress container
body:
## Summary

Five PHPUnit tests in `PluginUpdaterTest.php` and one in `PluginBuilderIntegrationTest.php`
fail intermittently with `sd_ai_agent_mkdir_failed: Could not create directory:
/var/www/html/wp-content/uploads/sd-ai-staging/sd-test-updater-phpunit/` (or
`/wp-content/uploads/sd-ai-backups/sd-test-updater-phpunit-<timestamp>/`).

The failure surfaces only inside the `tests-wordpress` Docker container — the test
fixture cannot create directories under `wp-content/uploads/sd-ai-*/`.

## Affected tests

- `SdAiAgent\Tests\PluginBuilder\PluginUpdaterTest::test_stage_creates_directory`
- `SdAiAgent\Tests\PluginBuilder\PluginUpdaterTest::test_test_staged_passes_for_valid_plugin`
- `SdAiAgent\Tests\PluginBuilder\PluginUpdaterTest::test_rollback_restores_from_backup`
- `SdAiAgent\Tests\PluginBuilder\PluginUpdaterTest::test_update_replaces_live_plugin_files`
- `SdAiAgent\Tests\PluginBuilder\PluginBuilderIntegrationTest::test_updater_happy_path_replaces_files`

## Evidence

Worker for #1531 hit these on its rebased branch (main HEAD includes #1542, #1544,
#1545, #1546, #1547). Test summary from worker run:

```text
Tests: 2383, Assertions: 6459, Errors: 1, Failures: 10, Skipped: 104.
```

Failure detail (worker captured to `/tmp/phpunit-output.txt:160`):

```text
8) SdAiAgent\Tests\PluginBuilder\PluginUpdaterTest::test_test_staged_passes_for_valid_plugin
Failed asserting that WP_Error Object (
    'errors' => Array (
        'sd_ai_agent_mkdir_failed' => Array (
            0 => 'Could not create directory: /var/www/html/wp-content/uploads/sd-ai-staging/sd-test-updater-phpunit/'
        )
    )
    ...
) is of type "string".
```

## Hypothesis

The `tests-wordpress` container runs as user `1000:1000` (per
`~/.wp-env/<hash>/docker-compose.yml`). The `wp-content/uploads` directory is owned by
`www-data` (33:33) inside the container, so a `mkdir` from PHPUnit fails on permission.

This is intermittent because some test runs hit the upload dir after a previous test
created it with 777 perms, while others run first and fail.

## Reproduction

```bash
docker exec <wp-env-tests-wordpress-1> bash -c 'cd /var/www/html/wp-content/plugins/sd-ai-agent && php vendor/bin/phpunit --filter PluginUpdaterTest'
# expect 4-5 failures with sd_ai_agent_mkdir_failed
```

## Proposed fix

In `tests/SdAiAgent/PluginBuilder/PluginUpdaterTest.php::setUp()`, ensure the upload
sub-directories exist with correct permissions before each test:

```php
@mkdir( WP_CONTENT_DIR . '/uploads/sd-ai-staging', 0775, true );
@mkdir( WP_CONTENT_DIR . '/uploads/sd-ai-backups', 0775, true );
@chmod( WP_CONTENT_DIR . '/uploads/sd-ai-staging', 0775 );
@chmod( WP_CONTENT_DIR . '/uploads/sd-ai-backups', 0775 );
```

OR fix the `PluginUpdater` to use a tmp directory that is guaranteed writable.

OR add a `.wp-env.json` `mappings` entry to pre-create the upload dirs with 0775.

## Affects

- `tests/SdAiAgent/PluginBuilder/PluginUpdaterTest.php`
- `tests/SdAiAgent/PluginBuilder/PluginBuilderIntegrationTest.php`
- (potentially) `.wp-env.json`
- (potentially) `includes/PluginBuilder/PluginUpdater.php` (if the prod code has the
  same mkdir issue in real WordPress installs)

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All `PluginUpdaterTest` tests pass against `main`
- [ ] `PluginBuilderIntegrationTest::test_updater_happy_path_replaces_files` passes
- [ ] No regression in actual plugin-updater behaviour

title: Improve AI block-content validity (Studio-inspired six-phase plan)
body:
## Summary

Improve AI-generated block validity by adopting three patterns from Automattic Studio (github.com/Automattic/studio, `trunk` branch). Today our `sd-ai-agent/validate-block-content` ability uses PHP `parse_blocks()` which only checks comment-delimiter structure and silently accepts class/attribute drift that the editor itself rejects on load. This parent tracks the six child improvements that close that gap.

Prior art: #1038 (closed) rewrote the gutenberg-blocks skill and unhid block tools. This parent is the next iteration — replacing the static validator with real `wp.blocks.validateBlock()` and enforcing structural patterns.

## Research

Full architecture map of Studio's three-pillar approach (live validator + HTML policy + system-prompt cascade rules) captured in session conversation 2026-05-20. Source files:

- `apps/cli/ai/block-validator.ts` — runs each block through `wp.blocks.validateBlock( block, blockType )` in a real headless Chromium tab logged into the actual site's editor.
- `apps/cli/ai/block-content-policy.ts` — hard rule: `core/html` only for inline SVG / `<marquee>` / single `<script>`.
- `apps/cli/ai/plugin-recommendations.ts` — pattern → message map; e.g. `<form>` → "use Jetpack Forms" with example markup.
- `apps/cli/ai/system-prompt.ts` — "Block-theme layout cascade", "Working cadence", scaffold-then-fill rules.
- `apps/cli/ai/tools/scaffold-theme.ts` — minimal block-theme skeleton.

title: Phase 1: Live wp.blocks.validateBlock() validator (replaces parse_blocks)
body:
Ref #1583 ## What Replace the structural-only `parse_blocks()` validation in `sd-ai-agent/validate-block-content` with a live validator that runs each block through the real Gutenberg `wp.blocks.validateBlock( block, blockType )` save-function comparison — exactly the check the editor itself performs on load. Returns per-block `{ isValid, issues, originalContent, expectedContent }` so the model gets the **diff** of what it wrote vs what `save()` would have produced. Two implementation paths: - **Path A — in-process (preferred):** Render an admin-only page that enqueues `wp-blocks`, `wp-block-library`, and all registered third-party block scripts, then exposes a JS bridge (postMessage from a hidden iframe loaded in the admin chat UI) that runs the validator synchronously. No external browser required. - **Path B — headless Chromium:** Vendor Studio's `EditorPage` pattern using `chrome-php/chrome` or `symfony/panther`. Heavier dependency; works without modifying admin pages. **Recommendation: Path A.** We already run inside WordPress. Studio went headless because it runs externally. ## Why `parse_blocks()` only confirms block-comment delimiters parse. It silently accepts: - Missing `wp-block-heading` / `wp-block-list` classes (validator-applied classes the model often omits) - Attribute serialization drift (e.g. `{"level":3}` written but `

` in markup) - Class-attribute mismatches that strip core layout CSS (`alignwide`, `is-layout-flex`, `has-X-color`) - Inner-block markup that doesn't match the parent block's `save()` template All of these produce "This block contains unexpected or invalid content" in the editor — i.e. exactly the symptom users see today. title: Phase 3: Block-theme layout cascade rules in skill + system prompt
body:
Ref #1583 ## What Add a new "Block-theme layout cascade" section to `includes/Models/skills/gutenberg-blocks.md` (and ensure it's loaded into the system prompt for page-generation tool calls) teaching the three structural patterns for breaking out of `contentSize`: 1. **Full-bleed section + constrained inner content** (most common hero pattern) 2. **Full-bleed section + full-bleed inner** (image grids, edge-to-edge galleries) 3. **Standard constrained content** (omit `align`) Plus the failure-mode wording: *"if a 'full-width' section only spans the content column (~700px at 1280px viewport), the block markup is missing `align: \"full\"` on the outer group or has a mismatched inner `layout` type — fix in markup, not CSS."* ## Why Today our skills cover individual block markup well but miss the structural rule causing ~80% of "looks broken" outputs: children of `core/post-content` (or any `is-layout-constrained` container) are pinned to `theme.json` `settings.layout.contentSize` (~700px default). Custom CSS like `.hero { width: 100% }` does NOT win against `.is-layout-constrained > *:not(.alignwide):not(.alignfull)`. The model tries to fix the symptom with CSS, fails, and the user sees a narrow hero on a 1920px screen. Studio reference: `apps/cli/ai/system-prompt.ts` — search `"## Block-theme layout cascade"`. Highest-impact ~500-character addition possible to the prompt. ## Files to Modify - **EDIT:** `includes/Models/skills/gutenberg-blocks.md` — add new section after "Core rules" (around line 38). ~40 lines including worked example for each pattern. - **EDIT:** `includes/Models/skills/block-themes.md` — add a "See also: `gutenberg-blocks` → Block-theme layout cascade" cross-reference. - **AUDIT:** `includes/Core/SkillAutoInjector.php` — confirm `gutenberg-blocks` triggers on "hero", "full-width", "section", "landing", "landing page". Add missing keywords. ## Implementation Steps ### 1. Section content (adapt from Studio's `LOCAL_DESIGN_GUIDELINES` cascade subsection) ```markdown ## Block-theme layout cascade WordPress constrains children of `core/post-content` (and any constrained-layout container) to `theme.json`'s `settings.layout.contentSize` (~700px by default). Custom CSS like `.hero { width: 100% }` does NOT win against core's layout selectors (`.is-layout-constrained > *:not(.alignwide):not(.alignfull)`) because they're more specific. To break out of the content width, use these three patterns: ### Pattern A — Full-bleed section, constrained inner content Most common: full-width hero with text in the middle.

Inner content sits at contentSize

### Pattern B — Full-bleed section, full-bleed inner Image grids, edge-to-edge galleries, full-bleed footers.
### Pattern C — Standard constrained Omit `align` entirely; write blocks normally. ### Failure mode (memorise this) If a "full-width" section only spans the content column (~700px at a 1280px viewport), the block markup is missing `align: "full"` on the outer group or has a mismatched inner `layout` type. **Fix in markup, not CSS.** ``` ### 2. Verify auto-injector triggers ```bash git grep -n "trigger\|keyword" includes/Core/SkillAutoInjector.php ``` Add "hero", "full-width", "landing page", "section" if missing. ### 3. Cross-reference Add to `block-themes.md`: ```markdown ## See also - `gutenberg-blocks` → Block-theme layout cascade (the cause of ~80% of "looks broken" outputs) ``` ## Verification ```bash # Skill loads and contains the cascade rules wp eval ' $body = file_get_contents(SD_AI_AGENT_DIR . "/includes/Models/skills/gutenberg-blocks.md"); echo strpos($body, "Block-theme layout cascade") !== false ? "OK" : "MISSING"; ' # Auto-injection test npm run test:php -- --filter SkillAutoInjectorTest npm run verify ``` ## Acceptance Criteria - [ ] `gutenberg-blocks.md` contains the new `## Block-theme layout cascade` section with all three patterns and the failure-mode paragraph. - [ ] At least one auto-injector test asserts the skill loads for prompts containing "hero", "full-width", "landing page". - [ ] `block-themes.md` includes the cross-reference. - [ ] Tests, lint, build pass. ## Estimate ~1.5 h. title: Phase 4: Scaffold-then-fill cadence in agent prompt
body:
Ref #1583

## What

Add a "Working cadence" section to the agent system prompt instructing the model to:

- Write/Edit **one file per turn** for content >50 lines (read-only and small ops can batch)
- For long `style.css`: skeleton with `:root {}` + anchor comments first, fill one anchor per Edit
- For long page content: stage in a temp draft post with `<!-- section:hero -->` anchors, fill anchors one Edit at a time, apply once via `wp_update_post()`
- Never overwrite a freshly scaffolded `style.css` (it has the required theme header)

Audit `ScaffoldBlockThemeAbility` to confirm it produces a deliberately minimal baseline (no opinionated design content) matching Studio's `scaffold_theme` output.

## Why

Two failures the cadence rule eliminates:

1. **Gateway timeouts.** Asking a model to produce a complete 600-line `style.css` in one turn frequently times out, returns partial output, or burns the entire turn budget on a single file. Cadence is forced backpressure that produces deliverable increments.
2. **Lost screenshot-fix loop.** The validate → screenshot → fix loop only works if visual increments are small enough to inspect. A monolithic write blocks the feedback loop until the whole thing is done.

Studio reference: `apps/cli/ai/system-prompt.ts` — search `"## Working cadence"`. Specifically the "After site_create (or 'redesign'/'rebuild'/'start over' triggers), the next turn MUST be small" rule and the long-file skeleton/anchor approach.

## Files to Modify

- **EDIT:** `includes/Compat/ai-client/class-wp-ai-client-prompt-builder.php` — add `build_working_cadence_section()` returning the cadence rules string; inject into system prompt for conversations with content-generation or theme-modification tool calls.
- **EDIT or NEW:** `includes/Models/skills/site-specification.md` and/or a new `working-cadence.md` skill.
- **AUDIT:** `includes/Abilities/ScaffoldBlockThemeAbility.php` (590 lines) — confirm output is minimal. If it currently writes opinionated CSS, file a follow-up to slim it down.

## Implementation Steps

### 1. Cadence text (adapt from Studio; trim Studio-specific tool refs)

> **Working cadence:** one Write or Edit per turn for content >50 lines. Read-only inspection tools (`get-post`, `list-posts`, `get-block-type`) may be combined within a turn. Short prose between tools — no long design-plan essays.
>
> **Long files (style.css >200 lines, page content >300 lines): skeleton first, then fill across Edits.**
>
> - `style.css`: skeleton = `:root { ... }` custom properties + 6–10 anchor comments `/* === <concern> === */` (e.g. `reset`, `typography`, `hero`, `features`, `cta`, `footer`, `responsive`), <2KB total. Fill one anchor per Edit (300–2000B each) — `oldString` is the anchor line, `newString` is `<anchor>\n\n<styles>`.
> - Page content: create the post empty (`wp_insert_post` with empty content), write block markup to a draft using anchor comments `<!-- section:hero -->`, fill one anchor per Edit, then `wp_update_post()` with the assembled content.
>
> **Never overwrite a freshly scaffolded `style.css`** — it contains the required theme header. Always `Edit` to append, never `Write` to replace.

### 2. Wire into prompt builder

Render only when conversation includes a content-generation tool call (avoid bloating Q&A prompts). Use existing tool-detection logic in `class-wp-ai-client-prompt-builder.php` or add a flag in `Settings`.

### 3. Audit `ScaffoldBlockThemeAbility`

- Confirm it does not write opinionated CSS into scaffolded `style.css`.
- Confirm `theme.json` only sets `appearanceTools: true` and version (no custom palettes/typography/layout) — matches Studio's `renderThemeJson()`.
- If either is wrong, open follow-up issue.

## Verification

```bash
# Prompt builder includes cadence when content tools are in scope
npm run test:php -- --filter PromptBuilderCadenceTest

# Scaffolded theme has minimal style.css (theme header only)
wp eval '
  do_action("sd_ai_agent_scaffold_theme", ["name" => "Test Theme", "slug" => "test-theme"]);
  $css = file_get_contents(WP_CONTENT_DIR . "/themes/test-theme/style.css");
  echo strlen($css) < 500 ? "MINIMAL" : "BLOATED";
'

npm run verify
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] System prompt contains "Working cadence" section when a content-generation tool is in scope.
- [ ] System prompt does NOT contain it for pure-Q&A turns (regression test).
- [ ] `ScaffoldBlockThemeAbility` produces `style.css` with theme header only (<500 bytes) — fail loudly if regressed.
- [ ] At least one integration test exercises the "skeleton → anchor fill" pattern end-to-end.
- [ ] Tests, lint, build pass.

## Estimate

~3 h including audit and integration test.

## What

`ScaffoldBlockThemeAbility::default_theme_json()` currently produces a `theme.json` with:

- 3 custom colour palettes (`foreground`, `background`, `accent`)
- Layout sizes (`contentSize: 720px`, `wideSize: 1200px`)

title: lint-staged pre-commit hook self-blocks on unrelated bin/render-preview.js error
body:
## Symptom

The Husky pre-commit hook runs `wp-scripts lint-js --fix` via lint-staged when any `src/**/*.{js,jsx}` file is staged. The lint task is invoked without an argument override, so wp-scripts lints the whole project including `bin/render-preview.js` — which has a pre-existing `import/no-extraneous-dependencies` error:

```
/bin/render-preview.js
  64:21  error  'playwright' should be listed in the project's dependencies. Run 'npm i -S playwright' to add it
```

Result: any PR that touches a `src/` JS file is blocked by an error in an unrelated file outside the staged set, and the contributor has to use `--no-verify` (see PR for GH#1584, where the Phase 1 validator commit had to bypass the hook even though the staged files were lint-clean).

## Cause

`package.json` lint-staged config:

```json
"src/**/*.{js,jsx}": ["wp-scripts lint-js --fix"]
```

lint-staged passes the matched file list as positional args to the command — but `wp-scripts lint-js` invokes ESLint with its own glob defaults rather than honouring the passed paths, so it lints far more than just the staged files.

## Fix

Two options:

1. **Switch the lint-staged command** to ESLint directly, e.g.
   `"src/**/*.{js,jsx}": ["eslint --fix"]`. Then lint-staged's positional args go straight to ESLint and only the staged files are linted.

2. **Add `playwright` to devDependencies** so `bin/render-preview.js` no longer errors. Unblocks the hook for everyone immediately but does not address the underlying broad-lint behaviour.

Recommendation: do (1) (correctness) and optionally (2) if `bin/render-preview.js` is meant to be runnable without extra installs.

## Discovered while

Implementing GH#1584 (live block validator). All four hard verification gates passed (PHPUnit 2557/2557, lint:php, lint:js, lint:css, PHPStan, build) but the pre-commit hook still blocked the commit because of `bin/render-preview.js`. Used `--no-verify` to push past per AGENTS.md hook-self-block protocol and filed this issue as the required sibling-bug record.

title: PluginSandbox — Three-layer plugin safety testing
body:
## Summary

Build the foundational sandbox class that every other Plugin Builder component depends on. Implements a three-layer safety model to test generated/modified plugins without risking the parent WordPress process.

**This is the highest-priority issue — everything else depends on it.**

## Files

- **NEW**: `includes/PluginBuilder/PluginSandbox.php`

## Implementation Details

### Class: `GratisAiAgent\PluginBuilder\PluginSandbox`

Three public methods, one per safety layer:

#### Layer 1: `syntax_check(string \$file_path): array`
- Runs \`php -l \$file_path\` via \`proc_open()\` (not \`exec()\` — need stderr capture)
- Returns \`['pass' => bool, 'errors' => string[], 'file' => string]\`
- Must handle: missing file, non-PHP file, timeout (2s max)
- Use \`proc_open()\` with pipes for stdout/stderr, \`proc_close()\` for exit code
- Can also accept a directory path and check all \`.php\` files recursively

#### Layer 2: \`isolated_include_test(string \$plugin_dir, string \$main_file): array\`
- Writes a temporary sandbox test script to \`wp-content/gratis-ai-staging/sandbox-test-{random}.php\`
- Script contents: loads \`wp-load.php\` with \`--skip-plugins\` context, then \`include_once\` on the plugin main file
- Executes via: \`proc_open('php /path/to/wp-content/gratis-ai-staging/sandbox-test-{random}.php')\`
- Alternative (preferred if WP-CLI available): \`wp eval-file sandbox-test.php --skip-plugins\`
- Captures stdout, stderr, and exit code
- Returns \`['pass' => bool, 'errors' => string[], 'output' => string, 'duration_ms' => int]\`
- Cleans up temp script after test
- Timeout: 10s max (kill subprocess if exceeded)

The sandbox test PHP script template:
\`\`\`php
<?php
// Minimal WordPress bootstrap without plugins
define('ABSPATH', '{abspath}');
define('WP_PLUGIN_DIR', '{plugin_dir}');
// Don't load plugins during this test
define('WP_INSTALLING', true);
require_once ABSPATH . 'wp-settings.php';
// Try to include the plugin file
try {
    include_once '{plugin_main_file}';
    echo 'SANDBOX_OK';
} catch (Throwable \$e) {
    echo 'SANDBOX_FAIL:' . \$e->getMessage();
    exit(1);
}
\`\`\`

#### Layer 3: \`safe_activate(string \$plugin_file, string \$plugin_dir): array\`
- Sets a transient flag: \`set_transient('gratis_ai_sandbox_activating', \$plugin_file, 30)\`
- Registers a shutdown function that checks for fatal errors during activation
- Calls \`activate_plugin(\$plugin_file)\`
- If activation succeeds: delete transient, return success
- If activation fails (WP_Error or fatal): deactivate, restore backup, return failure details
- The transient flag enables auto-recovery: a mu-plugin or early hook checks on next request if the transient exists and the plugin caused a fatal, it auto-deactivates

Auto-recovery mechanism:
- Register via \`register_shutdown_function()\` in \`safe_activate()\`
- On fatal: the shutdown function logs the error, sets a transient with the error details
- Next request: check transient in an early \`plugins_loaded\` hook, auto-deactivate if still set

#### Helper: \`check_all(string \$plugin_dir, string \$main_file): array\`
- Convenience method that runs Layer 1 + Layer 2 sequentially
- Short-circuits on Layer 1 failure (no point running Layer 2 if syntax is broken)
- Returns combined results

### Patterns to follow

- Model on existing error handling in \`WordPressAbilities.php\` (return WP_Error objects)
- Use \`WP_Filesystem\` for file operations (see \`FileAbilities.php\` pattern)
- PSR-4: \`namespace GratisAiAgent\PluginBuilder;\`
- PHP 8.2+, \`declare(strict_types=1);\`, typed parameters and return types

### Testing

- Unit test: syntax_check with valid PHP, invalid PHP, missing file
- Unit test: isolated_include_test with a known-good plugin, a plugin with a fatal
- Integration test: safe_activate with a simple plugin
- Test timeout handling for hung subprocesses
- Test cleanup of temp files on success and failure

### Verification

\`\`\`bash
composer phpstan
composer phpcs
npm run test:php
\`\`\`

title: Split multi-part assistant messages with parallel function_calls before persisting to history
body:
## Bug

Conversations that include parallel tool calls (from Anthropic Claude) or text+tool_call assistant turns (from OpenAI gpt-5.x via the Responses API) fail with:

> Error: Function call parts must be the only part in a message for the OpenAI Responses API.

The exception is thrown client-side by `OpenAiTextGenerationModel::validateMessages()` in the `ai-provider-for-openai` plugin (commit `39ca23e`/dev branch, also v1.0.3) *before* any HTTP request is sent. Trace evidence (`wp_sd_ai_agent_provider_trace` rows 3569–3571): `status_code=0`, `error='no_result_event'`, `duration_ms ~20`, empty `response_body`.

## Root cause

`AgentLoop::run()` at `includes/Core/AgentLoop.php:733` appends the assistant `Message` verbatim:

```
$assistant_message = $result->toMessage();
…
$this->history[] = $assistant_message;
```

`$result->toMessage()` returns the first candidate, which can contain multiple parts:
- `[function_call, function_call]` — Anthropic parallel tool_use blocks
- `[text, function_call]` — assistant said something then called a tool
- `[text, function_call, function_call, function_call]` — text + parallel calls

The OpenAI Responses API contract requires each `function_call` to be its own top-level input item; a single `Message` cannot serialise into one. `ConversationSerializer::append_tool_response()` already solves the mirror problem for `function_response` (one tool result per message), but the equivalent splitter on the **assistant** side is missing.

## Trace evidence

Long conversation that started against Claude then switched to gpt-5.5. Offending messages observed in trace 3571:

| msg | parts | shape | ID format |
|---|---|---|---|
| `[01]` | 2 | `function_call + function_call` | `toolu_…` (Anthropic) |
| `[44]` | 2 | `text + function_call` | `functions.xxx:14` (OpenAI) |
| `[46]` | 4 | `text + 3× function_call` (parallel `file-write`) | OpenAI |
| `[54]` | 3 | `text + 2× function_call` (parallel `ability-call`) | OpenAI |

## Fix

Add `ConversationSerializer::append_assistant_message( array &\$history, Message \$message )`:
- ≤1 part, or no `function_call` part → append as-is
- Otherwise → split into one `ModelMessage` for non-function_call parts (text/reasoning) followed by one `ModelMessage` per `function_call` part, preserving order

Replace `\$this->history[] = \$assistant_message;` in `AgentLoop::run` with the call to the new helper.

## Tests

PHPUnit regression for each offending shape; assert that after appending, every resulting `Message` satisfies the invariant `count(function_call parts) <= 1 && (count(parts) <= 1 || no function_call part)`.

## Files

- includes/Core/ConversationSerializer.php
- includes/Core/AgentLoop.php:733
- tests/Unit/Core/ConversationSerializerTest.php (new or extend)

title: Use shared WordPress PHPUnit test runner
