Add a portable runner that uses a shared/global WordPress core + wordpress-tests-lib checkout and a local test DB so this plugin and sibling WordPress plugins can run PHPUnit without starting wp-env.

title: GH#1529 — feat(generate-image): add Theme Builder options, variations, and provenance metadata
body:
## Summary

Enhance the existing `sd-ai-agent/generate-image` ability for Theme Builder usage: richer inputs, multiple variations, media provenance metadata, and clearer prompt guidance for when AI generation beats stock photography.

The current code already registers `SdAiAgent\Abilities\ImageAbilities\GenerateImageAbility` through `sd-ai-agent/generate-image`. This issue is NOT to add a duplicate ability; it is to upgrade the existing implementation so Theme Builder can reliably produce brand-specific raster imagery.

## Why

Stock images cover generic photography. AI-generated images cover brand-specific compositions, concept illustrations, pattern backgrounds, product visualisations, and section accents. User feedback from the post-#1522 review: Theme Builder needs lots of visuals for best-quality websites.

## Proposed scope

- Extend `sd-ai-agent/generate-image` inputs with provider-supported options such as `size`, `style`, `variations`, and optional media-library reference images where supported.
- Save provenance metadata on generated attachments: provider/model, generation prompt, dimensions, and creation timestamp.
- Validate generated files after import: MIME type, dimensions, and moderation/safety flags when provider returns them.
- Teach Theme Builder prompt when to use `stock-image` vs `generate-image` (generic photography → stock; brand-specific/illustration/background motif → generate).
- Ensure all outputs are media-library attachments and scaffolded templates use local URLs/attachment IDs only.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Existing `sd-ai-agent/generate-image` remains the canonical ability name.
- [ ] Ability supports at least size/style/variation inputs where the configured provider supports them, with graceful no-op/fallback where unsupported.
- [ ] Generated images land in media library with provenance meta.
- [ ] Theme Builder prompt teaches stock vs generated-image selection.
- [ ] No external image URLs are written to theme files after generation.
- [ ] PHPUnit covers provider client mock, prompt validation, attachment meta storage, and unsupported-option fallback.

## Verification

```bash
composer phpstan
composer phpcs
npm run test:php -- --filter GenerateImage
```

Manual: run the Theme Builder walkthrough; confirm the agent generates a hero image, section accents, or pattern backgrounds when stock imagery is not specific enough.

## Related

- Existing ability: `includes/Abilities/ImageAbilities/GenerateImageAbility.php`
- Existing prompt references: `includes/Models/Agent.php`, `includes/Core/SystemInstructionBuilder.php`
- Filed during post-#1522 design review.

title: GH#1530 — feat(abilities): scrape existing sites to pre-fill Theme Builder interviews
body:
## Summary

Add a new ability `sd-ai-agent/site-scrape` that fetches and parses an
existing website to bootstrap the Theme Builder interview with real
brand data (name, tagline, address, phone, hours, about copy,
existing logo URL, social links, etc.). Used to dramatically shorten
the interview when the user already has a site they're rebuilding.

## Why

Most Theme Builder users will be migrating from an existing site, not
starting from nothing. Asking them to retype their address, hours,
about copy, and team bios is wasted effort. Scraping the existing
site once and pre-filling the interview turns a 20-minute interview
into a 2-minute "confirm what we found" session.

## Scope

### Inputs

- URL of an existing site (required)
- Optional: max pages to crawl (default 10)
- Optional: pages to target explicitly (e.g. `['/', '/about',
  '/contact', '/menu']`)
- Optional: extract preferences (full text vs structured-only)

### Outputs

Structured data:

```json
{
  "brand": {
    "name": "Bramble & Bean Coffee Co.",
    "tagline": "Slow down. Sip something good.",
    "logo_url": "https://existing-site.example/logo.png"
  },
  "contact": {
    "address": "47 Mill Lane, Hawthornden, Edinburgh EH18",
    "phone": "0131 555 0147",
    "email": "hello@example.com"
  },
  "hours": [
    { "day": "Tue", "open": "07:00", "close": "16:00" },
    ...
  ],
  "social": {
    "instagram": "https://instagram.com/example",
    "facebook": "..."
  },
  "pages": [
    { "url": "...", "title": "...", "text": "...", "headings": [...] }
  ]
}
```

### Implementation notes

- New `includes/Abilities/SiteScrapeAbility.php`
- New `includes/Services/SiteScraper.php` with:
  - `fetch()` via `wp_safe_remote_get()`
  - Schema.org JSON-LD parsing for structured data (lots of sites
    expose `Organization`, `LocalBusiness`, `Restaurant`, etc.)
  - Microformats / OpenGraph metadata parsing
  - Heuristic extraction for common patterns (phone regex, address
    via Google's libpostal-style parser or simple heuristics, hours
    in `<table>` patterns)
  - Fallback: send extracted page text + headings to the AI model
    with a structured-output schema and let the model fill the gaps
- Polite crawling: respect `robots.txt`, 1 req/s default rate
  limit, identify as `SuperdavAI/x.y.z (+plugin-url)`
- Cache results for 24 hours per URL to avoid re-fetching during
  the same interview session

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] New ability `sd-ai-agent/site-scrape` registered
- [ ] Returns the structured data shape above (with all fields
      optional — missing fields are returned as null, not absent)
- [ ] Schema.org / OpenGraph parsers cover common cases (test
      against 5+ real sites in test fixtures)
- [ ] Heuristic extractors handle phone, email, address, hours
- [ ] Falls back to AI-assisted extraction when heuristics fail
- [ ] Respects robots.txt and rate-limits
- [ ] Cache layer prevents redundant fetches
- [ ] Theme Builder agent prompt teaches it to offer this at the
      start of the interview: "Do you have an existing site? If yes,
      paste the URL and I'll pre-fill what I can."
- [ ] PHPUnit covers: schema.org parser, opengraph parser, hour
      heuristic, phone heuristic, address heuristic, cache layer,
      robots respect

## Verification

```bash
composer phpstan
composer phpcs
npm run test:php -- --filter SiteScrape
```

Manual: run the Theme Builder walkthrough; provide a real existing
café site URL; confirm the interview is shorter and starts pre-filled.

## Caveats

- Single-page apps (SPAs) won't yield useful HTML from a plain GET.
  Optional follow-up: integrate Playwright or a headless browser
  fallback for SPA sites. Out of scope for v1.
- Sites with anti-scraping (CloudFlare challenge, Akamai, etc.) will
  fail. Handle gracefully — return what was obtainable and let the
  agent ask for the rest.
- The user should consent to the scrape (one-line confirmation) since
  it makes outbound HTTP from their server. The ability surfaces this
  to the agent's UI layer.

## Related

- Filed during post-#1522 design review.
- Major accelerator for the "no placeholder content" issue — scraping
  produces the real data the agent then validates with the user.

title: GH#1528 — feat(stock-image): add candidate selection and attribution for Theme Builder imagery
body:
## Summary

Enhance the existing `sd-ai-agent/stock-image` ability so the Theme Builder can search multiple candidate stock images, present choices to the user, and import the selected result into the WordPress media library with attribution metadata.

The current code already registers `SdAiAgent\Abilities\ImageAbilities\StockImageAbility` and sources through Openverse/Pixabay (`includes/Abilities/ImageAbilities/StockImageAbility.php`, `includes/Abilities/ImageSources/ImageSourceFactory.php`). This issue is NOT to add a duplicate ability; it is to upgrade the existing stock-image path for the Theme Builder visual pipeline.

## Why

Theme Builder walkthroughs currently produce visually empty sites because the agent has no UX-friendly way to gather and choose imagery for specific sections. The no-external-URLs rule for theme files is correct — the solution is to import media first, then use local `/wp-content/uploads/...` URLs.

## Proposed scope

- Extend `sd-ai-agent/stock-image` to support search-result candidates instead of importing only the first viable hit.
- Add optional inputs: `orientation`, `colour`, `min_width`, `min_height`, `limit`, and provider preference.
- Preserve the existing Openverse/Pixabay chain; add Unsplash/Pexels only if credentials and licence handling are implemented cleanly.
- Store attribution in `_wp_attachment_image_alt` and `_sd_ai_agent_attribution` when an image is imported.
- Teach the Theme Builder agent to request stock imagery when the user has no uploaded photos and generic photography is suitable.
- Ensure theme/template files receive only local media-library URLs after import.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Existing `sd-ai-agent/stock-image` remains the canonical ability name. No duplicate `stock-image-search` ability is introduced unless maintainers explicitly choose a search/select split.
- [ ] The ability can return multiple candidates with thumbnail URL, provider, dimensions, licence, attribution, and provider image ID.
- [ ] A selected candidate can be imported into the media library.
- [ ] Imported attachments store attribution metadata.
- [ ] Theme Builder prompt knows when to call stock-image versus generate-image or user upload.
- [ ] No external image URLs are written to theme files; output used by scaffold is local media URL / attachment ID.
- [ ] PHPUnit covers provider mocks, attribution storage, and import path.

## Verification

```bash
composer phpstan
composer phpcs
npm run test:php -- --filter StockImage
```

Manual: run the Theme Builder walkthrough; confirm the agent fetches imagery, lets the user choose, imports selected assets, and uses local URLs in the rendered site.

## Related

- Existing ability: `includes/Abilities/ImageAbilities/StockImageAbility.php`
- Existing provider chain: `includes/Abilities/ImageSources/ImageSourceFactory.php`
- Filed during post-#1522 design review.
- Pairs with Theme Builder photo upload and AI image generation enhancements.

title: GH#1527 — feat(abilities): generate sanitised SVG logo candidates for Theme Builder
body:
## Summary

Add a new ability `sd-ai-agent/generate-logo-svg` that produces a
clean, on-brand SVG logo using AI when the user does not already have
one. The user can adopt it, iterate via prompt, or replace with their
own upload.

Every business needs a wordmark or symbol. Building a site without one
forces the agent to fall back on type-only branding, which works only
in a narrow range of styles. An AI-generated SVG mark is editable,
scalable, themeable, and free of CDN dependencies.

## Scope

### Inputs

- Brand name (required)
- Brand description / vertical (required)
- Direction (optional): one of
  - `wordmark` (type-only, e.g. styled "B&B")
  - `monogram` (initials inside a containing shape)
  - `symbol+wordmark` (icon next to type)
  - `symbol` (icon only, no type)
- Style cues from the chosen design direction (palette, voice)
- Existing logo URL or upload (optional — if present, the ability
  returns "user already has a logo" with the uploaded asset
  preserved as the active mark)

### Outputs

- One or more SVG candidates (default 3) written to the media library
  as `image/svg+xml` attachments
- The agent presents the candidates to the user; on selection, the
  chosen SVG is set as the site logo (via `set_theme_mod( 'custom_logo', ... )`)
  and a 16/32/180/512 favicon set is generated from it

### Implementation notes

- Use the connected AI provider's structured-output / function-call
  mode to request SVG markup directly. Validate the returned SVG:
  - Must parse as XML
  - Must not contain `<script>`, `<foreignObject>`, external `xlink:href`,
    or `<image href="http...">`
  - Must use only colours from the agreed palette (or be monochrome
    with a single fill placeholder the theme replaces)
  - Reasonable viewBox + intrinsic size
- If validation fails, reject and re-prompt up to N times before
  returning a fallback type-only wordmark.
- Save each candidate to the media library so the user can pick from
  thumbnails in the admin UI.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] New ability `sd-ai-agent/generate-logo-svg` registered in
      `includes/Abilities/GenerateLogoSvgAbility.php`
- [ ] Accepts brand name, description, vertical, and optional direction
- [ ] Returns N SVG candidates as media-library attachment IDs +
      data URIs for inline preview
- [ ] SVGs are sanitised; no script, no external refs, no broken XML
- [ ] On user selection, the chosen SVG is wired as site logo +
      favicon set
- [ ] Theme Builder system prompt knows to call this ability when no
      existing logo is available
- [ ] PHPUnit covers: parse-and-validate, sanitisation, selection +
      site-logo wiring
- [ ] Falls back gracefully to type-only wordmark if all AI candidates
      fail validation

## Verification

```bash
composer phpstan
composer phpcs
npm run test:php -- --filter GenerateLogoSvg
```

Manual: run the Theme Builder walkthrough; confirm the agent offers
logo candidates, the user picks one, and the site header renders the
chosen SVG.

## Caveats

- Some AI providers struggle with SVG output. The ability should
  prefer providers known to handle structured XML well, or post-
  process via Inkscape / svgcleaner if needed.
- Favicon generation from SVG requires Imagick or GD. Document the
  dependency clearly; fall back to embedding the SVG directly as the
  favicon (modern browsers support this) if rasterisation fails.

## Related

- Filed during post-#1522 design review.
- Pairs with image-acquisition abilities (stock search, image gen) —
  all part of the same goal: ship visual-rich sites.

title: GH#1525 — feat(theme-builder): require a real primary CTA in every front-page hero
body:
## Summary

The Theme Builder agent produces hero sections with no call-to-action
button. For conversion-driven sites (cafés, restaurants, shops, services,
events) the front-page hero is the highest-value pixel on the site and
MUST include a primary CTA pointing to the most-likely-converting page.

Example from the post-#1522 walkthrough: a single-location café front
page rendered with "Slow down. Sip something good." + opening hours +
address, but no `ORDER ONLINE` / `RESERVE` / `VIEW MENU` / `GET
DIRECTIONS` button. The hours-and-address block is good, but a button
should sit immediately under the hero copy.

## Root cause

The agent's system prompt and the `scaffold-block-theme` ability's
default `front-page.html` template do not require a hero CTA. The agent
treats the CTA as optional and frequently omits it.

## Proposed fix

Three layers:

### 1. System prompt update (theme-builder agent)

Add a hard rule to the Theme Builder agent's system prompt
(`includes/Models/Agent.php` seed data and any prompt builder logic):

> Every front-page hero MUST include exactly one primary CTA button.
> The CTA text and target are derived from the business vertical:
> - Café / restaurant → "View menu" → /menu/
> - Shop / e-commerce → "Shop now" → /shop/
> - Service business → "Get a quote" → /contact/
> - Event / venue → "Reserve" → /book/ or /events/
> - Content site → most-recent-post or featured category
>
> The CTA MUST be a real link to an existing page on the site, not
> "#" or a placeholder. If the target page does not yet exist, create
> it first.

### 2. `scaffold-block-theme` template default

Update `includes/Abilities/ScaffoldBlockThemeAbility.php` so the
default `front-page.html` template includes a `<!-- wp:button -->` block
slot in the hero, with a tool-callback marker the agent fills with the
real link.

### 3. Validation

Add a `validate_front_page_has_cta()` check that runs after scaffold
+ page creation. If the rendered front-page has no `<a class="...
wp-block-button__link">` inside the hero section, return a non-fatal
warning the agent can act on.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every Theme Builder walkthrough produces a front-page with a
      visible CTA button in the hero.
- [ ] CTA text and target are vertical-appropriate, not generic.
- [ ] CTA links to an existing published page (never `#`).
- [ ] System prompt rule is documented in the seed data.
- [ ] PHPUnit test asserts the scaffold default includes a CTA block
      slot.
- [ ] E2E test asserts the rendered front-page contains
      `.wp-block-button__link[href]:not([href="#"])` inside the hero.

## Verification

```bash
composer phpstan
composer phpcs
npm run test:php -- --filter ScaffoldBlockTheme
npm run test:e2e:playwright -- onboarding-theme-builder
```

Manual: run the Theme Builder walkthrough as a coffee shop, restaurant,
shop, and service business. Verify each gets an appropriate CTA.

## Caveats

- The CTA target may not exist at scaffold time if pages haven't been
  created yet. The agent SHOULD plan page creation order so the CTA's
  target page exists before the front-page is finalised.

## Related

- Filed during post-#1522 design review.
- Pairs with `feat(theme-builder): no placeholder content` — both
  enforce the principle that nothing ships incomplete.

title: GH#1526 — feat(theme-builder): enforce real content or no content for generated pages
body:
## Summary

The Theme Builder agent must ship every generated page as fully-developed
published content with no placeholder text, no Lorem-style filler, and no
"Edit this section to add your story" prompts. Any information the agent
needs MUST be gathered from the user during the interview phase before
any page is created.

## Principle

> Real content or no content. Never publish a stub.

The agent owns the interview. If it needs to write a 200-word About
section, it must KNOW (from the user) the founding year, the location,
the people, the values, the voice. If it needs to fill a Menu page, it
must HAVE the actual menu items + prices. If it has a Shop page, it
must HAVE real products.

Missing information is a blocker for that page, not a licence to fill
with placeholder copy.

## Root cause

Current behaviour observed during the post-#1522 walkthrough: the agent
created "Events" and "Shop Our Beans" pages with generic copy because
the interview didn't ask the user for events or for products. The pages
shipped published with content that reads like marketing-template
boilerplate.

## Proposed fix

### 1. Interview expansion

The Theme Builder agent's interview MUST be vertical-aware and cover
the full information surface needed for every page that will be
created. For a café, that means:

- Brand name, tagline, founding year, location(s), opening hours
- Story / about copy (collected verbatim or guided via several
  questions)
- Full menu (categories, items, prices, optional descriptions)
- Upcoming events (or "no events page" decision)
- Products to sell online (or "no shop page" decision)
- Team members + bios (or "no team page" decision)
- Photos available (see image-acquisition issues)

### 2. Page-creation prerequisite check

Before any `create-post` call, the agent must run a self-check: do I
have real, user-supplied content for this page? If not, the page is
not created. The user is told which information is missing and asked
to supply it (or asked whether to skip the page entirely).

### 3. Vertical-aware interview templates

Add interview question packs per vertical (café, restaurant, shop,
service business, portfolio, blog, event venue, etc.) in
`includes/Models/Agent.php` or a new `InterviewTemplate` model. The
Theme Builder agent picks the right pack based on vertical detected
in the first 2-3 questions.

### 4. Site-scrape ability as accelerator

If the user has an existing site, the agent can scrape it for brand
info, hours, address, and about copy to pre-fill the interview. See
the separate `site-scrape` ability issue.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] No generated page contains placeholder text, Lorem ipsum,
      "Replace this", "Edit this", "Add your...", or template-fill
      language.
- [ ] No generated page is `post_status = draft`. Pages are either
      published with real content, or not created at all.
- [ ] Interview covers every page the agent intends to create.
- [ ] Missing information triggers an explicit user prompt, not a
      placeholder.
- [ ] System prompt encodes the "real content or no content" rule.
- [ ] PHPUnit/Jest tests verify the system-prompt rule is loaded.
- [ ] E2E test asserts no page on the built site contains the strings
      `Lorem`, `Edit this`, `Add your`, `Replace this`.

## Verification

```bash
composer phpstan
composer phpcs
npm run test:php
npm run test:e2e:playwright -- onboarding-theme-builder
```

Manual: run walkthroughs for café, restaurant, shop, and service
business. Inspect every page. Reject any page with placeholder copy.

## Caveats

- This is a behaviour change that may make the interview longer.
  That's the right trade — longer interview, real published site,
  versus quick interview, fake-content site.
- The interview should still feel conversational, not like a form.
  The agent breaks information gathering into short natural
  questions, not a wall of fields.

## Related

- Extends the honesty principle from #1497 / #1518 (site
  configuration must reflect reality).
- Filed during post-#1522 design review.
- Pairs with `feat(abilities): site-scrape` and the image-acquisition
  abilities — both accelerate complete content collection.

title: GH#1524 — bug(create-menu): preserve requested menu item order
body:
## Summary

`sd-ai-agent/create-menu` does not preserve the order of menu items as
specified by the agent. Items end up alphabetised in the rendered nav.

Observed during the post-fix walkthrough on 2026-05-19: the Theme Builder
agent requested the nav order `HOME · MENU · OUR STORY · EVENTS · FIND
US · SHOP`. The live nav rendered as `EVENTS · HOME · MENU · OUR STORY ·
SHOP OUR BEANS · VISIT US` — alphabetical by post title.

## Root cause (likely)

`CreateMenuAbility::add_menu_item()` either:

1. Does not set `menu_order` at all, leaving WordPress to default-sort
   by post title.
2. Sets `menu_order = 0` for every item, ditto.

WP_CLI `nav-menu item add` and `wp_update_nav_menu_item()` both accept a
`menu-item-position` argument that controls ordering. The ability should
auto-increment this based on the order of items passed in the request.

## Proposed fix

In `includes/Abilities/CreateMenuAbility.php`:

```php
$position = 1;
foreach ( $items as $item ) {
    wp_update_nav_menu_item(
        $menu_id,
        0,
        [
            'menu-item-title'    => $item['title'],
            'menu-item-object'   => 'page',
            'menu-item-object-id'=> $item['page_id'],
            'menu-item-type'     => 'post_type',
            'menu-item-status'   => 'publish',
            'menu-item-position' => $position,  // <-- new
        ]
    );
    $position++;
}
```

The schema MAY also accept an explicit `position` per item for callers
that want to insert at a specific slot, but the default behaviour MUST
be "preserve the order I gave you".

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Calling `sd-ai-agent/create-menu` with items
  `[Home, Menu, Our Story, Events, Find Us, Shop]` produces a nav in
  exactly that order.
- [ ] Existing tests still pass.
- [ ] New PHPUnit test asserts position is set on each
  `wp_update_nav_menu_item` call.

## Verification

```bash
composer phpstan
composer phpcs
npm run test:php -- --filter CreateMenuAbility
```

Then run the Theme Builder walkthrough and confirm the live nav matches
the requested order.

## Caveats

- WordPress site editor (block themes) reads `wp_navigation` post types
  for site-editor nav, not the classic `nav_menu_item` taxonomy. Confirm
  which path the Theme Builder agent uses — if it builds a block
  navigation, the fix is different (`<!-- wp:navigation-link {...} -->`
  block ordering inside the parent `<!-- wp:navigation -->`).

## Related

- Filed during post-#1522 design review.
- Same walkthrough that produced PRs #1514, #1515, #1516, #1520, #1521,
  #1523.

title: auto-kickoff never fires on fresh start (regression in #1520)
body:
## Summary

PR #1520 (the fix for #1509 "kickoff message re-sent on every reload") **over-corrected** and introduced a new regression: the kickoff message now **never fires automatically**, not even on the very first call to `/onboarding/theme-builder-start` for a brand-new site.

End result on a clean install:

- Empty WordPress site, fresh session, `sd_ai_agent_settings.onboarding_complete=false`,
  `sd_ai_agent_theme_builder_started` option absent.
- User opens the AI Agent admin page → `OnboardingThemeBuilder` mounts → POSTs
  `/onboarding/theme-builder-start`.
- Server creates session, stamps `THEME_BUILDER_STARTED_OPTION = time()`, **returns
  `started_at: <unix timestamp>`** in the response (even on the first-create path).
- React component checks `if ( ! data.started_at ) sendMessage( ... )` — `started_at` is
  truthy (a timestamp number), so **kickoff is skipped**.
- User sees an empty chat with no greeting, no interview question, no Designer persona —
  just the regular chat UI with the model picker showing "Theme Builder". To proceed they
  must type a kickoff message manually.

This is verified end-to-end against `main @ 96728bf` (v1.14.0 prep) on WP 6.9.4:

```
wp option get sd_ai_agent_theme_builder_session_id   # 1
wp option get sd_ai_agent_theme_builder_started      # 1779203410
wp db query "SELECT LENGTH(messages) FROM wp_sd_ai_agent_sessions WHERE id=1;"
# => 2   (i.e. the JSON array '[]' — no kickoff message persisted)
```

## Root cause

`includes/Core/OnboardingManager.php::rest_theme_builder_start()` returns
`started_at` in **both** branches:

- **Resume branch (existing_session_id is set)** — returns
  `'started_at' => get_option( self::THEME_BUILDER_STARTED_OPTION )` (the saved value).
  Correct — this is the resume case, and kickoff should be skipped.
- **Fresh-create branch (no existing session)** — stamps
  `$started_at = time(); update_option( self::THEME_BUILDER_STARTED_OPTION, $started_at, false );`
  and then returns `'started_at' => $started_at`. **Wrong — this is the fresh-start case,
  and kickoff should fire.**

The JS check `if ( ! data.started_at )` (`src/components/onboarding-theme-builder.js`)
cannot distinguish "this server-side flag was just stamped 50 ms ago in the same request"
from "this server-side flag was stamped on a previous request". Both look the same from
the JSON payload.

## Reproduction

```bash
# 1. Start from a clean install.
wp post delete $(wp post list --post_type=any --format=ids) --force
wp db query "TRUNCATE TABLE wp_sd_ai_agent_sessions; TRUNCATE TABLE wp_sd_ai_agent_active_jobs;"
wp option delete sd_ai_agent_onboarding_complete sd_ai_agent_bootstrap_session_id \
  sd_ai_agent_theme_builder_session_id sd_ai_agent_theme_builder_started
wp eval '$s = get_option("sd_ai_agent_settings", []); $s["onboarding_complete"] = false; update_option("sd_ai_agent_settings", $s);'

# 2. Open the admin chat page.
xdg-open http://wordpress.local:8080/wp-admin/admin.php?page=sd-ai-agent

# 3. Observe: empty chat, no greeting. Reload — still empty (kickoff still won't fire).

# 4. Confirm the React path actually called the REST endpoint:
wp db query "SELECT id, LENGTH(messages) FROM wp_sd_ai_agent_sessions;"   # 1 row, 2 bytes
wp option get sd_ai_agent_theme_builder_session_id                          # 1
wp option get sd_ai_agent_theme_builder_started                             # <recent timestamp>
```

## Suggested fix

Two clean options — pick one. **Option A is recommended** because it keeps the truth on
the server and keeps the client check trivial.

### Option A — return an `is_fresh_start` boolean explicitly

```php
// includes/Core/OnboardingManager.php::rest_theme_builder_start()

// Resume branch:
return new \WP_REST_Response( [
    'success'        => true,
    'session_id'     => $existing_session_id,
    'agent_id'       => $theme_builder_agent_id,
    'kickoff_message'=> $kickoff_message,
    'started_at'     => get_option( self::THEME_BUILDER_STARTED_OPTION ),
    'is_fresh_start' => false,                          // <-- new
], 200 );

// ... full-create branch:
$started_at = time();
update_option( self::THEME_BUILDER_SESSION_OPTION, $session_id, false );
update_option( self::THEME_BUILDER_STARTED_OPTION, $started_at, false );

return new \WP_REST_Response( [
    'success'        => true,
    'session_id'     => $session_id,
    'agent_id'       => $theme_builder_agent_id,
    'kickoff_message'=> $kickoff_message,
    'started_at'     => $started_at,
    'is_fresh_start' => true,                           // <-- new
], 200 );
```

```js
// src/components/onboarding-theme-builder.js
.then( () => {
    if ( data.is_fresh_start ) {
        sendMessage( data.kickoff_message || /* default */ );
    }
} )
```

### Option B — don't stamp `started_at` until AFTER returning, and let the JS check whether
`started_at` is null

This is more fragile (requires `register_shutdown_function` or a follow-up POST to mark
the session "actually started"), and creates a window where two near-simultaneous mounts
could both try to send the kickoff. Not recommended.

### Existing test coverage

Look at the unit tests added in PR #1520 (file
`tests/SdAiAgent/Core/OnboardingManagerTest.php` or similar). They likely assert that
`started_at` is non-null on first call — that assertion is **the wrong shape** and needs
updating. The test that protects against the original bug (no duplicate kickoff on
second call) is still correct; just add an additional assertion that the **first** call
distinguishes itself from the second (via `is_fresh_start`).

## Verification

```bash
composer phpstan
composer phpcs
npm run lint:js
npm run build
npm run test:php
npm run test:js
npm run test:e2e:playwright -- onboarding-theme-builder
```

Manual:

1. Clean state (per the Reproduction section above).
2. Open admin chat page → `OnboardingThemeBuilder` mounts → kickoff message
   "I'd like to design a custom block theme..." appears in the chat,
   followed by the agent's interview question 1.
3. Reload the page → kickoff message is NOT re-sent (the original #1509 protection
   still works).
4. Conversation state persists across reloads.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] On a clean install, opening the admin chat page automatically sends the kickoff
      message and the agent responds with the interview start.
- [ ] Reload during the interview / build phase does NOT add a duplicate kickoff
      (the original #1509 fix continues to hold).
- [ ] `is_fresh_start` (or equivalent unambiguous signal) is returned by
      `/onboarding/theme-builder-start` and used by `OnboardingThemeBuilder`.
- [ ] Existing unit tests updated; new test asserts the first-call vs resume distinction.
- [ ] PHPCS, PHPStan, ESLint, build, Jest, PHPUnit, Playwright all green.

## Caveats

- This is a regression introduced by PR #1520 — it didn't exist before, only after.
- Severity: **P1** — the Theme Builder onboarding **does not start automatically** any
  more. Users have to know to type a kickoff phrase manually. That's worse than the
  original duplicate-kickoff bug because at least with the original bug the user knew
  the agent was alive and trying to talk to them.
- The fix is small and localised.

## Related

- PR #1520 / Issue #1509 — original fix that over-corrected.
- The original #1509 problem (kickoff re-sent on reload) is still correctly prevented
  by this fix; we only need to differentiate fresh-start from resume.
- Verified during the post-fix Theme Builder walkthrough on 2026-05-19.

title: GH#1510 — active_jobs rows stuck in 'processing' when AgentLoop terminates abnormally
body:
See https://github.com/Ultimate-Multisite/superdav-ai-agent/issues/1510 for the full worker-ready brief.

Root cause: AgentLoop inserts a row with status='processing' but has no shutdown handler / cron reaper / heartbeat to recover from PHP fatals, FastCGI timeouts, killed workers, or client disconnects. Walkthrough left row id=94 stuck since 2026-05-19 04:26:20 with empty pending_tools and tool_calls.

Fix (three layers): register_shutdown_function for normal exit, hourly cron reaper for SIGKILL/OOM, per-iteration heartbeat that advances updated_at. Files: includes/Core/AgentLoop.php, includes/Core/Database.php (schema migration for error/interrupted_at columns + index).

title: GH#1509 — Theme Builder kickoff message re-sent on every reload
body:
See https://github.com/Ultimate-Multisite/superdav-ai-agent/issues/1509 for the full worker-ready brief.

Root cause: /onboarding/theme-builder-start does not flip onboarding_complete (deliberately, unlike /bootstrap-start), so the React component re-mounts on every reload. OnboardingThemeBuilder's bootstrappedRef is component-local and resets on remount, so the kickoff POST fires again. Observed twice in a single walkthrough.

Fix: persist 'theme builder started' as a server-side per-user option and have the React component query server truth on mount. Files: includes/Core/OnboardingManager.php, src/components/onboarding-theme-builder.js.

title: AgentLoop sends temperature to reasoning models that reject it (gpt-5.5 → 400)
body:
Reproduction (2026-05-16): `wp sd-ai-agent prompt 'test' --provider=openai --model=gpt-5.5 --skip-tools` returns HTTP 400 from OpenAI: 'Unsupported parameter: temperature is not supported with this model.'

Root cause: `includes/Core/AgentLoop.php:1011` calls `$builder->using_temperature((float) $this->temperature)` unconditionally. OpenAI's reasoning-model family (gpt-5, gpt-5.5, gpt-5.5-pro, gpt-5-codex, gpt-5-pro, o1*, o3*, etc.) reject the temperature field — only the fixed value 1 is implicit.

Fix:
1. Detect reasoning-model IDs (prefix match: gpt-5, gpt-5.5, gpt-5-codex, gpt-5-pro, o1, o3, o4).
2. Skip using_temperature() when the model is in that class.
3. Add a regression test.

Verification: `wp sd-ai-agent prompt 'Reply with: GPT-5.5 OK' --provider=openai --model=gpt-5.5 --skip-tools --verbose` must succeed.

Related: #1450 regression, #1473 verification trigger.

title: Settings /providers: openai shows static 11-model list instead of SDK dynamic list (gpt-5/5.5 missing)
body:
## Symptom

On a site with both:
- A WP 7.0 Connectors API key set for OpenAI (`connectors_ai_openai_api_key`), AND
- The `ai-provider-for-openai` plugin active (registers SDK provider id `openai`)

…the `/sd-ai-agent/v1/providers` endpoint returns only the 11 static models from `Settings::DIRECT_PROVIDERS['openai']['models']` (gpt-4.1, gpt-4o, o1/o3/o4-mini) and never exposes the SDK's dynamic catalogue.

The SDK's `OpenAiProvider::modelMetadataDirectory()->listModelMetadata()` actually returns 128 models on this host, including the entire `gpt-5`, `gpt-5.4`, and `gpt-5.5` families plus codex/realtime/image variants. None of those reach the chat UI dropdown.

Verified locally:
```
wp eval '... $controller->handle_providers() ...' →
Provider: openai type=direct models=11
  - gpt-4.1-nano … o4-mini       (the 11 static entries)

Direct SDK directory call →
SDK model count: 128
  - gpt-5.5, gpt-5.5-pro, gpt-5.4, gpt-5.4-mini, gpt-5, gpt-5-codex, ...
```

## Root cause

`SettingsController::handle_providers()` (`includes/REST/SettingsController.php:713`) processes `DIRECT_PROVIDERS` first and then iterates SDK providers with:

```php
$added_ids = array_column( $providers, 'id' );
foreach ( $provider_ids as $provider_id ) {
    if ( in_array( $provider_id, $added_ids, true ) ) {
        continue;     // ← SDK 'openai' is skipped because static entry already added
    }
```

The SDK plugin (`ai-provider-for-openai`) registers its provider as `id => 'openai'` (see `lib/php-ai-client/.../OpenAiProvider::createProviderMetadata`), exactly matching the `DIRECT_PROVIDERS['openai']` key, so it's always suppressed once a WP 7.0 Connectors OpenAI key is present.

The same de-duplication exists in `CLI/ModelsCommand::fetch_providers()` (mirrors the REST logic).

## Why this regressed

Prior to PR #1336 (\"remove sd_ai_agent_provider_keys + duplicate credential storage\") the DIRECT_PROVIDERS guard used `get_provider_key()` reading the old `sd_ai_agent_provider_keys` option, which was almost never populated. So in practice DIRECT_PROVIDERS was skipped and the SDK loop won. Switching the guard to `get_connectors_api_key()` (WP 7.0 Connectors) flipped behaviour: any user with a Connectors OpenAI key set now gets the static fallback, even when a richer SDK provider is registered.

## Proposed fix

Invert the precedence so the SDK loop runs first. `DIRECT_PROVIDERS` becomes a true fallback used only when:
1. The SDK has no provider registered with that id, OR
2. The SDK has the provider but `listModelMetadata()` returned an empty list (e.g. live API failure)

When the SDK provides a non-empty model list, that wins. When the SDK only registered the provider but couldn't list models (no auth, network error), and a WP 7.0 Connectors key is set, fall back to the static catalogue so the UI still has a usable dropdown.

- `includes/CLI/ModelsCommand.php` → `fetch_providers()`

title: Fatal in AiClientEventTraceLogger: getContent()/getModel()/getInputTokens() do not exist on SDK DTOs
body:
The SDK event trace logger silently fatals on every successful AI call (and visibly fatals during shutdown when the watchdog runs) because it calls methods that do not exist on the WordPress\AiClient DTOs:

  - serialize_messages() line 239: $message->getContent() — Message has no getContent(); use getParts() (or Message::toArray()/jsonSerialize).
  - serialize_result() line 258: $result->getModel() — GenerativeAiResult has getProviderMetadata()/getModelMetadata(), no getModel().
  - serialize_result() lines 260-263 + on_after_generate_result lines 124-127: TokenUsage has getPromptTokens()/getCompletionTokens()/getTotalTokens()/getThoughtTokens() — not getInputTokens/getOutputTokens/getCacheCreationTokens/getCacheReadTokens.
  - serialize_result() line 274: $candidate->getContent() — Candidate has getMessage(), no getContent().

Reproduces 100% of the time when ProviderTrace is enabled and any AI call is made. The After handler fatal is swallowed silently by the WP hook system; the cleanup_stalled_events shutdown hook surfaces the fatal in CLI output.

Existing tests/SdAiAgent/Bootstrap/AiClientEventTraceHandlerTest.php was authored against a fictional API (RoleEnum::from, Message constructor with content:, Candidate with content:, etc.) and has clearly never executed — otherwise it would have caught all of this.

title: PR #1459 merged with red CI: stub mismatch breaks PHPStan/PHPUnit on main
body:

Root cause: stubs/wordpress-7-runtime.php describes an outdated WP 7.0 alpha API. The real WP 7.0 RC2 SDK (and bundled lib/php-ai-client/) has evolved:

- GenerativeAiResult adds getId(), getModelMetadata(), getCandidates(): Candidate[] (not Message[])
- TokenUsage adds getThoughtTokens()
- Candidate class with getMessage() + getFinishReason(): FinishReasonEnum — missing from stub

includes/Core/AiClientEventTraceLogger.php (added in #1459) uses real-SDK methods; PHPStan rejects them against stub shape.

Resolution path: update stubs/wordpress-7-runtime.php to match real SDK + add missing classes. PR #1463 will carry the fix since CI is currently red on its base.

title: Kimi K2.6 sessions stall mid-execution: preamble truncation undetected + wrong max_output_tokens cap
Client abilities not registered on page when wp.abilities API absent at registration time
body:
When floating-widget bundle initializes on a page where the @wordpress/abilities script module has not yet loaded (or is unavailable), registerClientAbility() returns early before populating the local clientCallbacks map. As a result, executeClientAbility() — which jobSlice uses to handle pending_client_tool_calls — throws 'Client ability X is not registered on this page' for screenshot-url, navigate-to, capture-screenshot, and insert-block.

Repro:
- Visit a frontend post page (e.g. /ultimate-ai-agent-.../) with show_on_frontend enabled
- Send a chat message that invokes screenshot-url or navigate-to
- Job poll loop returns pending_client_tool_calls
- jobSlice calls executeClientAbility() → error

Root cause: src/abilities/registry.js:189-192 returns early when abilitiesApiAvailable() is false, before line 208-210 stores the callback in clientCallbacks. executeClientAbility (line 311) only reads from clientCallbacks; if the entry is missing it throws.

Fix:
1. Move the clientCallbacks.set() above the wp.abilities API check so callbacks are registered locally even when the WP abilities API isn't yet loaded.
2. Keep the wp.abilities.registerAbility() call gated on availability (so the WP store is only updated when the API is present).
3. In executeClientAbility, optionally fall back to wp.abilities.executeAbility() when the local map miss happens but the API is available.

title: Fix method_exists guard skipping using_max_tokens and using_temperature on PromptBuilder wrapper
body: AgentLoop::build_prompt guards using_temperature/using_max_tokens with method_exists() which does not detect __call magic methods. The WP_AI_Client_Prompt_Builder wrapper routes snake_case methods through __call, so both guards return false and both setters are silently skipped. Result: max_tokens defaults to 4096 in AnthropicMaxTextGenerationModel and temperature is never set, causing frequent max_tokens truncations and ~47s slow retry cycles. Fix: replace method_exists() with is_callable() which respects __call.

title: fix(ai-client-bridge): normalise empty properties/items in using_abilities() for Anthropic draft-2020-12
body:
## Root cause (corrected)

`HttpTraceHandler::on_http_request_args()` (`includes/Bootstrap/HttpTraceHandler.php:120-166`, hooked on `http_request_args` priority 9) decodes the outgoing request body via `json_decode($body, true)` (associative-array mode), runs the prompt-cache strategy's `apply()`, then re-encodes via `wp_json_encode($mutated)`.

The decode collapses every `{}` (empty JSON object) into a PHP empty array `[]`. The strategy mutates only the cache-control marker. The re-encode then emits empty `properties` / `items` as `[]` — which Anthropic's draft-2020-12 validator rejects with HTTP 400 `tools.N.custom.input_schema: JSON schema is invalid`.

Pre-decode body (correct): `"properties":{}`
Post-decode → re-encode (broken): `"properties":[]`

The PR #1426 fix (replacing `oneOf` in `PostAbilities`) did not touch this code path.

## Reproduction
`wp sd-ai-agent prompt 'hi'` with `prompt_caching_enabled = true` (the default) fails with the 400 error.
With `prompt_caching_enabled = false` the same prompt succeeds, proving the cache-decorator is the culprit.

## Fix
After `$strategy->apply()` in `HttpTraceHandler::on_http_request_args`, walk the decoded body and convert known JSON-Schema empty-object positions (`tools[*].input_schema.properties`/`items`, recursively) back to `SdAiAgent\\Infrastructure\\Schema\\EmptyJsonObject` instances before re-encoding. `SchemaNormalizer::to_json_safe()` already does exactly this transformation; we apply it per-tool's `input_schema` (Anthropic) and per equivalent location for OpenAI/Gemini-shaped bodies.

## Files
- `includes/Bootstrap/HttpTraceHandler.php` — fix site (post-mutation schema repair)
- `includes/Infrastructure/Schema/SchemaNormalizer.php` — existing helper (no change needed)
- `tests/SdAiAgent/Bootstrap/HttpTraceHandlerSchemaTest.php` — new unit test asserting empty-object preservation through the cache-decorator round-trip

title: fix(provider-trace): missing cache_creation_tokens/cache_read_tokens columns in dbDelta schema
body:
PR #1387 added cache_creation_tokens and cache_read_tokens columns to includes/Models/ProviderTrace.php::get_schema() and bumped DB_VERSION to 19.2.0, but the inline provider_trace CREATE TABLE block inside includes/Core/Database.php::install() (lines 572-590) was NOT updated. Database::install() concatenates its own schema string and runs dbDelta against that — ProviderTrace::get_schema() is never called from the install path. Result: existing sites that already had DB_VERSION 19.1.0 upgraded to 19.2.0 without ever gaining the new columns, causing 'Unknown column cache_creation_tokens in INSERT INTO' fatals every time HttpTraceHandler->on_http_response fires.

Symptom (from current site at /home/dave/Git/superdav-ai-agent):
  Unknown column 'cache_creation_tokens' in 'INSERT INTO'
  ProviderTrace::insert() includes/Models/ProviderTrace.php:191
  ProviderTraceLogger::on_http_response() includes/Core/ProviderTraceLogger.php:208
  HttpTraceHandler->on_http_response() includes/Bootstrap/HttpTraceHandler.php:100

Confirmed via wp db query DESCRIBE: live wp_sd_ai_agent_provider_trace lacks both columns; sd_ai_agent_db_version option is already 19.2.0 so install() early-returns and never re-runs dbDelta.

Fix:
1. Add the two columns to the inline CREATE TABLE inside Database::install() so dbDelta picks them up on next install/upgrade.
2. Bump DB_VERSION to 19.2.1 so already-upgraded sites re-run install() and dbDelta adds the missing columns to existing tables.
3. (Optional cleanup) Make Database::install() call ProviderTrace::get_schema() instead of duplicating the SQL inline, eliminating drift class. Same likely applies to the other model classes that expose get_schema() but are duplicated inline in install().

Verification:
- wp option delete sd_ai_agent_db_version && wp eval 'SdAiAgent\\Core\\Database::install();' on a site missing the columns; then wp db query 'DESCRIBE wp_sd_ai_agent_provider_trace' should list cache_creation_tokens and cache_read_tokens.
- Trigger an LLM provider request with WP_DEBUG enabled and provider trace enabled; confirm no Unknown column fatal and the columns are populated.

title: Default max_output_tokens (4096) truncates tool-call inputs mid-JSON, causing agent loop failures
body:
Session 16 trace shows the model emitting valid tool calls whose JSON input payloads exceed 4096 output tokens (block HTML, run-php, wp-cli execute, create-block-content). Anthropic returns stop_reason: max_tokens with truncated input, the schema validator rejects with a misleading 'missing arguments' error, and the model loops through every alternative until the per-session tool-call cap is hit.

Root cause: includes/Core/Settings.php:289 sets default max_output_tokens = 4096 for all providers/models. Modern models support 8192–65535 (Anthropic 4.x, Gemini 2.5, GPT-4.1, o-series). The 4096 default was a lowest-common-denominator chosen when only Anthropic required max_tokens.

Fix: introduce a per-model output-tokens catalog in Settings (sibling to MODEL_CONTEXT_WINDOWS) and a resolver Settings::get_max_output_tokens_for_model($model_id). Treat default 0 in settings as 'auto per-model'. AgentLoop resolves at request time.

Also: surface stop_reason=max_tokens to the next turn instead of letting the schema validator produce a misleading 'missing arguments' error, so the model can react sensibly (split the payload).

Evidence: wp_sd_ai_agent_provider_trace rows 124–130 (session 16), all output_tokens 4094-4096, all stop_reason=max_tokens.

title: Fix wp.org submission hard-gate blockers (move_uploaded_file + missing composer.json)
body:
WP.org plugin-check hard-gates the submission with two findings on the wporg build zip:

1. **ERROR Generic.PHP.ForbiddenFunctions.Found**: `move_uploaded_file()` in `lib/php-ai-client/third-party/Nyholm/Psr7/UploadedFile.php` (`moveTo()` line ~101). This is dead code — our plugin only acts as an outbound HTTP client (PSR-18) and never receives or processes uploaded files. The class is bundled because Psr17Factory implements UploadedFileFactoryInterface, but `createUploadedFile()` is never called.

2. **WARNING missing_composer_json_file**: `/vendor` ships without a `composer.json` because `.distignore` line 35 (`/composer.json`) excludes the root manifest. WP.org allows and prefers shipping `composer.json` so reviewers can verify dependency provenance.

Both blockers prevent a human reviewer from even starting the review.

Plan:
- Remove `/composer.json` from `.distignore` so the manifest ships in both build variants.
- Patch `bin/build.sh` (wporg variant) to neutralise `moveTo()` in the bundled `UploadedFile.php` — replace its body with `throw new RuntimeException` so the literal `move_uploaded_file` token is removed. Class+interface stay intact for any reflection paths; the method becomes unreachable-by-design (we never accept uploads anyway).
- Verify bundled zip with grep: zero `move_uploaded_file` hits, presence of `composer.json` at root.
- Run plugin-check locally if available.

title: [bug] Fix 409 infinite loop when handle_tool_result returns WP_Error or hits no_paused_state
body:
When the agent loop pauses for client-side tools (e.g. screenshot-url), the browser POSTs results to /chat/tool-result. PR #1239 fixed the chained-pause and complete paths by calling update_job_after_resume(). However, two paths still leave the job transient stale, causing the browser's poll loop to keep seeing 'awaiting_client_tools' with the same pending call:

1. **WP_Error path** (RestController.php:424-426): When resume_after_client_tools() returns a WP_Error (e.g. provider failure during the model call after the screenshot is processed), the function returns early without updating the job transient. Next poll re-runs the same screenshot, POSTs again, but paused_state was consumed by the first POST → 409.

2. **no_paused_state path** (RestController.php:379-385): When paused_state is null (already consumed), we return 409 but never clear/update the job transient. The browser treats 409 as 'already processed', resumes polling, sees 'awaiting_client_tools' again, re-executes the screenshot, POSTs again → 409 again. Infinite loop.

Reproduction: User reported infinite tool-result?_locale=user 409 requests after a screenshot-url call. Network tab shows repeated screenshot ability calls with same args, all POSTs returning 409.

Fix:
- 409 path: also call update_job_after_resume() to mark job as 'error' (or 'complete' with empty result) so the transient/DB row clears the pending_client_tool_calls.
- WP_Error path: similarly update the transient to 'error' status before returning the WP_Error so the browser's next poll sees an error and stops.
- Add unit/integration test covering both paths.

Files:
- includes/REST/RestController.php (handle_tool_result, update_job_after_resume)
- tests/SdAiAgent/REST/RestControllerToolResultTest.php (new or extend existing)
- src/store/slices/jobSlice.js (verify error status handling — already exists at line 559 'if (result.status === error)')

Verification: composer phpstan, composer phpcs, npm run test:php on the new test.
