title: PluginBuilderAbilities — Register all plugin builder abilities
body:
## Summary

Create the Abilities API registration class that exposes all Plugin Builder functionality to the agent loop. This class registers four new abilities that the AI agent can call during conversations.

## Files

- **NEW**: \`includes/Abilities/PluginBuilderAbilities.php\`
- **EDIT**: Plugin bootstrap (wherever abilities are registered — likely \`gratis-ai-agent.php\` or an init class)

## Implementation Details

### Class: \`GratisAiAgent\Abilities\PluginBuilderAbilities\`

Follows the exact pattern of \`PluginDownloadAbilities.php\` and \`WordPressAbilities.php\`:

1. A main class with static \`register()\` and \`register_abilities()\` methods
2. Static proxy methods (for backwards-compatible test access)
3. Individual ability classes extending \`AbstractAbility\`

### Abilities to Register

#### 1. \`GeneratePluginAbility\` — \`gratis-ai-agent/generate-plugin\`

\`\`\`php
input_schema:
  type: object
  properties:
    description:
      type: string
      description: "Natural language description of the desired plugin"
    extend_plugin:
      type: string
      description: "Optional: slug of existing plugin to create an extension/addon for"
    extend_theme:
      type: string
      description: "Optional: slug of existing theme to create an extension for"
  required: [description]

output_schema:
  type: object
  properties:
    slug: { type: string }
    plugin_file: { type: string }
    status: { type: string }  # installed, failed
    plan: { type: object }
    files_generated: { type: integer }
    review_result: { type: object }
    errors: { type: array }
\`\`\`

Execute flow:
1. Call \`PluginGenerator::generate_plan()\` with description (+ hooks from HookScanner if extending)
2. Call \`PluginGenerator::generate_code()\` with plan
3. Call \`PluginGenerator::review_code()\` — if critical issues, regenerate affected files
4. Call \`PluginInstaller::install_plugin()\` or \`install_complex_plugin()\`
5. Record in DB with status='installed'
6. Return result with all details

Annotations: \`readonly: false, destructive: false, idempotent: false\`
Permission: \`current_user_can('install_plugins')\`

#### 2. \`SandboxTestPluginAbility\` — \`gratis-ai-agent/sandbox-test-plugin\`

\`\`\`php
input_schema:
  type: object
  properties:
    slug:
      type: string
      description: "Plugin directory slug to test"
  required: [slug]

output_schema:
  type: object
  properties:
    slug: { type: string }
    syntax_check: { type: object }  # pass, errors
    include_test: { type: object }  # pass, errors, output, duration_ms
    overall_pass: { type: boolean }
\`\`\`

Execute flow:
1. Resolve plugin directory from slug
2. Find main plugin file (from DB record or by scanning for plugin header)
3. Call \`PluginSandbox::check_all()\`
4. Update sandbox_result in DB
5. Return results

Annotations: \`readonly: true, destructive: false, idempotent: true\`
Permission: \`current_user_can('install_plugins')\`

#### 3. \`SandboxActivatePluginAbility\` — \`gratis-ai-agent/sandbox-activate-plugin\`

\`\`\`php
input_schema:
  type: object
  properties:
    slug:
      type: string
      description: "Plugin directory slug to activate safely"
  required: [slug]

output_schema:
  type: object
  properties:
    slug: { type: string }
    status: { type: string }  # active, failed, rolled_back
    message: { type: string }
    error: { type: string }
\`\`\`

Execute flow:
1. Verify plugin passed sandbox test (check DB sandbox_result)
2. Call \`PluginSandbox::safe_activate()\`
3. Update DB status to 'active' or 'failed'
4. Return result

Annotations: \`readonly: false, destructive: false, idempotent: true\`
Permission: \`current_user_can('activate_plugins')\`

#### 4. \`UpdatePluginSandboxedAbility\` — \`gratis-ai-agent/update-plugin-sandboxed\`

\`\`\`php
input_schema:
  type: object
  properties:
    slug:
      type: string
      description: "Plugin slug to update"
    modifications:
      type: object
      description: "Map of relative file paths to new content"
      additionalProperties: { type: string }
    description:
      type: string
      description: "Description of what changed"
  required: [slug, modifications]

output_schema:
  type: object
  properties:
    slug: { type: string }
    status: { type: string }  # updated, rolled_back, failed
    backup_path: { type: string }
    sandbox_result: { type: object }
    message: { type: string }
\`\`\`

Execute flow:
1. Call \`PluginUpdater::update()\` (which handles backup → stage → test → swap)
2. Update DB record
3. Return result

Annotations: \`readonly: false, destructive: false, idempotent: false\`
Permission: \`current_user_can('install_plugins')\`

### Registration Pattern

\`\`\`php
public static function register(): void {
    add_action('wp_abilities_api_init', [__CLASS__, 'register_abilities']);
}

public static function register_abilities(): void {
    if (!function_exists('wp_register_ability')) {
        return;
    }
    wp_register_ability('gratis-ai-agent/generate-plugin', [
        'label'         => __('Generate Plugin', 'gratis-ai-agent'),
        'description'   => __('Generate a WordPress plugin from a natural language description...', 'gratis-ai-agent'),
        'ability_class' => GeneratePluginAbility::class,
        'show_in_rest'  => true,
    ]);
    // ... repeat for other 3 abilities
}
\`\`\`

### Bootstrap Registration

Add \`PluginBuilderAbilities::register();\` to the plugin's ability registration chain, alongside the existing calls to \`WordPressAbilities::register()\`, \`FileAbilities::register()\`, etc.

### Dependencies

- Depends on: PluginSandbox, PluginGenerator, PluginInstaller, PluginUpdater, Database migration
- This is the "glue" class — it cannot be completed until the underlying classes exist, but the structure can be written with placeholder instantiations

### Testing

- Unit test each ability with mocked dependencies
- Test permission callbacks require correct capabilities
- Test input validation (missing required fields, invalid slugs)
- Test the full generate → install flow with mocked AI responses

### Verification

\`\`\`bash
composer phpstan
composer phpcs
# Verify abilities are registered:
wp eval 'var_dump(wp_get_ability("gratis-ai-agent/generate-plugin"));'
\`\`\`

title: Database migration — generated_plugins table
body:
## Summary

Add the \`generated_plugins\` database table and associated query methods to track all AI-generated plugins through their lifecycle (draft → installed → active → failed → deleted).

## Files

- **EDIT**: \`includes/Core/Database.php\`

## Implementation Details

### Table Schema

Add to the existing \`Database::install()\` method's SQL string (follows the pattern of other tables in the method):

\`\`\`sql
CREATE TABLE {prefix}gratis_ai_agent_generated_plugins (
  id bigint(20) unsigned NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  slug varchar(200) NOT NULL,
  plugin_file varchar(400) NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  description text NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  plan_json longtext NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  status varchar(20) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'draft',
  sandbox_result text DEFAULT NULL,
  version varchar(20) NOT NULL DEFAULT '1.0.0',
  created_at datetime NOT NULL,
  updated_at datetime NOT NULL,
  created_by bigint(20) unsigned NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  PRIMARY KEY (id),
  UNIQUE KEY slug (slug),
  KEY status (status),
  KEY created_by (created_by)
) {charset};
\`\`\`

Status values: \`draft\`, \`installed\`, \`active\`, \`failed\`, \`deleted\`

### Version Bump

- Current: \`const DB_VERSION = '14.0.0';\`
- New: \`const DB_VERSION = '15.0.0';\`
- This triggers the \`dbDelta()\` migration on next page load

### Table Name Method

Add to the existing table name methods section:

\`\`\`php
public static function generated_plugins_table_name(): string {
    global \$wpdb;
    return \$wpdb->prefix . 'gratis_ai_agent_generated_plugins';
}
\`\`\`

### Query Methods

Add static methods following the existing pattern in Database.php:

\`\`\`php
public static function insert_generated_plugin(array \$data): int|false
public static function update_generated_plugin(string \$slug, array \$data): bool
public static function get_generated_plugin(string \$slug): object|null
public static function list_generated_plugins(string \$status = ''): array
public static function update_generated_plugin_status(string \$slug, string \$status): bool
public static function delete_generated_plugin_record(string \$slug): bool
\`\`\`

### Pattern to Follow

Look at existing methods in Database.php like \`get_modified_plugins()\`, \`record_modified_file()\`, etc. They use:
- \`global \$wpdb;\` with \`/** @var \\wpdb \$wpdb */\`
- \`\$wpdb->prepare()\` for all queries with user input
- \`\$wpdb->insert()\`, \`\$wpdb->update()\`, \`\$wpdb->get_row()\`, \`\$wpdb->get_results()\`
- Return typed results

### Integration with dbDelta

The \`Database::install()\` method uses WordPress's \`dbDelta()\` which handles both creating new tables and altering existing tables. Adding the new CREATE TABLE statement to the existing SQL string is sufficient — dbDelta will create the table on upgrade and skip it if it already exists with the correct schema.

### Dependencies

- No code dependencies (this is foundational)
- Required by: PluginInstaller, PluginUpdater, PluginBuilderAbilities

### Testing

- Test that DB version bump triggers migration
- Test insert/get/update/delete/list query methods
- Test status transitions (draft → installed → active)
- Test unique slug constraint (duplicate insert returns error)

### Verification

\`\`\`bash
composer phpstan
composer phpcs
# Activate plugin in dev environment to test migration:
wp plugin deactivate gratis-ai-agent && wp plugin activate gratis-ai-agent
# Verify table exists:
wp db query "DESCRIBE wp_gratis_ai_agent_generated_plugins"
\`\`\`

title: PluginInstaller — Write, track, and manage generated plugins
body:
## Summary

Build the file installation and tracking layer that writes AI-generated plugin files to \`wp-content/plugins/\` and records them in the database. Acts as the bridge between PluginGenerator (produces code) and PluginSandbox (tests code).

## Files

- **NEW**: \`includes/PluginBuilder/PluginInstaller.php\`

## Implementation Details

### Class: \`GratisAiAgent\PluginBuilder\PluginInstaller\`

#### Method: \`install_plugin(string \$slug, string \$main_file_content, string \$description, array \$plan): array|WP_Error\`
- For single-file plugins
- Creates \`wp-content/plugins/{slug}/{slug}.php\` via \`WP_Filesystem\`
- Records in \`gratis_ai_agent_generated_plugins\` table with status='installed'
- Path traversal protection: validate slug contains only \`[a-z0-9-]\`, no \`..\`, no absolute paths
- Returns \`['slug' => string, 'plugin_file' => string, 'path' => string, 'status' => 'installed']\`

#### Method: \`install_complex_plugin(string \$slug, array \$files, string \$description, array \$plan): array|WP_Error\`
- For multi-file plugins
- \$files is \`['relative/path.php' => 'content', ...]\`
- Creates the directory structure under \`wp-content/plugins/{slug}/\`
- All paths must be relative, within the slug directory
- Path traversal protection on every file path
- Normalizes paths: strips common prefixes if the generated structure includes the slug redundantly (e.g., \`cookie-banner/cookie-banner/file.php\` → \`cookie-banner/file.php\`)
- Records in DB with status='installed'

#### Method: \`update_plugin_files(string \$slug, array \$files): array|WP_Error\`
- Updates specific files in an existing generated plugin
- Used by the self-healing loop when sandbox testing fails and the agent regenerates specific files
- Each file update tracked in the changes_log (via existing ChangeLogger)

#### Method: \`delete_generated_plugin(string \$slug): array|WP_Error\`
- Removes plugin directory and DB record
- Must deactivate first if active
- Only works on AI-generated plugins (checks DB record exists)

#### Method: \`get_generated_plugin(string \$slug): array|null\`
- Returns DB record + filesystem status for a generated plugin

#### Method: \`list_generated_plugins(string \$status = ''): array\`
- Lists all generated plugins, optionally filtered by status
- Joins with filesystem check to detect orphaned records

### Path Traversal Protection

Critical security requirement. Every file path must:
1. Be relative (no leading \`/\`)
2. Not contain \`..\/\`
3. Not contain null bytes
4. Resolve within \`WP_CONTENT_DIR/plugins/{slug}/\`
5. Use \`wp_normalize_path()\` + \`realpath()\` check after write

Implement as a private method: \`validate_plugin_path(string \$slug, string \$relative_path): string|WP_Error\`

### Patterns to follow

- Use \`WP_Filesystem\` for all file operations (see \`FileAbilities.php\` — it initializes WP_Filesystem and uses \$wp_filesystem->put_contents(), etc.)
- Track modifications via \`Database::record_modified_file()\` (existing method in Database.php)
- Return WP_Error on failures
- PSR-4: \`namespace GratisAiAgent\PluginBuilder;\`

### Database interaction

- Uses the new \`generated_plugins\` table (see Database migration issue)
- CRUD methods: insert, update status, get by slug, list all, delete record
- Consider adding these as static methods on the Database class (following existing pattern) or as methods on PluginInstaller itself

### Dependencies

- Depends on: Database migration (for the generated_plugins table)
- Used by: PluginBuilderAbilities

### Testing

- Unit test: install_plugin creates correct directory structure
- Unit test: path traversal attacks are blocked
- Unit test: install_complex_plugin handles multi-file structures
- Unit test: delete_generated_plugin removes files and DB record
- Test path normalization (redundant slug prefixes)
- Test slug validation (reject invalid characters)

### Verification

\`\`\`bash
composer phpstan
composer phpcs
\`\`\`

title: PluginGenerator — AI-powered plan and code generation
body:
## Summary

Build the AI-powered code generation engine that takes a natural language plugin description and produces working WordPress plugin code. Uses the WordPress 7.0+ AI Client SDK (\`wp_ai_client_prompt()\`) for all AI calls.

## Files

- **NEW**: \`includes/PluginBuilder/PluginGenerator.php\`

## Implementation Details

### Class: \`GratisAiAgent\PluginBuilder\PluginGenerator\`

#### Method: \`generate_plan(string \$description, array \$context = []): array|WP_Error\`
- Takes the user's natural language description
- Calls \`wp_ai_client_prompt()\` with a structured system prompt that produces a plan JSON
- Plan JSON schema:
  \`\`\`json
  {
    "name": "Cookie Consent Banner",
    "slug": "cookie-consent-banner",
    "version": "1.0.0",
    "description": "Adds a GDPR-compliant cookie consent banner",
    "author": "AI Agent",
    "type": "single-file|multi-file",
    "files": [
      {
        "path": "cookie-consent-banner.php",
        "purpose": "Main plugin file with activation hooks",
        "dependencies": []
      },
      {
        "path": "includes/frontend.php",
        "purpose": "Frontend banner rendering",
        "dependencies": ["cookie-consent-banner.php"]
      }
    ],
    "hooks_used": ["wp_footer", "wp_enqueue_scripts"],
    "settings": ["banner_text", "accept_button_text", "cookie_expiry_days"],
    "has_admin_page": true,
    "has_frontend_output": true,
    "estimated_complexity": "simple|moderate|complex"
  }
  \`\`\`
- Optional \`\$context\` param can include: target plugin hooks (from HookScanner), existing plugin files (for extension plugins), error context from failed generation attempts

#### Method: \`generate_code(array \$plan): array|WP_Error\`
- Takes the validated plan JSON
- Generates code file-by-file, passing previously generated files as context
- For single-file plugins: one \`wp_ai_client_prompt()\` call
- For multi-file plugins: sequential calls respecting \`dependencies\` order
- Each file generation prompt includes:
  - The plan JSON
  - The file's purpose from the plan
  - Previously generated files (for cross-file reference consistency)
  - WordPress plugin standards (plugin header, text domain, etc.)
- Returns \`['files' => ['path' => 'content', ...], 'plan' => array]\`

#### Method: \`generate_file(array \$plan, array \$file_spec, array \$prior_files = []): string|WP_Error\`
- Generates a single file's code
- \$file_spec is one entry from plan['files']
- \$prior_files maps path => content of already-generated files
- Includes code quality instructions in the prompt: strict_types, proper escaping, nonce verification, etc.

#### Method: \`review_code(array \$files, array \$plan): array|WP_Error\`
- After all files are generated, runs a review pass
- Prompt asks the AI to review for: security issues, WordPress coding standards violations, missing sanitization/escaping, potential fatal errors, missing dependencies
- Returns \`['approved' => bool, 'issues' => [...], 'suggested_fixes' => [...]]\`
- If issues found, can feed back into generate_file() for targeted fixes

### AI Prompt Design

System prompt for plan generation should include:
- WordPress plugin structure conventions
- Available hooks and APIs
- The user's WordPress version and active plugins (for compatibility awareness)
- Constraints: PHP 8.0+ minimum (widely available), proper plugin header format

System prompt for code generation should include:
- The full plan for context
- WordPress coding standards highlights
- Security requirements (nonce verification, capability checks, data sanitization)
- i18n requirements (text domain usage)

### Integration with AgentLoop

The PluginGenerator is called via abilities (see PluginBuilderAbilities issue), not directly from the agent loop. The agent decides when to call the generate-plugin ability based on user intent.

### Patterns to follow

- Use \`wp_ai_client_prompt()\` exactly as other AI-calling abilities do (see any ability that calls the AI SDK)
- Model on \`Settings::get('default_model')\` for model selection (via \`AbstractAbility::get_configured_model()\`)
- Return WP_Error on failures, never throw exceptions
- PSR-4: \`namespace GratisAiAgent\PluginBuilder;\`

### Dependencies

- Depends on: nothing directly (but PluginBuilderAbilities wires it into the agent)
- Used by: PluginBuilderAbilities (generate-plugin ability), PluginInstaller (to write generated files)

### Testing

- Unit test: generate_plan with mock AI response
- Unit test: generate_code with mock AI responses, verify file context building
- Unit test: review_code with mock AI response
- Test plan JSON schema validation
- Test multi-file dependency ordering

### Verification

\`\`\`bash
composer phpstan
composer phpcs
\`\`\`

title: Plugin Builder & Sandbox System — AI-powered plugin generation with safe activation
body:
## Epic: Plugin Builder & Sandbox System

A major feature that lets the AI agent generate, install, test, and safely activate WordPress plugins — all within the same WordPress install that runs the agent itself.

### Architecture Overview

**Three-layer safety model:**

- **Layer 1: Static Analysis** — `php -l` syntax check on every generated file. Cheap, instant, catches ~60% of fatal errors.
- **Layer 2: Isolated Process Test** — WP-CLI subprocess: `wp eval-file sandbox-test.php --skip-plugins`. Loads WordPress core + tries `include_once` on the plugin. If fatal, subprocess dies, parent process survives.
- **Layer 3: Transactional Activation** — `activate_plugin()` with error handler + shutdown function. Transient flag so next request auto-deactivates on fatal. Immediate rollback: deactivate + restore backup.

### New classes (all under `includes/PluginBuilder/`)

| Class | Purpose |
|-------|---------|
| `PluginSandbox.php` | 3-layer safety: syntax → isolated include → activation |
| `PluginGenerator.php` | Plan + code generation via `wp_ai_client_prompt()` |
| `PluginInstaller.php` | Write files to `wp-content/plugins/`, track in DB |
| `PluginUpdater.php` | Sandboxed live updates to running plugins |
| `HookScanner.php` | Scan plugins/themes for hooks to enable extension plugins |

### New abilities (registered via `wp_register_ability()`)

| Ability | Purpose |
|---------|---------|
| `gratis-ai-agent/generate-plugin` | Takes a description, produces plan + code |
| `gratis-ai-agent/sandbox-test-plugin` | Runs layers 1+2 against a plugin directory |
| `gratis-ai-agent/sandbox-activate-plugin` | Layer 3: safe activation with rollback |
| `gratis-ai-agent/update-plugin-sandboxed` | For live updates: backup → stage → test → swap |
| `gratis-ai-agent/scan-plugin-hooks` | Scan installed plugin for hooks |
| `gratis-ai-agent/scan-theme-hooks` | Scan installed theme for hooks |

### Database additions

New table `{prefix}gratis_ai_agent_generated_plugins` to track all AI-generated plugins with status, plan JSON, sandbox results, etc.

### Agent loop integration flow

1. User: "Create a plugin that adds a cookie consent banner"
2. Agent calls `generate-plugin` → AI generates plan, then code
3. Agent calls `sandbox-test-plugin` → runs layers 1+2
4. If pass → agent calls `sandbox-activate-plugin`
5. If fail → agent reads error, calls generate again with error context (self-healing loop)

### Child issues

This epic is decomposed into 8 implementation issues covering: sandbox testing, code generation, file installation, live updates, database migration, abilities registration, hook scanning, and integration tests.

### Inspiration

Architecture informed by WP-Autoplugin (https://github.com/WP-Autoplugin/wp-autoplugin/) but adapted to our WordPress 7.0+ AI Client SDK / Abilities API architecture. We take: plan→code pipeline, hook scanning, code review pass, file context building. We do NOT take: their AI API layer, admin pages, activation approach, or code directly.

title: fix(wp-cli): skip ability registration when wp binary unavailable
body:
## Summary

Do not register the `wp-cli/execute` ability (nor the `wp-cli` category)
when WP-CLI is unavailable on the host. Today the ability is always
registered, then fails at execute time with a friendly error
(improved in PR #1603). That still leaks the tool into
`sd-ai-agent/ability-search` results, the model burns turns trying it,
and the only signal back is "WP-CLI binary not found, continue with
something else."

The cleaner fix is upstream: if there is no usable `wp` binary, or
`proc_open` is disabled, the ability should never be registered and
must not surface in ability discovery at all.

## Background

PR #1603 (`GH#1599`) hardened the runtime error messages in
`includes/Abilities/WpCliAbilities.php` so the model continues gracefully
after a failed call. It did not address the upstream problem: the
ability is registered unconditionally during bootstrap.

## Scope

### Behaviour

- `WpCliAbilities::register_ability()` returns early (no
  `wp_register_ability(...)`) when either:
  1. `is_proc_open_available()` is false, OR
  2. `find_wp_cli()` returns a `WP_Error` (no usable binary found via
     filter, constant, candidate paths, PATH scan, or `which`).
- `WpCliAbilities::register_category()` is skipped in the same
  conditions (or only registered when the ability itself registers, so
  we do not advertise an empty category).
- Result: `sd-ai-agent/ability-search` does not return `wp-cli/execute`
  on hosts without WP-CLI, and `ToolDiscovery` does not list it in any
  tier.

### Implementation notes

- Detection is already cheap: `find_wp_cli()` caches the resolved path
  in `self::$cached_binary` and `path_is_usable()` is a `file_exists()`
  + `is_readable()` check. Calling it once during registration is fine.
- Preserve the existing runtime guards inside `handle_execute()` as
  defence-in-depth (binary may disappear between bootstrap and
  execution, filters may flip availability, etc.). Do not delete them.
- Keep the `sd_ai_agent_wp_cli_binary` and
  `sd_ai_agent_wp_cli_proc_open_available` filters working: evaluate
  them inside the registration check too, so a host that injects a
  binary via filter still gets the ability.
- Bootstrap timing: `register_ability()` runs on
  `abilities_api_init` (verify the hook in `Plugin.php`). At that
  point ABSPATH is defined and the filesystem is reachable, so the
  binary scan is safe. If the hook fires before plugins/filters can
  attach `sd_ai_agent_wp_cli_binary`, add a late re-check on
  `init` / `rest_api_init` and register lazily if it then becomes
  available. (Verify need empirically; do not add the late hook
  speculatively.)
- Multisite: registration is per-request, so a network with mixed
  hosts will Just Work — each request scans the local filesystem.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] On a host without `wp` binary and without
      `SD_AI_AGENT_WP_CLI_PATH`, `wp-cli/execute` is NOT present in
      `wp_get_abilities()` / `ability-search` results.
- [ ] On a host with `wp-cli.phar` next to `wp-config.php`,
      `wp-cli/execute` IS registered and discoverable.
- [ ] On a host with `proc_open` disabled, `wp-cli/execute` is NOT
      registered regardless of binary presence.
- [ ] `sd_ai_agent_wp_cli_binary` filter that points at a real binary
      causes the ability to register, even if no binary would have
      been auto-detected.
- [ ] PHPUnit covers all four cases above (mock `function_exists`
      where needed, or use the existing
      `sd_ai_agent_wp_cli_proc_open_available` filter).
- [ ] Runtime guards inside `handle_execute()` remain (regression
      protection).
- [ ] `ToolDiscovery` tests assert `wp-cli/execute` is absent when
      registration is skipped.

## Verification

```bash
npm run lint:php
composer phpstan
npm run test:php -- --filter WpCli
npm run test:php   # full suite per worker self-verification protocol
```

Manual:

1. On a host without `wp`: install plugin, open ability-search,
   confirm `wp-cli/execute` is absent.
2. Add `wp-cli.phar` next to `wp-config.php`, reload, confirm it
   appears.
3. `define( 'SD_AI_AGENT_WP_CLI_PATH', '/nonexistent' )`, confirm it
   disappears.

## Files likely touched

- `includes/Abilities/WpCliAbilities.php` —
  `register_ability()`, `register_category()`, possibly a small
  `is_available()` helper that consolidates the
  proc_open + binary checks.
- `tests/SdAiAgent/Abilities/WpCliAbilitiesTest.php` (or sibling) —
  add the four registration-gating tests.
- `tests/SdAiAgent/Tools/ToolDiscoveryTest.php` — assert absence
  when WP-CLI is unavailable.

## Related

- Follow-up to PR #1603 (`GH#1599`,
  https://github.com/Ultimate-Multisite/superdav-ai-agent/pull/1603).
- Same family as other "do not advertise unusable abilities" work
  (e.g. WooCommerce abilities only when WooCommerce is active).

## Caveats

- Do NOT cache the registration decision across requests in a
  persistent option. If wp-cli is added/removed on disk between
  requests we want the next request to pick it up. The existing
  per-request `self::$cached_binary` is sufficient.
- Do NOT silently swallow filter-injected binaries that fail
  `path_is_usable()`. Behaviour should match
  `find_wp_cli()` exactly so a misconfigured filter is debuggable via
  the same error path.

title: GH#1536 — bug(create-menu): support navigation labels distinct from page titles
body:
## Summary

`sd-ai-agent/create-menu` should accept a `navigation_label` per item
that is distinct from the linked page's `post_title`. Current behaviour
forces the nav label to match the page title.

Example from the post-#1522 walkthrough: page titled "Shop Our Beans"
appeared in the nav verbatim, when the agent's design preview had
already (correctly) shortened it to "Shop" — three letters instead of
fifteen.

## Root cause

`CreateMenuAbility` (or whatever powers create-menu) uses
`wp_update_nav_menu_item()` with `menu-item-title` derived from the
linked post's title rather than from the caller's explicit value.

`wp_update_nav_menu_item()` already accepts a custom title via
`menu-item-title` — the ability just needs to plumb the caller-supplied
label through.

## Proposed fix

In `includes/Abilities/CreateMenuAbility.php`:

```php
'menu-item-title' => $item['navigation_label'] ?? $item['title'] ?? $page->post_title,
```

Schema addition:

```json
{
  "items": [
    {
      "page_id": 123,
      "navigation_label": "Shop"
    }
  ]
}
```

If `navigation_label` is omitted, fall back to the page title (current
behaviour, no regression).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Schema accepts `navigation_label` per item, optional
- [ ] Provided label is used as the rendered nav label
- [ ] Omitted label falls back to the page title (no regression)
- [ ] PHPUnit covers both the override and fallback paths

## Verification

```bash
composer phpstan
composer phpcs
npm run test:php -- --filter CreateMenuAbility
```

Manual: re-run the Theme Builder walkthrough; confirm "Shop Our Beans"
page renders as "Shop" in the nav.

## Caveats

- Same caveat as the menu-ordering issue: if the Theme Builder uses
  the block-navigation system (`wp:navigation-link`) instead of the
  classic nav menu, the fix is in the block markup the agent emits,
  not in `wp_update_nav_menu_item`.

## Related

- Filed during post-#1522 design review.
- Companion to `bug(create-menu): respect requested menu item order`.

title: GH#1535 — feat(theme-builder): validate palette contrast before scaffold
body:
## Summary

Before scaffolding a block theme, validate the chosen palette against
WCAG AA contrast minimums (4.5:1 for body text, 3:1 for large text and
UI components). Reject or auto-adjust palettes that fail.

## Why

The post-#1522 walkthrough produced a theme using sage green on
parchment for all-caps small-text kickers. Visually charming but
borderline on contrast. A site that fails WCAG isn't just an
accessibility problem — for businesses operating in the UK / EU /
US public sector it's a legal exposure.

The agent should catch this automatically, not rely on the user to
spot it.

## Scope

### Palette validation

Add a `PaletteValidator` service in `includes/Services/`:

```php
$validator = new PaletteValidator( $palette );
$result    = $validator->check();
// $result->failures: array of failing pairs (fg, bg, ratio, required)
// $result->suggestions: minimal hex adjustments to pass
```

For each pair the theme will combine (heading-on-bg, body-on-bg,
button-text-on-button-bg, link-on-bg, kicker-on-bg, etc.), compute
relative luminance and contrast ratio.

### Auto-correction

If a pair fails, offer the user:

1. A nudge to one or both colours that brings the pair into
   compliance (darken the foreground, lighten the background, or
   pick the nearest passing tone from a Material/Tailwind-style
   ramp).
2. The option to mark the pair as non-text (decorative) — those are
   exempt from contrast minimums.
3. The option to accept the failure with a documented exception
   (the resulting theme.json includes a comment noting the choice).

### Integration

Runs at the END of the direction-selection step, before
`scaffold-block-theme` is called. If a direction fails, the agent
either fixes it autonomously or surfaces the failure to the user
with options.

### Tooling

There are well-tested PHP libraries for this (e.g. `mexitek/phpcolors`
for manipulation, `tinycolor` patterns for contrast). Pick a small
dependency or implement from scratch — the WCAG contrast formula
is ~20 lines.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `PaletteValidator` service implemented and tested
- [ ] Theme Builder flow runs validation pre-scaffold
- [ ] Failing palettes trigger user-visible options
- [ ] Selected palette guaranteed to pass AA for body + large-text
      defined pairs, OR explicitly marked decorative
- [ ] PHPUnit covers ratio computation, failure detection, and
      suggestion logic
- [ ] E2E test runs a deliberately-failing palette and confirms the
      flow does not proceed to scaffold without resolution

## Verification

```bash
composer phpstan
composer phpcs
npm run test:php -- --filter PaletteValidator
npm run test:e2e:playwright -- onboarding-theme-builder
```

Manual: run the walkthrough with a low-contrast direction. Confirm
the agent surfaces the failure and resolves it before scaffolding.

## Caveats

- AAA (7:1) is stricter; we target AA. Document this clearly in the
  theme.json output.
- Some directions intentionally use low-contrast pairing for
  decorative-only elements. The validator must not produce false
  positives on those.

## Related

- Filed during post-#1522 design review.
- Lower priority than the content / imagery issues, but it's the
  kind of automation that quietly raises the floor on every site
  the agent produces.

title: GH#1534 — feat(theme-builder): add photo upload step to the discovery interview
body:
## Summary

The Theme Builder interview should explicitly ask the user to upload
photos of their space, products, team, and events. Uploads land
directly in the media library and the agent weaves them into the
generated site (hero, gallery, about, menu items, etc.).

This is the third leg of the image acquisition strategy alongside
stock-image-search and generate-image.

## Why

User-supplied photos are always the most valuable imagery — they show
the actual business. The agent should treat photo upload as a
first-class interview step, not an afterthought.

## Scope

### Interview UX

During the discovery interview, after the brand vertical is
established, the agent asks:

> "I can use real photos to make this site shine. Do you have photos
> of (a) your space / shopfront, (b) your products / drinks / food,
> (c) your team, (d) any events or special moments? Upload as many
> as you like — I'll pick the best ones for each section. If you
> don't have any yet, I'll use a mix of stock and AI-generated
> images, and you can swap them later."

A drag-and-drop area appears inline in the chat. Uploaded files:

- Land in the media library
- Are tagged with `_sd_ai_agent_interview_upload` meta and a
  category guess (`space` / `product` / `team` / `event`) from
  filename + visual recognition (optional ML step) + the agent's
  conversation context
- Are surfaced back to the agent immediately with media IDs +
  thumbnails so it can plan their use

### Implementation notes

- New React component `OnboardingPhotoUpload` in
  `src/components/`
- Drag-and-drop wrapper around `wp.media.editor` or a direct
  `media-handle-upload` REST call
- Server-side: extend `MediaAbility` (or add a new
  `BulkUploadAbility`) to accept multiple files in one call
- Categorisation: simple heuristic on first pass (filename
  keywords); optional later upgrade via image classification

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Interview asks for photos at the appropriate moment
- [ ] User can drag-and-drop multiple files in the chat UI
- [ ] Uploaded files reach the media library
- [ ] Files are tagged so the agent can find them later
- [ ] The agent acknowledges uploads in the chat ("Got the 8
      photos — I'll use the shopfront for the hero and the latte
      art set for the menu page")
- [ ] No placeholder copy — if the user has zero photos, the agent
      falls back to stock + AI generation (per the other abilities)
- [ ] PHPUnit covers the bulk-upload path and meta tagging

## Verification

```bash
composer phpstan
composer phpcs
npm run test:php
npm run test:e2e:playwright -- onboarding-theme-builder
```

Manual: walkthrough with 5+ real photos uploaded. Confirm they
appear on the built site.

## Caveats

- Large uploads stress PHP `upload_max_filesize` and
  `post_max_size`. The component should chunk large files or warn
  the user to compress first.
- EXIF orientation handling matters — many phone photos come
  rotated. WordPress core handles this, but verify against the
  generated theme's image blocks.

## Related

- Filed during post-#1522 design review.
- Completes the image-acquisition trio with stock-image-search and
  generate-image.

title: GH#1532 — feat(theme-builder): show mobile previews during design direction selection
body:
## Summary

During the "pick a design direction" step, the Theme Builder agent
should present each candidate design as both a desktop preview
(~1280px) AND a mobile preview (~375px) side-by-side. The user is
choosing how their site will FEEL across devices, not just on
desktop.

## Why

The post-#1522 walkthrough produced three desktop-only previews. The
chosen direction (split layout: dark brown left + cream right) is
striking on desktop but its reflow behaviour at mobile width is
critical — a poorly-reflowed split layout becomes a tall, awkward
scroll. The user is making a design decision blind to half the
viewport spectrum.

## Scope

### Preview generation

The current preview pipeline writes one full HTML file per direction.
The new pipeline writes the same content but renders TWO viewports:

- Desktop: 1280×800 viewport screenshot
- Mobile: 375×812 viewport screenshot

Both are rendered server-side using Playwright or Chromium-headless
against the preview HTML, then saved to
`wp-content/uploads/sd-ai-agent/design-previews/<theme-slug>/`.

### UI presentation

The admin chat surfaces both screenshots side-by-side per direction.
Click-to-zoom on either. The screenshots are the ground truth — the
HTML preview file itself is also viewable for advanced inspection.

### Implementation notes

- Add a `PreviewRenderer` service in `includes/Services/`
- Reuse the existing Playwright setup from E2E tests for the
  headless rendering, or use a lighter `wp-cli puppeteer` if
  available
- Cache rendered screenshots so they don't regenerate on every
  message
- Add a `viewport` parameter to the file-write preview output so
  the agent can request additional viewports (tablet, ultra-wide)
  if needed

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Each design direction renders both desktop and mobile
      screenshots
- [ ] Both are shown to the user during direction selection
- [ ] Click-to-zoom works on both
- [ ] Screenshot generation is reliable (fails-soft: if mobile
      render fails, desktop still ships with a clear "mobile preview
      unavailable" marker — not a blocker)
- [ ] PHPUnit covers the PreviewRenderer service
- [ ] E2E test asserts both viewports are present in the chat UI

## Verification

```bash
composer phpstan
composer phpcs
npm run test:php -- --filter PreviewRenderer
npm run test:e2e:playwright -- onboarding-theme-builder
```

Manual: run the Theme Builder walkthrough; confirm both viewports
appear; pick a direction that looks bad on mobile; verify it's
visually obvious.

## Caveats

- Headless rendering on shared hosts may be blocked (no Chromium
  binary, restricted exec()). Provide a clean fallback that
  renders previews client-side via responsive iframes if
  server-side rendering is unavailable.
- This adds load time to the direction-selection step. Render in
  parallel and stream the desktop screenshot first so the user
  isn't blocked.

## Related

- Filed during post-#1522 design review.
- Pairs with `feat(theme-builder): preview-to-scaffold fidelity` —
  both improve trust in the preview step.

title: GH#1533 — investigation(theme-builder): audit preview-to-scaffold visual fidelity gaps
body:
## Summary

Investigate and document the gap between Theme Builder DESIGN PREVIEWS
(rich HTML mockups) and SCAFFOLD OUTPUT (the actual WordPress block
theme). Where design moments are lost during scaffold, either close
the gap or set the user's expectation honestly before they choose a
direction.

## Why

In the post-#1522 walkthrough, the chosen direction ("The Handwritten
Journal") featured a distinctive dashed-orange line under the
header. That detail was the soul of the direction. The built theme
did NOT clearly carry that detail through — it was either omitted or
visually attenuated.

This breaks user trust: "you showed me this, you built me that".

## Scope

This is an investigation issue first, then a corrective work issue.

### Phase 1: audit

For each of 5 sample directions across different verticals, produce a
side-by-side comparison:

- Original preview HTML render (desktop + mobile)
- Final scaffold render (desktop + mobile)
- Bullet list of design elements PRESENT in preview but ABSENT in
  scaffold

Output as a single doc at `docs/theme-builder-fidelity-audit.md`.

### Phase 2: classify gaps

For each gap, classify as:

- **Mechanical** — scaffold ability literally doesn't support this
  element (e.g. dashed borders aren't expressible in default block
  styles). Fix by extending `scaffold-block-theme`.
- **Promptable** — the agent could include this if its system
  prompt and tool descriptions explained how. Fix by updating
  prompts and adding examples.
- **Out of scope** — the preview took a liberty (e.g. custom JS
  animations) that no scaffold should ever ship. Fix by tightening
  the preview generation prompt so it doesn't promise what it can't
  deliver.

### Phase 3: close the top 10 gaps

Implement the top 10 fixes by total impact (preview → scaffold
fidelity). Each as a small PR.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Audit doc exists at `docs/theme-builder-fidelity-audit.md`
- [ ] At least 5 sample verticals are audited
- [ ] Each gap is classified and assigned a fix path
- [ ] Top 10 fixes are implemented and merged
- [ ] After fixes, re-running the same walkthrough produces a
      scaffold that visually matches the chosen preview at >= 85%
      identity (subjective design-team review)

## Verification

Visual review by user + at least one design-aware reviewer. Optional:
pixelmatch or odiff-based diff between rendered preview and rendered
scaffold over the same viewport, with a threshold check in E2E.

## Caveats

- This is a multi-PR effort. Phase 1 (audit) is small. Phase 2
  (classification) is medium. Phase 3 (fixes) may produce 10+ PRs.
- The honest path may be to constrain the preview generation prompt
  to ONLY use design elements the scaffold can faithfully reproduce.
  That's a cleaner contract than chasing parity in every direction.

## Related

- Filed during post-#1522 design review.
- Pairs with `feat(theme-builder): mobile preview` — both improve
  the trust contract around preview selection.

title: GH#1531 — feat(theme-builder): generate structured hospitality menu pages with prices
body:
## Summary

For hospitality verticals (café, restaurant, bar, food truck), the
`/menu/` page is the single highest-traffic page on the site. It must
auto-generate as a structured categorised price list (categories →
items → prices, optionally descriptions), not as a single block of
prose.

## Why

A café's menu is the conversion-relevant content. A user landing on
`/menu/` wants to scan categories, find a drink, see a price, and
decide whether to visit. A prose paragraph saying "We serve a variety
of seasonal drinks" fails this completely.

## Scope

### Interview additions

The Theme Builder agent must ask, during the interview for hospitality
verticals:

1. "What categories does your menu have?" (e.g. Espresso, Pour-Over,
   Filter, Cold, Tea, Food)
2. For each category: "List the items, with prices."
3. Optional per item: short description (2 lines max), allergens,
   dietary tags (V, VG, GF)

### Page generation

Build `/menu/` with a structured layout. Possible block compositions:

- `<!-- wp:columns -->` per category, with `<!-- wp:heading -->` for
  the category name and `<!-- wp:group -->` per item containing the
  item name + price (right-aligned) + optional description.
- Or a custom block pattern `sd-ai-agent/menu-section` providing the
  same structure with theme-aware styling.

### Other verticals follow the same principle

- Restaurant → starters/mains/desserts/wines
- Service business → services with price ranges or "from £X"
- Shop → at minimum, featured products with price + buy buttons
  (WooCommerce required; agent should detect and integrate)
- Portfolio → projects with image + role + year

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] For hospitality verticals, the interview captures structured
      menu data (categories + items + prices + optional descriptions)
- [ ] The `/menu/` page renders as a categorised price list, not
      prose
- [ ] Item prices align consistently (right-aligned or tabular)
- [ ] Each category has a clear visual break
- [ ] Allergen / dietary tags render as small badges next to items
- [ ] No placeholder copy ("Our menu changes seasonally") — the page
      contains the user's real items or is not created
- [ ] PHPUnit covers menu structure rendering
- [ ] E2E test asserts `/menu/` contains at least one category and
      at least one priced item

## Verification

```bash
composer phpstan
composer phpcs
npm run test:php
npm run test:e2e:playwright -- onboarding-theme-builder
```

Manual: run the Theme Builder walkthrough for a café and a restaurant.
Inspect `/menu/`. It must be skim-readable in 5 seconds.

## Caveats

- Some businesses want a downloadable PDF menu instead of an HTML
  menu (à la carte restaurants do this). The interview should
  detect this preference and the agent can embed a PDF viewer
  alongside or instead of inline HTML.
- Price formatting depends on locale. Default to the locale of the
  WP site (`get_locale()`), with currency derived from address /
  country or asked in the interview.

## Related

- Filed during post-#1522 design review.
- Pairs with `feat(theme-builder): no placeholder content` — both
  require structured user input during interview.

title: GH#1512 — extend Theme Builder 'no external URLs' rule to web fonts
body:
See https://github.com/Ultimate-Multisite/superdav-ai-agent/issues/1512 for the full worker-ready brief.

Root cause: Theme Builder system prompt forbids external image URLs (around includes/Models/Agent.php lines 625, 647) but is silent on web fonts. Walkthrough produced design previews and a scaffolded theme that all load https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=... — GDPR-hostile, WP.org reviewer-flagged, and inconsistent with the existing image rule.

Fix: extend the prompt rule to forbid fonts.googleapis.com / fonts.gstatic.com / use.typekit.net / fonts.adobe.com etc; require system font stacks in previews and self-hosted WOFF2 in scaffolded themes; optionally add a server-side scanner in FileWriteAbility/ScaffoldBlockThemeAbility that rejects writes containing those substrings.

title: GH#1511 — scaffolded theme.json uses schema version 2 instead of 3
body:
See https://github.com/Ultimate-Multisite/superdav-ai-agent/issues/1511 for the full worker-ready brief.

Root cause: ScaffoldBlockThemeAbility::default_theme_json() correctly returns version 3, but the model is supplying its own theme_json override with version 2 in the tool input and the ability accepts it as-is. Walkthrough produced wp-content/themes/bramble-and-bean/theme.json with 'version': 2.

Fix (two layers): system prompt in includes/Models/Agent.php explicitly instructs v3 with the trunk schema URL; ScaffoldBlockThemeAbility coerces caller-supplied version < 3 to 3 (and logs the coercion) as a durable safety net.

title: issue-sync-helper.sh: dedupe new issues against recently-closed ones with matching task IDs
body:
On 2026-05-19 03:47:08Z, issue-sync-helper.sh auto-created #1504 as a duplicate of #1373 (closed completed 2026-05-14 via PR #1413).

## Root cause

issue-sync-helper.sh reads TODO.md and creates a GitHub issue for any `[ ]` task entry that doesn't have a matching OPEN issue with the same task ID/title. It does NOT check CLOSED issues, so when a TODO.md entry was never marked `[x]` after its tracking issue closed, the sync re-creates a duplicate on the next run.

## Reproduction

1. Close an issue with title starting `tNNN: ...` via PR merge.
2. Leave the matching TODO.md line as `[ ] tNNN ...`.
3. Push any commit to main.
4. Issue Sync workflow runs and creates a duplicate of the closed issue.

## Proposed fix

Before creating a new issue, the sync helper should:
1. Query closed issues from the last N days (e.g. 30) matching `tNNN:` in the title.
2. If found, either:
   a. Skip creation and log a warning recommending the TODO.md entry be marked `[x]`, OR
   b. Auto-mark the TODO.md entry as `[x]` with the closing PR ref pulled from the closed issue's metadata.

Option (b) is more aggressive but eliminates the drift entirely.

## Evidence
- Closed #1373 (completed 2026-05-14 via PR #1413).
- Auto-created duplicate #1504 at 2026-05-19 03:47:08Z (3s after PR #1503 merged).
- Closed #1504 manually with #1507 marking TODO.md.

## Related
- #1507 (TODO.md fix)
- #1504, #1373

title: Add Restart Setup Assistant control to Settings → Advanced (GH#1505)
body: Add a v2-correct restart affordance: clears onboarding state and lets the existing direct-routing gate in src/admin-page/index.js fire on next chat-page mount, dropping the user into the Setup Assistant agent (site with content) or Theme Builder agent (empty install). Re-implements PR #1502 with v2-correct shape (no wizard language), since PR #1503 reverted PR #1502.

title: Add Settings button to relaunch onboarding wizard
body: Add an Advanced-tab UI control + REST endpoint that resets onboarding state (TRIGGERED, COMPLETE, BOOTSTRAP_SESSION, THEME_BUILDER_SESSION, scan status, and settings.onboarding_complete) so the OnboardingWizard gate re-fires on the next chat visit.

title: E2E shard 2 flake: client-abilities.spec.js:518 snapshotDescriptors timeout
body:
tests/e2e/client-abilities.spec.js:518 'client-abilities — snapshotDescriptors › snapshotDescriptors returns 2 descriptors with expected shape' intermittently times out at 30s on Playwright locator.waitFor, which then cascades into 'Target page, context or browser has been closed' errors and fails the rest of the shard 2 suite. Has been observed on multiple PRs in this trace branch lineage including PR #1463 (CI cleanup), PR #1465, PR #1466, PR #1467. Shards 1 and 3 consistently pass.

Investigation:
- Test expects 2 client-ability descriptors to be returned via snapshotDescriptors().
- 30s wait suggests either a timing race between client-ability registration and snapshot, OR a regression from a recent PR that changed ability registration order.
- Need to check whether failure correlates with PR #1451/#1453/#1454 (client ability callback registration changes) or PR #1464 (preamble streaming).

Repro: trigger E2E Tests workflow on any trace-related PR.

title: Stream model preamble text to UI before tool calls
body:
When the model emits assistant text in the same turn as one or more tool calls, the text (preamble) is currently dropped from the live progress stream — only the tool-call name and result appear in the UI's running message. The preamble text only becomes visible when the loop completes and the full assistant message is persisted.

Goal: surface preamble text in the live RunningMessage UI in the order it was produced, so the user sees context like 'I will create a hero block, then update the homepage' before the tool card renders.

Implementation:
- AgentLoop::log_tool_calls() interleaves preamble entries (type=preamble, text=...) with call entries while iterating message parts, preserving original order.
- src/components/chat-redesign/message-helpers.js pairToolCalls() returns heterogeneous items (preamble blocks and tool pairs) preserving order.
- src/components/chat-redesign/message-items.js RunningMessage and AssistantMessage render preamble items between tool cards.

Acceptance: a turn with text+call parts shows the text immediately above the tool card during execution.

title: Exclude .eslintignore from wporg build zip
body: The wporg target of bin/build.sh shipped /.eslintignore inside superdav-ai-agent-{version}-wporg.zip because .distignore only listed /.eslintrc* and the always-applied extras + post-copy find sweep also only covered .eslintrc*. WP.org plugin-check flags shipped lint dotfiles. Fix: add /.eslintignore (top-level anchor) to .distignore alongside the existing /.eslintrc* lines, add **/.eslintignore to the tree-wide extras in build.sh, and add -o -name '.eslintignore' to the post-copy find sweep. Verified by simulating the rsync+sweep step against the working tree — no .eslintignore at any depth in the staged build dir. Repro: bin/build.sh --target=wporg then 'unzip -l superdav-ai-agent-*-wporg.zip | grep eslintignore' (previously showed superdav-ai-agent/.eslintignore at 1315 bytes).

title: fix(ci): PHPCS alignment warnings in Settings.php fail Static Analysis on every PR
body:
Static Analysis (PHPCS + PHPStan) workflow has been failing on every PR (#1433 merged failing, #1435 hits the same on first push) with ~35 WordPress.Arrays.MultipleStatementAlignment.DoubleArrowNotAligned warnings in includes/Core/Settings.php lines ~439-469 around brand_*, budget_*, skill_*, third_party_mode keys. PHPCBF can auto-fix all 35 violations.

These are warnings, not errors, so PHPCS is being run with -n disabled or warning-severity at error level. Either:
- Run phpcbf on Settings.php to auto-fix the alignment, OR
- Adjust the .phpcs.xml.dist to suppress WordPress.Arrays.MultipleStatementAlignment.DoubleArrowNotAligned warnings (already excluded MultipleStatementAlignment.LongIndexSpaceBeforeDoubleArrow elsewhere — same family).

Currently every PR shows a red Static Analysis check, eroding the signal value of CI.

title: Default sd_ai_agent_third_party_mode flip: legacy → auto (with migration)
body:
## Why

Phase-1 lands the resolver and admin notice with `sd_ai_agent_third_party_mode = legacy` to avoid surprising existing sites. Phase 2 (this issue) flips the default to `auto` so new installs get safer behaviour from day one, while existing sites are auto-migrated to preserve current visibility.

## What

1. Bump plugin version major.
2. New `includes/Core/Upgrades/UpgradeTo_X_Y_Z.php` (slot in to the existing upgrade chain):
   - If existing site has `sd_ai_agent_third_party_mode === 'legacy'` (or unset), scan currently registered abilities, snapshot every namespace currently present, and write `third_party_namespace_decisions` with all of them set to `allow`. Then flip `sd_ai_agent_third_party_mode` to `auto`.
   - For fresh installs, default `auto` with empty decisions map.
3. Update CHANGELOG.md with the behavioural change and migration notes.
4. Update readme.txt FAQ entry: \"Why are some abilities not available to the AI agent on my site?\" → explain tiered trust + namespace decisions.

## Acceptance criteria

- Upgrade test: site with `legacy` mode and 50+ third-party abilities upgrades to `auto` with all namespaces auto-allowed; no visible behaviour change.
- Fresh-install test: new activation defaults to `auto`, no namespaces pre-allowed, admin notice surfaces unclassified abilities.
- Manual rollback path documented: `wp option update sd_ai_agent_third_party_mode legacy` restores old behaviour.

title: Thread AbilityVisibility through all four exposure surfaces (replace ai_hidden checks)
body:
## Why

Once `AbilityVisibility` lands, every existing `\$meta['ai_hidden']` check becomes a candidate for replacement. The four surfaces must agree on visibility or we get drift bugs.

**Critical:** `REST/McpController.php` currently exposes ALL abilities (no `ai_hidden` filter at all). This is the highest-value fix in the whole epic — external MCP clients should not see third-party abilities the site owner hasn't sanctioned.

## What

Replace inline `! empty( \$meta['ai_hidden'] )` checks with the appropriate `AbilityVisibility::for_*()` call at each site:

1. `Core/AgentLoop.php:1422` — `for_ai_chat()`
2. `Tools/ToolDiscovery.php:343` (manifest), `:993` (search candidates) — `for_ai_chat()`
3. `REST/AgentController.php:583` (admin picker) — `for_admin_picker()`
4. `REST/McpController.php:228` (`get_mcp_tools()`) — **add `for_mcp()` gate (currently missing)**
5. `Services/AbilityExplorerService.php` — surface `classify()` as a new `visibility` column without filtering (admin sees everything but knows what AI sees).

## Acceptance criteria

- All four surfaces consult `AbilityVisibility` instead of inline meta inspection.
- New unit/integration tests assert MCP endpoint hides `private-*` abilities.
- Existing tests (`ToolDiscoveryTest`, `AgentLoopTest`, `McpControllerTest`) updated; behaviour preserved for current `ai_hidden` semantics.
- Settings flag `sd_ai_agent_third_party_mode` introduced with three values: `legacy` (current behaviour: everything except `ai_hidden` is public), `auto` (the tiered-trust model from the epic), `strict` (only explicit `meta.mcp.public === true`). Default `legacy` for now — flipped in a later release.

## Files

- Modify: `includes/Core/AgentLoop.php`, `includes/Tools/ToolDiscovery.php`, `includes/REST/AgentController.php`, `includes/REST/McpController.php`, `includes/Services/AbilityExplorerService.php`, `includes/Core/Settings.php`
- Modify tests: `tests/SdAiAgent/Tools/ToolDiscoveryTest.php`, `tests/SdAiAgent/Core/AgentLoopTest.php`, `tests/SdAiAgent/REST/McpControllerTest.php`

title: Add meta.mcp.public = true to all sd-ai-agent/* ability registrations
body:
## Why

We should eat our own dog food. Every `sd-ai-agent/*` ability is by definition meant for AI consumption (that's why it lives in this plugin). Declaring `meta.mcp.public = true` explicitly:

1. Aligns us with the WordPress/mcp-adapter convention.
2. Means our abilities don't need the namespace-allowlist heuristic — they classify as `public-explicit`.
3. Sets the example for downstream plugin authors and reviewers.

## What

For every `wp_register_ability()` call under `sd-ai-agent/` (and the `wp-cli/execute` ability we register), add:

```php
'meta' => [
    'mcp' => [ 'public' => true ],
    'annotations' => [ /* keep existing readonly/destructive/idempotent */ ],
    'show_in_rest' => true,
],
```

Sites to update (use rg to find all):
- `includes/Abilities/PostAbilities.php` (8 abilities)
- `includes/Abilities/MemoryAbilities.php` (3 abilities)
- `includes/Abilities/SkillAbilities.php` (2 abilities)
- `includes/Abilities/KnowledgeAbilities.php`
- `includes/Abilities/WordPressAbilities.php` (~14 abilities)
- `includes/Abilities/BlockAbilities.php` (~8 abilities)
- `includes/Abilities/FileAbilities.php` (~7 abilities)
- `includes/Abilities/GitAbilities.php` (~6 abilities)
- `includes/Abilities/MediaAbilities.php`, `MenuAbilities.php`, `OptionsAbilities.php`, `UserAbilities.php`, `SiteHealthAbilities.php`, `EditorialAbilities.php`, `SeoAbilities.php`, `MarketingAbilities.php`, `FeedbackAbilities.php`, `NavigationAbilities.php`, `CustomPostTypeAbilities.php`, `CustomTaxonomyAbilities.php`, `DatabaseAbilities.php`, `DesignSystemAbilities.php`, `GlobalStylesAbilities.php`, `GoogleAnalyticsAbilities.php`, `GscAbilities.php`, `InternetSearchAbilities.php`, `PluginBuilderAbilities.php`, `PluginDownloadAbilities.php`, `ThemeBuilderAbilities.php`, `ToolCapabilities.php`, `WpCliAbilities.php`
- `includes/Abilities/ImageAbilities/GenerateImageAbility.php`, `StockImageAbility.php`
- `includes/Abilities/AiImageAbilities.php`, `ContentAbilities.php`
- Single-file abilities: `ActivateThemeAbility.php`, `GeneratePluginAbility.php`, `GetPageHtmlAbility.php`, `GitDiffAbility.php`, `GitListAbility.php`, `GitPackageSummaryAbility.php`, `GitRestoreAbility.php`, `GitRevertPackageAbility.php`, `GitSnapshotAbility.php`, `NavigateAbility.php`, `SandboxActivatePluginAbility.php`, `SandboxTestPluginAbility.php`, `ScaffoldBlockThemeAbility.php`, `ScanPluginHooksAbility.php`, `ScanThemeHooksAbility.php`, `UpdatePluginSandboxedAbility.php`
- Meta-tools in `includes/Tools/ToolDiscovery.php` (`ability-search`, `ability-call`)

## Skip
- `ai_hidden = true` abilities (block-content/markdown-to-blocks if any). They are intentionally private.
- JS ability stubs registered via `JsAbilityCatalog` — those are client-side and not exposed to MCP.

## Acceptance criteria

- Every server-side `wp_register_ability('sd-ai-agent/...')` call has explicit `meta.mcp.public => true` unless `ai_hidden` is also set.
- New PHPUnit assertion that scans the registry and fails if any `sd-ai-agent/*` ability lacks `meta.mcp.public` AND isn't `ai_hidden`.
- Tests pass under `npm run test:php`.

title: AbilityVisibility resolver + PartnerAllowlist (centralize four duplicated gates)
body:
## Why

`ai_hidden` is checked in four separate files with subtly different logic:
- `Tools/ToolDiscovery.php:343, 993`
- `Core/AgentLoop.php:1422`
- `REST/AgentController.php:583`
- (Missing entirely from `REST/McpController.php` — security gap)

Each is a place to forget a future visibility rule. Centralize.

## What

1. New `includes/Core/AbilityVisibility.php`:
   ```php
   final class AbilityVisibility {
       public static function for_ai_chat( WP_Ability $a ): bool;
       public static function for_mcp( WP_Ability $a ): bool;
       public static function for_admin_picker( WP_Ability $a ): bool;
       public static function classify( WP_Ability $a ): string;
       // Returns: public-explicit, public-partner, public-heuristic,
       //          private-explicit, private-unknown.
   }
   ```
2. New `includes/Abilities/ThirdParty/PartnerAllowlist.php` with two const arrays:
   - `NAMESPACES`: trusted ability-name prefixes (e.g. `woocommerce-rest`, `multisite-ultimate`, `mcp-adapter`)
   - `CATEGORIES`: trusted category slugs (e.g. `site`, `user`, `ai-experiments`, `woocommerce-rest`)
   - Filterable: `sd_ai_agent_partner_namespaces`, `sd_ai_agent_partner_categories`.
3. Logic order in `classify()`:
   - explicit `meta.ai_hidden === true` → private-explicit
   - explicit `meta.mcp.public === false` → private-explicit
   - explicit `meta.mcp.public === true` → public-explicit
   - first-party namespace (`sd-ai-agent/*`, `wp-cli/*`) → public-partner
   - partner allowlist match → public-partner
   - category in trusted categories list → public-heuristic
   - registered category has non-empty label+description → public-heuristic
   - has non-empty `description` AND `category` → public-heuristic
   - otherwise → private-unknown
4. **No call-site changes yet** — that's the next sub-issue. Land the resolver as a pure additive change, fully unit-tested, before threading.

## Acceptance criteria

- 100% unit-test coverage of `classify()` decision tree.
- `for_ai_chat()` and `for_mcp()` return identical results unless explicit `meta` says otherwise (recommend collapsing — confirm in epic discussion).
- No call-site touched yet; existing behaviour unchanged.
- New constants/filters documented in PHPDoc.

## Files

- New: `includes/Core/AbilityVisibility.php`
- New: `includes/Abilities/ThirdParty/PartnerAllowlist.php`
- New: `tests/SdAiAgent/Core/AbilityVisibilityTest.php`
- New: `tests/SdAiAgent/Abilities/ThirdParty/PartnerAllowlistTest.php`

title: Epic: Standards-aligned third-party ability visibility (meta.mcp.public + tiered trust)
body:
## Why

Today every registered WordPress ability is exposed to the in-chat AI agent and the public MCP endpoint by default. Visibility is opt-OUT via the proprietary `meta.ai_hidden` flag. There is no opt-IN signal, no gate on the MCP endpoint, and no policy for third-party abilities that pour in from plugins like WooCommerce, Multisite Ultimate, or any future MCP-aware plugin.

The senior dev review surfaced this directly: "not all Abilities should be exposed as AI tools" — and the WordPress ecosystem already has a published convention. The MCP Adapter v0.5.0 (WordPress/mcp-adapter, Apr 2026) defines `meta.mcp.public = true` as the canonical signal. WooCommerce 10.3+ already follows it. Plugin authors are increasingly expected to declare it.

## What

Adopt `meta.mcp.public` as the primary signal for both in-chat AI exposure and MCP-endpoint exposure. Add a deterministic tiered-trust resolver for abilities that pre-date the convention so users do NOT have to toggle visibility per ability. Centralize the visibility decision into one `AbilityVisibility` class consumed by all four exposure surfaces (chat Tier-1 tools, chat Tier-2 manifest, MCP endpoint, admin picker).

## Tiered trust model (zero per-ability user config)

- **Tier A — explicit public:** `meta.mcp.public === true`. Always exposed.
- **Tier B — explicit private:** `meta.mcp.public === false` OR `meta.ai_hidden === true`. Never exposed.
- **Tier C — implicit (no flag):** Apply heuristic, deterministic from registry state:
  1. First-party namespace allowlist (`sd-ai-agent/*`, `wp-cli/*`, core categories `site`/`user`/`ai-experiments`).
  2. Verified-partner namespace allowlist (`woocommerce-rest/*`, `multisite-ultimate/*`, `mcp-adapter/*` — short curated list, code-shipped, filterable).
  3. Category-quality signal: ability has a `category` registered with non-empty `label` + `description` → public.
  4. Schema-quality gate: ability has non-empty `description` AND `category` set → public; otherwise private.
  5. Unknown namespace that fails the gate: private; surface in a batched admin notice (one entry per plugin namespace, not per ability).

## Surfaces affected

1. In-chat Tier-1 (FunctionDeclarations) — `AgentLoop::resolve_abilities()` line 1381-1432
2. In-chat Tier-2 manifest — `ToolDiscovery::build_manifest_section()` line 326
3. MCP endpoint — `McpController::get_mcp_tools()` line 228 (currently UNGATED — security gap)
4. Admin ability picker — `AgentController::handle_list_abilities()` line 570
5. Abilities Explorer — `AbilityExplorerService::get_explorer_list()` (visibility column)

## Acceptance criteria

- Single `AbilityVisibility` resolver replaces all four duplicated `ai_hidden` checks.
- MCP endpoint respects the same gate as in-chat exposure.
- Existing first-party abilities (`sd-ai-agent/*`) automatically classified as public via namespace allowlist.
- WooCommerce/Multisite-Ultimate abilities continue to work without manual configuration.
- New `meta.mcp.public => true` added to all `sd-ai-agent/*` ability registrations.
- Admin sees a one-time informational summary on upgrade, not a per-ability toggle list.
- Three-phase rollout: legacy → auto → strict, with `sd_ai_agent_third_party_mode` setting.

## References

- WordPress/mcp-adapter v0.5.0 README — canonical `meta.mcp.public` pattern
- AGENTS.md "Canonical Naming" — preserves `sd-ai-agent/` namespace
- Existing `WooCommerceIntegrationHandler.php` — partner integration pattern to extend

title: Add Anthropic prompt caching support (KV cache utilisation)
body:
## Problem

Provider trace analysis of session 122-128 (8 consecutive Anthropic API calls) shows the plugin currently sends ~21,000-25,000 input tokens per turn with **zero prompt cache utilisation**: every response shows `cache_creation_input_tokens=0` and `cache_read_input_tokens=0`. The system prompt (~38KB / ~10K tokens) and 16 tool definitions (~10K tokens) are byte-stable across consecutive turns (verified via SHA-256 hash of system+tools across traces 122 and 123) but lack the `cache_control` markers Anthropic requires to opt into prompt caching.

Estimated cost impact on a typical 7-turn Opus session: input cost ~$2.38 today vs ~$0.79 with caching (66% reduction). Bigger savings on longer conversations and on slower models that re-process the same prefix repeatedly.

## Scope

Provider-aware prompt-cache strategy. Of the four installed connectors:

- **Anthropic / Anthropic Max** — REQUIRES explicit `cache_control: {type: "ephemeral"}` markers on the last block of each cacheable region. This is where the work is.
- **OpenAI** — automatic server-side caching for prefixes >=1024 tokens, no client opt-in needed. Telemetry-only ingest.
- **DeepSeek / Grok / Groq / Cerebras** (via any-compatible connector) — automatic caching. Telemetry-only ingest.
- **Google Gemini** — implicit cache for 2.5; explicit CachedContent API is a future enhancement.

## Design decisions

1. **Strategy pattern** keyed on provider_id. Anthropic strategy injects `cache_control` markers via `ModelConfig::setCustomOption()` (the SDK passes customOptions through to provider-side `prepareGenerateTextParams()` in both anthropic and anthropic-max plugins, line 177-188 / 275-288).
2. **Two breakpoints** for Anthropic:
   - End of `system` array (caches system prompt) 
   - End of `tools` array (caches tools as well, since cache scope is positional and tools come before system in Anthropic's API ordering)
3. **No breakpoint on messages** in v1 — conversation history changes every turn so the marginal value is lower; revisit if multi-turn tool loops show cache misses.
4. **Provider-agnostic telemetry**: extend `sd_ai_agent_provider_trace` table with `cache_creation_tokens` and `cache_read_tokens` columns, parse from response usage block for ALL providers (Anthropic uses `cache_creation_input_tokens` + `cache_read_input_tokens`; OpenAI uses `usage.prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens`; DeepSeek uses `prompt_cache_hit_tokens`).
5. **Settings toggle** off by default for one release to allow opt-in testing; default on in the release after.

## Acceptance criteria

- New `SdAiAgent\Core\PromptCache\` namespace with `CacheStrategyInterface` and `AnthropicCacheStrategy`, `NoopCacheStrategy`
- `AgentLoop::send_prompt()` consults a strategy resolver before calling the SDK
- New setting `prompt_caching_enabled` (bool, default true)
- `ProviderTrace` schema migration adds two integer columns; existing rows backfill to 0
- `ProviderTrace::insert()` extracts cache token counts from response_body usage block across all known providers
- WP-CLI `wp ai-agent trace list` shows CCreate/CRead columns
- REST `/trace` list response includes cache token counts
- Admin trace viewer shows the new columns with hit-rate display
- Unit tests cover strategy resolution and Anthropic marker injection
- PHPUnit covers ProviderTrace cache-token extraction for Anthropic, OpenAI, DeepSeek response shapes
- PHPCS / PHPStan clean
- New trace after the change shows cache_creation_input_tokens > 0 on first turn, cache_read_input_tokens > 0 on second turn
