title: feat(abilities): sd-ai-agent/list-allowed-roots
body:
> **MANDATORY before opening a PR:** satisfy the [Worker Self-Verification Protocol](https://github.com/Ultimate-Multisite/superdav-ai-agent/blob/main/AGENTS.md#worker-self-verification-protocol) in `AGENTS.md`. Run the full PHPUnit suite (`npm run test:php`, not filtered), `npm run lint:php|js|css`, `composer phpstan`, `npm run build`, and paste the verification summary block in the PR body. Filtered PHPUnit runs are NOT sufficient.

## Summary

Add a `sd-ai-agent/list-allowed-roots` ability that returns the resolved (`realpath`-normalised) list of filesystem directories where the AI is permitted to read or write. The model should be told (via the ability description) to call this before any file write so it picks a valid target path without trial-and-error.

## Why

The AI today has to guess at filesystem layout via `WP_CONTENT_DIR` or `ABSPATH`, and on hosts where `WP_CONTENT_DIR` is symlinked or mounted at an alternate path (e.g. Jurassic Ninja, some VIP setups, Bedrock) the guess is wrong and writes fail with `path_not_allowed`. Each failed write burns a tool-call round trip.

Haydi solves this with `haydi_get_allowed_roots` — see `~/Git/haydi/includes/class-filesystem-guard.php::build_allowed_roots()` for the dedup-by-resolved-path pattern.

## Files

**Create:**

- `includes/Abilities/ListAllowedRootsAbility.php` — extends `AbstractAbility`. Returns an associative array `{ label: absolute_path }` for each allowed root. Labels are human-readable (`'plugins'`, `'themes'`, `'uploads'`, `'ai-edits'`). Dedupe by resolved `realpath` so symlinked / alternate-mount duplicates collapse.
- `tests/SdAiAgent/Abilities/ListAllowedRootsAbilityTest.php`.

**Modify:**

- `includes/Bootstrap/AbilitiesHandler.php` — register the new ability.
- `includes/Tools/ToolDiscovery.php` — consider adding `sd-ai-agent/list-allowed-roots` to `DEFAULT_TIER_1`. Tier 1 is gated by token budget (`MAX_TIER_1 = 15`) — only add if you can demonstrate one of the existing tier-1 entries is lower-value. Otherwise leave it as tier-2 (discoverable via `ability-search`).

## Reference pattern

`~/Git/haydi/includes/class-filesystem-guard.php::build_allowed_roots()` — the dedup-by-resolved-path pattern:

```php
// Two different logical roots (WP_CONTENT_DIR/plugins and
// ABSPATH/wp-content/plugins) often resolve to the same physical
// directory. Dedupe on realpath() to avoid showing duplicates.
$by_real = array();
foreach ( $raw as $label => $path ) {
    $real = realpath( $path );
    if ( false !== $real && is_dir( $real ) && ! isset( $by_real[ $real ] ) ) {
        $by_real[ $real ]   = true;
        $resolved[ $label ] = $real;
    }
}
```

Reimplement the equivalent in our `ListAllowedRootsAbility`. Source: <https://github.com/Automattic/haydi/blob/trunk/includes/class-filesystem-guard.php>

Roots to expose:

- `plugins` → `WP_PLUGIN_DIR`
- `themes` → `get_theme_root()`
- `mu-plugins` → `WPMU_PLUGIN_DIR` (only if exists)
- `uploads` → `wp_upload_dir()['basedir']`
- `ai-edits` → `WP_CONTENT_DIR . '/uploads/ai-edits'` (only if exists — directory existence is the opt-in, mirroring Haydi)

Any custom roots a site has whitelisted via the `sd_ai_agent_allowed_roots` filter (add the filter if it does not exist; reuse if it does).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `sd-ai-agent/list-allowed-roots` ability registered.
- [ ] Returns associative array of label → resolved absolute path.
- [ ] Symlinked / alternate-mounted duplicates collapse to one entry.
- [ ] `ai-edits` scratchpad appears only when the directory exists.
- [ ] Categorised as read-only / idempotent in `meta.annotations`.
- [ ] Ability description tells the model to call this before any file write.
- [ ] If existing `FileAbilities` validation uses a hard-coded root list, refactor to read from the same canonical source so the ability and the validator never disagree.

## Verification

```bash
npm run verify
```

Manual:

- Run the ability via WP-CLI: `wp eval "print_r( wp_get_ability('sd-ai-agent/list-allowed-roots')->execute([]) );"`.
- Confirm the returned paths are valid `realpath`-resolved absolute paths.

## Caveats

- If our `FileAbilities` currently builds its root list inline, refactor to a shared resolver (`SdAiAgent\Core\Filesystem\AllowedRoots::resolve()`) used by both the ability and the path validator. Otherwise the model gets one answer and writes fail with another.
- Do not expose private paths (e.g. `wp-config.php` directory) — only the existing AI-writeable allowlist.

## Priority

`priority:medium` `type:feature`. Trivial implementation, measurable win in reduced failed tool calls.

title: refactor(safety): enforce wp_is_file_mod_allowed per write context
body:
> **MANDATORY before opening a PR:** satisfy the [Worker Self-Verification Protocol](https://github.com/Ultimate-Multisite/superdav-ai-agent/blob/main/AGENTS.md#worker-self-verification-protocol) in `AGENTS.md`. Run the full PHPUnit suite (`npm run test:php`, not filtered), `npm run lint:php|js|css`, `composer phpstan`, `npm run build`, and paste the verification summary block in the PR body. Filtered PHPUnit runs are NOT sufficient.

## Summary

Every mutating file ability must call `wp_is_file_mod_allowed( $context )` before doing anything, where `$context` is resolved per-path (`plugin_files`, `theme_files`, `upload_files`). This makes us honour `DISALLOW_FILE_EDIT`, `DISALLOW_FILE_MODS`, and any hosting-specific filters that restrict file modification.

## Why

Today, our `FileWriteAbility`, `FileEditAbility`, `FileDeleteAbility` gate on `current_user_can('manage_options')` plus path-traversal validation, but do not consult `wp_is_file_mod_allowed`. On managed WordPress hosts (e.g. WP Engine, Pantheon, VIP) where file modification is locked down via `DISALLOW_FILE_MODS`, our writes succeed at the WordPress level when they should be blocked — risking host-policy violations and silent breakage on deploy.

Haydi gates every mutation with a per-path-context check; see `~/Git/haydi/includes/class-filesystem-guard.php::resolve_file_mod_context()` and the `wp_is_file_mod_allowed` calls at the top of `write_file`, `delete_file`, `move_file`, `copy_file`, `delete_dir`, `restore_specific_backup`.

## Files

**Create:**

- `includes/Core/Filesystem/FileModGate.php` — single helper class with:
  - `public static function context_for_path(string $path): string` — returns `'plugin_files' | 'theme_files' | 'upload_files'` based on which root the resolved path is inside.
  - `public static function assert_allowed(string $path): true|WP_Error` — calls `wp_is_file_mod_allowed( self::context_for_path( $path ) )`, returns `WP_Error('file_mod_not_allowed', ..., ['status' => 403])` on false.
- `tests/SdAiAgent/Core/Filesystem/FileModGateTest.php`.

**Modify:**

- `includes/Abilities/FileWriteAbility.php` — call `FileModGate::assert_allowed($path)` as the first guard inside `execute_callback`, before any path-traversal validation. Return the `WP_Error` if it fails. For moves/copies, check both source and destination paths.
- `includes/Abilities/FileEditAbility.php` — same.
- `includes/Abilities/FileDeleteAbility.php` — same.
- Any other mutating filesystem ability (search for `FileAbilities::handle_*` / `WP_Filesystem` writes / `wp_delete_file`).
- `includes/PluginBuilder/PluginSandbox.php` — `layer3_activate` writes to disk indirectly via WP's plugin activation; the `plugin_files` context should also be enforced before triggering an install/upgrade.
- `includes/Abilities/UpdatePluginSandboxedAbility.php` — `plugin_files` context.

## Reference pattern

`~/Git/haydi/includes/class-filesystem-guard.php`:

- `resolve_file_mod_context( string $path ): string` (`plugin_files` / `theme_files` / `upload_files` dispatch based on `path_is_inside` of the resolved root).
- Every public mutating method starts with:

```php
if ( ! wp_is_file_mod_allowed( $this->resolve_file_mod_context( $path ) ) ) {
    return new WP_Error( 'file_mod_not_allowed', 'File modifications are not allowed on this site.', array( 'status' => 403 ) );
}
```

Source: <https://github.com/Automattic/haydi/blob/trunk/includes/class-filesystem-guard.php>

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `FileModGate::context_for_path()` returns the correct context for every path under `WP_PLUGIN_DIR`, `get_theme_root()`, and `wp_upload_dir()['basedir']`.
- [ ] `FileModGate::assert_allowed()` returns `true` when the matching `wp_is_file_mod_allowed( $context )` is true; returns a `WP_Error` with `status: 403` otherwise.
- [ ] Every mutating file ability calls `FileModGate::assert_allowed` as the first guard.
- [ ] When `define('DISALLOW_FILE_MODS', true)` is set in `wp-config.php`, all mutating abilities return `file_mod_not_allowed` and do not touch the disk.
- [ ] When `define('DISALLOW_FILE_EDIT', true)` is set but `DISALLOW_FILE_MODS` is not, `plugin-editor`-equivalent writes (in-place edits to existing files) are blocked but plugin install/activation is not.
- [ ] Path-traversal validation still runs after the file-mod gate — defence in depth.
- [ ] Pre-existing PHPUnit tests still pass.

## Verification

```bash
npm run verify
```

New tests must cover:

```bash
npm run test:php -- --filter FileModGateTest
```

- Path inside plugins → `plugin_files`.
- Path inside themes → `theme_files`.
- Path inside uploads → `upload_files`.
- Path under `ABSPATH` but not in those roots → safe default (`upload_files` per Haydi, document the choice).
- `DISALLOW_FILE_MODS` true → blocks all three contexts.
- `DISALLOW_FILE_EDIT` true alone → blocks in-place edits, permits installs.

Manual:

```bash
wp config set DISALLOW_FILE_MODS true --raw
```

Run a chat that triggers `file-write`; confirm `file_mod_not_allowed` is returned.

## Caveats

- `wp_is_file_mod_allowed` is filterable; some hosts add their own logic. Our gate inherits whatever the host filter decides — that is the correct behaviour.
- The path may not exist yet (new file write). `context_for_path` must walk up the path to the nearest existing ancestor for resolution. See Haydi's `resolve_file_mod_context` for the pattern.
- This change is mostly defensive — most sites do not set `DISALLOW_FILE_MODS`. But for those that do, our current code silently bypasses host policy, which is a real bug.

## Priority

`priority:medium` `type:feature`. Compliance/defence-in-depth.

title: feat(chat): command palette (Cmd/Ctrl+K) entry
body:
> **MANDATORY before opening a PR:** satisfy the [Worker Self-Verification Protocol](https://github.com/Ultimate-Multisite/superdav-ai-agent/blob/main/AGENTS.md#worker-self-verification-protocol) in `AGENTS.md`. Run the full PHPUnit suite (`npm run test:php`, not filtered), `npm run lint:php|js|css`, `composer phpstan`, `npm run build`, and paste the verification summary block in the PR body. Filtered PHPUnit runs are NOT sufficient.

## Summary

Register a "Interact with AI" entry in WordPress's command palette (Cmd/Ctrl+K) so the chat is launchable from anywhere in WP-Admin without navigating to the menu item.

## Why

WordPress core ships a command palette via `@wordpress/commands`. Haydi adds itself to it (see `Haydi_Plugin::enqueue_commands` in `~/Git/haydi/haydi.php`) — a 15-LOC inline script that makes the feature reachable site-wide. Discoverability win, near-zero cost, no maintenance burden.

## Files

**Modify:**

- `includes/Admin/UnifiedAdminMenu.php` — add an `admin_enqueue_scripts` handler (or extend the existing one) that:
  1. Checks `current_user_can( 'manage_options' )`.
  2. Checks `wp_script_is( 'wp-commands', 'registered' )`. If not, return — palette is not available on this admin screen.
  3. `wp_enqueue_script( 'wp-commands' )`.
  4. `wp_add_inline_script( 'wp-commands', $inline )` where `$inline` registers a command via `wp.data.dispatch( 'core/commands' ).registerCommand({ name: 'sd-ai-agent/open', label: 'Interact with AI', callback: ... })`.
- The callback should navigate to the chat page URL (`admin_url( 'admin.php?page=sd-ai-agent' )` or whichever the canonical page slug is — verify in `UnifiedAdminMenu`).

## Reference pattern

`~/Git/haydi/haydi.php::enqueue_commands()` — exact pattern. Upstream: <https://github.com/Automattic/haydi/blob/trunk/haydi.php>

Key details:

- Wrap in IIFE; guard with `typeof wp === 'undefined' || ! wp.data`.
- Wrap the `registerCommand` call in a `try { ... } catch ( _e ) {}` so admin screens without the commands store do not throw.
- Use `wp_json_encode` for the URL to safely embed it in the inline script.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] On any WP-Admin page where `wp-commands` is registered, Cmd/Ctrl+K opens the palette with "Interact with AI" as an entry.
- [ ] Selecting the entry navigates to the chat page.
- [ ] Non-`manage_options` users do not see the entry.
- [ ] No JS console errors on screens where `wp-commands` is not registered.
- [ ] Inline script is escaped via `wp_json_encode` for the URL — no XSS surface.

## Verification

```bash
npm run verify
```

Manual:

- Visit `/wp-admin/index.php`.
- Press Cmd+K (macOS) / Ctrl+K (Linux/Windows).
- Type "Interact" — entry should appear; selecting it loads the chat page.

## Caveats

- `wp-commands` is not available on every admin screen (e.g. the legacy customizer). The guard handles that.
- Do not pull in `@wordpress/commands` as a build-time dependency; rely on the runtime enqueue so we benefit from core's lazy loading.

## Priority

`priority:low` `type:feature`. Cheap polish; defer until other items land if capacity is tight.

title: audit: confirm token_get_all(TOKEN_PARSE) on every PHP write path
body:
> **MANDATORY before opening a PR:** satisfy the [Worker Self-Verification Protocol](https://github.com/Ultimate-Multisite/superdav-ai-agent/blob/main/AGENTS.md#worker-self-verification-protocol) in `AGENTS.md`. Run the full PHPUnit suite (`npm run test:php`, not filtered), `npm run lint:php|js|css`, `composer phpstan`, `npm run build`, and paste the verification summary block in the PR body. Filtered PHPUnit runs are NOT sufficient.

## Summary

Audit every file-write code path in the plugin to confirm PHP content is validated with `token_get_all( $content, TOKEN_PARSE )` **before** it touches disk. If any path is missing the lint step, add it. Produce a short audit doc enumerating all write paths and the gate each one passes through.

## Why

`FileAbilities.php` advertises a `Lint PHP content for syntax errors` helper that uses `token_get_all( $content, TOKEN_PARSE )` — the same technique Haydi uses to catch syntax errors before the file hits disk (see `~/Git/haydi/extensions/haydi-files.php` in the release zip). The audit's question is: **does every write call site actually invoke that helper, or are there bypasses?**

Risk: a write path that skips the lint can save broken PHP, which then causes a fatal on the next request and triggers the new post-mutation health check to revert. Reverting is fine — but catching the bug *before* writing is cheaper and clearer to the user.

## Files

**Audit (read-only first; the actionable output drives subsequent edits):**

Search the codebase for every place that calls `file_put_contents`, `WP_Filesystem::put_contents`, `fwrite`, `file_put_contents_atomic`, or any equivalent. For each call site, document:

- File and line
- Caller (which ability or service)
- Whether PHP content is the payload (skip CSS/JS/JSON writes)
- Whether `token_get_all` lint is called before the write
- Whether the lint failure path returns a `WP_Error` to the AI without writing

Suggested starting greps:

```bash
git ls-files | xargs rg -n 'put_contents|file_put_contents|fwrite\('
git ls-files | xargs rg -n 'token_get_all'
```

**Likely call sites to inspect:**

- `includes/Abilities/FileWriteAbility.php`
- `includes/Abilities/FileEditAbility.php`
- `includes/PluginBuilder/PluginSandbox.php` (layer 1 syntax check should cover this for the plugin-generation path)
- `includes/PluginBuilder/PluginGenerator.php`
- `includes/Abilities/ThemeBuilderAbilities.php`
- `includes/Abilities/UpdatePluginSandboxedAbility.php`

**Deliverable (this issue produces a PR with):**

- `docs/file-write-lint-audit.md` — table of every write path with the lint-gate status.
- For any path missing the lint, an Edit applying `token_get_all( $content, TOKEN_PARSE )` validation that returns `WP_Error` before writing.
- A new PHPUnit test per gap closed, asserting that invalid PHP input returns a `WP_Error` and does not write.

## Reference

`includes/Abilities/FileAbilities.php` — the canonical helper. Confirm its signature, error code, and where it lives so the audit doc references it consistently.

Pattern (paraphrased; verify the in-tree version):

```php
try {
    $tokens = token_get_all( $content, TOKEN_PARSE );
} catch ( \ParseError $e ) {
    return new \WP_Error( 'invalid_php', $e->getMessage() );
}
```

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `docs/file-write-lint-audit.md` exists, enumerates every PHP-write call site in the plugin, and notes the lint gate for each.
- [ ] At least one of the file-content-bearing abilities is confirmed lint-gated; any that are not get the gate added.
- [ ] Each gap closed has a new PHPUnit test asserting "invalid PHP input → `WP_Error`, no disk write".
- [ ] Non-PHP writes (CSS/JS/JSON/text) are explicitly noted in the audit doc as not requiring the lint.
- [ ] The audit doc is dated and credits the source review (this issue).

## Verification

```bash
npm run verify
```

For each new test:

```bash
npm run test:php -- --filter <NewTestClassName>
```

## Caveats

- `token_get_all` with `TOKEN_PARSE` requires PHP ≥ 7.0 (we are on 8.2 minimum, so this is fine).
- The catch should be `\ParseError` (extends `\Error`, not `\Exception`). A bare `catch (\Exception)` will miss it.
- Do not lint CSS/JS as PHP — the gate must be conditional on the target file extension (`.php`).
- This is an audit-first issue; if the audit shows every path is already gated, the PR is just the doc plus any test gaps. That is a valid completion state — say so in the PR body.

## Priority

`priority:medium` `type:chore`. Discovery-first work that may produce 0 or many fixes depending on what the audit finds.

title: fix(filesystem): canonicalise WP_CONTENT_DIR paths before mkdir/backup operations
body:
> **MANDATORY before opening a PR:** satisfy the [Worker Self-Verification Protocol](https://github.com/Ultimate-Multisite/superdav-ai-agent/blob/main/AGENTS.md#worker-self-verification-protocol) in `AGENTS.md`.

## Summary

Plugin generation and sandboxed plugin update fail on this local dev install because `WP_CONTENT_DIR` resolves to a path containing `../` (`/home/dave/Git/superdav-ai-agent/../wordpress/wp-content`). WordPress `wp_mkdir_p()` fails on these unnormalised paths even though the target parent is writable.

This blocks non-trivial plugin generation and active-plugin sandboxed updates in the exact shared dev layout documented in `AGENTS.md` (`../wordpress`).

## Evidence

On `main` at `5393a3f`:

```bash
wp eval 'var_dump(WP_CONTENT_DIR); var_dump(wp_mkdir_p(WP_CONTENT_DIR."/plugins/sd-e2e-counter-widget/"));'
# string containing /superdav-ai-agent/../wordpress/wp-content
# bool(false)
```

But native mkdir succeeds against the same resolved parent:

```bash
wp eval 'var_dump(is_writable(WP_CONTENT_DIR."/plugins")); var_dump(mkdir(WP_CONTENT_DIR."/plugins/sd-e2e-counter-widget-test",0777,true));'
# bool(true)
# bool(true)
```

`sd-ai-agent/generate-plugin` fails:

```text
WP_ERROR sd_ai_agent_mkdir_failed Could not create plugin directory: /home/dave/Git/superdav-ai-agent/../wordpress/wp-content/plugins/sd-e2e-counter-widget/
```

`sd-ai-agent/update-plugin-sandboxed` also fails when creating backup dirs:

```text
WP_ERROR sd_ai_agent_mkdir_failed Could not create directory: /home/dave/Git/superdav-ai-agent/../wordpress/wp-content/uploads/sd-ai-backups/sd-e2e-counter-widget-2026-05-25-201741/
```

## Expected

All filesystem paths derived from `WP_CONTENT_DIR`, plugin roots, theme roots, upload dirs, and backup dirs should be canonicalised before directory creation / sandbox staging / backup creation. A path containing `../` should not make `wp_mkdir_p()` fail when the resolved target is inside an allowed root.

## Likely files

- `includes/PluginBuilder/PluginGenerator.php`
- `includes/Abilities/UpdatePluginSandboxedAbility.php`
- `includes/PluginBuilder/PluginSandbox.php`
- `includes/Abilities/FileAbilities.php`
- any new/shared filesystem path helper from #1826/#1827

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `generate-plugin` succeeds when `WP_CONTENT_DIR` contains `../` but resolves inside the real `../wordpress/wp-content` directory.
- [ ] `update-plugin-sandboxed` backup dir creation succeeds in the same environment.
- [ ] New path helper canonicalises nearest existing ancestor + appends safe suffix for not-yet-existing child dirs.
- [ ] Path canonicalisation does not permit traversal outside allowed roots.
- [ ] PHPUnit covers `WP_CONTENT_DIR` with `../` in the path.

## Verification

```bash
npm run verify
wp eval 'wp_set_current_user(1); $r=wp_get_ability("sd-ai-agent/generate-plugin")->execute(["slug"=>"sd-e2e-path-probe","install"=>true,"description"=>"Create a tiny plugin with a shortcode."]); var_export(is_wp_error($r) ? $r->get_error_message() : $r);'
```

title: Bug: create-post mutations are missing from the AI Agent Changes log
body:
## Summary
`sd-ai-agent/create-post` successfully created a draft post during browser smoke testing, but the post creation was not recorded in the AI Agent Changes log. This leaves agent-created content without a revertable audit entry.

## Evidence
- Environment: local WordPress admin at the repo-documented dev site, plugin `Superdav AI Agent` v1.16.1 network-active.
- Browser task submitted through the AI Agent panel:
  - `Create a draft post titled 'Agent Browser Evaluation Draft 20260525' with one paragraph saying this draft was created by the Superdav AI Agent browser smoke test. Do not publish it.`
- Session evidence from `wp_sd_ai_agent_sessions`:
  - user prompt present in session `19`.
  - model called `wpab__sd-ai-agent__create-post` with args:
    - `title`: `Agent Browser Evaluation Draft 20260525`
    - `post_type`: `post`
    - `status`: `draft`
  - model reply reported `Post ID: 267`, `Status: draft`, `Type: post`.
- WordPress verification:
  - `wp post list --post_type=post --post_status=any --fields=ID,post_title,post_status --format=json` included `{"ID":267,"post_title":"Agent Browser Evaluation Draft 20260525","post_status":"draft"}`.
  - `wp post get 267 --field=post_content` returned `This draft was created by the Superdav AI Agent browser smoke test.`
- Change log verification:
  - `SELECT id, session_id, object_type, object_id, object_title, ability_name, field_name, after_value, created_at FROM wp_sd_ai_agent_changes_log WHERE object_title LIKE '%Agent Browser%' OR after_value LIKE '%Agent Browser%' ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 20;`
  - Result: no rows.
  - Latest change-log rows did record unrelated post/page/meta changes, so the table was present and functioning, but this `create-post` mutation was missing.

## Expected behaviour
Any successful `sd-ai-agent/create-post` mutation should create a Changes entry with the session ID, object type, object ID, object title, ability name, changed fields, and revertability status. A draft created by the agent should be visible in AI Agent → Changes and be revertable when safe.

## Files / patterns to inspect
- `includes/Abilities/PostAbilities.php`, especially `handle_create_post()` and batch-create paths.
- `includes/Core/ChangeLogger.php` and `includes/Models/ChangesLog.php` for post creation recording contracts.
- `includes/Bootstrap/ChangeLoggingHandler.php` for hooks that may miss direct ability-created posts.
- `includes/REST/ChangesController.php` only if the row exists but is filtered from the UI; in this repro the DB query found no row.
- Existing tests in `tests/SdAiAgent/Abilities/PostAbilitiesTest.php`; add coverage asserting `handle_create_post()` records a changes-log row.

## Suggested fix
Record create-post mutations at the same layer that performs `wp_insert_post()` or through a guaranteed post-insert hook that receives the active session/ability context. Preserve the canonical ability name `sd-ai-agent/create-post` and avoid any namespace/slug renames.

## Verification
- PHP unit coverage for `PostAbilities::handle_create_post()` creating a draft and writing a `changes_log` row.
- Browser smoke: create a draft via AI Agent chat, then confirm AI Agent → Changes shows the new post with ability `sd-ai-agent/create-post` and a valid revert action.
- Required local gates before PR: `npm run verify`.

title: Security: WooCommerce order tools persist customer PII in AI session messages
body:
## Summary
The WooCommerce order-list ability returns sensitive customer order fields into AI session logs. During a read-only WooCommerce audit, `woocommerce/orders-list` returned full billing/shipping structures including customer contact/address fields. Those raw tool responses are stored in `wp_sd_ai_agent_sessions.messages`.

Do not include real customer values in this issue or any follow-up comments.

- Browser prompt marker: `Complex capability test C 20260526 WooCommerce read-only`.

Order-list/order-get tool responses used by the AI Agent should default to redacted/minimized fields unless the user explicitly asks for customer contact details and has the required capability. Stored session messages should not persist unnecessary PII.

Recommended safe defaults:
- Keep order ID, status, total, currency, dates, product line summary, customer ID, and high-level attribution as needed.
- Redact or omit email, phone, postal address, IP address, user-agent, transaction IDs, and order keys from AI-visible/storeable responses unless explicitly requested.
- Apply the same scrubber before logging/storing tool responses.

## Files / patterns to inspect
- `includes/Bootstrap/WooCommerceIntegrationHandler.php`
- WooCommerce ability registration/response filtering around `woocommerce/orders-list` and `woocommerce/orders-get`.
- `includes/Core/ToolResultTruncator.php` and any existing secret/PII scrubbing layer.
- Session persistence in `includes/Core/AgentLoop.php` / session models.

## Verification

- Confirm `wp_sd_ai_agent_sessions.messages` for `woocommerce/orders-list` contains no email, phone, postal address, IP address, user-agent, transaction ID, or order key values.

title: fix(agent-loop): raw <tool_call> text leak when model invokes ability outside Tier-1 manifest
body:
## What

When the model is asked to perform an action that requires an ability outside the Tier-1 manifest, it sometimes emits the tool invocation as a raw text string like `<tool_call>wpab__sd-ai-agent__get-themes</tool_call>` inside the assistant reply, instead of going through the Tier-2 `ability-search` → `ability-call` flow (or using the JSON `tool_calls` channel).

The result is shown verbatim to the end user, the requested action does not run, and the run terminates after 1 iteration with a misleadingly "successful" reply.

## Evidence

Sovereign site `david.sdaiagent.com` (blog 84) on multi-tenancy stack, provider `ultimate-ai-connector-compatible-endpoints` (the OpenAI-compatible connector plugin v2.1.2), model `hf:zai-org/GLM-5.1` via `https://api.synthetic.new/openai/v1`. 168 abilities registered (3 `core/*`, 13 `multisite-ultimate/*`, 2 `sd-ai-agent-custom/*`, 4 `sd-ai-agent-js/*`, 116 `sd-ai-agent/*`).

Test prompt (no Tier-2 guidance):

> "List the themes installed on this site. Then activate the 'twentytwentyfour' theme if it is installed."

Result captured via direct `AgentLoop->run()` call:

```
OK 1.88s iterations=1 tool_calls=0
REPLY:
<tool_call>wpab__sd-ai-agent__get-themes</tool_call>
```

No actual tool call was issued — `tool_calls=0`. The string was returned to the user, no theme was listed, no theme was activated, the loop exited after 1 iteration.

When the same intent is reprompted with explicit guidance:

> "Use the ability-search tool to find a theme-related ability, then use ability-call to invoke it..."

…the agent works correctly (4 iterations, ability-search → ability-call, returns the active theme name with no leaked XML).

This is reproducible with GLM-5.1. Likely affects other models trained primarily on Anthropic-style XML tool-call output. The model knows about a tool concept (it constructs `wpab__sd-ai-agent__get-themes`, the correct prefix scheme), but rather than calling it through `ability-call`, it serializes the call into the assistant content channel.

## Where

- `includes/Core/AgentLoop.php` — likely needs an interceptor on assistant `content` text that matches `<tool_call>([^<]+)</tool_call>` and routes to `ability-call` (or back to the model with a corrective system message). `resolve_abilities()` at line 1660 controls what the model sees as direct tools.
- System/Tier-1 prompt that lists the Tier-2 manifest — needs an explicit instruction that **non-Tier-1 abilities must be invoked via `sd-ai-agent/ability-call`** and **must never be emitted as text**.

## How

Two complementary fixes, either is enough alone but both together is more robust:

**A. Defensive interceptor in `AgentLoop` (server-side)**

After each model response, before showing `reply` to the user:

1. Scan the assistant text for `<tool_call>([^\s<>]+)</tool_call>` (and any near-variants the model produces — e.g. `<tool>NAME</tool>`, `<function_call name="NAME"/>`).
2. If found and the captured name matches a known ability in the manifest, synthesise a `tool_calls` entry with `name="sd-ai-agent/ability-call"` and `arguments={"ability": "<resolved-name>"}` and re-enter the loop instead of returning the text to the user.
3. If found but the name is unknown, return a corrective tool-use error to the model ("Tool 'X' is not invokable as text; use `sd-ai-agent/ability-call` with the ability name as an argument") and re-enter the loop.

**B. Strengthen the Tier-2 catalog system prompt**

Where the Tier-2 manifest is rendered into the system prompt, add a concrete example: "To invoke any ability listed in the catalog below, you MUST call `sd-ai-agent/ability-call` with `{ability: "<name>", arguments: {...}}`. Never write the ability name as text in your reply."

## Acceptance criteria

1. Without any explicit Tier-2 guidance in the user prompt, the test prompt "List the themes installed on this site" results in either a working tool-call chain (search → call) or a corrective re-prompt — never raw `<tool_call>...</tool_call>` text in the user-visible reply.
2. Test covering the interceptor: add a unit test that feeds a mock model response containing `<tool_call>NAME</tool_call>` and asserts the loop intercepts it instead of returning it as content.
3. Existing tests still pass (`npm run verify` — lint + phpstan + test:php + build).
4. Manual repro on a real provider (GLM-5.1, Mistral, or any model trained mostly on XML tool calling) confirms the fix.

## Verification commands

```bash
npm run verify
```

Manual repro (requires a configured sovereign site + GLM-5.1-class model):

```bash
wp --url=<sovereign-site> eval '
$loop = new \SdAiAgent\Core\AgentLoop("List the themes installed on this site.", [], [], ["max_iterations" => 5]);
$out = $loop->run();
echo "tool_calls=".count($out["tool_calls"] ?? []).PHP_EOL;
echo "reply=".$out["reply"].PHP_EOL;
'
```

Expected after fix: `reply` contains a real theme list or "I will use ability-search…" never the literal substring `<tool_call>`.

## Related observations (separate issues)

- Tool-call observability: `?` placeholder entries are counted in `tool_calls` length but represent assistant channel messages, not actual function calls. Tracked separately.
- Duplicate consecutive `ability-search` and `ability-call` invocations from GLM-5.1 (model emits the same call twice in a row). Tracked separately.

title: observability: AgentLoop tool_calls includes empty channel entries and duplicate consecutive search/call invocations
body:
## What

Two related observability/efficiency issues surfaced while exercising real-provider runs on a sovereign tenant:

1. **`tool_calls` count includes channel/placeholder entries with empty names**, inflating the metric and making run logs hard to interpret.
2. **Model often emits the same `ability-search` (and `ability-call`) request twice consecutively**, wasting tokens and provider time.

Both observed with `hf:zai-org/GLM-5.1` via `ai-provider-for-any-openai-compatible` v2.1.2 (provider id `ultimate-ai-connector-compatible-endpoints`).

## Evidence

### (1) Placeholder `?` entries in `tool_calls`

From a real run of the agent test harness:

```
=== activate ollie theme ===
OK 14.29s iter=4 tc=10
  [1] ?
  [2] ?
  [3] wpab__sd-ai-agent__ability-search
  [4] wpab__sd-ai-agent__ability-search
  [5] ?
  [6] wpab__sd-ai-agent__ability-call
  [7] wpab__sd-ai-agent__ability-call
  [8] ?
  [9] wpab__sd-ai-agent__get-themes
  [10] wpab__sd-ai-agent__get-themes
```

10 entries, but only 4 are real abilities — 6 entries have `?` (no `name` and no `function.name`). The reporter code is:

```php
$name = $tc["name"] ?? $tc["function"]["name"] ?? "?";
```

so the placeholder fallback fires when neither key is present. These appear to be assistant-channel/thinking entries that were folded into `tool_calls` rather than into `messages` or a `thoughts` channel. The user-visible side effect: dashboards and run logs report inflated tool-call counts (e.g., 30 instead of ~15 for the mu-plugin test), which obscures both billing math and rate-limiting decisions.

### (2) Duplicate consecutive search/call invocations

In the same run above: `ability-search` is called at positions 3+4 (identical), and `ability-call` at 6+7 (identical), then `get-themes` at 9+10 (identical). In the mu-plugin creation test (40s, 9 iters), this pattern repeated multiple times within the 30 reported tool_calls.

If these are intentional parallel calls executed concurrently, that should be visible in the schema (e.g. a `parallel_id`). If they are accidental duplicates from the model hedging, the loop should dedupe per-iteration before dispatch.

Test that produced both observations:

```bash
wp --url=<sovereign-site> eval '
$loop = new \SdAiAgent\Core\AgentLoop(
  "Activate the WordPress theme with the slug ollie. Use ability-search if needed. Then confirm which theme is active.",
  [], [], ["max_iterations" => 10]
);
$out = $loop->run();
echo "iter=".$out["iterations_used"]." tc=".count($out["tool_calls"]).PHP_EOL;
foreach ($out["tool_calls"] as $i => $tc) {
  echo " [".($i+1)."] ".($tc["name"] ?? $tc["function"]["name"] ?? "?").PHP_EOL;
}
'
```

## Where

- `includes/Core/AgentLoop.php` — how `tool_calls` is populated and what shape entries take. Need to split assistant-channel/thinking entries out of the returned `tool_calls` array (or rename the channel/placeholder entries to a clear field).
- `includes/REST/SessionController.php:367-411` (the `/run` endpoint) — `tool_calls` is exposed to clients here, so the schema change affects the chat UI consumer as well.
- `includes/Core/AgentLoop.php` dedupe — the loop dispatcher should consider deduping identical `name+arguments` calls within a single iteration when the provider does not flag them as parallel.

## How

**(1) Separate channels in the return shape:**

```
return [
  "reply" => ...,
  "history" => ...,
  "tool_calls" => [ /* only real ability invocations with name + arguments */ ],
  "messages" => [ /* assistant channel/thinking/plan entries */ ], // new
  "token_usage" => ...,
  "iterations_used" => ...,
  "model_id" => ...,
];
```

Or keep one array but tag each entry with `"kind" => "tool_call"|"channel"|"plan"` so consumers can filter.

**(2) Per-iteration dedupe:**

Before dispatching a batch of `tool_calls` from a single model response, hash each entry by `(name, canonical_json(arguments))` and skip duplicates. Log a `[Superdav AI Agent] event=tool_call_deduplicated count=N` line so this is visible in monitoring.

If parallel intent is legitimate, the model/provider needs an explicit signal — fail safe to "dedupe" otherwise.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `AgentLoop->run()` return value contains only real ability invocations in `tool_calls` (every entry has a non-empty `name` resolving to a known ability). Test prompt for theme activation reports `tool_calls` count between 2 and 4 (search + call), not 10.
2. Channel/plan entries are exposed under a separate field (or tagged with a `kind`), but never as nameless entries inside `tool_calls`.
3. Identical consecutive calls (same name + same arguments) within a single model response are deduplicated before dispatch unless explicitly flagged as parallel by the provider.
4. New unit tests cover both behaviours (channel separation, dedupe).
5. `npm run verify` passes.

## Verification commands

```bash
npm run verify

# Repro on real provider
wp --url=<sovereign-site> eval '
$loop = new \SdAiAgent\Core\AgentLoop(
  "Activate the WordPress theme with the slug ollie. Use ability-search if needed. Then confirm.",
  [], [], ["max_iterations" => 10]
);
$out = $loop->run();
echo "tool_calls=".count($out["tool_calls"]).PHP_EOL;
echo "channel=".count($out["messages"] ?? []).PHP_EOL; // expected after fix
'
```

## Out of scope

- The raw `<tool_call>NAME</tool_call>` text leak is a separate functional bug (already filed as a sibling issue).

title: ci: validate bin/build.sh flags ↔ defines ↔ stripped_paths ↔ .distignore-wporg are in sync
body:
## Problem

`bin/build.sh --target=wporg` rewrites the bundled main plugin file
to force a list of `SD_AI_AGENT_FEATURE_*` constants to `false` so
they cannot be re-enabled in the WordPress.org distribution. The
list of constants lives in a `flags` bash array near the top of the
file (currently `RUN_PHP`, `SCAFFOLD_BLOCK_THEME`, `PLUGIN_BUILDER`,
and — as of PR #1923 — `WP_REST_DISPATCHER` and `WP_CLI_DISPATCHER`).

A companion `stripped_paths` array lists ability source files that
must be physically removed from the zip and verified after rsync.
Each `flags` entry generally pairs with a `stripped_paths` entry.

There is currently no CI check that:

1. Every constant in the `flags` array is actually `defined()` in
   the unmodified `superdav-ai-agent.php` (so a typo silently
   becomes a no-op rewrite).
2. Every `stripped_paths` entry maps to a real file in the unmodified
   source tree (so a renamed/moved file silently passes
   "verified stripped").
3. Every ability file in `.distignore-wporg` whose source defines a
   `SD_AI_AGENT_FEATURE_*` gate also appears in the `flags` array
   (defence-in-depth coupling).

The flags array's comment also drifted out of sync with the array
itself between PRs (the comment mentioned `run-php` before
`RUN_PHP` was added to the array). A simple narrative-comment
ratchet would catch this.

## Acceptance criteria

A new CI job (or extension of `Verify canonical identifiers`) that
fails when any of the following are true:

- A `flags` entry's `SD_AI_AGENT_FEATURE_<name>` is not present in
  the unmodified `superdav-ai-agent.php` as a `define()` or
  `defined()` line.
- A `stripped_paths` entry does not correspond to an existing file
  in the source tree.
- The `flags` array narrative comment header does not list every
  constant in the array (case-insensitive substring match is fine).

## Files to inspect

- `bin/build.sh` — the `flags` and `stripped_paths` arrays
  (currently around the `wporg_strip_files` section).
- `.github/workflows/canonical-naming-guard.yml` — extension target
  if folding into the existing canonical-naming guard.
- `superdav-ai-agent.php` — source of truth for which feature
  constants exist.
- `.distignore-wporg` — cross-reference list for stripped paths.

## Verification

```bash
# Negative test 1: remove an entry from superdav-ai-agent.php's
#                  defines and confirm the new check fails the build.
# Negative test 2: add a typo to flags=("BOGUS") and confirm fail.
# Negative test 3: add a non-existent path to stripped_paths and
#                  confirm fail.
# Positive test:   run on main with the new check enabled and
#                  confirm pass.
bash bin/build.sh --target=wporg
```

## Reference pattern

PR #1922 (run-php) and PR #1923 (wp-rest + wp-cli) both add a
`flags` entry, a `stripped_paths` entry, a `.distignore-wporg`
entry, and a runtime `Features::is_enabled()` gate as a four-piece
set. The CI check should enforce that whenever any one of the four
pieces is added, the others are present too — at minimum that the
`flags` ↔ `defined()` ↔ `stripped_paths` ↔ `.distignore-wporg`
quadrilateral is internally consistent.

## Priority

`priority::medium` — not user-visible, but every future "exclude
this dispatcher from wp.org" PR will silently regress without this
check. The cost of getting it wrong is high (a stripped flag
silently shipping enabled).

## Origin

Discovered while preparing PR #1923 (`strip-wp-rest-cli-from-wporg`).
The flags-array narrative comment on main referenced `run-php`
before `RUN_PHP` was actually in the array, indicating the
historical add-RUN_PHP PR drifted comment from array. Filed as
follow-up rather than expanding PR #1923 scope.

title: docs: carve out wp-rest/* and wp-cli/* as deliberate non-canonical ability namespaces in AGENTS.md
body:
## Problem

`AGENTS.md` documents the canonical ability namespace as
`sd-ai-agent/` (e.g. `sd-ai-agent/memory-save`,
`sd-ai-agent/skill-load`). However, the abilities registered by
`includes/Abilities/WpRestAbilities.php` and
`includes/Abilities/WpCliAbilities.php` deliberately use the
non-canonical namespaces `wp-rest/` and `wp-cli/`:

- `wp-rest/discover`
- `wp-rest/inspect`
- `wp-rest/execute`
- `wp-cli/execute`

This is intentional — the namespace mirrors the underlying system
(WordPress REST API and `wp` CLI binary respectively), and these
abilities are generic dispatchers rather than plugin-specific
features. Renaming them to `sd-ai-agent/wp-rest-*` would be a
breaking change for every consumer that has already pinned these
ability IDs, and would also be misleading: the abilities dispatch
into WordPress core / WP-CLI core, not into superdav-ai-agent code.

The canonical-naming rules in `AGENTS.md` are protective ("never
rename `sd-ai-agent` → `superdav-ai-agent`") rather than
prescriptive ("every ability must start `sd-ai-agent/`"), but the
absence of any explicit carve-out for these two namespaces means a
future worker could file a misguided "canonicalise ability
namespaces" PR — exactly the failure mode the canonical-naming
section is meant to prevent.

## Acceptance criteria

A short, durable carve-out in `AGENTS.md` under the canonical
naming section that:

- Names `wp-rest/*` and `wp-cli/*` as the only two ability
  namespaces deliberately outside `sd-ai-agent/`.
- States the reason (mirror the underlying system; generic
  dispatcher; breaking change to rename; misleading prefix).
- Forbids renaming-to-canonical PRs for these two namespaces, in
  the same tone as the existing "do not rename" rules.
- References PRs #1922 and #1923 as the place where the dual-gate
  hardening was applied without canonicalising the namespace.

No code changes; this is a docs-only insight-triage update per the
"Contributor Insight Triage" section of `AGENTS.md`.

## Files to inspect

- `AGENTS.md` — root file, under the "CANONICAL NAMING - DO NOT
  CHANGE" → "Rules for Agents" block. Add a new rule entry (call
  it rule 7 or append to rule 1) covering `wp-rest/` and `wp-cli/`.

## Verification

```bash
rg -n "wp-rest|wp-cli" AGENTS.md
# Should show the new carve-out with the deliberate-exception
# rationale and the PR #1922/#1923 references.
```

## Reference pattern

Existing rule entries 1–6 in the same section follow the format
"NEVER do X" + "the reason X is wrong" + "examples of past
mistakes (do NOT repeat): PR #NNN". The new entry should follow
the same format for consistency.

## Priority

`priority::low` — docs-only insight triage, no immediate user
impact, but prevents a future misguided rename PR from burning
review cycles.

## Origin

Discovered while preparing PR #1923. The wp-rest/wp-cli abilities
were explicitly called out as "out of scope" of PR #1922's
`CORE_CAP_MAP` chokepoint precisely because their non-canonical
namespace prevented inclusion. The maintainer note that worker
discovery should produce durable guidance applies here.

title: PHPUnit suite: non-deterministic test-isolation flakes in InsertPattern/PostAbilities/RevertToRevision/RestController suites
body:
## Summary

The full `npm run test:php` suite produces a non-deterministic set of failures in three Ability test families that pass cleanly when run in isolation. Failure set varies across runs while the totals stay roughly constant (5–10 failures, 2–5 errors). Classic test-isolation / state-leak flake — earlier tests mutate shared DB state (custom-tools seed dup-key warnings, registered block patterns, post revisions, memory rows) that the suspect tests then read.

## Reproduction

```bash
git checkout main
composer install
npm ci
npm run test:php   # observe failure set A
npm run test:php   # observe failure set B (different)
```

Run any single failing suite in isolation:

```bash
npm run test:php -- --filter='InsertPatternTest|PostAbilitiesTest|RevertToRevisionTest|BlockAbilitiesTest'
```

This passes 99/99 every time.

## Evidence — three full-suite runs on commit `ebcf1e7` (origin/main HEAD as of 2026-05-30)

Run 1 (working tree at ebcf1e7, no t276 changes applied):
```
1) InsertPatternTest::test_invalid_anchor_returns_error
2) InsertPatternTest::test_registered_pattern_before_top_level
3) InsertPatternTest::test_refs_assigned_to_inserted_blocks
4) PostAbilitiesTest::test_handle_list_posts_legacy_status_field_backward_compat
5) RevertToRevisionTest::test_new_revision_differs_from_source_revision
Plus 2 errors in BlockAbilitiesTest::test_handle_get_page_blocks_flat_mode_path_correctness
and PostAbilitiesTest::test_handle_get_post_type_mismatch.
Tests: 3508, Assertions: 14427, Errors: 2, Failures: 5, Skipped: 114, Incomplete: 4.
```

Run 2 (t276 branch, full suite):
```
1) InsertPatternTest::test_missing_pattern_returns_error
2) InsertPatternTest::test_invalid_anchor_returns_error
3) InsertPatternTest::test_unknown_pattern_returns_error_with_suggestions
4) InsertPatternTest::test_dry_run_does_not_persist
5) PostAbilitiesTest::test_handle_create_post_default_status_is_draft
6) PostAbilitiesTest::test_handle_list_posts_legacy_status_field_backward_compat
7) RevertToRevisionTest::test_zero_expected_current_revision_id_produces_stale_revision
8) RestControllerTest::test_update_memory
9) RestControllerTest::test_delete_memory
10) RestControllerTest::test_update_memory_not_found
Tests: 3508, Assertions: 14442, Failures: 10, Skipped: 114, Incomplete: 4.
```

Run 3 (t276 branch, full suite, earlier in same session):
```
1) InsertPatternTest::test_unknown_pattern_returns_error_with_suggestions
2) InsertPatternTest::test_registered_pattern_after_top_level
3) InsertPatternTest::test_multi_block_pattern_inserts_all
4) PostAbilitiesTest::test_handle_list_posts_meta_query_exists
5) PostAbilitiesTest::test_handle_list_posts_legacy_status_field_backward_compat
6) RevertToRevisionTest::test_zero_expected_current_revision_id_produces_stale_revision
Tests: 3508, Assertions: 14446, Failures: 6, Skipped: 114, Incomplete: 4.
```

Only `PostAbilitiesTest::test_handle_list_posts_legacy_status_field_backward_compat` fails in every run; everything else rotates.

## Root cause hypotheses (in order of suspicion)

1. **`CustomTools::seed_examples` is not idempotent under test reinit.** Every full-suite run emits dup-key `wp_die` warnings for `weather-api`, `zapier-webhook`, `clear-object-cache`, `maintenance-mode`, `site-health-check`. The dup-key INSERTs do not crash but they leave the test DB in an unknown state and may consume the auto-increment range that other tests assert against. Fix: `CustomTools::seed_examples` should use `INSERT IGNORE` or `ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE`, or `create()` should check existence first.
2. **Block-pattern registration is process-global, not per-test.** `register_block_pattern()` writes to `WP_Block_Patterns_Registry`, which persists across tests within the same PHP process. `InsertPatternTest` registers test patterns and other suites may register patterns with overlapping names that win in the registry.
3. **Post revisions are not cleaned up between tests.** `RevertToRevisionTest::test_*_revision_id_produces_stale_revision` reads revision counts that drift when earlier tests in the run created posts with revisions.
4. **`RestControllerTest::test_*_memory` uses fixed memory IDs that may collide with memories left over from earlier suite phases.**

## Suggested fixes (worker-ready, in priority order)

1. **`includes/Tools/CustomTools.php` — `seed_examples()` and `create()`**: switch the seed-row INSERT path to skip duplicates silently. Verify with `npm run test:php` — dup-key warnings must disappear from the output. File: `includes/Tools/CustomTools.php`, search for `INSERT INTO `. Reference pattern: `wpdb->query( "INSERT IGNORE INTO ..." )` or pre-check via `$wpdb->get_var( "SELECT slug FROM ... WHERE slug = %s" )`.
2. **`tests/SdAiAgent/Abilities/InsertPatternTest.php` setUp/tearDown**: ensure `WP_Block_Patterns_Registry::get_instance()->unregister_all()` (or per-pattern unregister) runs in `setUp()` and `tearDown()` so every test starts from a known empty registry. Verify with five back-to-back `npm run test:php -- --filter='InsertPatternTest'` runs against the full suite (use a wrapper that runs the full suite five times and reports any failing-test variance).
3. **`tests/SdAiAgent/Abilities/RevertToRevisionTest.php`**: have each test factory-create its own post + revisions inside `setUp()` and `wp_delete_post( ..., true )` in `tearDown()` rather than relying on auto-increment ranges. Verify same as above.
4. **`tests/SdAiAgent/REST/RestControllerTest.php` memory tests**: capture the memory ID returned from the create call and use it in the subsequent update/delete instead of a hard-coded ID.

## Verification

```bash
# After fixes, all of these must succeed five times in a row without failures:
for i in 1 2 3 4 5; do npm run test:php 2>&1 | grep -E "^Tests:|^OK \("; done
```

The summary line must read `OK (3508 tests, ...)` or `Tests: 3508, ..., Failures: 0, Errors: 0` (Skipped > 0 acceptable) for every iteration.

## Cross-references

- Surfaced during t276 (unify Setup Assistant + Theme Builder onboarding agent) PR self-verification.
- Same `PostAbilitiesTest::test_handle_list_posts_legacy_status_field_backward_compat` failure has been the only deterministic flake — likely the simplest first target.
- The five dup-key warnings (`weather-api`, `zapier-webhook`, `clear-object-cache`, `maintenance-mode`, `site-health-check`) have been visible in every test-suite log going back at least to before ebcf1e7 — they have been treated as noise but they are the most likely upstream cause.

## Scope

Pure test-infrastructure fixes — no behavior change to production code unless `CustomTools::seed_examples` needs the dedup guard (which is a production-side fix that also benefits real installs that re-run activation).

## Labels

`type:bug`, `area:tests`, `priority:medium`, `origin:interactive`

title: Frontend live-preview pipeline (parent)
body:
## Parent task: Frontend live-preview pipeline

Goal: make the frontend floating widget (`Settings → General → Show on
public-facing pages`) **default-on** with a "good UX" — when the AI agent
updates content via abilities, the visible page reflects those changes
without a manual reload.

Today the toggle ships but is off by default, and even when enabled the
user has to refresh to see anything the agent changed. This parent task
tracks the four phases needed to close that gap.

## Phases

| Phase | Status | Issue | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 (spike) | In review | PR #1946 | Producer side of a reflection bus — one ability (`update-post`) emits `affected`; JS bus + emitter + console consumer; no DOM refresh yet |
| 2a | Available | #1948 | Extend `affected` to remaining content-mutating abilities |
| 2b | Available | #1949 | First reflector — current-post DOM morph via `morphdom` |
| 2c | Available | #1950 | Reflector — global styles re-fetch |
| 2d | Available | #1951 | Reflector — navigation menus |
| 2e | Available | #1952 | Fallback toast for tools without a dedicated reflector |
| 3  | Available | #1953 | Frontend widget hardening — cap-gate, cache headers, perf budget |

## Constraints (apply to every phase)

- Cap-gate stays at `manage_options`. Widening to editors is a separate
  security review, not in scope here.
- No new REST namespaces. Reflectors fetch existing public URLs and
  inspect existing `core/*` endpoints only.
- Bundle budget: each reflector lands in the `floating-widget` chunk,
  not the always-loaded admin bundle. Soft target: total reflector code
  + `morphdom` under 10 KB minified after the existing
  `webpackPrefetch: true` chunk.
- Cache busting: public frontends often sit behind page caches
  (WP Super Cache, Cloudflare). Reflectors that re-fetch a URL must
  append a fresh `_=<timestamp>` query and treat cache misses as the
  expected case.
- Listener errors must never abort the chat loop. The bus already
  catches and `console.error`s; reflectors must keep their own guards
  too (try/catch around the morph).

## Reference pattern

`src/store/reflection-bus.js` + `src/store/reflection-emitter.js` (shipped
in PR #1946) are the *only* coupling point between the chat poll loop
and the reflector layer. New reflectors:

1. Import `bus from 'src/store/reflection-bus'`.
2. Subscribe with `bus.on((event) => {…})` and inspect `event.affected.kind`.
3. Return early if the reflector doesn't handle that kind.
4. Otherwise perform the DOM refresh strategy described in the
   per-phase issue.

## Verification (parent)

The parent is "done" only when:

- All child issues are closed.
- `npm run verify` is green on `main`.
- Manual smoke test on the dev wp-env confirms: from an admin viewing
  any public post, asking the agent to change the title/content updates
  the visible DOM within ~1s of the model returning, with no manual
  reload.
- `'show_on_frontend' => true` is the shipped default in
  `Settings::defaults()`.

## DO NOT close this issue when the spike PR merges

PR #1946 references this parent with `For #<this issue>` so auto-merge
will not close it. Close it explicitly only after Phase 3 ships.

title: Phase 2a: Extend affected producer to all content-mutating abilities
body:
## Phase 2a — Extend `affected` producer to all content-mutating abilities

For #1947 — parent: Frontend live-preview pipeline. Builds on PR #1946.

## Goal

Every server-side ability that mutates user-visible site content must
return an `affected` descriptor with the same shape PR #1946 introduced
for `update-post`. This is purely additive — no caller inspects this
field today; reflectors (Phase 2b-d) will.

## Reference shape

```php
'affected' => [
    'kind'      => 'post' | 'menu' | 'global_styles' | 'media' | 'term',
    'post_id'   => int,     // when kind = post|media
    'post_type' => string,  // when kind = post
    'term_id'   => int,     // when kind = term
    'taxonomy'  => string,  // when kind = term
    'menu_id'   => int,     // when kind = menu
    'url'       => string,  // public permalink/URL of affected entity
    'fields'    => string[],// names of mutated fields
],
```

## Files to modify

| Ability file | Methods to extend | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `includes/Abilities/PostAbilities.php` | `handle_create_post`, `handle_append_post_content`, `handle_delete_post`, `handle_batch_create_posts`, `handle_set_featured_image` | `update-post` already done in PR #1946 — use `build_affected_payload()` as the reference |
| `includes/Abilities/ContentAbilities.php` | `handle_update_content` (and any other content-mutating handlers in this file) | inspect first; this file may delegate to `PostAbilities` |
| `includes/Abilities/MenuAbilities.php` | every handler that calls `wp_update_nav_menu_item` / `wp_create_nav_menu` / `wp_delete_nav_menu` | `kind = 'menu'`; `url` = home URL (menus appear site-wide) |
| `includes/Abilities/GlobalStylesAbilities.php` | every handler that writes to `wp_global_styles` posts or `customize_changeset` | `kind = 'global_styles'`; `url` = home URL |
| `includes/Abilities/MediaAbilities.php` | `handle_upload_media`, `handle_edit_image`, any attachment-meta writes | `kind = 'media'`; `url` = attachment URL |
| `includes/Abilities/TaxonomyAbilities.php` | `wp_insert_term` / `wp_update_term` / `wp_delete_term` callers | `kind = 'term'`; `url` = term link |

Use `git grep -nE "wp_update_post|wp_insert_post|wp_delete_post|wp_update_nav_menu_item|wp_insert_term|wp_update_term"` in `includes/Abilities/` to confirm the full set before starting; the table above is the floor, not the ceiling.

## Reference pattern

`PostAbilities::build_affected_payload()` (added in PR #1946, see
`includes/Abilities/PostAbilities.php` after #1946 merges) is the
template. Keep each ability's helper private to its own class — do NOT
extract a shared `AbstractAbility::build_affected_payload()` until at
least three abilities have shipped their own (premature abstraction
risk; the per-kind shape differs).

Append the new `'affected' => [...]` key at the END of each existing
return array. Never restructure the surrounding response — backward
compatibility for everything else is non-negotiable.

## Tests required

For each modified handler, add at least one test mirroring
`PostAbilitiesTest::test_handle_update_post_returns_affected_payload`:

- Calls the handler with a known input.
- Asserts the response contains `affected`.
- Asserts `affected.kind` is correct.
- Asserts `affected.url` is non-empty.
- Asserts `affected.fields` contains at least one expected field name.

Place tests next to existing tests for the same ability
(`tests/SdAiAgent/Abilities/*.php`). Do NOT create new test files for
this — extend the existing ones.

## Also update the `output_schema` of each ability

Mirror the schema addition PR #1946 made to the `update-post` ability
registration. Without this, the WordPress AI Client SDK / MCP exposure
will not advertise the field.

## Verification

```bash
npm run lint:php
composer phpstan
npm run test:php
```

Final PHPUnit summary MUST read `Errors: 0, Failures: 0`. Capture the
summary in the PR body under `## Worker self-verification`.

Quick smoke after build:

```bash
rg -nE "'affected'\s*=>" includes/Abilities/
```

Should list every modified ability file plus `PostAbilities.php` (from
PR #1946).

## Out of scope (do NOT do)

- Do NOT add any client-side reflectors. That is Phase 2b/c/d.
- Do NOT flip `show_on_frontend` default.
- Do NOT touch `AgentLoop` or the REST job-status response. The
  `affected` field rides through automatically as part of the existing
  `tool_call_log[].response` shape.
- Do NOT rename `sd-ai-agent/` ability namespaces.

## Estimated effort

4-6h. About 30 minutes per ability handler, plus tests, plus a final
full-suite PHPUnit run.

Phase 2d: Reflector for navigation menus
body:
## Phase 2d — Reflector: navigation menus

For #1947 — parent: Frontend live-preview pipeline. Builds on Phase 2a + 2b.

## Goal

When the agent updates a navigation menu (block-theme `core/navigation`
block or classic-theme `wp_nav_menu` widget), the visible nav updates
within ~1s without a full reload.

## Prerequisite

- Phase 2a `affected` producer ships for `MenuAbilities` with
  `kind = 'menu'` and `url = home_url()`.
- Phase 2b reflector dispatcher is in place.

## Files to create

- `src/floating-widget/reflectors/menu.js`
- `src/floating-widget/reflectors/__tests__/menu.test.js`

## Files to modify

- `src/floating-widget/reflectors/index.js` — add `case 'menu':`.

## Strategy

Block themes render navigation as `<nav class="wp-block-navigation">`
elements. Classic themes render as `<ul class="menu">` inside a wrapper
hooked to `wp_nav_menu_args`. Both can appear multiple times on one page
(header, footer, mobile). We morph every matching element.

The reflector reuses the `morphdom` helper added in Phase 2b — DO NOT
duplicate it. Import from `./dom-morph`.

## Reference pattern

```js
// src/floating-widget/reflectors/menu.js — pseudocode
import { morphTargetFromFresh, fetchFreshPage } from './dom-morph';

const MENU_SELECTORS = [
    'nav.wp-block-navigation',
    '.wp-block-navigation',
    '.menu',
    '.nav-menu',
    'ul.wp-block-navigation__container',
];

export async function reflectMenu( event ) {
    try {
        const fresh = await fetchFreshPage( window.location.href );
        for ( const selector of MENU_SELECTORS ) {
            const currents = document.querySelectorAll( selector );
            const freshes = fresh.querySelectorAll( selector );
            // Morph in document order; assumes themes render menus in
            // the same order across requests.
            const pairs = Math.min( currents.length, freshes.length );
            for ( let i = 0; i < pairs; i++ ) {
                morphTargetByElement( currents[ i ], freshes[ i ] );
            }
        }
    } catch ( err ) {
        console.warn( '[sd-ai-agent] menu reflector failed', err );
    }
}
```

Note: `fetchFreshPage` and a new `morphTargetByElement` are exported
from `./dom-morph`. The Phase 2b PR added `morphTargetFromFresh(doc,
freshDoc, selector)`; this issue asks the Phase 2b author to also
expose a lower-level `morphTargetByElement(currentEl, freshEl)` so this
phase can reuse it. If Phase 2b shipped without that export, add it as
the first commit of this PR.

## Tests

`menu.test.js` (jsdom):

- Fixture: document with two `<nav class="wp-block-navigation">`
  elements (header + footer), each with three menu items.
- Mock `fetch` to return fresh HTML where both nav elements have four
  items.
- Call `reflectMenu({ affected: { kind: 'menu', url: '/' } })`.
- Assert: both `<nav>` elements now have four items, in the right
  order.

Edge cases:

- Fresh page has fewer nav elements than current → only morph the pairs
  that exist (do not delete extra current navs — they may be a
  theme-specific responsive duplicate).
- Selector matches zero current elements → silent no-op.
- Fetch fails → caught and logged.

## Verification

```bash
npm run lint:js
npm run test:js -- src/floating-widget/reflectors/__tests__/menu.test.js
npm run build
```

Manual smoke test:

1. Open the site front page on the dev wp-env.
2. Open the floating widget.
3. Ask the agent: "Add a 'Contact' link to the primary navigation menu."
4. The visible nav updates to include "Contact" within ~1s.

## Out of scope

- Do NOT swap server-rendered HTML for client-rendered React menus.
  WordPress core's `wp-block-navigation` is server-rendered; this
  reflector handles the SSR output.
- Do NOT handle the WP admin Appearance → Menus screen. That is a
  block-editor surface and has its own state.
- Do NOT touch widget-rendered legacy menus (`<div class="widget">`
  wrappers). They are out of the supported subset; the fallback toast
  (Phase 2e) catches them.

## Estimated effort

3-4h.

title: Phase 2e: Fallback reload-toast for unmapped affected kinds
body: ## Phase 2e — Fallback "reload to see changes" toast For #1947 — parent: Frontend live-preview pipeline. Builds on Phase 2b. ## Goal When the agent finishes a tool call whose `affected.kind` does NOT have a dedicated reflector (Phase 2b/c/d), show a small one-click toast in the corner of the page: "Site updated — reload to see changes." This is the honest UX floor: better than silently showing stale content, worse than a real reflector. Used for `kind = 'media'`, `kind = 'term'`, and anything else without a mapped strategy. ## Prerequisite - Phase 2b reflector dispatcher (`src/floating-widget/reflectors/index.js`) is in place. ## Files to create - `src/floating-widget/reflectors/fallback-toast.js` - `src/floating-widget/reflectors/fallback-toast.css` - `src/floating-widget/reflectors/__tests__/fallback-toast.test.js` ## Files to modify - `src/floating-widget/reflectors/index.js` — add `default: showFallbackToast( event ); break;` to the `switch (event.affected.kind)` block. ## Behavior 1. On first matching event, render a fixed-position toast at the bottom-right (above the FAB) with copy: *"Agent updated the site. Reload to see changes."* plus a primary "Reload" button and a secondary "Dismiss" button. 2. If more matching events arrive while the toast is visible, increment a badge counter ("Agent made 3 updates. Reload to see changes."). 3. "Reload" calls `window.location.reload()`. 4. "Dismiss" hides the toast. The counter resets to zero. If another event arrives later, the toast reappears. 5. The toast does NOT auto-dismiss. The user must explicitly act. ## Visual constraints - Must not overlap the FAB. Position: `bottom: 88px; right: 24px;` (the FAB sits at `bottom: 24px; right: 24px;` with a 48px diameter). - CSS class prefix `sd-ai-agent-` per AGENTS.md. - Plain DOM + CSS — no React, to keep this in the always-loaded chunk rather than `widget-panel` lazy chunk. title: Phase 3: Frontend widget hardening — cap-gate, cache headers, perf budget
body:
## Phase 3 — Frontend widget hardening: cap-gate review, cache headers, perf budget

For #1947 — parent: Frontend live-preview pipeline. Builds on Phase 2a-e.

## Goal

Make the frontend floating widget shippable to non-admin users without
regressing security or perf budgets. Three concrete deliverables:

1. **Cap-gate review.** Decide and document the user-facing cap that
   may use the frontend widget. Today it is `manage_options`. Survey
   every ability the widget can invoke and produce a recommendation.
2. **Cache headers / cache-bust strategy.** Reflectors fetch the public
   page URL; ensure WP Super Cache, Cloudflare, Varnish, and Nginx
   FastCGI cache return fresh HTML when the reflector requests it.
3. **Perf budget.** Add a CI gate that the `floating-widget` chunk
   stays under 80 KiB minified (today: ~69 KiB after PR #1946 +
   reflectors estimate).

This is one tracked work item but the three pieces are independent;
file three sibling PRs against this issue if helpful.

## Prerequisite

- All of Phase 2 (a-e) merged. Without the reflectors landed we cannot
  measure the real bundle size or exercise the cache path end-to-end.

## Part 1 — Cap-gate review

### Files to inspect

- Every ability under `includes/Abilities/*.php` — list the WP cap
  each one checks in its `execute()` / `permission_callback`.
- `includes/Settings.php` (or wherever `show_on_frontend` is gated) —
  current frontend-render cap check.
- `includes/REST/RestController.php` — the cap check applied to the
  REST endpoints that the widget calls from the frontend.

### Deliverable

A markdown table in `docs/frontend-widget-capabilities.md` listing each
ability, the cap it requires, and the verdict (`frontend-safe` /
`admin-only` / `needs-narrower-cap`). Plus a recommendation paragraph:
"The frontend widget should require cap X because Y."

Likely candidates: `edit_posts` (too broad — includes attachments),
`publish_posts`, or a new `sd_ai_agent_use_frontend` meta-cap mapped to
`manage_options` by default with a documented `map_meta_cap` filter.

### Verification

```bash
rg -nE "current_user_can|has_cap|require_capability" includes/Abilities/ includes/REST/ includes/Settings.php
```

The doc must cite at least one match per ability.

## Part 2 — Cache headers / cache-bust strategy

### Files to modify

- `src/floating-widget/reflectors/dom-morph.js` — confirm `fetchFreshPage`
  includes `cache: 'no-store'` AND a `_=<ts>` query parameter. Both are
  required: `cache: no-store` bypasses the browser cache, the query
  param bypasses Varnish / Cloudflare / WP Super Cache page caches
  that ignore the `Cache-Control: no-store` request header.
- `includes/Frontend/CachePolicy.php` (NEW) — a small handler that
  fires on `template_redirect` (priority 1, before any cache plugin)
  to detect the reflector-init request shape and send
  `Cache-Control: no-store, no-cache, must-revalidate` plus a header
  the agent can read. Use a custom request header — `X-Sd-Ai-Agent-Reflector: 1`
  — set by `fetchFreshPage`, and detect with
  `isset($_SERVER['HTTP_X_SD_AI_AGENT_REFLECTOR'])`.

### Plugin compatibility

The cache-bust query param defeats:

- WP Super Cache (default config caches by URL including query string —
  bypasses on unique query).
- W3 Total Cache (same).
- Cloudflare Cache Rules with default WordPress recipe (bypasses on
  query string by default).
- Nginx FastCGI cache with the WordPress recipe (bypasses query strings
  by default).

For sites that have customized their cache to ignore query strings,
the `X-Sd-Ai-Agent-Reflector` request header + matching `Cache-Control:
no-store` response is the second line of defence.

Document in `docs/frontend-widget-capabilities.md` (extend Part 1's
doc): "If your cache layer ignores query strings, configure it to bypass
when the request has header `X-Sd-Ai-Agent-Reflector: 1`."

### Verification

```bash
npm run test:js -- src/floating-widget/reflectors/__tests__/dom-morph.test.js
npm run lint:php
composer phpstan
npm run test:php -- --filter='CachePolicyTest'
```

Manual smoke test (against a wp-env with WP Super Cache active):

1. Visit a cached page; confirm `X-Cache: HIT` (or equivalent).
2. Trigger an agent post update.
3. Network panel shows the reflector request with `?_=…`, response
   `X-Cache: BYPASS`, and the visible page updates.

## Part 3 — Perf budget

### Files to create

- `scripts/check-bundle-size.js` — small Node script that reads
  `build/floating-widget.asset.php` or `build/floating-widget.js`,
  reports gzipped + raw minified size, and exits non-zero if either
  exceeds the budget.

### Files to modify

- `package.json` — add `"check:bundle": "node scripts/check-bundle-size.js"`
  and chain it into `npm run verify`.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (or whichever workflow runs `npm run build`)
  — invoke `npm run check:bundle` after the build step.

### Budgets

| Chunk | Minified | Gzipped |
|---|---|---|
| `floating-widget.js` (entry) | 80 KiB | 28 KiB |
| `widget-panel.js` (lazy) | 220 KiB | 70 KiB |

These numbers are 15% above the current measured values to leave
headroom. Reflectors should not push the entry chunk over 80 KiB —
morphdom is ~5 KiB minified.

### Verification

```bash
npm run build && npm run check:bundle
```

CI must fail when the gate trips. Add a PHPUnit-style summary line to
the worker self-verification block format:

```text
- Bundle:  floating-widget 69.2 KiB (budget 80 KiB), widget-panel 198 KiB (budget 220 KiB)
```

## Out of scope

- Do NOT design a new frontend permission model from scratch. Reuse
  existing WP caps; document the choice; ship.
- Do NOT add a service worker for offline reflection. The frontend
  widget requires the agent backend, which requires the network.
- Do NOT add CDN-level Edge Side Includes. Too much per-site
  configuration; the query-string bust covers the 95% case.

## Estimated effort

8-12h split across the three parts. Cap-gate review is the largest;
the doc + the actual code change (if `manage_options` is replaced) +
the test updates that follow from a cap change.

title: bug: contact form created but non-functional after WPForms Lite install
body:
## Description
Agent created a contact page with a WPForms Lite contact form, but the form did not work. The agent installed WPForms Lite, created a form via the `sd-ai-agent/create-contact-form` ability, and embedded the shortcode in the page. However, the user reported that the resulting contact form was non-functional.

## Expected Behavior
After creating a contact form and embedding it in a page, the form should be functional and ready to receive submissions. The agent should verify that the form renders correctly and is accessible to site visitors.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Request the agent to "setup a contact page"
2. Agent loads the contact-forms skill
3. Agent creates a page titled "Contact Us"
4. Agent searches for and installs WPForms Lite plugin
5. Agent calls `sd-ai-agent/create-contact-form` to create a form
6. Agent embeds the form shortcode in the page via `update-post`
7. Visit the contact page on the frontend — form does not work

## Root Cause
The agent has no visibility into whether the form actually renders or functions after creation. WPForms Lite does not register WP Abilities, so the agent cannot verify form functionality post-creation. The agent's memory note indicates awareness of this limitation but no recovery action was taken.

## Environment
- Plugin version: v1.16.2
- WordPress: 7.0
- PHP: 8.4.21
- Multisite: false
- Provider: ultimate-ai-connector-anthropic-max / claude-opus-4-8
- Theme: twentytwentyfour

title: Register first-party Superdav AI provider
body:
## Goal

Add a first-party WordPress AI Client SDK provider inside the Superdav AI Agent plugin that connects to the Superdav-hosted OpenAI-compatible AI service.

## Context

The plugin already routes AI requests through the WordPress AI Client SDK rather than direct vendor HTTP paths:

- `includes/Core/AgentLoop.php` builds requests with `wp_ai_client_prompt()` and SDK provider/model APIs.
- `includes/Core/ProviderCredentialLoader.php` loads connector credentials into the SDK registry.
- `includes/REST/SettingsController.php` discovers configured providers and models from the SDK registry.
- `includes/Core/Settings.php` validates saved default provider/model pairs against the live SDK registry.

Use the repo naming rules from `AGENTS.md`: keep the internal provider/code identifiers in the `sd-ai-agent` family. Do not rename plugin internals to `superdav-ai-agent` except for the existing slug/text-domain contexts.

## Proposed implementation

Create a first-party provider implementation under a focused namespace such as:

```text
includes/Infrastructure/AiClient/Superdav/SuperdavAiProvider.php
includes/Infrastructure/AiClient/Superdav/SuperdavAiTextGenerationModel.php
includes/Infrastructure/AiClient/Superdav/SuperdavAiModelMetadataDirectory.php
includes/Bootstrap/SuperdavAiProviderHandler.php
```

Register the provider with the default SDK registry during plugin bootstrap, for example from a DI handler:

```php
\WordPress\AiClient\AiClient::defaultRegistry()->registerProvider( SuperdavAiProvider::class );
```

Suggested canonical values:

- Provider ID: `sd-ai-agent-cloud`
- Display name: `Superdav AI`
- Credential option: `connectors_ai_sd_ai_agent_cloud_api_key`

## Requirements

- Use the WordPress AI Client SDK provider APIs; do not add a new direct HTTP fallback in `AgentLoop`.
- Implement an OpenAI-compatible text generation model using the SDK OpenAI-compatible base classes where possible.
- Base URL must be configurable/filterable, e.g. `sd_ai_agent_cloud_base_url`, and must not contain secrets.
- Support at minimum:
  - `GET /models`
  - `POST /chat/completions`
- Handle SDK registry failures gracefully, matching existing provider behaviour.
- Keep provider/model discovery cache-free at the plugin layer; rely on the SDK model metadata cache.

## Acceptance criteria

- `sd-ai-agent-cloud` is registered in `AiClient::defaultRegistry()`.
- The provider is returned by the plugin provider listing after credentials are configured.
- `AgentLoop` can select the provider through existing `default_provider` settings.
- Existing OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and third-party connector behaviour is unchanged.

## Verification

```bash
npm run test:php -- --filter='SettingsTest|AgentLoopTest'
npm run lint:php
composer phpstan
```
